Close to this sense are the watches, all of them waking, rousing and keeping the times: בְּאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַבֹּקֶר (Shemos 14:24), in the morning watch, and רֹאשׁ הָֽאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַתִּֽיכוֹנָה (Shoftim 7:19), at the head of the middle watch. Chazal say (Berachos 3a) that the night has three watches, and so it appears from the pasuk that speaks of the middle watch. That is why a city's watchman is called so, since he is awake at night, guards the city and knows the hours of the night. אָחַזְתָּ שְׁמֻרוֹת עֵינָי (Tehillim 77:5), You held the watches of my eyes: as though You had seized and held them fast, so that my eyes stay always awake and I do not sleep. Rabbi Moshe HaKohen took it from the first sense, reading שְׁמֻרוֹת as an adjective like שׁוֹמְרוֹת, guarding ones, the eyelids that guard the eyes: You held my eyelids, so that they did not close and I did not sleep.

וְשֹׁקֵט הוּא אֶל־שְׁמָרָיו (Yirmiyahu 48:11), and he has been quiet on his lees, and הַקֹּֽפְאִים עַל־שִׁמְרֵיהֶם (Tzefaniah 1:12), those congealed upon their lees. הִשָּׁמֵר וְהַשְׁקֵט (Yeshayahu 7:4), השמר and be quiet, is from this sense: sit upon your lees in rest and in quiet. It is accented on the last syllable, whereas in the sense of guarding the accent falls on the one before. Rav Saadiah Gaon took it as guarding, which comes to: guard yourself from making war, and be quiet, do not fear.

more.h: שָׁמִיר, the hard stone and the thorn
more.t: כְּשָׁמִיר חָזָק מִצֹּר (Yechezkel 3:9), like a shamir, harder than flint; בְּצִפֹּרֶן שָׁמִיר (Yirmiyahu 17:1), with a point of shamir; and מִצּוּר הַֽחַלָּמִֽישׁ (Devarim 8:15), out of the flinty rock, which the Targum Yerushalmi renders שמרי טינרא, the shamir of the rock. Some read בְּצִפֹּרֶן שָׁמִיר as the hard iron, named so for its strength, as the hard rock is called שמיר. In another sense שָׁמִיר is a thorn: קוֹץ שָׁמִיר תַּֽעֲלֶה (Yeshayahu 32:13), thorn, shamir, shall come up, which Radak glosses קוץ ושמיר, thorn and shamir; and שָׁמִיר וָשַׁיִת תֹּאכֵל (Yeshayahu 9:17), it shall consume shamir and shayis, shamir being one of the kinds of thorns.

ארח.sense: אֹרַח, a way, the noun the verb is taken from; also a custom or manner, a wayfarer, a caravan, named for the ways it travels, and a man's meal and upkeep.

more.t: וְאָרַח לְחֶבְרָה עִם פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן (Iyov 34:8), and he goes his way in company with workers of iniquity, is the verb, and the noun it is taken from is אֹרַח, whose sense is דרך, a way: וּכְאֹרַח אִישׁ יַמְצִאֶנּוּ (Iyov 34:11), and according to a man's way He will let it find him, and אָרְחִי וְרִבְעִי זֵרִיתָ (Tehillim 139:3), my way and my lying down You encompass. In the plural, חָדְלוּ אֳרָחוֹת (Shoftim 5:6), the ways ceased, he glosses as those who pass along the ways ceased, and אֳרָחוֹת עֲקַלְקַלּוֹת stands in the same pasuk, crooked ways. וְתִשְׁמוֹר כָּל אָרְחוֹתָי (Iyov 13:27), and You watch all my ways, has a kamatz in Ben Asher's reading and a cholam in Ben Naftali's.
לָאֹרֵחַ הַבָּא לוֹ (Shmuel II 12:4), the traveller who came to him: he is one going, עוֹבֵר אוֹרַח, passing along the way from place to place.
אֹרַח כַּנָּשִׁים (Bereishis 18:11), the way of women, he glosses מנהג כנשים, the custom of women; and likewise כִּי דֶרֶךְ נָשִׁים לִי (Bereishis 31:35), for the way of women is upon me.

אֹרְחַת יִשְׁמְעֵאלִים (Bereishis 37:25), a caravan of Yishmaelim, is as the Targum renders it, שְׁיָרַת עֲרָבָאֵי, a caravan of Arabians; and likewise אֹרְחוֹת דְּדָנִים (Yeshayahu 21:13), caravans of Dedanim. Because caravans are always going along the ways and roads, they themselves were named for the ways.

וַאֲרֻחָתוֹ אֲרֻחַת תָּמִיד (Melachim II 25:30) he glosses as his meal and his upkeep, a continual one, and טוֹב אֲרֻחַת יָרָק (Mishlei 15:17), better a meal of herbs. These, he says, do not fall outside the first sense but are counted within it.

קדשׁ.sense: To be holy, and to make holy; also, to become forbidden, as holy things are. A second sense is designating, as in appointing a fast or a war.

more.t: פֶּן־תִּקְדַּשׁ הַֽמְלֵאָה הַזֶּרַע (Devarim 22:9), lest the full yield of the seed תקדש, which he glosses: lest it become forbidden in benefit, as kodesh is. So Chazal said (Kiddushin 56b): from where do we know that kilayim of the vineyard are forbidden in benefit? It says there ואיש כי יקדיש את ביתו קדש, and when a man consecrates his house as holy, and it says here פן תקדש; as there it is forbidden in benefit, so here.

וְאֶל־כָּל־מַֽאֲכָל הֲיִקְדָּשׁ (Chaggai 2:12), or any food, היקדש: he glosses it היטמא, will it become tamei, that is, forbidden by its tumah as kodesh is forbidden. Chaggai was putting the laws of tumah to the kohanim, which they may have forgotten in the galus. His question was whether the food that stands fourth in tumah is tamei, the food alone, since he says היקדש, in the singular, and not היקדשו, in the plural; and they said no. Some of Chazal hold (Pesachim 17a) that the kohanim erred in this answer, a fourth degree being tamei in kodesh, though to the other question, of one made tamei by a corpse, they answered rightly. On this view, as Radak explains it, they knew a third degree in kodesh to be tamei but not a fourth, and in that they erred; that is why the navi answered them וַֽאֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ שָׁם טָמֵא הֽוּא, and what they offer there is tamei. Others of Chazal hold that they erred in neither; others, that Chaggai first asked them about a fifth degree in kodesh, and they rightly answered that it is not tamei; others, that he asked them before the decree on a fourth degree in kodesh. On the view that they did not err, Radak explains the navi's answer: though they know the laws of tumah and taharah, all that they offer is as though tamei, since they are slack in building the Beis. The whole parsha, he holds, bears out that they did not err, since throughout it the navi rebukes them over nothing but the Beis.

כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יִגַּע בִּבְשָׂרָהּ יִקְדָּשׁ (Vayikra 6:20), whatever touches its flesh becomes holy: food that touches the flesh of the chatas and absorbs from it becomes holy as it is. If the chatas is pasul, by piggul or some other disqualification, what touches it is pasul; if it is fit, what touches it is eaten by the stricter of the two. So shelamim flesh slaughtered the day before that touched a chatas slaughtered today is eaten that day only, by the law of shelamim, which are eaten for two days and one night, and not that night as the chatas is; and where both were slaughtered today, the shelamim flesh is eaten by the law of the chatas, that day and night only, and not the next day as other shelamim. כָּל־הַנֹּגֵעַ בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ יִקְדָּֽשׁ (Shemos 29:37), whatever touches the mizbeach becomes holy: even a korban already pasul that has gone up on the mizbeach is made fit by it, and once it has gone up it does not come down; and that is where it was fit for the mizbeach to begin with and became pasul only by one of the things that disqualify a korban.

וְעָשׂוּ לִי מִקְדָּשׁ (Shemos 25:8), and they shall make Me a sanctuary: the house of holiness is called מִקְדָּשׁ. A king's palace is called so as well, since it is like a mikdash, where none enter but those known there: כִּי מִקְדַּשׁ־מֶלֶךְ הוּא (Amos 7:13), for it is a king's mikdash.

Some read וְהָיָה לְמִקְדָּשׁ (Yeshayahu 8:14), and He shall be for a mikdash, from this sense: a place a man goes to be secure. On that reading לִשְׁנֵי בָתֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל, for the two houses of Yisrael, is to the one for good and to the other for ill, since Shevna and his party had made peace with the king of Ashur and Chizkiyahu and his party had not. It can also be read as designation, a designation of punishment, a stumbling block set before them, as וְנָתַתִּי מִכְשׁוֹל לְפָנָיו (Yechezkel 3:20), and I shall set a stumbling block before him; the two houses are then Pekach ben Remalyahu and Shevna with his party, both of whom wanted the kingdom of Beis David to fall.

קַדְּשׁוּ־צוֹם קִרְאוּ עֲצָרָה (Yoel 1:14), appoint a fast, call an assembly, and קַדְּשׁוּ עָלֶיהָ מִלְחָמָה (Yirmiyahu 6:4), appoint war against her: these and all like them are the sense of designating. The קָדֵשׁ and the קְדֵשָׁה, as in לֹא־תִֽהְיֶה קְדֵשָׁה (Devarim 23:18), there shall be no קדשה, are all of them those designated for lying with.

אמן.sense: To believe and trust; אֱמֶת, truth, of this root in his view; אָמֵן, it shall be true; to be firm and endure; to rear a child; the אָמָּן, one who excels at a craft.

more.t: לְמַעַן יַֽאֲמִינוּ (Shemos 4:5), that they may believe. All such forms are trust and acceptance, קרידינצא in his own vernacular, credence; and they come out of the sense of אמונה, since one who believes a thing gives it אמונה, credence, and holds it true.

In his own view אֱמֶת, truth, belongs to this root, its proper form being אֱמֶנֶת on the pattern of דְּבֶֽלֶת, the nun having fallen away for ease as it fell from בת, a daughter, whose proper form is בֶּֽנֶת; the dagesh it takes when suffixes are joined to it proves as much, and its plural is formed as בנות, daughters, is.

וְאָמַר כָּל־הָעָם אָמֵֽן (Devarim 27:17), and all the people shall say amen, is, it shall be true that whoever transgresses one of these shall be cursed, said either as a prayer or as acceptance, that they took the curse upon themselves should they transgress. So וְגַם־ אָמְנָה אֲחֹתִי בַת־אָבִי (Bereishis 20:12): and also, it is true that she is my sister, my father's daughter.

וְנֶֽאְמַן בֵּיתְךָ וּמַמְלַכְתְּךָ (Shmuel II 7:16), your house and your kingdom shall endure; יָתֵד בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן (Yeshayahu 22:23), a peg in a place strong and lasting; מַכּוֹת גְּדֹלֹת וְנֶאֱמָנוֹת (Devarim 28:59), great blows, strong and lasting; וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה (Shemos 17:12), and his hands were steady, that is, they stayed raised, and they did not let them down until the sun set. אֲנַחְנוּ כֹּֽרְתִים אֲמָנָה (Nechemiah 10:1), we are making an אֲמָנָה, a thing made to stand; and וְאֶת־ הָאֹמְנוֹת אֲשֶׁר צִפָּה חִזְקִיָּה (Melachim II 18:16), and the אֹמְנוֹת that Chizkiyah had overlaid, are the pillars that held the building up. Yonasan renders it וְיַת סְקוֹפַיָא, that is, the thresholds of the gates.

כַּֽאֲשֶׁר יִשָּׂא הָֽאֹמֵן אֶת־הַיֹּנֵק (Bamidbar 11:12), as the one who rears carries the suckling; וַתִּשָּׂאֵהוּ אֹֽמַנְתּוֹ (Shmuel II 4:4), and she who reared him carried him; הָאֱמֻנִים עֲלֵי תוֹלָע (Eichah 4:5), those reared on scarlet; וְאֶל־ הָאֹֽמְנִים אַחְאָב (Melachim II 10:1), and to the rearers of Achav, are those who reared him from his youth and were the men of his counsel, in whose charge the affairs of the kingdom lay. Here his father puts בָּנִים לֹֽא־ אֵמֻן בָּֽם (Devarim 32:20), children in whom there is no אֵמֻן, and Radak explains him to mean there is no upbringing in them, a perverse generation who do evil when they are done good, as it says וַיִּשְׁמַן יְשֻׁרוּן וַיִּבְעָט (Devarim 32:15), Yeshurun grew fat and kicked. Radak's own reading, given earlier in the entry, is children who do not believe, or in whom there is no truth.

more.h: Where he differs from Rabbi Yonah
more.t: Rabbi Yonah brought מֵסִיר שָׂפָה לְנֶאֱמָנִים (Iyov 12:20), He takes away the speech of the נֶאֱמָנִים, into this root. Radak holds it is from נאם and of its sense, as וַיִּנְֽאֲמוּ נְאֻֽם (Yirmiyahu 23:31), and they speak a speech, which is a term for speaking; the closing nun is added as the mark of an adjective, as in רחמן and נעמן, and men clear in their tongue who know the wisdom of speech are called נאמנים.

שֹלם.sense: שַׂלְמָה, a garment, as though שִֹמְלָה with its letters turned about.

more.t: One line, on עַל שֶׂה עַל שַׂלְמָה (Shemos 22:8), over a sheep, over a garment.

שׁלם.sense: To repay, in requital and payment. In another sense, to be complete or finished. In a third, peace, שָׁלוֹם, and from it the shelamim offering is named.

more.t: יְשַׁלְּמוּנִי רָעָה תַּחַת טוֹבָה (Tehillim 35:12), they repay me evil for good; שַׁלֵּם יְשַׁלֵּם שׁוֹר תַּחַת הַשּׁוֹר (Shemos 21:36), he shall surely pay ox for ox. The nouns are בָּאוּ יְמֵי הַשִּׁלֻּם (Hoshea 9:7), the days of requital have come, וְשִׁלֻּמַת רְשָׁעִים תִּרְאֶֽה (Tehillim 91:8), and you will see the requital of the wicked, and לִי נָקָם וְשִׁלֵּם (Devarim 32:35), Mine are vengeance and requital; the sense of all of them is requital and payment.

כִּי לֹֽא־שָׁלֵם עֲוֹן הָֽאֱמֹרִי עַד־הֵֽנָּה (Bereishis 15:16), for the sin of the Emori is not yet complete; וְשָֽׁלְמוּ יְמֵי אֶבְלֵֽךְ (Yeshayahu 60:20), and the days of your mourning shall be ended; וַתִּשְׁלַם כָּל־הַמְּלָאכָה (Melachim I 7:51), and all the work was finished. הָגְלָת שְׁלוֹמִֽים (Yirmiyahu 13:19) means that all of them went into exile, and in the same way his father read מוּסַר שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ (Yeshayahu 53:5) as the chastisement of all of us. אֶבֶן שְׁלֵמָה (Devarim 25:15) is a stone full in weight, and אֲבָנִים שְׁלֵמוֹת (Devarim 27:6) are whole stones, which have not been hewn.

שְֽׁלֵמִים הֵם אִתָּנוּ (Bereishis 34:21), they are at peace with us; הֲשָׁלוֹם אֲבִיכֶם הַזָּקֵן (Bereishis 43:27), is your aged father at peace, the word here an adjective. From this sense, אִם־גָּמַלְתִּי שׁוֹלְמִי רָע (Tehillim 7:5) is, did I repay evil to one who was at peace with me. In the heavy form it is to make peace: כִּֽי־הִשְׁלִימָה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁעַ (Yehoshua 10:4), for it made peace with Yehoshua. Where the verb takes an object, passing on to a third, it is to make others be at peace: גַּם־אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִם אִתּֽוֹ (Mishlei 16:7), even his enemies He makes to be at peace with him.

more.h: Why the שְׁלָמִים is so called
more.t: From this sense comes זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים (Vayikra 3:1), the shelamim offering, called so for how it is shared. Of the olah all is burnt whole and the hide goes to the kohanim; of the chatas and the asham the blood and the eimurim go to the mizbeach and the breast and thigh to the kohanim; but of the zevach shelamim the blood and the eimurim go to the mizbeach, the breast and thigh to the kohanim, and the rest of the flesh and the hide to the owners, so that this zevach is peace among them all, as the Sifra sets it out in parshas Ve'im Zevach Shelamim. For that reason it is also called מִלּוּאִים, as in כִּי אֵיל מִלֻּאִים הֽוּא (Shemos 29:22), for it is a ram of fillings, because it filled the will of all of them, all of them eating from it.
שׁוּבִי שׁוּבִי הַשּׁוּלַמִּית (Shir HaShirim 7:1), return, return, O Shulamis: she who dwells in Yerushalayim, which is called שָׁלֵם.

ראה.sense: To see, with the eyes and with the heart, which is to understand; מַרְאֶה and מַרְאָה, a sight and a vision; רֹאֶה, seeing, which he reads as prophecy.

more.t: וְלִבִּי רָאָה הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה וָדָֽעַת (Koheles 1:16), my heart saw much wisdom and knowledge. וַיַּרְא יַֽעֲקֹב כִּי יֶשׁ־שֶׁבֶר (Bereishis 42:1), Yaakov saw that there was grain, is either that he saw the people of the land going to Mitzrayim to buy grain, or that he saw in his heart, that is, he understood from what he had heard and seen, as the heart saw in Koheles. הַדּוֹר אַתֶּם רְאוּ (Yirmiyahu 2:31), you, O generation, see, is, give your mind to the word of Hashem; and of the heart's seeing too is רְאֵה דְבָרֶיךָ טוֹבִים וּנְכֹחִים (Shmuel II 15:3), see, your words are good and right, that is, give your mind and understand.

more.h: The other senses lent to sight
more.t: Because the eye's perception is greater than the rest, the other senses are spoken of as seeing: וְכָל־הָעָם רֹאִים אֶת־הַקּוֹלֹת (Shemos 20:15), all the people saw the sounds, and רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי (Bereishis 27:27), see the smell of my son.

שָׁגוּ בָּֽרֹאֶה (Yeshayahu 28:7), they erred in the seeing, is, they erred in prophecy; his father read it as, they erred in a thing seen by every man. רֹאֶה is a noun, seeing, and with the suffix of the one speaking, אַֽחֲרֵי רֹאִֽי (Bereishis 16:13) is, after my prophecy; so Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar wrote, and Radak says it is right. Radak also reads the same words as, after the One who sees me, that is, the One who appeared to me and saw me in my affliction.

לֹֽא־ אֶרְאֶה יָהּ (Yeshayahu 38:11), I shall not see Hashem, Rav Saadiah Gaon explained in the sense of thanksgiving, and Radak says it is right, since to see the Creator is to give thanks and praise before Him and to consider His ways.

Some read הֵמָּה יַבִּיטוּ יִרְאוּ ־בִֽי (Tehillim 22:18), they look, they gaze at me, as contempt, and so לְרַֽאֲוָה בָֽךְ (Yechezkel 28:17), to gaze at you. Radak holds there is no need to take them out of their own sense, and so Yonasan renders לְרַֽאֲוָה בָֽךְ as לְאִסְתַכְּלָא בָךְ, to look at you.

וְהֵסִיר אֶת־ מֻרְאָתוֹ (Vayikra 1:16), and he shall remove its crop, the מֻרְאָה being the bird's crop, as the Targum has it; וְשַׂמְתִּיךְ כְּרֹֽאִי (Nachum 3:6), and I will make you as filth, is of the sense of filth and soiling. Of וְהָֽרָאָה וְאֶת־הָאַיָּה (Devarim 14:13), and the ra'ah and the ayah, Chazal say (Chullin 63b) that the ra'ah is the da'ah, and that it is called ra'ah because it sees exceedingly.

עלה.sense: To go up; the עֹלָה, an offering named for going up whole, and the עֲלִיָּה, an upper room, are from it. Close to it, to be cut off and to cease. Also עָלֶה, a leaf.

more.t: עָלִיתָ לַמָּרוֹם (Tehillim 68:19), You went up on high; וְעָלָה הַגְּבוּל (Yehoshua 15:8), and the border goes up; וּבָשָׂר עָלָה (Yechezkel 37:8), and flesh came up over the sinews and the bones; כִּי עָלָה הַשָּׁחַר (Bereishis 32:27), for the dawn has come up, that is, the brightness of the day. מִֽלְמַֽעֲלֵה הֶחָֽרֶס (Shoftim 8:13) he reads as from the going up of the sun's brightness and its shining. Targum Yonasan has עַד לָא מֵעַל שִׁמְשָׁא, before the sun set, and in Yonasan's view the word means that the sun was still up, seen in the sky and not yet gone in under the earth.

עֹלָה הוּא אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ (Vayikra 1:13), it is an olah, a fire offering of pleasing savour. The korban is called so because it went up whole, all of it, upon the mizbeach. שֹׂנֵא גָזֵל בְּעוֹלָה (Yeshayahu 61:8), hating robbery in an olah, he explains: if a man brings before Me an olah that was stolen, I hate it, as it says וַֽהֲבֵאתֶם גָּזוּל (Malachi 1:13), and you have brought what was stolen.

more.h: A sense close to it: being cut off
more.t: יְצוּעִי עָלָֽה (Bereishis 49:4), from the day you profaned it my couch was cut off; שֻׁדַּד מוֹאָב וְעָרֶיהָ עָלָה (Yirmiyahu 48:15), Moav is plundered and her cities cut off; וַתַּעַל שִׁכְבַת הַטָּל (Shemos 16:14), and the layer of dew ceased; אַֽל־ תַּֽעֲלֵנִי בַּֽחֲצִי יָמָי (Tehillim 102:25), do not cut me off in the midst of my days. Some read וְעָֽלְתָה יָדוֹ עַל־יַד רֵעֵֽהוּ (Zecharyah 14:13) in this sense, his hand shall be cut off and cease against his fellow's hand, and so Targum Yonasan renders וְתִתְּלַשׁ יְדֵיהּ, and his hand shall be torn away. On that reading, when a man takes hold of his fellow's hand his own hand will be cut off, as it says הָמֵק בְּשָׂרוֹ (Zecharyah 14:12), his flesh shall rot away. Some read וְהַבַּיִת הַזֶּה יִֽהְיֶה עֶלְיוֹן (Melachim I 9:8), and this house shall be high, as cutting off and ruin too; Radak holds there is no need to take it out of the first sense, and reads it: this house, which is now high, when they sin, every passer by will be appalled and hiss.

more.h: Rooms above, steps, and the hours
more.t: וַיָּסַר אֶל־ הָֽעֲלִיָּה (Melachim II 4:11), and he turned in to the upper room, and עֲלִיַּת ־קִיר (Melachim II 4:10), a walled upper room, are from this sense: the upper room is so called because it is over the house and a man goes up to it. So too וְלֹא־תַֽעֲלֶה בְמַֽעֲלֹת (Shemos 20:23), and you shall not go up by steps, steps being so called because a man goes up on them. צֵל הַֽמַּֽעֲלוֹת (Yeshayahu 38:8), the shadow of the steps, Targum Yonasan renders טוּל אֶבֶן שְׁעַיָא, the shadow of the stone of hours, which is what the Mishnah (Keilim 12:4) calls אבן השעות, the stone of hours, one marked so as to know the hours of the day.

עַל is a word of this root, from the first sense, and much used: עֲלֵֽי ־עָשׂוֹר וַֽעֲלֵי ־נָבֶל (Tehillim 92:4), upon the asor and upon the nevel, and without the yud of the plural, עַל ־פְּנֵי הַמָּֽיִם (Bereishis 1:2), upon the face of the waters. It comes in the sense of with: וַיָּבֹאוּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים עַל ־הַנָּשִׁים (Shemos 35:22), the men came with the women. In the sense of beside: וְזָֽבַחְתָּ עָלָיו אֶת־עֹֽלֹתֶיךָ (Shemos 20:21), and you shall slaughter your olos beside it, since the slaughtering was not done on the mizbeach, and חֹנִים עַל ־הַיָּם (Shemos 14:9), encamped beside the sea. It stands for אל, to: וַיֵּלֶךְ אֶלְקָנָה הָֽרָמָתָה עַל ־בֵּיתוֹ (Shmuel I 2:11), and Elkanah went to Ramah, to his house. And it stands for the prefixed beis: הִמָּלֵט עַל ־נַפְשֶׁךָ (Bereishis 19:17) is like בנפשך, escape with your life.

וְהִנֵּה עֲלֵה ־זַיִת טָרָף בְּפִיהָ (Bereishis 8:11), and behold, a plucked olive leaf in her mouth, and וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ עֲלֵה תְאֵנָה (Bereishis 3:7), and they sewed fig leaves, are the leaf, a word well known. Of וְהָבִיאוּ עֲלֵי ־זַיִת (Nechemiah 8:15), and bring olive leaves, he says the branches together with the leaves are meant. His father read הִצִּית אֵשׁ עָלֶיהָ (Yirmiyahu 11:16) as kindling fire on its leaves, and Dunash read פֶּן יִפְקֹד עָלֶיהָ (Yeshayahu 27:3) from this: lest even the leaf be lacking, still less the fruit.

קדם.sense: To go before, which he holds takes in coming before someone to meet him; קֶדֶם, of old, and the east, as the west is called behind; and קָדִים, the east wind.

more.t: מִימֵי קֶדֶם (Yeshayahu 23:7), from days of old, and וּמֵרֹאשׁ הַרֲרֵי קֶדֶם (Devarim 33:15), and from the top of the ancient mountains; with the adjective, מְשַׁל הַקַּדְמֹנִי (Shmuel I 24:13 in his edition), the proverb of the ancients, and בְּיָמִים קַדְמוֹנִים (Yechezkel 38:17), in former days. Another pattern of the noun is תָּשֹׁבְןָ לְקַדְמָתָן (Yechezkel 16:55), they will return to their former state.

עַל־כֵּן קִדַּמְתִּי לִבְרֹחַ תַּרְשִׁישָׁה (Yonah 4:2), therefore I went ahead and fled to Tarshish, and אֲשֶׁר לֹֽא־ קִדְּמוּ אֶתְכֶם בַּלֶּחֶם וּבַמַּיִם (Devarim 23:5), that they did not come before you with bread and water: all of them are ענין הקדמה, going before, and the sense is known. Rabbi Yonah divides them into two senses; Radak holds there is no need, for קַדְּמָה פָנָיו הַכְרִיעֵהוּ (Tehillim 17:13) means, present Yourself before him in Your wrath and fury and bring him down, and so כִּֽי־תְקַדְּמֶנּוּ בִּרְכוֹת טוֹב (Tehillim 21:4), for You come before him with blessings of good, and the like; and presenting oneself is going before. In that pasuk בִּרְכוֹת is בברכות, with blessings, for the verb is intransitive.

more.h: The east is קדם, the west behind
more.t: The eastern quarter is called קדם, as the western, opposite it, is called אָחוֹר, behind: גַּן־בְּעֵדֶן מִקֶּדֶם (Bereishis 2:8), a garden in Eden, to the east, and הֵן קֶדֶם אֶהֱלֹךְ (Iyov 23:8), behold, I go east. קֵדְמָה מִזְרָחָה (Shemos 27:13), eastward, toward the sunrise, is doubled to make it plain, since מזרח is the clearer and better known word; so too נֶגְבָּה תֵימָֽנָה (Shemos 26:18), southward, to the south. The east wind is called קָדִים, as וְרוּחַ הַקָּדִים (Shemos 10:13), and the east wind; and the eastern sea is הַיָּם הַקַּדְמֹנִי (Yoel 2:20).

עור.sense: To wake and to rouse. Other senses: an enemy; baring and uncovering; עוֹר, skin; and blinding, with עִוֵּר, blind.

more.t: עוּרִי עוּרִי דְּבוֹרָה (Shoftim 5:12), awake, awake, Devorah, and the adjective אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה וְלִבִּי עֵר (Shir HaShirim 5:2), I sleep but my heart is awake. In the heavy form, הֵעִיר י"י אֶת־רוּחַ כּוֹרֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־פָּרַס (Ezra 1:4 in his edition), Hashem roused the spirit of Koresh king of Paras, הַעִירוֹתִי מִצָּפוֹן וַיַּאת (Yeshayahu 41:25), I have roused one from the north and he has come, and וְלֹֽא־ יָעִיר כָּל־חֲמָתֽוֹ (Tehillim 78:38), and He does not rouse all His wrath, which he marks פעלים יוצאים, transitive; while הָעִירָה וְהָקִיצָה (Tehillim 35:23), rouse Yourself and awake, and אָעִירָה שָּֽׁחַר (Tehillim 57:9), I will awake at dawn, he marks פעלים עומדים, intransitive. Rabbi Moshe HaKohen explained אָעִירָה שָּֽׁחַר as transitive: the sense is עוּרָֽה הַנֵּבֶל, awake, O harp, for I will rouse you at dawn.

וְהוּא עוֹרֵר אֶת־חֲנִיתוֹ (Shmuel II 23:18), and he roused his spear, and אִם־תָּעִירוּ (Shir HaShirim 2:7), if you rouse. Rabbi Yonah brings עַרְעֵר תִּתְעַרְעַר (Yirmiyahu 51:58) under this sense, meaning that the nations will shake and move to and fro; and so פָּנָה אֶל־תְּפִלַּת הָעַרְעָר (Tehillim 102:18), He turned to the prayer of the עַרְעָר, meaning one who rouses prayer continually. From this sense too Rabbi Yonah explained עִיר וּבֶהָלֽוֹת (Yirmiyahu 15:8), עִיר and terrors, עִיר meaning tumult and movement, and Radak says he explained it well.

more.h: A word he reads from Chazal
more.t: זַֽעֲקַת־שֶׁבֶר יְעֹעֵֽרוּ (Yeshayahu 15:5), a cry of breaking they יְעֹעֵֽרוּ, has been explained as ירועעו with its letters transposed, or as though it were יָעִירוּ, they rouse, with the first root letter doubled. In Radak's view it is a word of breaking, from Chazal's words (Sotah 20a): if the scroll was erased and she says, I will not drink, מערערין אותה; which means that if the sotah will not drink, they break and strike her.

וַיְהִי עָרֶֽךָ (Shmuel I 28:16), and He has become עָרֶךָ, means your enemy and the one who hates you. His father explained עִיר וּבֶהָלֽוֹת (Yirmiyahu 15:8) in this sense, an enemy and terrors. וּמָֽלְאוּ פְנֵֽי־תֵבֵל עָרִֽים (Yeshayahu 14:21), and they fill the face of the world with עָרִים, is read as though it said וּבַל ימלאו, and let them not fill, the בַל serving for two; and עָרִים are enemies, as Yonasan renders. It can also be read in its plain sense, cities: the one it speaks of destroyed cities, as the pasuk says וְעָרָיו הָרָס (Yeshayahu 14:17), and he destroyed its cities, and once he and his sons are dead the face of the world will fill with cities. On נָשֻׂא לַשָּׁוְא עָרֶֽיךָ (Tehillim 139:20), borne in vain are עָרֶֽיךָ, Rabbi Moshe HaKohen explained נשוא as a plain passive, as its form requires; on that reading עריך stands for Your name, so that the sense is: Your name is borne in vain in their mouth.

פְּשֹׁטָֽה וְעֹרָה (Yeshayahu 32:11), strip and bare, and לְמַעַן הַבִּיט עַל־ מְעֽוֹרֵיהֶֽם (Chavakuk 2:15), so as to look upon their nakedness, whose sense is baring and uncovering. עוֹר is skin, כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר (Bereishis 3:21), garments of skin. And עִוֵּר is to blind, וְאֶת־עֵינֵי צִדְקִיָּהוּ עִוֵּר (Yirmiyahu 39:7), and he blinded Tzidkiyahu's eyes, and as an adjective, blind, אוֹ פִקֵּחַ אוֹ עִוֵּר (Shemos 4:11), or seeing or blind.

more.h: The blind and the lame at Yerushalayim
more.t: הַעִוְרִים וְהַפִּסְחִים (Shmuel II 5:6), the blind and the lame, are images of bronze. In the Beraisa of Rabbi Eliezer (chapter 36), the men of Yevus made a covenant with Avraham, when they sold him the Cave of Machpelah, that his seed would not inherit their city; they made bronze images, set them in the city street and wrote the covenant of his oath on them, and told David he could not enter until he removed them. Rabbi Avraham Ibn Ezra reads הֱסִֽירְךָ as הסיר לך, that is: if we put out the blind and the lame to fight you, they would keep you from coming here, so strong is our building. Yonasan renders the words as the sinful and the guilty.

שֹדר.sense: No sense given here: one pasuk, וּשְׂדֵרֹת בָּֽאֲרָזִֽים (Melachim I 6:9), and s'deros with cedars, and a note that he has already explained it under the letter samech.

more.t: Two clauses and no more: the phrase וּשְׂדֵרֹת בָּֽאֲרָזִֽים (Melachim I 6:9), and s'deros with cedars, and his word that he has already explained it in the section of the letter samech. The sense itself is not set down here at all, which is why s'deros stands untranslated.

זבח.sense: To sacrifice, with זֶבַח, a sacrifice, and מִזְבֵּחַ, the place on which the sacrifices are offered.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר תִּזְבַּח בָּעֶרֶב (Devarim 16:4), what you slaughter at evening, and זְבַח לֵאלֹהִים תּוֹדָה (Tehillim 50:14), sacrifice thanksgiving to Elokim. In the heavy form: זִבַּח אָמוֹן וַיַּֽעַבְדֵֽם (Divrei HaYamim II 33:22), Amon sacrificed, and served them; לָהֶם אֲזַבֵּחַ וְיַעְזְרוּנִי (Divrei HaYamim II 28:23), to them I will sacrifice and they will help me; עַל־רָאשֵׁי הֶהָרִים יְזַבֵּחוּ (Hoshea 4:13), on the tops of the mountains they sacrifice.

וַיִּזְבַּח יַֽעֲקֹב זֶבַח בָּהָר (Bereishis 31:54), and Yaakov offered a sacrifice on the mountain, the noun taking a segol. For many, זְבָחִים שְׁלָמִים (Shemos 24:5), peace sacrifices; with a heh added, זִבְחָה, a sacrifice, and its plural זְבָחוֹת, as וְיֵבֹשׁוּ מִזִּבְחוֹתָֽם (Hoshea 4:19), and they will be ashamed of their sacrifices.

more.h: Why the incense altar is a מזבח
more.t: The place on which the sacrifices are offered is the מִזְבֵּחַ. וְעָשִׂיתָ מִזְבֵּחַ מִקְטַר קְטֹרֶת (Shemos 30:1), and you shall make an altar for burning incense, is called a מזבח although no sacrifices were offered upon it, because the blood of the sacrifice was sprinkled on it once in the year.

במה.sense: Its sense, he says, is known. He files it as weak in its last letter, after Rabbi Yonah, but holds it right to count it weak in its middle letter.

more.t: וַיִּקָּרֵא שְׁמָהּ בָּמָה (Yechezkel 20:29), its name was called Bamah; רַק הַבָּמוֹת לֹֽא־סָרוּ (Melachim II 12:4), only the high places were not removed; וּבָמוֹת עוֹלָם לְמֽוֹרָשָׁה (Yechezkel 36:2), the ancient high places for a possession; עַל־ בָּמֳותֵי אָרֶץ (Devarim 32:13), on the high places of the earth; אֶעֱלֶה עַל־ בָּמֳתֵי עָב (Yeshayahu 14:14), I will go up above the heights of the cloud; and עַל־ בָּֽמוֹתֵימוֹ תִדְרֹֽךְ (Devarim 33:29), you will tread on their high places. Of all of them he says only ענינם ידוע, their sense is known.

more.h: Which letter of the root is weak
more.t: He filed the word among those weak in the final heh, as Rabbi Yonah wrote. Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar filed it among those weak in the middle letter, because of the kamatz under the first root letter in the construct and with a suffix, as in קָמָה, standing grain, בְּקָמוֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּים (Shoftim 15:5), in the standing grain of the Pelishtim. That, Radak says, is the right one, and Rabbi Yonah himself wrote so in another place: better that במה be weak in its middle letter.

לאך.sense: A messenger, one sent, whether by men or by the Creator, the navi among them; and another sense in this root, מְלָאכָה, a man's work, his property and his affairs.

more.h: Whether the mem is of the root
more.t: וּמַלְאָךְ בָּא אֶל־אִיּוֹב (Iyov 1:14), a messenger came to Iyov; וַיָּשׁוּבוּ הַמַּלְאָכִים (Bereishis 32:7), the messengers returned; מַלְאֲכֵי אֱלֹהִים (Bereishis 28:12), messengers of Elokim. The mem of מלאך is one of the added letters. Radak wrote all these words under this root because Rabbi Yonah wrote them so, his view being that the mem is added; but it may also be said that the mem is of the root and the words have four letters.

וְלֹֽא־יִשָּׁמַע עוֹד קוֹל מַלְאָכֵֽכֵה (Nachum 2:14), and the voice of your messengers will be heard no more. He takes it as מלאכיךָ, your messengers, a tzere standing under the kaf of the suffix in place of a kamatz, and the heh like the heh of אֲשֶׁר־צִוִּיתִי אֹתָכָה (Shemos 29:35), that I commanded you. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the heh stands in place of a yud, as though מלאככִי, your messengers, like שׁוּבִי נַפְשִׁי לִמְנוּחָיְכִי (Tehillim 116:7), return, my soul, to your rest. Rabbi Yehudah ben Balaam wrote that קול מלאככה is the sound of the teeth eating the prey, as the pasuk says וְהִכְרַתִּי מֵאֶרֶץ טַרְפֵּךְ (Nachum 2:14), I will cut off your prey from the earth; and in the Persian tongue the millstones are called מלאככה, being the grinders, and the teeth are called grinders.

The noun is בְּמַלְֽאֲכוּת י"י (Chaggai 1:13), in the mission of Hashem. The sense of them all is known: being sent, whether by men or by the Creator. The navi is called a מלאך because he is Hashem's messenger: וַיִּשְׁלַח מַלְאָךְ וַיֹּֽצִאֵנוּ מִמִּצְרָיִם (Bamidbar 20:16), He sent a messenger and brought us out of Mitzrayim, is Moshe Rabbeinu; likewise וַיֹּאמֶר חַגַּי מַלְאַךְ י"י (Chaggai 1:13), Chaggai the messenger of Hashem said, and וַיִּֽהְיוּ מַלְעִיבִים בְּמַלְֽאֲכֵי הָֽאֱלֹהִים (Divrei HaYamim II 36:16), they were mocking the messengers of Elokim. So too is the explanation of וַיַּעַל מַלְאַךְ ־י"י מִן־הַגִּלְגָּל (Shoftim 2:1), the messenger of Hashem went up from the Gilgal, and וַיְהִי כְּדַבֵּר מַלְאַךְ י"י אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה (Shoftim 2:4), and it was, when the messenger of Hashem spoke these words; it is said (Vayikra Rabbah 1) that this messenger was Pinchas.

more.h: מְלָאכָה, work and what a man owns
more.t: Another sense in this root: מִכָּל־ מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָֽׂה (Bereishis 2:2), from all His work which He had made. It falls on a man's doing, his money and his affairs. וְהַמְּלָאכָה הָֽיְתָה דַיָּם (Shemos 36:7), the work was enough for them, means the silver and the gold they brought and the rest of the things; לְרֶגֶל הַמְּלָאכָה (Bereishis 33:14), at the pace of the work, means the cattle; and likewise וְכָל־ הַמְּלָאכָה נְמִבְזָה וְנָמֵס (Shmuel I 15:9), and all the goods that were despised and worthless.

In the construct: לִמְלֶכֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם (Yirmiyahu 7:18), filed here as to the work of the heavens, with the aleph missing, and אִם־לֹא שָׁלַח יָדוֹ בִּמְלֶאכֶת רֵעֵהוּ (Shemos 22:7), if he has not put his hand to his fellow's goods; and likewise where it is definite, וְהַֽלְוִיִּם בַּמְלָֽאכֶת (Divrei HaYamim II 13:10), and the Leviim at the work. The plural is מְלָאכוֹת, and in the construct the aleph is sounded: כֹּל מַלְֽאֲכוֹת הַתַּבְנִֽית (Divrei HaYamim I 28:19), all the works of the pattern, and לְסַפֵּר כָּל־ מַלְֽאֲכוֹתֶֽיךָ (Tehillim 73:28), to tell all Your works. Some read לִמְלֶכֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם with the mem as a root letter, a word of kingship, that is, the great star in the heavens; and Yonasan renders it לְכוֹכְבַת שְׁמַיָא, the star of the heavens.

אישׁ.sense: A man, a word that can take in women too; said even of what is not human; of the great man, the head and master of a thing; and of a husband.

more.h: Man and woman, and the plurals
more.t: מַכֵּה אִישׁ וָמֵת (Shemos 21:12), one who strikes a man so that he dies, and אַשְׁרֵי־ אִישׁ יָרֵא אֶת־י"י (Tehillim 112:1), happy is the man who fears Hashem. איש takes in male and female alike; in איש ואשה, man and woman, it is said of the male alone, since אשה, woman, is named beside it, and so too without אשה where the sense of the pasuk shows it. The plural is אֲלֵיכֶם אִישִׁים אֶקְרָא (Mishlei 8:4), to you, O men, I call. The shin of אשה is doubled for the quiescent yud lost from איש, and in the construct it is lightened to אֵשֶׁת; sometimes אשת stands on its own, as כְּמוֹ אֵשֶׁת לֵדָֽה (Yirmiyahu 13:21), like a woman in labour. The plural of אשה is אִשֹּׁת הַזִּמָּֽה (Yechezkel 23:44), the women of lewdness, but נשים, women, belongs to the root אנש and is written there.

more.h: Anything at all is called איש
more.t: Every thing is called איש and אשה, man and woman, though it is not human: of the keruvim, וּפְנֵיהֶם אִישׁ אֶל־אָחִיו (Shemos 25:20), and their faces, each man toward his brother; of the curtains, אִשָּׁה אֶל־אֲחֹתָהּ (Shemos 26:3), each woman to her sister; of the stars, אִישׁ לֹא נֶעְדָּֽר (Yeshayahu 40:26), not a man of them is missing; and of the beasts, אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ (Bereishis 7:2), a man and his wife, the male and its mate.

more.h: The great man, the master of a thing
more.t: גִּדְעוֹן בֶּן־יוֹאָשׁ אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shoftim 7:14), Gidon ben Yoash, a man of Israel, means the great one of Israel and its head; הֲלֽוֹא־ אִישׁ אַתָּה (Shmuel I 26:15) is, are you not a great man; י"י אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה (Shemos 15:3), Hashem is a man of war, is, He is great and the master of war; אִם־תִּמְצְאוּ אִישׁ (Yirmiyahu 5:3 in his edition), if you find a man, is a great man, a master of good deeds, and its explanation stands beside it, אִם־יֵשׁ עֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט, if there is one who does justice. In גַּם־בְּנֵי אָדָם גַּם־בְּנֵי־ אִישׁ (Tehillim 49:3), both the sons of adam and the sons of ish, בני אדם is said of the multitude and בני איש of the great. וְאִישָׁהּ זָקֵֽן (Melachim II 4:14), and her man is old, is her husband. וְאִם־ אִישׁ שְׂפָתַיִם יִצְדָּֽק (Iyov 11:2), and if a man of lips be in the right, is the master of lips, the master of the tongue, who dresses his arguments in his best words.

איש also comes without its yud, and some say the alef there stands in place of a yud, so that the word is יש, there is: אִם־ אִשׁ לְהֵמִין וּלְהַשְׂמִיל (Shmuel II 14:19), if there is any turning right or left, and עוֹד הַאִשׁ בֵּית רָשָׁע (Michah 6:10), is there still, in the house of the wicked; and so Yonasan rendered the first אִם אִית לְמִסְטֵי לְיַמִינָא, if there is turning to the right, and the second עוֹד הַאִית בֵּית רְשִׁיעָא, is there still in the house of the wicked, the heh of הַאִשׁ taking a patach because it asks, as in היש, is there. Radak's father read אִשׁ as fire, as in אִשׁ אלהים, the fire of Elokim, and עוֹד as in עוֹד יְֽהַלְלוּךָ סֶּֽלָה (Tehillim 84:5), they will ever praise You, selah: that is, all the days there will be fire in the house of the wicked, on account of the treasures of wickedness, אִשׁ taking a chirik where אֵשׁ takes a tzeirei, as חִין stands beside חֵן and בִּין beside בֵן. Radak says his father explained it well, but for the patach under the heh, which makes it look like the heh of a question. Both can also be read as they sound, of a man, and so the Chacham Rabbi Avraham explained it: that is, the honoured man of the city holds to his wickedness still after hearing the voice of the call, there being treasures of wickedness in his house. That reading too Radak calls good, save that it also pays no heed to the patach of the heh.
וַיַּכּוּ אִישׁ אִישׁוֹ (Melachim I 20:20), and they struck each man his man, means that each of them killed the one who came against him; אִישׁוֹ there is איש with its suffix.

more.h: אִישׁוֹן, the pupil of the eye
more.t: כְּאִישׁוֹן עֵינֽוֹ (Devarim 32:10), as the pupil of his eye, is בת עינו, the pupil, called so because the form of a man is seen in it; that is why the pasuk joins אִישׁוֹן to בת and says שָׁמְרֵנִי כְּאִישׁוֹן בַּת־עָיִן (Tehillim 17:8), guard me as the pupil of the eye. His father wrote that אִישׁוֹן is said to make small, since the form appears small in the eye. It is the way of the Hebrews to add letters to make a thing small, as in שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן (Vayikra 16:31), where שבת is said of the day itself from evening to evening and שבתון of the time added to it from the weekday to the holy, and הַֽאֲמִינוֹן אָחִיךְ (Shmuel II 13:20), has Aminon your brother been with you, where a letter is added to make the name small; the vernacular too adds letters to make a thing small. Or it is called so because it is black, as בְּאִישׁוֹן לַיְלָה וַֽאֲפֵלָֽה (Mishlei 7:9), in the blackness of night and gloom, which means in the blackness of the night; and in another measure, with the middle root letter fallen, בֶּאֱישׁוּן [ בֶּאֱשׁוּן ] חֹֽשֶׁךְ (Mishlei 20:20), in the blackness of darkness.

עיר.sense: A city; and a second sense, עַיִר, the donkey while it is still young, a word that fell on the wild ass as well.

more.t: וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר־ בָּעִיר (Bereishis 34:28), and what was in the city. The plural hides the yud in וַיִּתֶּן־אֹכֶל בֶּֽעָרִים (Bereishis 41:48), he put food in the cities, and עָרִים לָשָׁבֶת (Bamidbar 35:2), cities to dwell in; and shows it in וּשְׁלֹשִׁים עֲיָרִים לָהֶם (Shoftim 10:4), and they had thirty cities.

וְלֹא אָבוֹא בְּעִֽיר (Hoshea 11:9), and I will not come into a city, he reads as a phrase whose sense is left unsaid: I will not come into another city, but into Yerushalayim. Rabbi Yonah wrote in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak ben Rabbi Shaul that its sense is ואם לא אבא בעיר, and if I do not come into a city. That is, Radak explains, no place can contain Me; and the need for this is that the pasuk says בְּקִרְבֵּךְ קְדוֹשׁ (Hoshea 11:9), the Holy One is in your midst.
וְעָרֶיהָ עָלָה (Yirmiyahu 48:15) comes in the masculine, and he explains it as each and every one of her cities being cut off. It may also be that the masculine is said of the people in the city.

more.h: עָר מוֹאָב, and the root עור
more.t: עָר מוֹאָב (Bamidbar 21:28), Ar of Moav, can be read like עִיר, a city, or it is the name of the city. וּמָֽלְאוּ פְנֵֽי־תֵבֵל עָרִֽים (Yeshayahu 14:21), and they fill the face of the world with עָרִים, and וְהִשְׁמַדְתִּי עָרֶֽיךָ (Michah 5:13), and I will destroy your עָרִים, he has already explained, in two ways, under the root עור.

וְעַיִר פֶּרֶא אָדָם יִוָּלֵֽד (Iyov 11:12) he reads as וכעיר פרא: and like the colt of a wild ass a man is born. וְעַל־ עַיִר בֶּן־אֲתֹנֽוֹת (Zecharyah 9:9), and on a colt, the foal of she-asses; רֹֽכְבִים עַל־שְׁלֹשִׁים עֲיָרִים (Shoftim 10:4), riding on thirty colts; and with the middle root letter hidden, אֹֽסְרִי לַגֶּפֶן עִירֹה [ עִירוֹ ] (Bereishis 49:11), binding his colt to the vine. Its sense is the donkey while it is still small. The word fell on the פרא, the wild ass, as well, because the wild ass is like the donkey; but the wild ass is of the kind called chayah and the donkey of the kind called behemah, as Chazal said (Berachos 9b), כדי שיכיר בין חמור לערוד, that he may tell a donkey from an ערוד. The ערוד is the פרא.

רגז.sense: To tremble and move, out of fear or out of anger; and, where the verb takes an object, to set another trembling.

more.t: וְרָגַז וְשָׂחַק וְאֵין נָֽחַת (Mishlei 29:9), he is agitated and laughs, and there is no rest; וְרָֽגְזוּ וְחָלוּ (Devarim 2:25), they will tremble and be in anguish; וַתִּרְגַּז בִּטְנִי (Chavakuk 3:16), my belly trembled, and וְתַחְתַּי אֶרְגָּז (Chavakuk 3:16), and I tremble where I stand; מֽוֹסְדוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם יִרְגָּזוּ (Shmuel II 22:8), the foundations of the heavens tremble; and אַֽל־ תִּרְגְּזוּ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ (Bereishis 45:24), do not be agitated on the way. The sense he gives is trembling and movement, out of fear or out of anger.

חָדְלוּ רֹגֶז (Iyov 3:17), they have ceased from trembling; מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ וּמְֽרָגְזֶךָ (Yeshayahu 14:3), from your sorrow and from your trembling, where the serving mem takes a chirik; and with the feminine heh, וּמֵימֶיךָ בְּרָגְזָה וּבִדְאָגָה תִּשְׁתֶּֽה (Yechezkel 12:18), you will drink your water in trembling and in worry.

וַתִּרְגְּזִי ־לִי בְּכָל־אֵלֶּה (Yechezkel 16:43), and you set Me trembling with all these, is the verb taking an object. Likewise וְהִרְגִּיז לְיֹֽשְׁבֵי בָבֶֽל (Yirmiyahu 50:34), and he will set the dwellers of Bavel trembling; הַמַּרְגִּיז אֶרֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָהּ (Iyov 9:6), who shakes the earth out of her place; and לָמָּה הִרְגַּזְתַּנִי לְהַֽעֲלוֹת אֹתִי (Shmuel I 28:15), why have you stirred me, to bring me up. The reflexive: יַעַן הִתְרַגֶּזְךָ אֵלַי (Yeshayahu 37:29), because you stirred yourself against Me.

On וְאֵת הִֽתְרַגֶּזְךָ אֵלָֽי (Yeshayahu 37:28), and your stirring against Me, Rabbi Yonah wrote that the word may be said of the sound of thunder and of quaking, and then what is meant here would be your multiplying words against Me and making your tongue great against Me. In support of this stands וְשַֽׁאֲנַנְךָ עָלָה בְאָזְנָי (Yeshayahu 37:29), and the abundance of your words has come up into My ears, as Radak explains the word; and like it is וַתִּרְגְּזִי־לִי בְּכָל־אֵלֶּה, which Radak explains as you have done much in all these deeds.
תָּשִׂימוּ בָֽאַרְגַּז מִצִּדּוֹ (Shmuel I 6:8), you shall put in the chest at its side. He does not treat the word here, having written it in the section of aleph among the words of four letters.

אנף.sense: To be angry, ענין כעס; אף, anger, is of this root and sense, the dagesh in אַפּוֹ, his anger, standing for its missing nun; and the אֲנָפָה is a bird.

more.t: כִּי אָנַפְתָּ בִּי (Yeshayahu 12:1), for You were angry with me, and פֶּן־ יֶאֱנַף וְתֹאבְדוּ דֶרֶךְ (Tehillim 2:12), lest He be angry and you perish in the way; and גַּם־בִּי הִתְאַנַּף (Devarim 1:37), with me too Hashem was angry. All are ענין כעס, the sense of anger.

ואף הוא מזה השרש והענין, af too is of this root and this sense. With the pronoun suffixes it is אַפּוֹ, אַפִּי, אַפְּךָ, his anger, my anger, your anger, with a dagesh for the nun that is missing. It is written up again at the root אף on its own.
הָֽאֲנָפָה לְמִינָהּ (Vayikra 11:19), the anafah after its kind, is the name of a bird, and Chazal (Chullin 63a) say אנפה זו דיה רגזנית, the anafah is the dayah that is given to anger.

עצב.sense: Vexation and worry. From this idols are called עצבים, since dealing with them is worry and vexation, and by them one vexes Hashem. A near sense: toil and weariness.

more.t: וְלֹֽא־ עֲצָבוֹ אָבִיו (Melachim I 1:6), his father had not vexed him, which he glosses לא הרגיזו ולא הדאיגו, he did not vex him and did not cause him worry. Standing without an object, וַֽעֲצוּבַת רוּחַ (Yeshayahu 54:6), vexed in spirit, and וְעָשִׂיתָ מֵֽרָעָה לְבִלְתִּי עָצְבִּי (Divrei HaYamim I 4:10), which he explains: that You deal with me so that I am not vexed and do not worry from evil. So נֶעְצַב אֶל־דָּוִד (Shmuel I 20:34), he was vexed over David, וְעַתָּה אַל־ תֵּעָצְבוּ (Bereishis 45:5), now do not be vexed, and וַיִּתְעַצֵּב אֶל־לִבּֽוֹ (Bereishis 6:6), and He was vexed to His heart.

more.h: Where the verb takes an object
more.t: וְהֵמָּה מָרוּ וְעִצְּבוּ אֶת־רוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ (Yeshayahu 63:10), and they rebelled and vexed His holy spirit, which he glosses הרגיזו והדאיגו, they vexed it and caused it worry; כָּל־הַיּוֹם דְּבָרַי יְעַצֵּבוּ (Tehillim 56:6), all the day they vex my words; and יַֽעֲצִיבוּהוּ בִּֽישִׁימֽוֹן (Tehillim 78:40), they vexed Him in the wasteland.

more.h: The nouns, and one borrowed word
more.t: עֶצֶב in וְלֹֽא־יוֹסִף עֶצֶב עִמָּֽהּ (Mishlei 10:22), and adds no vexation with it, and וּדְבַר־ עֶצֶב יַֽעֲלֶה־אָֽף (Mishlei 15:1), and a word of vexation stirs up anger; לְמַֽעֲצֵבָה תִּשְׁכָּבֽוּן (Yeshayahu 50:11), you shall lie down in vexation; קֹרֵֽץ עַיִן יִתֵּן עַצָּבֶת (Mishlei 10:10), one who winks the eye gives vexation, and in construct וּבְעַצְּבַת ־לֵב רוּחַ נְכֵאָֽה (Mishlei 15:13), and by vexation of heart the spirit is broken; in the plural יָגֹרְתִּי כָל־ עַצְּבֹתָי (Iyov 9:28), I dreaded all my worries, and וּמְחַבֵּשׁ לְעַצְּבוֹתָֽם (Tehillim 147:3), and binds up their worries. ענין כלם הרוגז והדאגה, the sense of them all is vexation and worry. מְחַבֵּשׁ, binding up, is said of worry על דרך השאלה, as borrowed speech, since that very pasuk says הָרוּפֵא לִשְׁבוּרֵי לֵב, who heals the broken of heart.

more.h: Three ways to read one line
more.t: אִם־דֶּֽרֶךְ־ עֹצֶב בִּי (Tehillim 139:24) he reads as: if there is in me a way of vexation and worry over what befalls me, but I accept it all with love; or if I am walking an evil way that vexes You and angers You. And it may be explained from the name of the idols: if I am turning to the עצבים, the idols.

From this sense the images of avodah zarah are called עצבים, as הַעֶצֶב נִבְזֶה, a despised idol, and פֶּן־תֹּאמַר עָצְבִּי עָשָׂם (Yeshayahu 48:5), lest you say my idol did them; כי הם דאגה ורוגז, for they are worry and vexation to busy oneself with, and one vexes Hashem by them. So too עָשִׂינוּ לָהּ כַּוָּנִים לְהַעֲצִבָה (Yirmiyahu 44:19), we made her cakes לְהַעֲצִבָה, which is to make her idols; or לְהַעֲצִבָה may stand in for the word meant, לשמחה, to gladden her, and its ה is soft where the rule would give it a mappiq.

מַסִּיעַ אֲבָנִים יֵֽעָצֵב בָּהֶם (Koheles 10:9), one who moves stones toils and wearies himself with them; יָדֶיךָ עִצְּבוּנִי (Iyov 10:8), Your hands toiled and wearied themselves in forming me, said as a figure, while Rabbi Moshe ben Ezra takes it from the sinews, which are called עצבים. So בְּעִצָּבוֹן תֹּֽאכֲלֶנָּה (Bereishis 3:17), in toil you shall eat of it, and עִצְּבוֹנֵךְ וְהֵֽרֹנֵךְ (Bereishis 3:16), your toil and your pregnancy, where the sense is toil and weariness. And בְּכָל־ עֶצֶב יִהְיֶה מוֹתָר (Mishlei 14:23): in every toil a man toils there is gain and rank for him, since by much toil a man comes to rank and wealth and rule, while the toil of the lips and the weariness of talk bring only want, as the pasuk ends וּדְבַר־שְׂפָתַיִם אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר, but talk of the lips is only for want.

בהם.sense: A beast: a word for the whole kind and at times for one animal; בְהֵמוֹת (Iyov 40:15) is a single beast whose name is Behemos.

more.h: The ending, and a second form
more.t: זֹאת הַבְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכֵלוּ (Devarim 14:4), this is the beast that you shall eat, and בְּהֵמָה וָרֶמֶשׂ (Bereishis 1:24), beast and creeping thing, where the ה is the mark of the feminine; in construct וְאֵת בֶּֽהֱמַת הַֽלְוִיִּם (Bamidbar 3:41), and the beasts of the Leviim. But תַּחַת בְּהֶמְתָּם (Bamidbar 3:45), in place of their beasts, and בְּהֶמְתְּךָ לֹֽא־תַרְבִּיעַ כִּלְאַיִם (Vayikra 19:19), you shall not let your beast mate with another kind, do not come from בהמה at all but from a form בְּהֶמֶת, though it is not found, since from בהמה one would say בְּהֵמָֽתְךָ and not בְּהֶמְתְּךָ; so he wrote in his grammar, in the gate of nouns.

more.h: The kind, and the single animal
more.t: והוא שם כלל ופעם פרט, it is a word for the kind and at times for the one, as כִּי אִם־ הַבְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי רֹכֵב בָּֽהּ (Nechemiah 2:12), except the beast that I was riding on, the one animal.

הִנֵּה־נָא בְהֵמוֹת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂיתִי עִמָּךְ (Iyov 40:15), behold now Behemos, which I made with you, is בהמה אחת ששמה בהמות, one beast whose name is Behemos. Some say שְׁאַל־נָא בְהֵמוֹת וְתֹרֶךָּ (Iyov 12:7), ask now behemos and it will teach you, is that same beast, since וְתֹרֶךָּ, and it will teach you, is said in the singular. Radak holds there is no need for that: וְתֹרֶךָּ means each and every one of the beasts, or it falls on the kind; and so וְעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וְיַגֶּד־לָֽךְ, and the bird of the sky, and it will tell you.

בַּֽהֲמוֹת נֶגֶב (Yeshayahu 30:6), the beasts of the Negev. The navi foretold that the beasts of the Negev would come out to devour Yisrael as they went to seek help from Mitzrayim, carrying their wealth on the shoulders of young donkeys and their treasures on camels' humps to bribe Mitzrayim for aid, a people who would not profit them. The beasts are the ones the pasuk itself names, לָבִיא וָלַיִשׁ מֵהֶם אֶפְעֶה וְשָׂרָף מְעוֹפֵף, lion and lioness, from them viper and flying serpent. Mitzrayim is called Negev because it lies south of Eretz Yisrael; or נֶגֶב is meant as in אֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב נְתַתָּנִי (Shoftim 1:15), you have given me the land of the Negev, since wild beasts dwell in the wilderness and in the land of the Negev.

נער.sense: To roar, and in Chazal's usage the braying of a donkey; to shake out; and נַעַר, a youth, and so a servant of any age, since it is the way of the young to serve the old.

more.t: נָֽעֲרוּ כְּגוֹרֵי אֲרָיֹֽות (Yirmiyahu 51:38), they roar like lions' whelps, meaning שאגו והמו, they roared and made their noise; and Chazal use the word of a donkey, חמור נוער (Berachos 3a), a donkey brays. Rabbi Yonah puts כִּי נֵעוֹר מִמְּעוֹן קָדְשֽׁוֹ (Zecharyah 2:17), for He roars from His holy dwelling, in this root; it is an adjective on the pattern of יָכוֹל, able, save that the vowel changed because of the ayin. Radak's father put it here too, and said that the word is used of Hashem after the manner of י"י מִצִּיּוֹן יִשְׁאָג (Yoel 4:16), Hashem roars from Tzion.

גַּם־חָצְנִי נָעַרְתִּי (Nechemiah 5:13), I also shook out my lap, and נֹעֵר כַּפָּיו מִתְּמֹךְ בַּשֹּׁחַד (Yeshayahu 33:15), shaking his palms clear of holding a bribe. וְנֹעֵר בָּשָׁן וְכַרְמֶֽל (Yeshayahu 33:9), and Bashan and Carmel shake off, is shaking off its fruit and its crop; or the verb is intransitive. In the passive, נִנְעַרְתִּי כָּֽאַרְבֶּֽה (Tehillim 109:23), I am shaken off like a locust, and וְיִנָּֽעֲרוּ רְשָׁעִים מִמֶּֽנָּה (Iyov 38:13), and the wicked are shaken out of it; with an object, וְנִעֵר פַּרְעֹה וְחֵילוֹ (Tehillim 136:15), and He shook out Pharaoh and his army, and וַיְנַעֵר י"י אֶת־מִצְרַיִם (Shemos 14:27), and Hashem shook out Mitzrayim; and הִתְנַֽעֲרִי מֵעָפָר (Yeshayahu 52:2), shake yourself from the dust.

וְהָיָה הֶחָסֹן לִנְעֹרֶת (Yeshayahu 1:31), and the strong shall become tow, and in the Mishnah (Shabbos 4:1) בנעורת של פשתים, the tow of flax, which is what the one who dresses the flax shakes and beats out of it. Some read וְהַנַּעַר נָֽעַר (Shmuel I 1:24) from this, that the youth was sharp and knew good from bad, like one who shakes the refuse out.

כִּי־נַעַר אָנֹֽכִי (Yirmiyahu 1:6), for I am a youth. One small in years is called נער, and because it is the way of the small to serve the great, the attendant is called נער even when he is old in years: נַעַר עִבְרִי (Bereishis 41:12), a Hebrew attendant; וְהוּא נַעַר אֶת־בְּנֵי בִלְהָה (Bereishis 37:2), and he was an attendant with the sons of Bilhah; גֵּיֽחֲזִי נַֽעֲרוֹ (Melachim II 4:12), Geichazi his attendant; בְּנַֽעֲרֵי שָׂרֵי הַמְּדִינוֹת (Melachim I 20:14), by the attendants of the officers of the provinces. וּרְחַבְעָם הָיָה נַעַר (Divrei HaYamim II 13:7), and Rechavam was a youth, is כנער בדעתו, like a youth in his understanding. The young of the flock is also called נער: הַנַּעַר לֹֽא־יְבַקֵּשׁ וְהַנִּשְׁבֶּרֶת לֹא יְרַפֵּא (Zecharyah 11:16), the young one he will not seek, and the broken one he will not heal.

Radak reads וְהַנַּעַר נָֽעַר (Shmuel I 1:24), and the youth was a youth, as the child being still a small child, twenty-four months old, since the pasuk says עד הִגָּמֵל הנער, until the youth is weaned, and a child nurses until twenty-four months. His father wrote on those words גדול משניו, big for his years; that is, he was a youth bigger for his years than is usual.

more.h: Girls, and the days of youth
more.t: וְהַנַּֽעֲרָה יָפָה עַד־מְאֹד (Melachim I 1:4), the girl was very fair; נְעָרוֹת בְּתוּלוֹת (Esther 2:2), young girls, maidens; and רִבְקָה וְנַֽעֲרֹתֶיהָ (Bereishis 24:61), Rivkah and her girls. For the time of life, רַבַּת צְרָרוּנִי מִנְּעוּרָי (Tehillim 129:2), they have afflicted me much from my youth, and מְגֻדָּלִים בִּנְעוּרֵיהֶם (Tehillim 144:12), grown up in their youth. תָּמֹת בַּנֹּעַר נַפְשָׁם (Iyov 36:14) is their soul dying in youth, though some take that one from the second sense, that is, a hard death.

נגשֹ.sense: To press: pressing out silver and gold, pressing one's fellow, the נֹגֵשׂ who presses, and being pressed; all of them, he says, the sense of pressure.

more.h: Pressing, and the one who presses
more.t: נָגַשׂ אֶת־הַכֶּסֶף וְאֶת־הַזָּהָב (Melachim II 23:35), he pressed out the silver and the gold; לֹֽא־ יִגֹּשׂ אֶת־רֵעֵהוּ וְאֶת־אָחִיו (Devarim 15:2), he shall not press his fellow or his brother; וְכָל־עַצְּבֵיכֶם תִּנְגֹּֽשׂוּ (Yeshayahu 58:3), and all your laborers you press hard; אֵיךְ שָׁבַת נֹגֵשׂ (Yeshayahu 14:4), how he who pressed has ceased; and וְהַנֹּֽגְשִׂים אָצִים (Shemos 5:13), and those pressing them were urging them on.

In the passive, וְנִגַּשׂ הָעָם אִישׁ בְּאִישׁ וְאִישׁ בְּרֵעֵהוּ (Yeshayahu 3:5), the people shall be pressed, one man by another and each by his fellow; כִּי נִגַּשׂ הָעָם (Shmuel I 13:6), for the people were pressed; נִגַּשׂ וְהוּא נַֽעֲנֶה (Yeshayahu 53:7), he was pressed and he was afflicted; and יַעַן כִּי נִגַּשׁ הָעָם (Yeshayahu 29:13), because the people were pressed, a word whose spelling he weighs at the other root. כלם ענין לחץ, all of them a sense of pressure.

נגשׁ.sense: To draw near, and to bring near. Even moving off is said with it, since one who is far from the speaker's place is near to the other place.

more.t: וַיִּגַּשׁ אֵלָיו יְהוּדָה (Bereishis 44:18), and Yehudah drew near to him, וַתִּגַּשְׁןָ הַשְּׁפָחוֹת (Bereishis 33:6), the maidservants drew near, גְּשׁוּ ־נָא אֵלַי וַיִּגָּשׁוּ (Bereishis 45:4), draw near to me now, and they drew near, גּשִֽׁי הֲלֹם (Rus 2:14), come near here, עַד־ גִּשְׁתּוֹ עַד־אָחִֽיו (Bereishis 33:3), until he drew near to his brother, and with the pathach גַּשׁ פְּגַע־בּוֹ (Shmuel II 1:15), come near, strike him down.

more.h: Why it can mean move away
more.t: גְּשָׁה לִּי וְאֵשֵׁבָה (Yeshayahu 49:20) is גש שמה בעבורי שאשב בריוח, draw near over there for my sake so that I may sit with room, since the place is too narrow for me. So too גֶּשׁ הָלְאָה (Bereishis 19:9), draw near yonder: though the man is far from where the speaker stands, he is near to the other place, and the word is said of that nearness.

more.h: Whether one word has a sin or a shin
more.t: יַעַן כִּי נִגַּשׁ הָעָם הַזֶּה (Yeshayahu 29:13), because this people draws near: so Rabbi Yonah wrote it, and so it stands in some of the sefarim. But a note of the Mesorah counts four places with a sin and gives their catchwords: וְאִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל, and the men of Yisrael (Shmuel I 13:6), with its fellow (Shmuel I 14:24), יִרְֽהֲבוּ, they shall be insolent (Yeshayahu 3:5), and נַֽעֲנֶה, afflicted (Yeshayahu 53:7). By the Mesorah, then, this word has a shin, since those four alone have a sin. In some sefarim it is found with a sin, and the Targum's view is so, since he renders it חֲלַף דְאִיתְרַבְרַב עַמָא הָדֵין, because this people has grown haughty.

וְנִגַּשׁ מֹשֶׁה לְבַדּוֹ (Shemos 24:2), Moshe alone shall come near, וְנִגְּשָׁה יְבִמְתּוֹ (Devarim 25:9), his brother's widow shall come near, and וְגַם הַכֹּהֲנִים הַנִּגָּשִׁים (Shemos 19:22), the kohanim too who come near. Where the verb takes an object, וְהִגִּישׁוֹ אֲדֹנָיו (Shemos 21:6), his master shall bring him near, and וַיַּגֶּשׁ ־לוֹ וַיֹּאכַל (Bereishis 27:25), he brought it to him and he ate. Rabbi Yonah wrote that לֹא תַגִּישׁ וְתַקְדִּים בַּעֲדֵינוּ הָרָעָה (Amos 9:10), the evil shall not draw near or come upon us, is a verb that takes no object. Radak allows that it may be read as taking one, like its fellows: bring the enemies near and set them before us. In the passive, לֹא לִנְחֻשְׁתַּיִם הֻגָּשׁוּ (Shmuel II 3:34), they were not brought near to fetters.

תבה.sense: The ark, תֵּבָה, whose sense is known; its root may be תיב, though Rabbi Yonah files it under this one.

more.t: צֵא מִן־ הַתֵּבָה (Bereishis 8:16), go out of the ark, and תֵּבַת עֲצֵי־גֹפֶר (Bereishis 6:14), an ark of gopher wood; the word is known. The root may be תיב, the noun then standing on the pattern of צֵידָה, provision, and שֵֹיבָה, grey age. But Rabbi Yonah wrote it under this root, on the pattern of לֶחֶם הַפֶּחָה (Nechemiah 5:18), the governor's bread.

חלץ.sense: To part and withdraw; to draw off, as a shoe; to be drawn out of trouble; changes of clothing; the loins, and one girded for war; and, of the bones, to make fat.

more.t: חָלַץ מֵהֶם (Hoshea 5:6) is חלק ונפרד וסר מהם, he parted and separated and turned away from them. In the transitive, גַּם־תַּנִּין [תַּנִּים] חָלְצוּ (Eichah 4:3), even the tannim drew out: they brought out their breasts and uncovered them to nurse their young. וְחָֽלְצָה נַֽעֲלוֹ (Devarim 25:9), she shall draw off his shoe and take it away, and where the verb is strengthened, וְחִלְּצוּ אֶת־הָאֲבָנִים (Vayikra 14:40), they shall take the stones out and pull them from their place.

Because a man puts these on by taking those off, changes of clothing carry the name: וְהַלְבֵּשׁ אֹֽתְךָ מַֽחֲלָצֽוֹת (Zecharyah 3:4), and clothing you in changes of garments; הַמַּֽחֲלָצוֹת וְהַמַּֽעֲטָפוֹת (Yeshayahu 3:22), the changes of garments and the wraps; וְקַח־לְךָ אֶת־ חֲלִֽצָתוֹ (Shmuel II 2:21), and take for yourself his garments; and וַיִּקַּח אֶת־ חֲלִיצוֹתָם (Shoftim 14:19), and he took their garments.

In this same sense, rescue: צַדִּיק מִצָּרָה נֶחֱלָץ (Mishlei 11:8), the righteous is drawn out of trouble, that is, parted and removed from the trouble, and לְמַעַן יֵחָלְצוּן יְדִידֶיךָ (Tehillim 60:7), that Your beloved may be delivered. So חַלְּצָה נַפְשִׁי (Tehillim 6:5), deliver my soul, and יְחַלְּצֵנִי כִּֽי־חָפֵֽץ בִּֽי (Tehillim 18:20), He delivers me, for He delights in me. וָֽאֲחַלְּצָה צוֹרְרִי רֵיקָֽם (Tehillim 7:5) is: rather, I delivered him who is my enemy without cause; as if to say, have I repaid evil to one at peace with me? On the contrary, I would deliver him, though he is my enemy without cause.

more.h: The loins, and the armed man
more.t: חֲלָצֶיךָ in אֱזָר־נָא כְגֶבֶר חֲלָצֶיךָ (Iyov 38:3), gird your loins like a man, and in מֵֽחֲלָצֶיךָ יֵצֵֽאוּ (Bereishis 35:11), they shall come out of your loins, are the מתנים, the loins. The passive participle is חָלוּץ: וְעָבַר לָכֶם כָּל־ חָלוּץ (Bamidbar 32:21), and every armed man of you shall cross, one girded with weapons of war at the loins. So נֵֽחָלֵץ חֻשִׁים (Bamidbar 32:17), we will be armed quickly, and הֵחָֽלְצוּ מֵֽאִתְּכֶם (Bamidbar 31:3), be armed from among you. Rabbi Yonah wrote that this last is transitive; Radak says it is not, and that it is as though it said: let some of you be armed, the men and the mighty among you, and let them be against Midian. It may be that וקח לך את חליצתו, take for yourself his arms, is of this sense too: take yourself one of the lads who walk with me, that he may go back with you, and if you fear him, take his weapons of war, and you too will not kill him.

But וְעַצְמֹתֶיךָ יַֽחֲלִיץ (Yeshayahu 58:11), and He will make your bones fat, has the sense ידשן, will make fat, in the way of שְׁמוּעָה טוֹבָה תְּדַשֶּׁן ־עָֽצֶם (Mishlei 15:30), good tidings make the bone fat. In this sense Chazal said (Eruvin 39a) that one who goes before the teivah on Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah says והחליצנו י"י אלהינו, which Radak explains as: satisfy us and make us fat with Your mitzvos, Hashem our God; or give us rest, for so they explained it, a term of rest.

Chazal said (Vayikra Rabbah 34) that the word is used in four senses: ישלוף, to draw off, as וְחָֽלְצָה נַֽעֲלוֹ, she shall draw off his shoe; ישזיב, to rescue, as חַלְּצֵנִי (Tehillim 140:2), deliver me; יזיין, to arm, as חֲלוּצִים תַּֽעַבְרוּ (Devarim 3:18), you shall cross over armed; and יניח, to give rest, as וְעַצְמֹתֶיךָ יַֽחֲלִיץ, He will give your bones rest, as one says רצה והחליצנו, be pleased and give us rest.

אזן.sense: The ear, and to give ear; testing and understanding are ascribed to the ear, as it is where the act begins. Another sense: מֹאזְנַיִם, scales, dual for their two pans.

more.t: אֹֽזֶן ־אַֽהֲרֹן הַיְמָנִית (Vayikra 8:23), Aharon's right ear, הֲנֹטַע אֹזֶן הֲלֹא יִשְׁמָע (Tehillim 94:9), He who planted the ear, shall He not hear, and אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי (Tehillim 40:7), ears You have opened for me.

more.h: Why the ear is said to understand
more.t: הֲלֹא אֹזֶן מִלִּין תִּבְחָן (Iyov 12:11), does not the ear test words, שָׁמְעָה אָזְנִי וַתָּבֶן לָהּ (Iyov 13:1), my ear has heard and understood it, and כִּי אֹזֶן שָׁמְעָה וַתְּאַשְּׁרֵנִי (Iyov 29:11), for the ear heard and called me fortunate. סמך הבחינה והתבונה והחנינה לאזן, ואינה אלא ללב: the testing and the understanding and the favour are set upon the ear, though they belong to the heart alone, לפי שהיא תחלת הפעולה, because the ear is where the act begins; and so with וַתְּאַשְּׁרֵנִי, and it called me fortunate. In the same way, וּבִתְבוּנוֹת כַּפָּיו יַנְחֵם (Tehillim 78:72), and with the understanding of his hands he led them.

הַאֲזִינוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם (Devarim 32:1), give ear, O heavens, is הטו אזן, incline the ear, and so every word of this sense in this root. Of this sense too are אָזִין עַד תְּבוּנֹתֵיכֶם (Iyov 32:11), I gave ear to your reasonings, and שֶׁקֶר מֵזִין עַל לְשׁוֹן הַוֹּת (Mishlei 17:4), a liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue, whose regular forms would be אַאֲזִין and מַאֲזִין.

more.h: The scales, and one disputed word
more.t: בְּמֹאזְנַיִם לַעֲלוֹת (Tehillim 62:10), in the scales they go up, and מֹאזְנֵי צֶדֶק אַבְנֵי צֶדֶק (Vayikra 19:36), just scales, just weights: their sense is known, the instrument one weighs with, called in the dual because it has two pans. On וְאִזֵּן וְחִקֵּר (Koheles 12:9), Rabbi Yonah ibn Janach takes it from this sense, which Radak puts as: he weighed one matter against another and searched them out. Rabbi Yehudah put the word with the first sense, of the ear.

Rabbi Yonah, in one of the ways he gives, put וְיָתֵד תִּהְיֶה לְךָ עַל אֲזֵנֶךָ (Devarim 23:14), and you shall have a peg upon your gear, under this root. Radak holds the right account is that the alef is added, and that it means כלי זיניך, your weapons.

רחם.sense: To have mercy, and רַחֲמִים, mercies; in another sense, to love; רֶחֶם, the womb, said in contempt of a woman herself; and הָרָחָמָה, a bird said to pity its young.

more.t: רַחֵם אֲרַחֲמֶנּוּ (Yirmiyahu 31:19), I will surely have mercy on him, and וְרִחַמְךָ וְהִרְבֶּךָ (Devarim 13:18), and He will have mercy on you and multiply you. In the passive, אֲשֶׁר־בְּךָ יְרֻחַם יָתוֹם (Hoshea 14:4), in You the orphan is shown mercy, and וּמוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָם (Mishlei 28:13), one who confesses and forsakes is shown mercy. The adjective is רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן (Tehillim 86:15), merciful and gracious, and with a yud of relation, יְדֵי נָשִׁים רַחֲמָנִיּוֹת (Eichah 4:10), the hands of compassionate women. The sense of all of them, he says, is compassion, and it is known. In בְּרֹגֶז רַחֵם תִּזְכּוֹר (Chavakuk 3:2), in wrath remember mercy, רַחֵם may be an infinitive, but it is more correct as a noun.

more.h: Where it is love, not mercy
more.t: Another sense: אֶרְחָמְךָ (Tehillim 18:2), where the ches carries a kamatz chatuf, means like אוהבך, I love You, from the Targum of וַיֶּאֱהַב (Bereishis 25:28), and he loved, which is וּרְחֵם. Some take רחם תזכור from this sense, which would mean: in the time of wrath You will remember the love of the fathers. Ibn Ezra explains אֶרְחָמְךָ from the first sense, meaning I will seek mercy from You.

כָל־פֶּטֶר־רֶחֶם (Shemos 13:12), every first issue of the womb, and אֲשֶׁר בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם אִמּוֹ (Bamidbar 12:12), who when he comes out of his mother's womb. It comes with a patach, רַחַם רַחֲמָתַיִם (Shoftim 5:30), a maiden and two maidens, and in pause the resh takes a kamatz, כָּל־פֶּטֶר רָחַם (Yechezkel 20:26), every first issue of the womb. In וְרַחְמָה הֲרַת עוֹלָם (Yirmiyahu 20:17), and her womb pregnant for ever, the heh is quiescent where it ought to carry a mappik.

more.h: The sea coming out of a womb
more.t: By way of borrowing, בְּגִיחוֹ מֵרֶחֶם יֵצֵא (Iyov 38:8), when it burst out, it came forth from the womb, is said of the sea: when He brought it forth it was as one coming out of a womb; that is, when the waters went out and were gathered He hedged it about, so that it should not pass the limit He set for it, which is the sand.

more.h: From the womb, from the dawn
more.t: מֵרֶחֶם מִשְׁחָר (Tehillim 110:3), from the womb, from the dawn, Radak explains of the day you were born and came out of the womb: that dawn was the dew of your youth, the dew that came down that dawn being yours; that is, it was good for you, as a man says that a dew of blessing came down on the day he was born. In Ibn Ezra's view it is borrowed like the sea's womb, מִשְׁחָר being from the time the dawn rises, as though it went out of its place like one coming out of a womb; and Ibn Ezra explains the pasuk: if you must make war, they will come to you on that day as a willing rain, from the time the dawn rises, like the dew you were used to seeing in your youth when you were a shepherd.

The word is applied to the woman herself: רַחַם רַחֲמָתַיִם לְרֹאשׁ גֶּבֶר (Shoftim 5:30), which Radak explains as a maiden and two maidens for every man's head; they were called so by way of contempt. וְאֶת־הָרָחָמָה (Devarim 14:17), and the rachamah, they said is a bird that pities its young greatly.

מלך.sense: To reign; מֶלֶךְ, a king; מְלוּכָה, מַמְלָכָה and מַלְכוּת, kingship. In another sense, to take counsel. And מֹלֶךְ, an avodah zarah served with two fires.

more.t: בְּחֶבְרוֹן מָלַךְ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים (Melachim I 2:11), in Chevron he reigned seven years, and וּמָלַךְ מֶלֶךְ וְהִשְׂכִּיל (Yirmiyahu 23:5), a king shall reign and prosper. Of a woman, וַעֲתַלְיָה מֹלֶכֶת עַל הָאָרֶץ (Melachim II 11:3), and Asalyah reigned over the land. Where the verb takes an object, הִמְלִיךְ אֶת שָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 15:35), he made Shaul king; in the passive, אֲשֶׁר הָמְלַךְ עַל מַלְכוּת כַּשְׂדִּים (Daniel 9:1), who was made king over the kingdom of the Kasdim. The sense of kingship, he says, is known.

The noun is מֶלֶךְ, a king, and the plural אַרְבָּעָה מְלָכִים (Bereishis 14:9), four kings, written also with an alef of prolongation, לְעֵת צֵאת הַמְּלָאכִים (Shmuel II 11:1), at the time kings go out. Kingship is מְלוּכָה: וְאֶת דְּבַר הַמְּלוּכָה לֹא הִגִּיד לוֹ (Shmuel I 10:16), but the matter of the kingship he did not tell him. Other forms are מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים (Shemos 19:6), a kingdom of kohanim, and מַמְלְכוּת עוֹג (Yehoshua 13:12), the kingdom of Og; and without the added mem, מַלְכוּת כַּשְׂדִּים (Daniel 9:1), the kingdom of the Kasdim. Its plural is אַרְבַּע מַלְכֻיוֹת (Daniel 8:22), four kingdoms, where, tav and heh being alike, the yud that stands for the heh in the plural takes the place of the tav, as in גָּלוּת, exile, and גָּלֻיּוֹת, exiles. Some explain לִמְלֶכֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם (Yirmiyahu 7:18), to the מְלֶכֶת of the heavens, from this sense, meaning to a great star in the heavens.

In another sense, וַיִּמָּלֵךְ לִבִּי עָלַי (Nechemiah 5:7), my heart took counsel within me: its sense is taking counsel, and it resembles the Aramaic מִלְכִּי יִשְׁפַּר עֲלָיךְ (Daniel 4:24), let my counsel be pleasing to you, and the words of Chazal (Berachos 29b), המלך בקונך וצא, take counsel with your Maker and go out. Some explain from this בֶּן מַלְכֵי קֶדֶם (Yeshayahu 19:11) as a son of counsellors of old.

Rabbi Yonah explained מְלָכִין (Mishlei 31:3) from this sense of counsel, and so also הֲתִמְלֹךְ כִּי אַתָּה מְתַחֲרֶה בָאָרֶז (Yirmiyahu 22:15), התמלך because you vie with the cedar, the tav drawn out with a maarich and the mem with a sheva and a patach, which Radak explains: do you think in your heart to liken and equal yourself to the great king. There is no need, Radak says, to take them out of the sense of kingship. That pasuk in Mishlei he explains under the root מחה; and הֲתִמְלֹךְ כִּי אַתָּה מְתַחֲרֶה בָאָרֶז is: do you imagine yourself a king, and grow proud to vie with the cedar, that is, with one greater than you; that is, the kingship is not yours, to be proud over one greater than you.

אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִזַּרְעוֹ לַמֹּלֶךְ (Vayikra 20:2), who gives of his seed to the Molech, and וּלְמֹלֶךְ שִׁקֻּץ בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן (Melachim I 11:7), and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon: it is the name of an avodah zarah. Its service was that a man handed his son to its priests, and they made two great fires and passed the son on his feet between the two fires. In לֹא תִתֵּן (Vayikra 18:21), you shall not give, is the handing to the priests, and in לְהַעֲבִיר, to pass over, the passing through the fire.

אדם.sense: To be red, with אָדוֹם, red, and אֲדַמְדָּם, very red or red mixed with white; אֲדָמָה, land, field or dust; and אָדָם, man, called after the ground he was taken from.

more.t: אָדְמוּ עֶצֶם מִפְּנִינִים (Eichah 4:7), they were ruddier of bone than pearls, and in the passive וְעֹרֹת אֵילִם מְאָדָּמִים (Shemos 25:5), rams' skins dyed red. So אִם־יַאְדִּימוּ כַתּוֹלָע (Yeshayahu 1:18), if they redden like crimson, and אַל־תֵּרֶא יַיִן כִּי יִתְאַדָּם (Mishlei 23:31), do not look at wine when it reddens. The adjectives are דּוֹדִי צַח וְאָדוֹם (Shir HaShirim 5:10), my beloved is white and ruddy, פָרָה אֲדֻמָּה (Bamidbar 19:2), a red cow, and אַדְמוֹנִי עִם־יְפֵה עֵינַיִם (Shmuel I 16:12), ruddy with fair eyes. The stone called אֹדֶם, in אֹדֶם פִּטְדָה (Shemos 28:17), odem and pitdah, is named so because it is red.

Where the second and third root letters are doubled, as אוֹ אֲדַמְדָּם (Vayikra 13:49), or very red, it means much redness; and Chazal in Sifra said ירקרק ירוק שבירוקים, yerakrak is the greenest of the greens, and אדמדם is אדום שבאדומים, the reddest of the reds. In נֶגַע לָבָן אֲדַמְדָּם (Vayikra 13:42), a white reddish affliction, and לְבָנָה אֲדַמְדֶּמֶת (Vayikra 13:24), white and reddish, it is blended and mixed of two appearances, white and red.

Man is called after the אֲדָמָה, the ground, that he was taken from, and the species is called by his name, אָדָם. אֲדָמָה comes for land, עַל־פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה (Bamidbar 12:3), on the face of the earth; for a field, עֹבֵד אַדְמָתוֹ (Mishlei 12:11), one who works his field, and אִם־עָלַי אַדְמָתִי תִזְעָק (Iyov 31:38), if my field cries out against me; and for dust, וַאֲדָמָה עַל־רֹאשׁוֹ (Shmuel I 4:12), and dust on his head. Joined to dust it is אַדְמַת־עָפָר (Daniel 12:2), the ground of dust, as טִיט הַיָּוֵן (Tehillim 40:3), miry clay.

more.h: One man, all men, and some of them
more.t: אָדָם stands for the individual, אָדָם כִּי־יַקְרִיב מִכֶּם קָרְבָּן (Vayikra 1:2), a man of you who brings an offering; for the whole, מֵאָדָם עַד־בְּהֵמָה (Bereishis 6:7), from man to beast; and for part of the whole, אֶת־הָאָדָם (Yeshayahu 6:12), the men. וְהוּא יִהְיֶה פֶּרֶא אָדָם (Bereishis 16:12), and he shall be a wild ass of a man, he glosses as a man of the wilderness, like a wild ass. In גַּם־בְּנֵי אָדָם גַּם־בְּנֵי־אִישׁ (Tehillim 49:3), both the sons of אָדָם and the sons of אִישׁ, the first are the common people and the second the great, as in גִּדְעוֹן בֶּן־יוֹאָשׁ אִישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shoftim 7:14), Gideon son of Yoash, the אִישׁ of Israel, which means Israel's great one and its head. וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל וּבָאָדָם (Yirmiyahu 32:20), and in Israel and among mankind, means among the rest of mankind, that is, among the nations, and Yonasan renders פְּרִישָׁן בּגוֹ בְּנֵי אֱנָשָׁא, wonders among the sons of man.

אָדָם is used of women alone: וְנֶפֶשׁ אָדָם מִן־הַנָּשִׁים (Bamidbar 31:35), and persons of the women, and כְּתִפְאֶרֶת אָדָם לָשֶׁבֶת בָּיִת (Yeshayahu 44:13), like the beauty of a person, to sit in a house. His father explains כְּתִפְאֶרֶת אָדָם: and for what? לָשֶׁבֶת בָּיִת, to sit in a house and for no other use, as וְיַנִּיחֻהוּ תַחְתָּיו, and they set it in its place, and מִמְּקוֹמוֹ לֹא יָמִישׁ, from its place it does not stir. הַרְחֵק מְאֹד בֵאָדָם (Yehoshua 3:16), very far off at Adam, is the name of a city.

רום.sense: To be high and to raise up: רָם, high; מָרוֹם, a height; תְּרוּמָה, what is set apart, since setting apart, he holds, is itself a raising.

more.t: יָדֵנוּ רָמָה (Devarim 32:27), our hand is high, and with the middle root letter showing as an alef, וְרָאֲמָה וְיָשְׁבָה תַחְתֶּיהָ (Zecharyah 14:10), it shall be lifted up and dwell in its place; רוּמָה עַל־הַשָּׁמַיִם (Tehillim 57:6), be exalted above the heavens. The adjectives are עַל כָּל־גֵּאֶה וָרָם (Yeshayahu 2:12), on all that is proud and high, הֶהָרִים הָרָמִים (Devarim 12:2), the high mountains, and עֵינַיִם רָמוֹת (Mishlei 6:17), haughty eyes; with an alef, רָאמוֹת לֶאֱוִיל חָכְמוֹת (Mishlei 24:7), wisdom is high for a fool. A height is עָלִיתָ לַמָּרוֹם (Tehillim 68:19), You went up on high, and מְרֹמֵי קָרֶת (Mishlei 9:3), the heights of the city; and וַתַּעֲשִׂי־לָךְ רָמָה (Yechezkel 16:24) is, and you made yourself a raised place.

הֲרִמֹתִי יָדִי (Bereishis 14:22), I have lifted my hand, תָּרִימוּ תְרוּמָה (Bamidbar 15:20), you shall set apart a terumah, and וּכְסִילִים מֵרִים קָלוֹן (Mishlei 3:35), fools raise up shame. וַיָּרֶם יָד בַּמֶּלֶךְ (Melachim I 11:26), he raised a hand against the king, means that he rebelled against him, and that is what raising a hand against him is. אֲשֶׁר הוּנַף וַאֲשֶׁר הוּרָם (Shemos 29:27) is what was waved and what was lifted off; what separates terumah from waving is set out under the root נוּף.

more.h: Lifting the ash from the mizbeach
more.t: וְהֵרִים אֶת־הַדֶּשֶׁן (Vayikra 6:3), and he shall lift up the ash: Chazal explained that he lifted a panful of the ash every day and set it east of the ramp. But the carrying out of the ash, of which it says וְהוֹצִיא אֶת־הַדֶּשֶׁן (Vayikra 6:4), and he shall carry out the ash, was not every day, only when there was much ash on the mizbeach and no room for the arrangement. Though they brought the heap down each day and took it out, the mitzvah was the daily lifting alone and not the clearing of the mizbeach, for on the regalim they did not clear it and left the heap as it stood, since it is an adornment to the mizbeach.

more.h: Raising comes not from the wilderness
more.t: וְלֹא מִמִּדְבַּר הָרִֽים (Tehillim 75:6 in his edition), and not from the wilderness is raising: raising and enlarging come to a man neither from the rising of the sun nor from its setting nor from the wilderness; they do not come from all his striving and his going here and there, but only from Hashem, as it says כִּי־אֱלֹהִים שֹׁפֵט זֶה יַשְׁפִּיל וְזֶה יָרִים (Tehillim 75:8), for Elokim is the judge, He lowers one and lifts another. Some sefarim read ממדבר with a patach, from the wilderness of, and then הָרִים would be from הַר, mountains; even so the first is correct, and a patach outside a construct has cases like it, מִשְׁפַּט אֶחָד יִהְיֶה לָכֶם (Vayikra 24:22), one law shall there be for you, and וּמִקְסַם חָלָק (Yechezkel 12:24), and smooth divination. In the midrash Rabbi Abba says every הָרִים in Tanach means mountains but this one, which means exaltations, since a man is not exalted by these ways; and what does Hakadosh Baruch Hu do? He takes property from one and gives it to another.

גִּדַּלְתִּי וְרוֹמַמְתִּי (Yeshayahu 1:2), I reared and exalted, אֲרוֹמִמְךָ אֱלוֹהַי הַמֶּלֶךְ (Tehillim 145:1), I will exalt You, my Elokim the King, and רוֹמְמוֹת אֵל בִּגְרוֹנָם (Tehillim 149:6), the exaltations of Hashem in their throat. All of this sense is raising up. Rabbi Yonah divided between them; Radak holds there is no need, for separating one thing from another is itself a raising. So too וּכְסִילִים מֵרִים קָלוֹן, and fools raise up shame: a fool raises shame and brings it upon himself.

more.h: The palace, and the precious stone
more.t: וְאַרְמוֹן עַל־מִשְׁפָּטוֹ יֵשֵׁב (Yirmiyahu 30:18), and a palace shall stand on its own place, may be derived from this sense, called so since it is a high building; he has already given it as a root of its own, אָרַם. רָאמוֹת (Iyov 28:18) is one of the precious stones, and some explain it as אַלְמוֹנִים, which is what is called coral in the vernacular.

דרך.sense: To tread, on the ground or in a winepress, and to draw a bow. דֶּרֶךְ is a way; a man's custom, dealings and desires, and the mitzvos and aveiros, are all called so.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר דָּֽרַךְ־בָּהּ (Devarim 1:36), which he trod upon, דָּרַךְ כּוֹכָב מִֽיַּֽעֲקֹב (Bamidbar 24:17), a star has trodden forth from Yaakov, and אֲשֶׁר תִּדְרֹךְ כַּֽף־רַגְלְכֶם (Yehoshua 1:3), that the sole of your foot shall tread. The added form is intransitive in לֹֽא־הִדְרִיכֻוהוּ בְנֵי־שָׁחַץ (Iyov 28:8), that is, the proud beasts have not trodden in it. It is transitive in יַדְרֵךְ עֲנָוִים בַּמִּשְׁפָּט (Tehillim 25:9), He makes the humble tread in judgment, and הַדְרִיכֵנִי בַֽאֲמִתֶּךָ (Tehillim 25:5), make me tread in Your truth; and מְנוּחָה הִדְרִיכֻהוּ (Shoftim 20:43) is ממנוחה הדריכוהו, from rest they made him tread, and so Targum Yonasan renders it, מִבֵּית נְיַחֲהוֹן טְרָדוּנוּן, from the house of their rest they drove them. With an added mem, מִדְרַךְ כַּף־רָגֶל (Devarim 2:5), the treading of the sole of a foot; and in this sense תִּדְרְכִי נַפְשִׁי עֹֽז (Shoftim 5:21), tread, my soul, in strength, which lacks the beis of service and means you shall trample the enemies in strength.

דֶּרֶךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ נֵלֵךְ (Bamidbar 20:17), we will go by the king's way, and זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ לְכוּ בוֹ (Yeshayahu 30:21), this is the way, walk in it. לַעֲשׂוֹת דַּרְכּֽוֹ (Shoftim 17:8), to make his way, is to make his way on from them and to stay there.
