In פֶּן־יֶאֱנַף וְתֹאבְדוּ דֶרֶךְ (Tehillim 2:12), lest He be angry and you perish, the word דרך means that you will perish on account of the way, that is, because your way is one that perishes, as it says וְדֶרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים תֹּאבֵֽד (Tehillim 1:6), and the way of the wicked shall perish. In the same manner נֹבֶלֶת עָלֶהָ (Yeshayahu 1:30), withering of leaf, is one whose leaves wither.

אָֽנֹכִי הֹלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ כָּל־הָאָרֶץ (Melachim I 2:2), I am going in the way of all the earth, is according to custom; in כִּֽי־הִשְׁחִית כָּל־בָּשָׂר אֶת־דַּרְכּוֹ עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ (Bereishis 6:12), for all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth, the way is its custom; and כִּי־דֶרֶךְ נָשִׁים לִי (Bereishis 31:35), for the way of women is upon me, is the custom of women, which is niddah, and so אֹרַח כַּנָּשִֽׁים (Bereishis 18:11), the way of women. וּמַטֵּהוּ יִשָּֽׂא־עָלֶיךָ בְּדֶרֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם (Yeshayahu 10:24), and he will lift his staff over you in the way of Mitzrayim, is after the custom of Mitzrayim, as the Egyptians used to strike you. So too וּנְשָׂאוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם (Yeshayahu 10:26) is after His custom, what He did in Mitzrayim, and the great hand He showed against them. וּנְשָׂאוֹ may mean He will lift him off you and make an end of him; or it may be said of the staff, that He will raise His staff over him as He did in Mitzrayim, and so ומטהו על הים, and His staff over the sea, is that He will rouse His staff over him as He roused it over the sea when the Egyptians drowned.

more.h: Why all of them are one sense
more.t: They are all one sense, since a man's desires, his dealings and whatever he exerts himself in are all called דֶּרֶךְ; and so are the mitzvos and the aveiros, as אֶת־הַדֶּרֶךְ יֵלְכוּ בָהּ (Shemos 18:20), the way they shall walk in, and דֶּרֶךְ צַדִּיקִים (Tehillim 1:6), the way of the righteous. In דַּֽרְכֵי עַמִּי (Yirmiyahu 12:16), the ways of My people, the dalet is held by a ga'ya, and the Mesorah notes it as the only one with a ga'ya.

more.h: The winepress and the threshing floor
more.t: כְּדֹרֵךְ בְּגַֽת (Yeshayahu 63:2), as one treading in a winepress; אַתָּה תִדְרֹֽךְ־זַיִת וְלֹֽא־תָסוּךְ שֶׁמֶן (Michah 6:15), you shall tread olives and not anoint with oil, which Ben Asher reads with a cholam and Ben Naftali with a kamatz chatuf; and דֹֽרְכִים גִּתּוֹת בַּשַּׁבָּת (Nechemiah 13:15), treading winepresses on Shabbos. כְּגֹרֶן עֵת הִדְרִיכָהּ (Yirmiyahu 51:33) is like a threshing floor at the time of its treading, and the sense of these is trampling and threshing. So too דָּרַכְתָּ בַיָּם סוּסֶיךָ (Chavakuk 3:15), You trod Your horses in the sea, means that as You trod them in the sea, so they trod in the mire of many waters; or else that You trod in the sea upon Your horses, which are the clouds.

In the sense of drawing and bending the bow, דָּרַךְ קַשְׁתּוֹ (Eichah 2:4), he drew his bow, and וְכָל־קַשְּׁתֹתָיו דְּרֻכוֹת (Yeshayahu 5:28), and all his bows are drawn. Since in drawing the bow the arrow is drawn as well, it is said of the arrow too: דָּרְכוּ חִצָּם דָּבָר מָֽר (Tehillim 64:4), they drew their arrow, a bitter word. The heavy form is וַֽיַּדְרְכוּ אֶת־לְשׁוֹנָם (Yirmiyahu 9:2), and they bend their tongue, which by rule would be וידריכו.

שׂרה.sense: שָׂרִיתָ עִם־אֱלֹהִים, you contended with Elokim, and its noun, הַמִּשְׂרָה, dominion. He calls the sense known and does not define it.

more.t: וּבְאוֹנוֹ שָׂרָה אֶת־אֱלֹהִים (Hoshea 12:4), in his strength he contended with Elokim, and כִּי־שָׂרִיתָ עִם־אֱלֹהִים (Bereishis 32:29), for you have contended with Elokim; and the noun לְמַרְבֵּה הַמִּשְׂרָה (Yeshayahu 9:6), for the increase of the dominion. He adds only that the sense is known, and does not define it.

שׁרה.sense: שִׁרְיָן, a coat of mail; מִשְׁרַת עֲנָבִים, a steeping of grapes, known from Chazal's usage; and הַשָּׁרוֹן, which has been explained as level land and a fat place.

more.t: Rabbi Yehudah put שֵׁרִיתִיךָ לְטוֹב (Yirmiyahu 15:11) under this root, and Rabbi Yonah wrote the same; they explained it as akin to the Aramaic וּמְשָׁרֵא קִטְרִין (Daniel 5:12), and loosing knots, so that on their reading it is I have released you for good. Radak has already written it under another root. His father explains תַּחַת כָּל הַשָּׁמַיִם יִשְׁרֵהוּ (Iyov 37:3), under all the heavens He looses it, from this root, and Radak spells out what that comes to: that He looses the binding of the clouds and rains upon the corners of the earth. The same words are also read from steeping. שָׁרוֹתַיִךְ מַעֲרָבֵךְ (Yechezkel 27:25) Radak has written under another root again, and its sense is given there.

וְכָל מִשְׁרַת עֲנָבִים (Bamidbar 6:3), and any steeping of grapes, which he says is known from the words of Chazal: אין שורין דיו וסממנין (Shabbos 1:5), one may not steep ink and dyes, and so they said ולא במי משרה (Berachos 3:5), and not in the water of steeping.

וַיִּלְבַּשׁ צְדָקָה כַּשִּׁרְיָן (Yeshayahu 59:17), he put on righteousness as a coat of mail, בֵּין הַדְּבָקִים וּבֵין הַשִּׁרְיָן (Melachim I 22:34), between the joints and the mail, and וּמִשְׁקַל הַשִּׁרְיוֹן (Shmuel I 17:5), the weight of the mail. וְשִׁרְיוֹן קַשְׂקַשִּׂים (Shmuel I 17:5), a mail of scales, is one made in the manner of scales. With a heh, חֲנִית מַסָּע וְשִׁרְיָה (Iyov 41:18), spear, dart and coat of mail, the שִׁרְיָה being, he says, the תחרה. The plural, with a cholam, is וְשִׁרְיֹנוֹת וּקְשָׁתוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 26:14), coats of mail and bows.

חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן (Shir HaShirim 2:1), the rose of the Sharon, and הָיָה הַשָּׁרוֹן כָּעֲרָבָה (Yeshayahu 33:9), the Sharon has become like a wilderness: it has been explained as a land of level ground and a fat place, and so וְעַל הַבָּקָר הָרֹעִים בַּשָּׁרוֹן (Divrei HaYamim I 27:29), and over the cattle grazing in the Sharon. שִׁרְטַי הַשָּׁרוֹנִי, Shirtai the Sharonite, is a name.

ירה.sense: Three senses: casting, as of lots or arrows; teaching, and its noun תּוֹרָה, how a mitzvah is to be done; and rain, the יוֹרֶה.

more.t: יָרָה בַיָּם (Shemos 15:4), He cast into the sea, הַמַּצֵּבָה אֲשֶׁר יָרִיתִי (Bereishis 31:51), the pillar that I have cast, וְיָרִיתִי לָכֶם גּוֹרָל (Yehoshua 18:6), I will cast lots for you, and לִירוֹת בְּמוֹ־אֹפֶל (Tehillim 11:2), to shoot in the dark. With an alef in place of the heh, לִירוֹא בַּחִצִּים וּבָאֲבָנִים גְּדֹלוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 26:15), to shoot arrows and great stones. In the passive, אוֹ־יָרֹה יִיָּרֶה (Shemos 19:13), or he shall surely be shot. וַנִּירָם אָבַד חֶשְׁבּוֹן he reads as we shot at them and fought them until Cheshbon perished. הַמּוֹרִים אֶל־עֲבָדֶךָ (Shmuel II 11:24), the shooters at your servants, וַיִּמְצָאֻהוּ הַמּוֹרִים אֲנָשִׁים בַּקָּשֶׁת (Shmuel I 31:3), and the shooters, men with the bow, found him, and וַיֹּרֵם אֱלֹהִים (Tehillim 64:8), and God cast at them: all of these are casting. From this sense his father explains מִי כָמֹהוּ מוֹרֶה (Iyov 36:22), who is like Him in casting down: its meaning is one who casts down and brings low to the earth.

אֲשֶׁר הוֹרָהוּ יְהוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן (Melachim II 12:3), which Yehoyada the kohen taught him, וַיֹּרֵנִי וַיֹּאמֶר לִי (Mishlei 4:4), he taught me and said to me, הוֹרוּנִי וַאֲנִי אַחֲרִישׁ (Iyov 6:24), teach me and I will be silent, וְלֹא־שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּקוֹל מוֹרָי (Mishlei 5:13), I did not listen to the voice of my teachers, אֱלֹהָיו יוֹרֶנּוּ (Yeshayahu 28:26), his God teaches him, and וּלְהוֹרֹת נָתַן בְּלִבּוֹ (Shemos 35:34), He put it in his heart to teach: all of them are a matter of teaching. מִגִּבְעַת הַמּוֹרֶה בָּעֵמֶק (Shoftim 7:1), from the hill of the Moreh in the valley, may be from this, or else a place name; if from this, there was a lookout on the hill who would give word to those living in the valley when an army came upon them, and so Targum Yonasan, מִגִבְעֲתָא דְמִסְתַּכְיָא, from the hill of the lookout. Rabbi Yehudah said that הֹרוֹ וְהֹגוֹ מִלֵּב דִּבְרֵי־שָׁקֶר (Yeshayahu 59:13), on this reading teaching and uttering words of falsehood from the heart, may well be from this root. Radak has already written it under the root הָרָה, and that is the correct one; and there he wrote as well that his father put it under this root and this sense.

more.h: תּוֹרָה, and the words beside it
more.t: The noun from this sense, the teaching of the Torah and the mitzvah, is תּוֹרָה: אֶת־הַחֻקִּים וְאֶת־הַתּוֹרֹת (Shemos 18:20), the statutes and the teachings, and מִצְוֹתַי חֻקּוֹתַי וְתוֹרֹתָי (Bereishis 26:5), My mitzvos, My statutes and My teachings; and possibly וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הָאָדָם (Shmuel II 7:19), and this is the teaching of man. Four words each have their own sense: הַתּוֹרָה is the manner of the mitzvah, how it is to be done; הַמִּשְׁפָּט is the law between one man and his fellow; הַחֹק is the thing decreed upon a man to do, whether as a mitzvah or as a custom; and הַמִּשְׁמֶרֶת is the guarding against transgressing a mitzvah and the fence made about it. Each is a sense of its own, but in places one comes in place of another, as each one's own root will explain.

יוֹרֶה וּמַלְקוֹשׁ (Devarim 11:14) is the early and the late rain, and with an alef for the heh, וּמַרְוֶה גם הוא יוֹרֶא (Mishlei 11:25), and one who gives drink is himself rain: one who gives the poor drink is himself called a יוֹרֶה, like the rain that waters the earth. So too אֶת־הַמּוֹרֶה לִצְדָקָה (Yoel 2:23), the rain for righteousness, and וְהָיוּ עֵינֶיךָ רֹאוֹת אֶת־מוֹרֶיךָ (Yeshayahu 30:20), your eyes shall see your rain. וְלֹא־יִכָּנֵף עוֹד מוֹרֶיךָ is that your rain shall no longer be gathered in, for they were in a time of drought, as it says לֶחֶם צָר וּמַיִם לָחַץ, bread of distress and water of oppression; the tidings are of plenty, that the rain will no longer be held back and they will see with their own eyes that it is near. Some read מוֹרֶיךָ from the second sense, teaching: that is, those who teach you the straight way will not be far off at the corner of the earth, and they are Chizkiyahu and his officers. His father writes אֱלֹהָיו יוֹרֶנּוּ from the third sense, that He will give him rain.

לבן.sense: White. The brick, הַלְּבֵנָה, may be from it, since what is burnt whitens; the moon, לְבָנָה, is named for looking white. Also לִבְנֶה, a tree, and לְבוֹנָה, a resin.

more.h: The brick, and the brick kiln
more.t: וַתְּהִי לָהֶם הַלְּבֵנָה לְאָבֶן (Bereishis 11:3), and the brick served them for stone, with the verb נִלְבְּנָה לְבֵנִים (Bereishis 11:3), let us make bricks, and לִלְבֹּן הַלְּבֵנִים (Shemos 5:7), to make the bricks. The kiln in which the bricks are burnt is called מַלְבֵּן, as בַּמַּלְבֵּן (Shmuel II 12:31), in the kiln, which he reads as: he burnt them in the brick kiln. Yonasan renders it וּגְרַר יַתְהוֹן בְּשׁוּקַיָא, and he dragged them through the streets, which Radak explains: he was dragging them through the streets to put them to a hard and contemptible death. As for rendering במלבן as בשוקיא, in the streets, perhaps Yonasan holds that a street is called מלבן because it is lined with colonnades set in order on this side and that, from Chazal's מלבנות התבואה (Peah 3:1), which are beds of grain, so called because they are set in order; so too they said מלבנות הפתחים (Bava Basra 69a), the doorposts on either side of the doorway. בַּמֶּלֶט בַּמַּלְבֵּן (Yirmiyahu 43:9), in the mortar, in the brickworks, is the place where bricks are made, and הַֽחֲזִיקִי מַלְבֵּֽן (Nachum 3:14), make the kiln strong, means build the brick kiln.

more.h: Whether the brick comes from white
more.t: He says the bricks may be from the sense of whiteness, since everything burnt in fire whitens, and so יִתְבָּֽרְרוּ וְיִתְלַבְּנוּ וְיִצָּֽרְפוּ (Daniel 12:10), they shall be purified and made white and refined; and so Chazal said of this matter מלבנן באור והן טהורים (Avodah Zarah 75b), one whitens them in fire and they are tahor.

כְּזֶרַע גַּד לָבָן (Shemos 16:31), like coriander seed, white: the mon was white and its grains were like coriander seed. מַחְשׂף הַלָּבָן (Bereishis 30:37), laying bare the white; וּֽלְבֶן ־שִׁנַּיִם מֵֽחָלָֽב (Bereishis 49:12), white of teeth from milk; and כֵּהוֹת לְבָנֹת (Vayikra 13:39), dull white spots. Standing of itself, כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ (Yeshayahu 1:18), they shall be white as snow, and הִלְבִּינוּ שָֽׂרִיגֶֽיהָ (Yoel 1:7), her branches have whitened, that is, they dried and turned white. Taking an object, וּלְבָרֵר וְלַלְבֵּן עַד־עֵת קֵץ (Daniel 11:35), to purify and to whiten until the time of the end, where the form should have been וּלְהַלְבֵּן, and with the heh gone its vowel was thrown onto the prefixed lamed.

Rabbi Yonah explained לִבְנַת הַסַּפִּיר (Shemos 24:10) as a noun, the whiteness of the sapphire, and so the Gaon said, that the sapphire is white. Ibn Ezra wrote in his commentary that the sapphire is red, his proof being אָֽדְמוּ עצם מפנינים סַפִּיר גִּזְרָתָֽם (Eichah 4:7), they were ruddier of bone than pearls, their form was sapphire, where the sense is doubled, as in זַכּוּ נְזִירֶיהָ מִשֶּׁלֶג צַחוּ מֵחָלָב, her nezirim were purer than snow, whiter than milk; and further, why does the pasuk say כמעשה, like the work of, when it should have said כמראה, like the appearance of, the whiteness of the sapphire? Rather, the correct view is that it is from לְבָנָה, a brick, as חֶֽשְׁכַת ־מַיִם (Tehillim 18:12), darkness of waters, is from חֲשֵׁכָה, darkness, and so לבנת הספיר, a brick of sapphire, is like the sapphire stone that Yechezkel saw. The derash goes the same way: that they saw the likeness of a brick under the feet of the Kisei HaKavod, to see and remember that Yisrael were enslaved under the hand of Mitzrayim at the work of bricks.

more.h: The moon, the tree, and לְבוֹנָה
more.t: וְחָֽפְרָה הַלְּבָנָה (Yeshayahu 24:23), and the moon shall be abashed: it is the moon, called so because it appears white. תַּחַת אַלּוֹן וְלִבְנֶה (Hoshea 4:13), under oak and livneh, and מַקַּל לִבְנֶה (Bereishis 30:37), a rod of livneh, are a tree whose name comes from לבן, white, and Rabbi Yonah wrote that it is the one called לובני in Arabic. לְבֹנָה זַכָּה (Vayikra 24:7), pure levonah, is well known, and עִם כָּל־עֲצֵי לְבוֹנָה (Shir HaShirim 4:14), with all trees of levonah, are the trees the levonah comes from, for levonah is the resin of a tree.

עַל מוּת לַבֵּן (Tehillim 9:1), upon the death of Labben, or upon the death, for Ben: some take לבן as the name of one of David's enemies, at whose death the mizmor was made; some take it as נָבָל with its letters reversed. His father wrote that the lamed is a prefix and that בֵּן is the name of a singer, set out in Divrei HaYamim among the second rank, זְכַרְיָהוּ בֵּן וְיַֽעֲזִיאֵל וּשְׁמִֽירָמוֹת (Divrei HaYamim I 15:18), Zecharyahu, Ben, and Yaaziel and Shemiramos; David said the mizmor on the death of Golyas and the victory over the Pelishtim, and Ben the singer played it. If you ask why it is not לְבֵן with a sheva, as לְאָסָף, since the article does not come on a man's name or a city's, the answer is that though it is not the way of the language it comes at times for the sake of definiteness, as it does on a city's name: אֲשֶׁר בַּשֶּׂכוּ (Shmuel I 19:22), which is at Sechu, and וַֽיִּפְקְדֵם בַּטְּלָאִים (Shmuel I 15:4), and he counted them at Telaim; and here the article was used so the name should not be confused with the ordinary word for a son.

ספן.sense: The roofing of houses and covering them over; close to it, שְׂפֻנֵי, hidden things, written with a sin; and the סְפִינָה, a ship, a known word.

more.t: וַיִּסְפֹּן אֶת־הַבַּיִת (Melachim I 6:9), and he roofed the house; וְסָפוּן בָּאֶרֶז (Yirmiyahu 22:14), and roofed with cedar; לָשֶׁבֶת בְּבָֽתֵּיכֶם סְפוּנִים (Chaggai 1:4), to sit in your roofed houses. The noun is עַד־קִירוֹת הַסִּפֻּן (Melachim I 6:15), up to the walls of the roofing. All of them are the roofing of houses and the covering of them.

חֶלְקַת מְחֹקֵק סָפוּן (Devarim 33:21) is a portion of a lawgiver, roofed over: the share of Bnei Gad was the portion of a lawgiver and a ruler, the whole of it built and roofed as it should be, a hint at the cities they took across the Yarden.
Close to this sense is וּשְׂפֻנֵי טְמוּנֵי חֽוֹל (Devarim 33:19), the hidden things stored away in the sand. It is written with a sin, and שפוני is like טמוני, buried.
אֶל־יַרְכְּתֵי הַסְּפִינָה (Yonah 1:5), to the innermost part of the ship, of which he says only that it is known.

חרס.sense: The sun, and from it the eastern gate of the Beis HaMikdash; in another sense the dry scab, named for the potsherd it is scratched with.

more.t: הָֽאֹמֵר לַחֶרֶס וְלֹא יִזְרָח (Iyov 9:7), who tells the sun and it does not rise, and בְּטֶרֶם יָבֹא הַחַרְסָה (Shoftim 14:18), before the sun went in; their sense is the sun. From this the eastern gate of the Beis HaMikdash is called שַׁעַר הַֽחַרְסִות (Yirmiyahu 19:2), the gate of the sun, because it was set facing the rising of the sun.
מִֽלְמַֽעֲלֵה הֶחָֽרֶס (Shoftim 8:13) Yonasan takes from this same sense, rendering it עַד לָא מֵעַל שִׁמְשָׁא, before the sun set.

Another sense: וּבַגָּרָב וּבֶחָרֶס (Devarim 28:27), with the scab and with the cheres. It is the dry scab, called so because it is scratched with a חרס, a potsherd, as it says וַיִּֽקַּֽח־לוֹ חֶרֶשׂ לְהִתְגָּרֵד בּוֹ (Iyov 2:8), he took himself a potsherd to scrape himself with.

חזר.sense: The חֲזִיר, the pig, which he calls known and does not explain; in the Mishnah the root is much used for חזרה, going back.

more.t: וְאֶֽת־ הַֽחֲזִיר (Vayikra 11:7), and the pig, which he marks ידוע, known, and nothing further. He adds that in the Mishnah they used this root much in the language of חזרה, going back.

כתב.sense: To write. The nouns כְּתָב and מִכְתָּב are each both the writing itself and a letter sent; and כְּתֹבֶת קַֽעֲקַע, a mark gouged into the flesh and written in.

more.t: וְכָתַב לָהּ סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת (Devarim 24:1), and he writes her a bill of severance; וְהִיא כְתוּבָה פָּנִים וְאָחוֹר (Yechezkel 2:10), and it was written front and back; כָּל־ הַכָּתוּב לַחַיִּים (Yeshayahu 4:3), everyone written down for life; וְכָתוֹב בַּסֵּפֶר וְחָתוֹם (Yirmiyahu 32:44), writing it in the deed and sealing it. וְזֶה יִכְתֹּב יָדוֹ (Yeshayahu 44:5) is יכתוב בידו: and this one will write with his hand.

וַיִּכְתֹּב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶת־הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה בְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרַת אֱלֹהִים (Yehoshua 24:26), and Yehoshua wrote these words in the book of the Torah of God: Yonasan renders that he wrote them וְאַצְנְעִינוּן בְּסֵפֶר אוֹרַיְתָא, and laid them away in the book of the Torah. Chazal are divided over it (Makkos 11a): some say it speaks of the eight pesukim from the death of Moshe to the end of the Torah, that Yehoshua wrote them in the Torah; others say it speaks of the parsha of the cities of refuge, that Yehoshua wrote it in his own sefer as it stands in the Torah. By the plain sense of the pasuk it would seem that what Yehoshua wrote was the covenant he cut with Yisrael, and then its meaning is as Yonasan rendered, since the words of the covenant cannot have been written in the Sefer Torah.

more.h: The noun for the writing itself
more.t: הַכֹּל בִּכְתָב (Divrei HaYamim I 28:19), the whole of it in writing; מְדִינָה וּמְדִינָה כִּכְתָבָהּ (Esther 3:12), every province in its own script. With a mem added, וְהַמִּכְתָּב מִכְתַּב אֱלֹהִים הוּא (Shemos 32:16), and the writing was the writing of Hashem.

כְתָב אֲשֶׁר־נִכְתָּב בְּשֵׁם־הַמֶּלֶךְ (Esther 8:8), a writ written in the king's name; and with a mem, וַיָּבֹא אֵלָיו מִכְתָּב מֵאֵֽלִיָּהוּ הַנָּבִיא (Divrei HaYamim II 21:12), and a letter came to him from Eliyahu HaNavi. In the passive, בְּשֵׁם הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרשׁ נִכְתָּב (Esther 3:12), in the name of King Achashverosh it was written.
וְעַל־לִבָּם אֶכְתֲּבֶנָּה (Yirmiyahu 31:33), I will write it on their heart: Ben Naftali points the tav with a sheva and a patach, Ben Asher with a kamatz chatuf.

וּכְתֹבֶת קַֽעֲקַע (Vayikra 19:28), an incised writing: a man gouges into his flesh and writes in the incision. In the heavy form, וּֽמְכַתְּבִים עָמָל כִּתֵּֽבוּ (Yeshayahu 10:1), and the writers who have written oppression; and it may be that the verb there reaches a third party.

לחם.sense: To eat, and לֶחֶם, food of every kind, said most of all of bread; from this sense, מִלְחָמָה, war, and to fight, since in war the sword eats on this side and on that.

more.h: Eating, and food of every kind
more.t: כִּי לָֽחֲמוּ לֶחֶם רֶשַׁע (Mishlei 4:17), for they have eaten the food of wickedness; כִּֽי־תֵשֵׁב לִלְחוֹם אֶת־מוֹשֵׁל (Mishlei 23:1), when you sit to eat with a ruler; לְכוּ לַֽחֲמוּ בְֽלַֽחֲמִי (Mishlei 9:5), come, eat of my food. וּלְחֻמֵי רֶשֶׁף (Devarim 32:24) he glosses אכולי רשף, eaten up by the fiery bolt. Some read וְשֹׁרֶשׁ רְתָמִים לַחְמָֽם (Iyov 30:4), the root of the broom is their food, from this sense; Radak has already written of it under the root חָמַם. Every לֶחֶם, he says, is a word for food in general. It falls on meat alone, as לֶחֶם אִשֶּׁה (Vayikra 3:11), the food of the fire offering, and אֶת־קָרְבָּנִי לַחְמִי לְאִשַּׁי (Bamidbar 28:2), My offering, My food, for My fires; it takes in meat and terumos together at לֶחֶם אֱלֹהָיו (Vayikra 21:22), the food of his God, and likewise מִלֶּחֶם אָבִיהָ תֹּאכֵל (Vayikra 22:13), she eats of her father's food. It settled on bread more than on other foods because bread is the mainstay of what a man eats.

לְהוֹצִיא לֶחֶם מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ (Tehillim 104:14), to bring bread out of the earth, names the end the grass is for, since bread does not come out of the ground but through causes that go before it. So too צֶמַח בְּלִי יַֽעֲשֶׂה־ קֶּמַח (Hoshea 8:7), growth that makes no flour: the end of the growth is the flour, though acts pass into acts before it is reached, and the flour is not the last end either, for the last end is the bread, in what suits a man.

נַשְׁחִיתָה עֵץ בְּלַחְמוֹ (Yirmiyahu 11:19) is let us destroy the tree with its fruit: he takes בְּלַחְמוֹ as בפריו, its fruit. His father reads the words turned about, נשחיתה לחמו בעץ, that is, let us ruin his food with the tree. The tree is the one called in Arabic דפל"א, which is a deadly poison, and of it was said that Hashem showed him a tree and he cast it into the water (Shemos 15:25), a miracle inside a miracle, as Chazal say (Yelamdenu, Beshalach). Yonasan renders the same way, נִרְמֵי סַמָא דְמוֹתָא בְּמֵיכְלֵיהּ, let us cast deadly poison into his food.

מֵֽאָשֵׁר שְׁמֵנָה לַחְמוֹ (Bereishis 49:20), out of Asher, his bread shall be rich, takes in every food: whatever his land brings out will be rich. שְׁמֵנָה, rich, belongs to his land, as though the pasuk said a rich land will be his bread, the words being cut short as at וּמַֽאֲכָלוֹ בְּרִאָֽה (Chavakuk 1:16), and his food is fat. Or else שְׁמֵנָה is said of לַחְמוֹ, meaning by it an עוּגָה, a cake, or a חַלָּה, a loaf, which is a feminine word; and likewise לֶחֶם תְּנוּפָה שְׁתַּיִם (Vayikra 23:17), two of wave bread, means חַלּוֹת, loaves.

more.h: War, and whom a man fights for
more.t: מִלְחָמָה, war, is from this same sense, because in war there is the eating of the sword from this side and from that. The verb from it: לְחַם אֶת־ לֹֽחֲמָֽי (Tehillim 35:1), fight those who fight me, and לֹחֵם יִלְחָצֵֽנִי (Tehillim 56:2), a fighter presses me; and אִם־ נִלְחֹם נִלְחַם בָּֽם (Shoftim 11:25), did he ever fight against them, and וַיִּלָּחֶם עִם־לִבְנָֽה (Yehoshua 10:29), he fought with Livnah. Three he glosses as fighting on someone's behalf: אֲֽשֶׁר־ נִלְחַם אָבִי עֲלֵיכֶם (Shoftim 9:17), that my father fought over you, is בעבורכם, for your sake; כִּי י"י נִלְחָם לָהֶם (Shemos 14:25), for Hashem fights for them, is בעבורם, on their behalf; and יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם (Shemos 14:14), He will fight for you, is on your behalf. וַיִּלָּֽחֲמוּנִי חִנָּֽם (Tehillim 109:3) he glosses וילחמו בי חנם, they fought against me for nothing.

אָז לָחֶם שְׁעָרִים (Shoftim 5:8), then fighting at the gates: Rabbi Yonah writes that לָחֶם is a past verb of the light form, on the measure of יָבֵשׁ חָצִיר (Yeshayahu 40:7), the grass is withered. Though it has a segol, a segol at times comes in place of a tzere; were it of the heavy form the lamed would have a patach, as is usual, but since it has a kamatz it is a past verb of the light form. Radak adds that it may also be a noun on the pattern of חָמֵץ, leaven, so that the words say there was war in the gates, though this one has a segol and that one a tzere.

ככר.sense: A large loaf of bread, and a piece of bread; the plain of the Yarden; and the talent of gold or silver, sixty litrin, the holy talent twice that.

more.t: וְכִכַּר לֶחֶם אַחַת (Shemos 29:23), and one loaf of bread, is a large loaf, since the rest were חלות and רקיקים, cakes and wafers.
וְכִכַּר־לָחֶם (Shmuel I 2:36) is, as its Targum has it, פִּתָּא דְלַחְמָא, that is, a piece of bread.
כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן (Bereishis 13:11), the plain of the Yarden, as its Targum renders it, מֵישַׁר יַרְדְּנָא, the level plain of the Yarden.

כִּכַּר זָהָב (Shemos 25:39), a talent of gold; וַיָּצַר כִּכְּרַיִם כֶּסֶף (Melachim II 5:23), he bound up two talents of silver; וַיִּקַּח בְּיָדוֹ עֶשֶׂר כִּכְּרֵי־כֶסֶף (Melachim II 5:5), he took ten talents of silver in his hand. The ordinary talent was sixty litrin, and the talent of kodesh double it, a hundred and twenty litrin.

פתת.sense: Cutting and breaking into pieces, as פַת־לֶחֶם, a piece of bread, and פִּתִּים, pieces.

more.t: פָּתוֹת אֹתָהּ פִּתִּים (Vayikra 2:6), break it into pieces, is a sense of cutting and breaking, and so פַת ־לֶחֶם (Bereishis 18:5), a piece of bread, וְאֹכַל פִּתִּי לְבַדִּי (Iyov 31:17), that I ate my morsel alone, and מִפִּתּוֹ תֹאכַל (Shmuel II 12:3), it would eat of his morsel.

מַשְׁלִיךְ קַֽרְחוֹ כְפִתִּים (Tehillim 147:17), casting His ice like morsels, is like a thing broken up into bits; the word in its fuller form is וּבִפְתוֹתֵי לֶחֶם (Yechezkel 13:19), for scraps of bread.

Rabbi Yehudah records another sense in this root, for the heavy form וַֽהֲפִתִּיתָ בִּשְׂפָתֶֽיךָ (Mishlei 24:28); by rule the word would be הֲפִתּוֹתָ, with a cholam. Radak takes it up again under the root פָּתָה, in its proper form. It may also be from the sense given here, breaking and cutting, as suits the pasuk, אַל־תְּהִי עֵֽד־חִנָּם בְּרֵעֶךָ (Mishlei 24:28), be not a witness against your fellow without cause: if you are a witness against him without cause, you break him and strike him with your lips. On that reading, וַֽהֲפִתִּיתָ בִּשְׂפָתֶֽיךָ means and you would break him with your lips.

חרר.sense: To be scorched, burnt with heat. From it come the חֲרָרָה, a cake baked on the coals; the kindling of a quarrel; and חַרְחֻר, a sickness that burns from much heat.

more.t: וְעַצְמִי־ חָרָה מִנִּי־חֹֽרֶב (Iyov 30:30), my bone is burnt with heat; וְחָרָה נְחֻשְׁתָּהּ (Yechezkel 24:11), and its copper is burnt; עַל־כֵּן חָרוּ ישְׁבֵי אֶרֶץ (Yeshayahu 24:6), therefore the dwellers of the earth are scorched. In the passive, וְהָֽעֲצָמוֹת יֵחָֽרוּ (Yechezkel 24:10), the bones will be burnt; and with a chirik under the nun, נִחַר גְּרוֹנִי (Tehillim 69:4), my throat is scorched, and וְעַצְמוֹתַי כְּמוֹקֵד נִחָֽרוּ (Tehillim 102:4), my bones are burnt as a hearth.

נָחַר מַפֻּחַ (Yirmiyahu 6:29), the bellows is scorched: the instrument they blow the fire with is kindled and burnt from standing so long in the fire, and the lead is spent, the lead the smiths put in with the silver in refining it so that the fire should not destroy the silver; and for all that, the wicked are not drawn off. It is a mashal for Yisrael. The navi speaks to them הַשְׁכֵּם וְהַֽעֲרֵב, early and late, until he is as one burnt up from speaking to them, his throat scorched from calling to them without stopping, as it says elsewhere עַל־כֵּן חָצַבְתִּי בַּנְּבִיאִים הֲרַגְתִּים בְּאִמְרֵי־פִי (Hoshea 6:5), therefore I hewed at them by the nevi'im, I slew them with the words of My mouth; and with all this they take no rebuke and do not believe the navi's voice.

The noun is וְשָׁכַן חֲרֵרִים בַּמִּדְבָּר (Yirmiyahu 17:6), he dwells in the scorched places of the wilderness, a sense of burning and kindling from much heat; the singular of חררים is חָרֵר or חֲרָרָה. From this the cake baked on the coals is called חֲרָרָה, as in ולא חררה על גבי גחלים (Shabbos 1:10), nor a cake upon coals, and it is called so because its face is scorched. The Talmud Yerushalmi explains סַלֵּי חֹרִי (Bereishis 40:16), baskets of חֹרִי, and its meaning, as Radak gives it, is that the baskets were full of חררות, such cakes.

With the first root letter doubled, לְחַרְחַר ־רִֽיב (Mishlei 26:21), to kindle a quarrel and set it burning; the patach under the second ches stands in place of a tzere. From the same, וּבַֽחַרְחֻר וּבַחֶרֶב (Devarim 28:22), and with burning and with the sword: a sickness that burns from much heat.

עוף.sense: Three senses: to fly; darkness, which most commentators take the other way, as brightness; and weariness, with עָיֵף borrowed for one who thirsts.

more.t: כַּֽחֲלוֹם יָעוּף (Iyov 20:8), he flies off like a dream; מֵחֵץ יָעוּף יוֹמָֽם (Tehillim 91:5), the arrow that flies by day; וַיָּעָף אֵלַי אֶחָד מִן־הַשְּׂרָפִים (Yeshayahu 6:6), one of the Serafim flew to me, where the first root letter is read with a short kamatz. Also כִּי־גָז חִישׁ וַנָּעֻֽפָה (Tehillim 90:10), it passes quickly and we fly away. Doubled, וְעוֹף יְעוֹפֵף עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 1:20), and let birds fly over the earth; and turned back on itself, כָּעוֹף יִתְעוֹפֵף כְּבוֹדָם (Hoshea 9:11), their glory will fly off like a bird.

מֻעָף בִּיעָף (Daniel 9:21), made to fly, in flight, may belong to this root, its yud added as the yud of יְקוּם is added to קוּם, and Radak has set it out already under the root יָעַף. Rabbi Yehudah brings here מְגִלָּה עָפָֽה (Zecharyah 5:1), a flying scroll, and so the Targum, which renders it מְגִלָה פִּרְחָא, a flying scroll. Some read it as folded, from the Targum of וְכָפַלְתָּ (Shemos 26:9), and you shall fold, which is וְתֵיעוּף.

תָּעֻפָה כַּבֹּקֶר תִּהְיֶֽה (Iyov 11:17), which he reads as: if you grow dark now, you will be like the morning. So too עֹשֵׂה שַׁחַר עֵיפָה (Amos 4:13), who makes the dawn darkness, and אֶרֶץ עֵיפָתָה כְּמֽוֹ־אֹפֶל (Iyov 10:22), a land of darkness like gloom, that last carrying two feminine endings as יְשׁוּעָתָה does. His father writes that כמו אפל, like gloom, is a place where the sun does not shine for six months, which is not under the line of the earth and which the light of the sun does not reach. The rest of the pasuk Radak takes himself: ולא סדרים, and no order, is that there is no order of moon and stars there, and וַתֹּפַע כְּמוֹ־אֹֽפֶל, and it is dark like gloom, is that the darkness is like that same gloom. The noun, in another form, is מְעוּף צוּקָה (Yeshayahu 8:22), the darkness of distress, and in the passive כִּי לֹא מוּעָף לַֽאֲשֶׁר מוּצָק לָהּ (Yeshayahu 8:23): it was not made dark for Eretz Yisrael at the first as it is now, for the first trouble, when Pul king of Ashur exiled them, was light and took only Zevulun and Naftali away, while this last time Sancheriv bore down hard. מוּעָף may be a noun, and so מוּצָק. Rabbi Yehudah brings הֲתָעִיף עיניך בו (Mishlei 23:5), will you make your eyes dark upon it, into this group as well. The sense of them all is darkness and gloom.

more.h: Read the other way, as light
more.t: Most of the commentators take תָּעֻפָה כַּבֹּקֶר תִּהְיֶֽה and הֲתָעִיף עיניך בו the other way, of flashing and light, and explain עֹשֵׂה שַׁחַר עֵיפָה the same way. בְּעֽוֹפְפִי חַרְבִּי עַל־פְּנֵיהֶם (Yechezkel 32:10), when I brandish my sword before them, is in this sense when I make it flash and flame as I draw it from its sheath; or it can be read from the first sense, of movement, when I wave it and shake it over them to kill, and movement is close to flight. The noun here is doubled: בְּעַפְעַפֵּי־שָֽׁחַר (Iyov 3:9), the glow of dawn and its light. In this sense the pupil of the eye is called עפעף: לְֽעַפְעַפַּי תְּנוּמָֽה (Tehillim 132:4), slumber to the pupils of my eyes; עַפְעַפָּיו יִבְֽחֲנוּ בְּנֵי אָדָֽם (Tehillim 11:4), the pupils of His eyes try the sons of man; וְעַל עַפְעַפַּי צַלְמָֽוֶת (Iyov 16:16), and on the pupils of my eyes is the shadow of death; and וְעַפְעַפֵּינוּ יִזְּלוּ־מָֽיִם (Yirmiyahu 9:17), the pupils of our eyes will run with water, which Targum Yonasan renders וְגַלְגַלֵי עֵינָנָא יִגְרוּן מַיָא, the balls of our eyes will run with water.

In the words of Chazal it is used this way: אין מדליקין בצרי, one may not light with balsam, מפני שהוא עף, because it flies (Shabbos 25b), that is, it darts and moves off the lamp and spatters here and there; and היתה מעופפת בזמן שכנפיה נוגעות בקן חייב לשלח (Chullin 140b), if she was hovering, at a time when her wings touch the nest, one is bound to send her away, that is, she is stirring, not flying but near to flight. So too, in Radak's own view, וְעָפוּ בְכָתֵף פְּלִשְׁתִּים יָמָּה (Yeshayahu 11:14), and they shall move on the shoulder of the Pelishtim seaward: Israel will move toward the side of the Pelishtim to spoil and to plunder there. בכתף stands as a construct although it is not pointed as one, which would be בְּכֶתֶף with segol; Ben Asher wrote that it came so because of the peh of פלשתים, to set the reading right.

עָֽיְפָה נַפְשִׁי לְהֹֽרְגִֽים (Yirmiyahu 4:31), my soul is faint before the killers; וְהֽוּא־נִרְדַּם וַיָּעַף וַיָּמֹֽת (Shoftim 4:21), he was asleep and spent and died; and וַיָּעַף דָּוִֽד (Shmuel II 21:15), and David grew weary. These last two take a patach in the first root letter to keep them apart from וַיָּעָף אלי, and he flew to me, which is the other sense. The adjective is עָיֵף וְיָגֵעַ (Devarim 25:18), weary and worn. Since a weary man thirsts for water, a thirsty man is called עָיֵף by borrowing, though there is no weariness in him at all but thirst alone, as it says וְכַֽאֲשֶׁר יַֽחֲלֹם הַצָּמֵא וְהִנֵּה שֹׁתֶה וְהֵקִיץ וְהִנֵּה עָיֵף וְנַפְשׁוֹ שֽׁוֹקֵקָה (Yeshayahu 29:8), as when the thirsty man dreams and here he is drinking, and he wakes and here he is thirsty and his soul longs. So too land that thirsts because no rain has fallen on it: בְּאֶֽרֶץ־צִיָּה וְעָיֵף בְּלִי־מָֽיִם (Tehillim 63:2), in a dry and thirsty land without water; נַפְשִׁי כְּאֶֽרֶץ־ עֲיֵפָה לְךָ סֶֽלָה (Tehillim 143:6), my soul is to You like a thirsty land, selah; and כְּצֵל סֶֽלַע־כָּבֵד בְּאֶרֶץ עֲיֵפָֽה (Yeshayahu 32:2), like the shade of a heavy rock in a thirsty land. Some take וְעָפוּ בְכָתֵף פְּלִשְׁתִּים from this sense, and Radak has explained it under the root כָּתֵף.

חשׁב.sense: To think and to plan, and to take a thing for something or nothing. Since craft and counting rest on thought, it serves for both, and Chazal call the חֹשֵׁב a weaver.

more.t: וְשָׁאוּל חָשַׁב לְהַפִּיל אֶת־דָּוִד, Shaul planned to bring David down; וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה (Bereishis 50:20), you thought evil against me, Elokim thought it for good; and וְלֹֽא־יָדַעְתִּי כִּֽי־עָלַי חָֽשְׁבוּ מַֽחֲשָׁבוֹת (Yirmiyahu 11:19), I did not know they had laid plans against me. In the heavy form, חִשַּׁבְתִּי יָמִים מִקֶּדֶם (Tehillim 77:6), I thought over days of old; וַֽאֲחַשְּׁבָה לָדַעַת זֹאת (Tehillim 73:16), I thought, so as to know this; מַה־ תְּחַשְּׁבוּן (Nachum 1:9), what do you plot against Hashem; לֵב אָדָם יְחַשֵּׁב דַּרְכּוֹ (Mishlei 16:9), a man's heart plans his way; and וְאֵלַי יְחַשְּׁבוּ (Hoshea 7:15), and against Me they plan. In וְהָאֳנִיָּה חִשְּׁבָה לְהִשָּׁבֵֽר (Yonah 1:4), and the ship thought to be broken, it is the men of the ship who thought she would break, in the way of וְכָל־ הָאָרֶץ בָּאוּ מִצְרַיְמָה (Bereishis 41:57), and all the land came to Egypt, which means all the men of the land, and וַתִּרְעַב כָּל־אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם (Bereishis 41:55), and all the land of Egypt hungered, and those like them. The sense of thought, he says, is known.

וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ עֵלִי לְשִׁכֹּרָֽה (Shmuel I 1:13), Eli took her for a drunken woman; and יַחְשֹׁב תְּהוֹם לְשֵׂיבָֽה (Iyov 41:24), one would take the deep for grey hair, which he explains: one who sees the deep white would take it for grey hair.

Since a craft goes by thought, the word is used of craftsmanship: לַחְשֹׁב מַֽחֲשָׁבֹת (Shemos 31:4), to devise designs, and מַֽעֲשֵׂה חֹשֵׁב תַּֽעֲשֶׂה אֹתָֽם (Shemos 26:1), you shall make them the work of a designer. The noun is וְחֵשֶׁב אפדתו (Shemos 28:8), the band of its efod, with five vowel points, and וַיַּעַשׂ בִּירֽוּשָׁלַם חִשְּׁבֹנוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 26:15), he made devices in Yerushalayim, with the shin doubled for ornament. On מעשה רוקם כמעשה חושב, the embroiderer's work like the designer's work, the Chachamim in Yoma 72b ask what it means, and Rabbi Elazar answers שרוקמין במקום שחושבים, that they embroider at the place where they do the designer's work; a braisa there teaches רוקם מעשה מחט ולפיכך פרצוף אחד, embroidery is needlework and so has one face, חושב מעשה אורג, לפיכך שני פרצופין, the designer's work is weaving and so has two faces.

The same word serves for reckoning and for the philosopher's inquiry: וּבַקֵּשׁ חָכְמָה וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן (Koheles 7:25), to seek wisdom and reckoning; כִּי אֵין מַֽעֲשֶׂה וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן (Koheles 9:10), for there is no deed and no reckoning; and וְהֵמָּה בִקְשׁוּ חִשְּׁבֹנוֹת רַבִּֽים (Koheles 7:29), but they sought many reckonings, with the shin doubled for ornament, which he takes as the devices and matters men raise over the Creator's work, why He made this so and why that was so, when He made man upright and all His work is in faithfulness. Of number likewise, since number rests on thought: Hashem does not reckon iniquity to a man (Tehillim 32:2). In the passive, אַךְ לֹֽא־ יֵֽחָשֵׁב אִתָּם הַכֶּסֶף הַנִּתָּן עַל־יָדָם (Melachim II 22:7), no reckoning was made with them of the money given into their hand; in the heavy form, וְחִשַּׁב אֶת־שְׁנֵי מִמְכָּרוֹ (Vayikra 25:27), he shall count the years of his sale, and וְלֹא יְחַשְּׁבוּ אֶת־הָֽאֲנָשִׁים (Melachim II 12:16), and they made no reckoning with the men; and turned back on itself, וּבַגּוֹיִם לֹא יִתְחַשָּֽׁב (Bamidbar 23:9), and among the nations it shall not reckon itself.

more.h: Counted for nothing, or for much
more.t: Near to this is לֹא חָשַׁב אֱנֽוֹשׁ (Yeshayahu 33:8), he took no account of man, which he glosses as he took no notice of them and counted them for nothing; and like it נִבְזֶה וְלֹא חֲשַׁבְנֻֽהוּ (Yeshayahu 53:3), despised, and we did not account him; אֲשֶׁר־כֶּסֶף לֹא יַחְשֹׁבוּ (Yeshayahu 13:17), who set no store by silver; and וּלְחֹֽשְׁבֵי שְׁמֽוֹ (Malachi 3:16), those who give heed to His name. יַֽחֲשָׁב לִי (Tehillim 40:18), Hashem will take account of me, means: may my prayers and pleas be reckoned before Him, and may He take notice of the poverty and want I am in; and from this the Chachamim in Avodah Zarah 25b call an honoured man אדם חשוב, a man of account. In the passive, אֵין כֶּסֶף לֹא נֶחְשָׁב בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה לִמְאֽוּמָה (Melachim I 10:21), there was no silver, it was not reckoned as anything in Shlomo's days, which he explains as there being no silver in any of the vessels, since they were all gold, because silver counted for nothing in Shlomo's days; and וְנֶחְשַׁב לָכֶם תְּרֽוּמַתְכֶם (Bamidbar 18:27), your terumah shall be reckoned to you; מַדּוּעַ נֶחְשַׁבְנוּ כַבְּהֵמָה (Iyov 18:3), why are we counted as beasts; כִּֽי־בַמֶּה נֶחְשָׁב הֽוּא (Yeshayahu 2:22), for of what account is he; הֲלוֹא נָכְרִיּוֹת נֶחְשַׁבְנוּ לוֹ (Bereishis 31:15), are we not accounted strangers by him; לֹא יֵֽחָשֵׁב לוֹ פִּגּוּל יִֽהְיֶה (Vayikra 7:18), it shall not be reckoned to him, it shall be piggul; and רְפָאִים יֵחָֽשְׁבוּ אַף־הֵם כַּֽעֲנָקִים (Devarim 2:11), the Refaim too were accounted Anakim.

קטף.sense: To cut off: the sense of them all is כריתה, cutting.

more.t: אֵת רֹאשׁ יְנִֽיקוֹתָיו קָטָף (Yechezkel 17:4), he cut off the top of its young shoots; וְקָֽטַפְתָּ מְלִילֹת (Devarim 23:26), and you may cut off ears of grain; מֵרֹאשׁ יֹֽנְקוֹתָיו רַךְ אֶקְטֹף (Yechezkel 17:22), from the top of its shoots I will cut off a tender one; and in the passive עֹדֶנּוּ בְאִבּוֹ לֹא יִקָּטֵף (Iyov 8:12), while it is still in its greenness it is not cut off. Of all of them: ענינם ענין כריתה, their sense is a sense of cutting.

דוד.sense: An uncle, the father's brother; a beloved, and love; a pot; a basket; and perhaps the דּוּדָאִים, a plant's root in the likeness of a man.

more.t: דּוֹד שָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 10:14), Shaul's uncle, which he glosses as אחי אביו, his father's brother; לִבְנֵי דֹֽדֵיהֶן (Bamidbar 36:11), to the sons of אחי אביהן, their father's brothers; and דֹּדָֽתְךָ הִֽוא (Vayikra 18:14), she is אשת אחי אביך, your father's brother's wife.

לְעֵינֵי חֲנַמְאֵל דֹּדִי (Yirmiyahu 32:12), before the eyes of Chanamel my uncle, means the son of my uncle, this being the way of the Hebrews, as וְגַם אֶת־לוֹט אָחִיו (Bereishis 14:16), and also Lot his brother, means his brother's son. Or it may be that this was a different Chanamel who was his uncle and was there at the purchase, since the Chanamel who sold was the son of Shallum, and Shallum was Yirmiyahu's uncle, while the Chanamel present at the purchase was his uncle, his father's brother; and so Targum Yonasan rendered it, לְעֵינֵי חֲנַמְאֵל אַחֲבִי, before the eyes of Chanamel my father's brother.

דּוֹדִי לי ואני לו (Shir HaShirim 2:16), my beloved is mine and I am his, which he glosses as ידידי ואהובי, my dear one and my beloved; כִּֽי־טוֹבִים דֹּדֶיךָ (Shir HaShirim 1:2), for your loves are good, אהביך וידידותיך, your loves and your endearments; and so אֶתֵּן אֶת־ דֹּדַי לָֽךְ (Shir HaShirim 7:13), I will give my love to you, and נִרְוֶה דֹדִים עַד־הַבֹּקֶר (Mishlei 7:18), let us drink our fill of love until the morning.

בַכִּיּוֹר אוֹ בַדּוּד (Shmuel I 2:14), in the basin or in the pot; כַּפָּיו מִדּוּד תַּֽעֲבֹֽרְנָה (Tehillim 81:7), his hands passed from the pot; and וַיָּשִׂימוּ אֶת־רָֽאשֵׁיהֶם בַּדּוּדִים (Melachim II 10:7), and they put their heads in the pots. The vav takes a vowel in בַּסִּירוֹת וּבַדְּוָדִים (Divrei HaYamim II 35:13), in the cauldrons and in the pots; the sense of all of them is pots. In שְׁנֵי דּֽוּדָאֵי תְאֵנִים (Yirmiyahu 24:1), two baskets of figs, the alef is added, as the alef of לֻֽלָאֹת חֲמִשִּׁים (Shemos 36:17), fifty loops, is added, and the pasuk after it says הדּוּד אחד, the one basket, without it; their sense is baskets. וישימו את ראשיהם בדודים may likewise be בסלים, in baskets.

הַֽדּוּדָאִים נָֽתְנוּ־רֵיחַ (Shir HaShirim 7:14), the dudaim gave off their scent; וַיִּמְצָא דֽוּדָאִים בַּשָּׂדֶה (Bereishis 30:14), and he found dudaim in the field; and בְּדֽוּדָאֵי בְּנִי (Bereishis 30:16), with my son's dudaim. The alef in them may be an addition, or they may be another root altogether. They are the root of a plant in the likeness of a man, male and female, called mandragores in the vernacular.

ערס.sense: Dough: רֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֹתֵכֶם, the first of your dough, a sense he calls well known.

more.t: רֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֹתֵכֶם (Bamidbar 15:20), the first of your dough, and וְרֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֽוֹתֵיכֶם (Yechezkel 44:30), and the first of your dough: פירושו בצק, its meaning is dough, והוא ידוע, and it is well known.

צפר.sense: To rise early in the morning; a going round, as the turban wound round the head; צִפּוֹר, a bird; צְפִיר, a he-goat; and צִפֹּרֶן, a nail, and an iron stylus.

more.t: יָשֹׁב וְיִצְפֹּר (Shoftim 7:3), let him turn back and rise early: its sense is ישכים בבקר, let him rise early in the morning, and the Targum of בֹּקֶר, morning, is צַפְרָא. So too in בָּאָה הַצְּפִירָה (Yechezkel 7:7), it has come, הַצְּפִירָה being the decree that comes upon you in the morning.

Some explain both וְיִצְפֹּר and הַצְּפִירָה as a sense of going round, and Yonasan renders הַצְּפִירָה as מַלְכוּתָא, kingdom. וְלִצְפִירַת תִּפְאָרָה (Yeshayahu 28:5), and for a turban of glory, is the turban that is wound round the head. The Mishnah (Keilim 16:7) has הקופה משיעשה בה שתי צפירות לרחב שלה, the basket, from when two windings are made in it across its breadth, והערק משיעשה בה צפירה אחת, and the erek, from when one winding is made in it; that is, the going round that is made about a basket.

כָּל־ צִפּוֹר טְהֹרָה (Devarim 14:11), every clean bird; כֹּל צִפּוֹר כָּל־כָּנָף (Yechezkel 17:23), every bird of every wing; and שְׁתֵּֽי־ צִפֳּרִים חַיּוֹת טְהֹרוֹת (Vayikra 14:4), two live clean birds. In the masculine, כְּצִפּוֹר בּוֹדֵד עַל־גָּֽג (Tehillim 102:8), like a lone bird on a roof, and אֲשֶׁר־שָׁם צִפֳּרִים יְקַנֵּנוּ (Tehillim 104:17), where birds make their nests. It is a name covering every bird, but sometimes a particular one: in גַּם־ צִפּוֹר מָצְאָה בַיִת וּדְרוֹר קֵן לָהּ (Tehillim 84:4), the bird too has found a house and the swallow a nest, the second word is particular and so the first is particular too, a small bird; and because its kind is so numerous, every bird came to be called by its name.

וְהַצָּפִיר הַשָּׂעִיר (Daniel 8:21), and the he-goat, the sa'ir, וּצְפִיר הָֽעִזִּים (Daniel 8:8), and the he-goat of the goats, and צְפִירֵי חַטָּאת שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר (Ezra 8:35), twelve he-goats for a sin offering; the word is known, and the Targum of שְׂעִיר (Bereishis 37:31), a goat, is צְפִיר. The doubling in וְהַצָּפִיר הַשָּׂעִיר is to make the sense plain, as in נֶגְבָּה תֵימָֽנָה (Shemos 26:18), southward, to the south, and קֵדְמָה מִזְרָֽחָה (Bamidbar 34:15), eastward, toward the sunrise, where the second word is plainer than the first; for צפיר is not common in the language as שעיר is, but belongs to Aramaic. Or else השעיר is from וְיִשְׂתָּעֵר עָלָיו מֶלֶךְ הַצָּפוֹן (Daniel 11:40), the king of the north will storm against him.

more.h: The nail, and the iron stylus
more.t: בְּצִפֹּרֶן שָׁמִיר (Yirmiyahu 17:1), with a stylus of shamir, and וְעָֽשְׂתָה אֶת־ צִפָּרְנֶֽיהָ (Devarim 21:12), she shall do her nails; the word is known. Since a man digs with his nails, the iron pen that digs was called a ציפורן, and so the pasuk says בְּצִפֹּרֶן שָׁמִיר, for שמיר is the hard iron; and the Midrash likewise has נטל צפורן של ברזל, he took an iron stylus.

כנף.sense: A wing; by borrowing, shelter under a wing and a garment's lower edge; the ends of the earth; light spreading as a wing spreads; and יִכָּנֵף, to be gathered in.

more.t: כָּל־בַּעַל כָּנָֽף (Mishlei 1:17), every owner of a wing, and כֹּל צִפּוֹר כָּל־ כָּנָֽף (Bereishis 7:14), every bird, every wing, which he glosses as כל צפור בעל כנף, every bird that owns a wing. So כְּנַף ־רְנָנִים נֶעֱלָסָה (Iyov 39:13), the wing of the renanim rejoices; וְלָהֵנָּה כְנָפַיִם כְּכַנְפֵי הַֽחֲסִידָה (Zecharyah 5:9), and they had wings like the wings of the stork; יִפְרֹשׂ כְּנָפָיו (Devarim 32:11), it spreads its wings; and כַּנְפֵי יוֹנָה נֶחְפָּה בַכֶּסֶף (Tehillim 68:14), the wings of a dove overlaid with silver. The sense is known.

By borrowing, אֲשֶׁר־בָּאת לַֽחֲסוֹת תַּֽחַת־ כְּנָפָֽיו (Rus 2:12), under whose wings you have come to take shelter, which is to shelter in His shade. The lower edge of a garment is called a כנף: עַל־צִיצִת הַכָּנָף (Bamidbar 15:38), on the fringe of the edge; על ארבע כַּנְפוֹת כסותך (Devarim 22:12), on the four edges of your covering; and וְנָגַע בִּכְנָפוֹ אֶל־הַלֶּחֶם (Chaggai 2:12), and he touches the bread with the edge of his garment.

Likewise מִכְּנַף הָאָרֶץ (Yeshayahu 24:16), from the end of the earth, and לֶאֱחֹז בְּכַנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ (Iyov 38:13), to take hold of the ends of the earth: both are בקצות הארץ, at the ends of the earth. אֶשָּׂא כַנְפֵי ־שָׁחַר (Tehillim 139:9), should I take up the wings of dawn, means: if I go to the far end of the east.

וּמַרְפֵּא בִּכְנָפֶיהָ (Malachi 3:20), and healing in its wings, likens the spreading of light to the spreading of a wing; and וְעַל כְּנַף שִׁקּוּצִים מְשֹׁמֵם (Daniel 9:27), and over the wing of abominations one is appalled, he takes as: over the spreading of the abominations a man will be appalled and full of wrath. In וְלֹֽא־ יִכָּנֵף עוֹד מוֹרֶיךָ (Yeshayahu 30:20), and your moreh will be gathered in no more, the verb means לא יאסף ולא יעצר, will not be gathered in and not held back, and its like is in Chazal's language, who call the gathering of people and their assembling כנופיא (Yoma 51a). Some explain it as לא ירחק, will not be far off, which Radak explains as not being at the edge of the earth. The pasuk is explained further at the root ירה.

אנה.sense: Mourning; in another sense, the causing and bringing about of a thing; and in a third, אֳנִי, a ship.

more.t: וְאָנוּ הַדַּיָּגִים (Yeshayahu 19:8), the fishermen mourn, and וְאָנוּ וְאָֽבְלוּ פְּתָחֶיהָ (Yeshayahu 3:26), her gates mourn and grieve. The noun is תַּֽאֲנִיָּה וַֽאֲנִיָּֽה (Eichah 2:5), mourning and lament. The sense is ענין אבל, mourning.

אִנָּה לְיָדוֹ (Shemos 21:13), where Hashem brought it about to his hand; and turned back on itself, כִּֽי־ מִתְאַנֶּה הוּא לִֽי (Melachim II 5:7), he is seeking an occasion against me. The noun is כִּי־ תֹאֲנָה הֽוּא־מְבַקֵּשׁ מִפְּלִשְׁתִּים (Shoftim 14:4), for he was seeking an occasion from the Pelishtim, and in another form תַּֽאֲנָתָהּ מִי יְשִׁיבֶנָּה (Yirmiyahu 2:24), her occasion, who can turn it back? Their sense is ענין גרם הדבר וסבובו, a thing's being caused and brought round.

בַּל־תֵּלֶךְ בּוֹ אֳנִי ־שַׁיִט (Yeshayahu 33:21), no rowing ship will go on it, and אַחַת לְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים תָּבוֹא אֳנִי תַרְשִׁישׁ נֹֽשְׂאֵת זָהָב וָכֶסֶף (Melachim I 10:22), once in three years the ships of Tarshish came bearing gold and silver. In the masculine, אֳנִי חִירָם אֲשֶׁר־נָשָׂא זָהָב מֵֽאוֹפִיר (Melachim I 10:11), Chiram's fleet, which carried gold from Ophir; with the feminine heh, וְהָאֳנִיָּה חִשְּׁבָה לְהִשָּׁבֵֽר (Yonah 1:4), and the ship was near to breaking; and in the plural, אֳנִיּוֹת אֵבֶה (Iyov 9:26), ships of אֵבֶה. Their sense is ספינה, a ship.

בכר.sense: Firstborn, and the firstborn's right; the first fruit, בִּכּוּרִים; a woman bearing her first child; and the firstborn of camels, the young ones.

more.t: בְּכוֹר אֶתְּנֵהוּ (Tehillim 89:28), I will make him a firstborn. The plural comes both in the feminine way, מִבְּכֹרוֹת צֹאנוֹ (Bereishis 4:4), of the firstlings of his flock, and in the masculine, וְאֶת־בְּכוֹרֵי בְקָרֵינוּ (Nechemiah 10:37), and the firstborn of our herds. Another adjective is הַבְּכִירָה (Bereishis 19:31), the elder daughter, from בָּכִיר, on the pattern of שָֹכיר, a hired man.

לָֽחֳדָשָׁיו יְבַכֵּר (Yechezkel 47:12), month by month it will bear first fruits, which is how he glosses it, ישא בכורים; and לֹא יוּכַל לְבַכֵּר (Devarim 21:16), he may not make one the firstborn, which he glosses לתת לו משפט הבכורה, to give him the right of the firstborn. In the passive, אֲשֶׁר יְבֻכַּר (Vayikra 27:26), what is made a firstling.

רֵאשִׁית בִּכּוּרֵי אַדְמָתְךָ (Shemos 23:19), the first of the first fruits of your ground; תְּאֵנִים עִם־בִּכּוּרִים (Nachum 3:12), fig trees with first fruits; and with a feminine ending, כְּבִכּוּרָה בִתְאֵנָה (Hoshea 9:10), like a first fruit on the fig tree. Another adjective, with a patach under the beis, is כִּתְאֵנֵי הַבַּכֻּרוֹת (Yirmiyahu 24:2), like the first-fruit figs. Of them all he says ענינם ידוע, their sense is known, and it is the first fruit.
צָרָה כְּמַבְכִּירָה (Yirmiyahu 4:31), distress like hers who bears her first child, whose pangs are the stronger.

At Iyov 18:13, the angel set over death is called בְּכוֹר מָֽוֶת, firstborn of death, because he has a great portion in death; or death before its time is so called. His father explains it as the first illness to come upon a man, of which he dies, or as a phrase turned about, בכור בדיו, the firstborn of his branches. Radak takes that second reading to mean that death will eat the firstborn of his branches, which are his sons. And בְּכוֹרֵי דַלִּים (Yeshayahu 14:30), the firstborn of the poor, Radak takes of Yisrael, who have the firstborn's portion and a great portion in poverty.

בִּכְרָה קַלָּה (Yirmiyahu 2:23), a swift firstborn she-camel, and בִּכְרֵי מִדְיָן וְעֵיפָה (Yeshayahu 60:6), the firstborn camels of Midyan and Eifah: these are the firstborn of the camels, male and female, which are young. The Targum renders the one הוֹגְנֵי מִדְיָן, the sucklings of Midyan, and the other יַנְקָא קַלִילָא, a swift suckling, since הוגני in the plural means sucklings and little ones, as Chazal say (Sanhedrin 52a), many old camels carry the hides of young ones.

סכך.sense: To cover over, and at times to screen off as a partition; the nouns סֻכָּה, a booth, and מָסָךְ, a screen; and סָךְ, a count.

more.t: סֹֽכְכִים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם (Shemos 25:20), covering with their wings, and כְּרוּב הַסֹּכֵךְ (Yechezkel 28:16), the covering keruv; יְסֻכֻּהוּ צֶאֱלִים (Iyov 40:22), the shady trees cover him. So too וְשַׂכֹּתִי כַפִּי (Shemos 33:22), and I will cover with My palm, though it is written with a sin. Of one who covers another, בְּאֶבְרָתוֹ יָסֶךְ לָךְ (Tehillim 91:4), He will cover you with His pinion, and וַיָּסֶךְ בִּדְלָתַיִם יָם (Iyov 38:8), He screened off the sea with doors.

Most of the root, he says, is סיכוך למעלה, covering from above; but part of it is a partition and shield that divides one thing from another. So וְסַכֹּתָ עַל־הָֽאָרֹן אֶת־הַפָּרֹֽכֶת (Shemos 40:3), you shall screen the aron with the paroches, since the paroches was not over the aron but beside it, dividing between it and the ohel moed; and so פָּרֹכֶת הַמָּסָֽךְ (Shemos 35:12), the screening paroches, and מָסַךְ הַפֶּתַח (Shemos 35:15), the screen of the entrance.

וְסֻכָּה תִּהְיֶה לְצֵל־יוֹמָם מֵחֹרֶב (Yeshayahu 4:6), a booth for shade by day from the heat, and בַּסֻּכֹּת תֵּֽשְׁבוּ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים (Vayikra 23:42), you shall dwell in booths seven days. With an added mem, פָּרַשׂ עָנָן לְמָסָךְ (Tehillim 105:39), He spread a cloud for a screen; its proper form, he says, is מִסְכָךְ, on the pattern of מִכְלָל.

וְהֻכַן הַסֹּכֵֽךְ (Nachum 2:6), the covering is made ready: boards with hides over them, under which those attacking a city come up to the wall and dig beneath it, shielded from the stones thrown down on them from above.

From this root and this sense is מוּסַךְ הַשַּׁבָּת (Melachim II 16:18), the covering for Shabbos. It is on the pattern of מוֹרָד (Melachim I 7:29), whose root is רָדַד; though the one has a shuruk and the other a cholam, the two are one. Rabbi Yonah explained it מחסה המשמרה, the shelter of the watch; Radak takes that to be the place where the men of the watch take cover. Yonasan renders it טִיקוּס, which Radak leaves unexplained. Rashi wrote that it is the roof of a tent made for shade, to sit under in the azarah on Shabbos.

כִּי אֶעֱבֹר בַּסָּךְ (Tehillim 42:5), for I would pass in the סָךְ, is in the number of the congregation, counted within it. Chazal have the like of a total count, סך הכל (Avodah Zarah 11b), the sum of it all, and with a mem added, סכום מקח (Beitzah 29b), the sum of a purchase.

אלף.sense: A thousand. In other senses, an אַלּוּף, a chief and a great man; learning and teaching; and אֲלָפִים, oxen.

more.t: אֶלֶף לַמַּטֶּה (Bamidbar 31:4), a thousand to a tribe, הִנֵּה אַלְפִּי הַדַּל בִּמְנַשֶּׁה (Shoftim 6:15), my thousand is the poorest in Menasheh, and שָׂרֵי אֲלָפִים (Shemos 18:21), captains of thousands, of which he says ענינם ידוע, their sense is known. From the same sense, צֹאונֵנוּ מַֽאֲלִיפוֹת (Tehillim 144:13), which he glosses יולדות לאלפים, bearing by the thousands.

אַלּוּפִי וּמְיֻדָּֽעִי (Tehillim 55:14), my chief and my acquaintance, אַלּוּף נְעֻרַי אָֽתָּה (Yirmiyahu 3:4), You are the chief of my youth, and אַלּוּף תֵּימָן אַלּוּף אוֹמָר (Bereishis 36:15), the chief Teiman, the chief Omar. The sense of all of them is שר וגדול, a prince and a great man. Chazal (Sanhedrin 99b) said כל אלוף מלכותא בלא תגא, every aluf is kingship without a crown. Radak explains: he lacks nothing of being a king but the crown, for a man is called king when he is crowned and aluf when he is not.

Some read הִנֵּה אַלְפִּי הַדַּל בִּמְנַשֶּׁה (Shoftim 6:15), behold, אַלְפִּי is the poorest in Menasheh, from the sense of a chief, taking it as my father, which what follows would bear out: וְאָֽנֹכִי הַצָּעִיר בְּבֵית אָבִֽי, and I am the youngest in my father's house. They read וְצֵלַע הָאֶלֶף (Yehoshua 18:28), and Tzela Ha'elef, the same way, as the great one. Yonasan read כְּכֶבֶשׂ אַלּוּף (Yirmiyahu 11:19) from it, rendering כְּאִימֵר בְּחִיר, like a choice lamb.

פֶּן־תֶּאֱלַף (Mishlei 22:25), lest you learn his ways; and where the verb takes an object, כִּֽי־יְאַלֵּף עֲוֹֽנְךָ פִיךָ (Iyov 15:5), which he glosses כי ילמד עונך פיך, your sin teaches your mouth; וַֽאֲאַלֶּפְךָ חָכְמָֽה (Iyov 33:33), and I will teach you wisdom; and מַלְּפֵנוּ מִבַּֽהֲמוֹת אָרֶץ (Iyov 35:11), teaching us from the beasts of the earth, whose proper form is מְאַלְּפֵנוּ.

בָּנוּי לְתַלְפִּיּוֹת (Shir HaShirim 4:4), built for talpiyos: some read it from this root with the alef dropped for ease, the full form being לְתַֽאַלְפִּיּוֹת. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the tav stands in place of the alef, so that it is as אַלְפִּיּוֹת and its sense is teaching; Radak explains him to mean that the tower, being high, is something wayfarers are taught by. Radak himself will explain it at root תלל as a compound word.

In שְׁגַר־אֲלָפֶיךָ (Devarim 7:13), the offspring of your oxen, and וְהָֽאֲלָפִים וְהָֽעֲיָרִים (Yeshayahu 30:24), the oxen and the young donkeys, the word is oxen. In another form, אַלּוּפֵינוּ מְֽסֻבָּלִים (Tehillim 144:14), our oxen laden, either laden with flesh, that is, fat and full of meat, or laden with work, there being much to work with them. In כְּכֶבֶשׂ אַלּוּף יוּבַל לִטְבוֹחַ (Yirmiyahu 11:19) a kaf of comparison or an added vav is wanting: like a lamb, like an ox, or like a lamb and an ox led to the slaughter.

בקר.sense: To seek out and examine; from this בֹּקֶר, morning, when every thing is made out by daylight; and a second sense, בָּקָר, cattle.

more.t: וְדָֽרַשְׁתִּי אֶת־צֹאנִי וּבִקַּרְתִּֽים (Yechezkel 34:11), I will seek out My flock and look them over; לֹֽא־יְבַקֵּר הַכֹּהֵן (Vayikra 13:36), the kohen shall not examine; and יִֽהְיֶה־לִּי לְבַקֵּֽר (Melachim II 16:15), it shall be for me to inspect, which he glosses כשיעלה בלבי לבקרו, when it comes into my heart to inspect it. The noun is כְּבַקָּרַת רֹעֶה עֶדְרוֹ (Yechezkel 34:12), like a shepherd's looking over his flock. All of them, he says, are דרישה ובקור, seeking and examining.

From this sense the morning is called בֹּקֶר, because in the morning every thing is made out by the light of day, while its opposite, the evening, is when all things mix together and a man cannot tell them apart. And the light is called בקר: כּוֹכְבֵי בֹקֶר (Iyov 38:7), stars of the morning, as though it said stars of light, like כָּל־כּוֹכְבֵי אֽוֹר (Tehillim 148:3), all the stars of light, and those, he says, are the seven that serve. Likewise the morning is called אור: מִן־הָאוֹר עַד־מַֽחֲצִית הַיּוֹם (Nechemiah 8:3), from the light until midday, as though it said from the morning. And וּלְבַקֵּר בְּהֵיכָלֽוֹ (Tehillim 27:4) can be read from this, like ולשחר: to seek at dawn in His Heichal.

At Vayikra 19:20, which he glosses מולקת תהיה, she shall be lashed. Rav Saadiah Gaon wrote that the word is בקורת because the lashes are given with רצועה של בקר, a strap of cattle hide. Or the bet may stand in place of a peh, the two being close in sense because they come from one place in the mouth, as the Mishnah's הבקר לעניים (Peah 6:1), declared free for the poor, is as הפקר, ownerless; and Targum Yerushalmi renders וּנְטַשְׁתָּהּ (Shemos 23:11), and you shall let it lie, with ותבקרון יתה, and you shall leave it ownerless. The sense of בִּקֹּרֶת תִּֽהְיֶה is that she is הפקר, not having been freed, and therefore they are not put to death, though there is lashing. Chazal say, in Kerisos, that the lashing is hers and not his, since the pasuk says תִּֽהְיֶה, she shall be, and not יהיו, they shall be.

Another sense: צֹאן־וּבָקָר (Bereishis 13:5), flocks and herds, whose sense he calls known; in the plural, אִם־יַֽחֲרוֹשׁ בַּבְּקָרִים (Amos 6:12), does one plough with oxen. And the verb from it, כִּֽי־בוֹקֵר אָנֹכִי (Amos 7:14), for I am a בוקר, which he explains as רועה הבקר, a herdsman of cattle.

גבן.sense: Cheese, גְּבִנָּה, whose sense he calls known; two words Rabbi Yonah brought under this root, Radak files under גב, holding that correct.

more.t: One pasuk, הֲלֹא כֶֽחָלָב תַּתִּיכֵנִי וְכַגְּבִנָּה תַּקְפִּיאֵֽנִי (Iyov 10:10), did You not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese, of which he says ידוע, its sense is known. Rabbi Yonah brought אֽוֹ־ גִבֵּן אוֹ־דַק (Vayikra 21:20), or a hunchback or a dwarf, and הָרִים גַּבְנֻנִּים (Tehillim 68:17), many-peaked mountains, under this root. Radak has already written them under the root גב, and that, he says, is correct.

חרץ.sense: Moving, and the diligent, who move about for their food; decreeing and judgment; cutting, with the threshing sledge and a trench; cheeses; and gold.

more.t: לֹֽא־ חָרַץ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְאִישׁ אֶת־לְשֹׁנֽוֹ (Yehoshua 10:21) means: not one man of them moved his tongue at Yisrael, the lamed of לאיש being an extra one like the lamed of הַשְּׁלִשִׁי לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם (Divrei HaYamim I 3:2), the third, Avshalom; or it means to a man of Bnei Yisrael, that not one of them moved his tongue even at a single man of Bnei Yisrael, and all the less at all of them together. So too לֹא יֶֽחֱרַץ ־כֶּלֶב לְשֹׁנוֹ (Shemos 11:7), no dog shall move its tongue, and אָז תֶּחֱרָץ (Shmuel II 5:24), then you shall move. The sense of these is ענין התנועה, movement.

מַחְשְׁבוֹת חָרוּץ אַךְ־לְמוֹתָר (Mishlei 21:5), the thoughts of the diligent are only to profit. וְהֽוֹן־אָדָם יָקָר חָרֽוּץ (Mishlei 12:27) he reads as though turned about, והון אדם חרוץ יקר, the wealth of a diligent man is precious; and some take חרוץ there for a noun, so that the precious thing in a man's wealth is החריצות, diligence itself. In the plural, וְיַד חָרֽוּצִים תַּֽעֲשִֽׁיר (Mishlei 10:4), the hand of the diligent makes rich, and וְנֶפֶשׁ חָֽרֻצִים תְּדֻשָּֽׁן (Mishlei 13:4), the soul of the diligent shall be made fat; the sense of all of it is movement. They are men who move about for their food and do their work in uprightness and justice, diligent and quick to acquire this world and the next, the opposite of the lazy and the deceitful.

כֵּן מִשְׁפָּטֶךָ אַתָּה חָרָֽצְתָּ (Melachim I 20:40), so is your judgment, you yourself have decreed it; בְּעֵמֶק הֶֽחָרוּץ (Yoel 4:14), in the valley of decree, which the Targum renders בְּמֵישַׁר פִּלוּג דִינָא, the plain where judgment is divided; כִּי כָלָה וְנֶחֱרָצָה (Yeshayahu 10:23), for destruction, and decreed, whose meaning is: and the destruction is decreed; and אִם חֲרוּצִים יָמָיו (Iyov 14:5), if his days are decreed, a passive participle, that is, גזורים, decreed.

כִּי לֹא בֶֽחָרוּץ יוּדַשׁ קֶצַח (Yeshayahu 28:27), for קֶצַח, black cumin, is not threshed with a חָרוּץ, means with a מורג חרוץ, which cuts and threshes the grain, as in הִנֵּה שַׂמְתִּיךְ לְמוֹרַג חָרוּץ חָדָשׁ (Yeshayahu 41:15), behold, I have made you a new threshing sledge that cuts. It is a board of wood with fine stones set under it, to cut the straw and bring the grain out of its husk; the tool's name is מורג, and it is called חרוץ for its work, cutting the husk from the grain. Though they are one tool, there may be some difference between מורג and חרוץ; or חרוץ describes the מורג as one that cuts well, and such a great heavy tool is not fit for threshing קצח and fine seed.

וּבַֽחֲרִצֵי הַבַּרְזֶל (Shmuel II 12:31), and with cutters of iron, and בַּֽחֲרֻצוֹת הַבַּרְזֶל (Amos 1:3), with cutters of iron, are like it, the sense of all of them being החתוך והכריתה, cutting and severing. So too אֽוֹ־ חָר֣וּץ אֽוֹ־יַבֶּ֗לֶת (Vayikra 22:22), or חָרוּץ or with a wart, where חָרוּץ has been explained as cut, and Chazal explain it, in Bechoros, as an eyelid split or nicked, or a lip split or nicked. And וְנִבְנְתָה רְחוֹב וְחָרוּץ (Daniel 9:25), and it shall be built, street and trench, is a digging cut into the ground, as the Mishnah's חריץ שבין שתי חצרות (Eruvin 7:3), a trench between two courtyards.

חֲרִצֵי הֶֽחָלָב (Shmuel I 17:18), which the Targum renders גוּבְנִין דַחֲלָבָא, cheeses of milk: it may be that they are so named because they are pressed in the making, and their making resembles the work of the חרוץ in threshing. מֵחָרוּץ וּמִפָּז (Mishlei 8:19), than gold and fine gold, בִּֽירַקְרַק חָרֽוּץ (Tehillim 68:14), with the greenish hue of gold, וְחָרוּץ כְּטִיט חוּצֽוֹת (Zecharyah 9:3), and gold like the mud of the streets, and יִרְפַּד חָרוּץ עֲלֵי־טִֽיט (Iyov 41:22), he spreads gold upon the mud, are all of them gold, though some explain precious stones. Rabbi Yonah wrote that וְיַד חָרֽוּצִים תַּֽעֲשִֽׁיר (Mishlei 10:4) and וְנֶפֶשׁ חָֽרֻצִים תְּדֻשָּֽׁן (Mishlei 13:4), the hand of the חָרוּצִים makes rich and the soul of the חָֽרֻצִים shall be made fat, may be from this too, and Radak takes his meaning to be the great merchants, the gold men, that is, those who hold the gold.

כסס.sense: Number: תָּכֹסּוּ עַל־הַשֶּֽׂה, you shall make your count for the lamb; and the מֶכֶס, the tax, is named for number, being taken by count.

more.t: תָּכֹסּוּ עַל־הַשֶּֽׂה (Shemos 12:4), you shall make your count for the lamb, and in the same pasuk בְּמִכְסַת נְפָשֹׁת, by the number of souls; אֵת מִכְסַת הָֽעֶרְכְּךָ (Vayikra 27:23), the count of your valuation; and on another pattern וַיְהִי הַמֶּכֶס (Bamidbar 31:37), and the tax was. All of them are ענין מנין, a sense of number.

more.h: Why the tax is called מֶכֶס
more.t: The tax is named for number, because those who take the tax take by number from the one who passes them, a fifth or a sixth or a tenth, according to the law and the custom.

more.h: The mem becomes a root letter
more.t: Chazal used the word so much, as in היה עובר על בית המכס (Kilayim 9:3), one who was passing by the tax house, that they fixed the mem as a root letter and called the collectors מוכסים: אין פורטין מתיבת המוכסים (Bava Kamma 113a), one does not change money out of the collectors' chest. So too they fixed the tav of תְּחִלָּה, a beginning, and said מַתְחִיל, he begins, and the tav of תְּרוּמָה, terumah, and said תּוֹרֵם, he separates terumah.

גזל.sense: To rob, a sense he calls known, with גֵּזֶל, robbery; and in another sense גּוֹזָל, the small bird, which beside the turtledove is the young of the dove.

more.t: וְהֵשִׁיב אֶת־הַגְּזֵלָה אֲשֶׁר גָּזָל (Vayikra 5:23), and he shall return the robbed thing that he robbed; אֲשֶׁר גָּֽזְלוּ עַבְדֵי אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ (Bereishis 21:25), which the servants of Avimelech had seized; and פֶּן־תִּגְזֹל אֶת־בְּנוֹתֶיךָ מֵֽעִמִּֽי (Bereishis 31:31), lest you seize your daughters from me. In the passive, וְֽנִגְזְלָה שְׁנָתָם (Mishlei 4:16), and their sleep is robbed from them. The noun is בְגָזֵל (Vayikra 5:21), by robbery, and bound to the next word, גֵּזֶל אָח (Yechezkel 18:18), robbery of a brother, and וְגֵזֶל מִשְׁפָּט וָצֶדֶק (Koheles 5:7), and the robbing of justice and right. Their sense is known, ענינם ידוע.

וְתֹר וְגוֹזָֽל (Bereishis 15:9), a turtledove and a young bird, is the young of the dove. The pasuk says גוֹזָֽל, whose sense is the small bird, as עַל־גּֽוֹזָלָיו יְרַחֶף (Devarim 32:11), it hovers over its young, because of the doves only the small ones are fit for a korban.

עצר.sense: To withhold and hold back, and in a close sense to hold up or detain. From it rule is called עֶצֶר, holding the people in, and a gathering עֲצָרָה, held in one place.

more.t: וְעָצַר אֶת־הַשָּׁמַיִם (Devarim 11:17), and He shuts up the heavens, and הֵן יַעְצֹר בַּמַּיִם וְיִבָשׁוּ (Iyov 12:15), He holds back the waters and they dry up. In the passive, וְהַמַּגֵּפָה נֶֽעֱצָֽרָה (Bamidbar 17:15), the plague was stayed. The noun is שְׁאוֹל וְעֹצֶר רָחַם (Mishlei 30:16), the grave and the withholding of the womb. The sense is withholding.

כִּי אִם־אִשָּׁה עֲצֻֽרָה ־לָנוּ (Shmuel I 21:6), a woman has been kept from us, he takes as מנועה ממנו, withheld from us; that is, held back on our account, she not having been with us as before when I set out, and the young men's vessels were holy, so the bread is clean for us to eat. The bread itself carries no me'ilah, since there is none in the lechem hapanim once the bezichin have been burned; and even the loaves still on the shulchan, which the shulchan makes holy and in which there is me'ilah all the while they lie on it, they could eat, since there was no other bread and they were hungry, and nothing stands before pikuach nefesh but avodah zarah, gilui arayos and shefichus damim. This explanation appears from the words of Chazal in Menachos 95b, and he has given the pasuk another explanation under the root חָלַל.

In a close sense the word is holding up. וְלֹא עָצַרְתִּי כֹּֽחַ (Daniel 10:8) he reads as לא עכבתי הכח לעצמי, I kept no strength back for myself; וְלֹא עָֽצְרוּ לָלֶכֶת אֶל־תַּרְשִֽׁישׁ (Divrei HaYamim II 20:37) as they kept no strength to go to Tarshish; and אַל־ תַּֽעֲצָר ־לִי לִרְכֹּב (Melachim II 4:24) as אל תעכב לי הבהמה לרכוב, do not hold the animal back from me to ride. So נַעְצְרָה ־נָּא אוֹתָךְ (Shoftim 13:15), let us detain you, and עוֹדֶנּוּ עָצוּר בַּֽחֲצַר הַמַּטָּרָה (Yirmiyahu 33:1), he was still shut up in the court of the guard. נֶעְצָר לִפְנֵי (Shmuel I 21:8), held back before Hashem, is kept there to pray; and the noun מֵעֹצֶר וּמִמִּשְׁפָּט לֻקָּח (Yeshayahu 53:8), he was taken from confinement and from judgment, is the place where he was held, and hints at the exile. Of all of them the sense is holding up and withholding.

more.h: What is shut in and what is left out
more.t: On עָצוּר וְעָזוּב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim I 14:10), shut up and left in Yisrael, and on וְאֶפֶס עָצוּר וְעָזֽוּב (Devarim 32:36), and there is none shut up or left, his father takes עָצוּר as the wealth shut up in the houses and עָזוּב as the cattle left out in the field.

more.h: Rule, which holds the people in
more.t: From this, kingship and dominion are called עֶצֶר, as יוֹרֵשׁ עֶצֶר (Shoftim 18:7), an heir to rule, and זֶה יַעְצֹר בְּעַמִּֽי (Shmuel I 9:17), this one shall hold sway over My people, because the king or the ruler restrains the people from going out and from doing anything without his leave, in the manner of וּבִלְעָדֶיךָ לֹֽא־יָרִים אִישׁ אֶת־יָדוֹ וְאֶת־רַגְלוֹ (Bereishis 41:44), without you no man shall lift his hand or his foot.

From this a gathering of men in one place is called עֲצָרָה, as קַדְּשׁוּ־צוֹם קִרְאוּ עֲצָרָה (Yoel 1:14), sanctify a fast, call an assembly, and עֲצֶרֶת בֹּגְדִים (Yirmiyahu 9:1), an assembly of traitors, because they are held and stay in the place of their gathering. His father explains עֲצֶרֶת בֹּֽגְדִֽים (Yirmiyahu 9:1) as a kingdom of traitors, from יוֹרֵשׁ עֶצֶר, an heir to rule. The festival is called עֲצֶרֶת because the people are held back in it from doing work, and the eighth day of Sukkos is the one called עצרת on its own (Divrei HaYamim II 7:9), either because it had nothing to be named by, as chag hamatzos and chag hashavuos and chag hasukkos have, or because the olei regel were held there after they had finished Sukkos, to keep that day holy.

המה.sense: To make a noise: nations in tumult, innards moaning, bears and dogs and doves, the sound of a harp, and a city loud with it.

more.t: הָמוּ גוֹיִם מָטוּ מַמְלָכוֹת (Tehillim 46:7), the nations were in tumult, the kingdoms tottered; עַל־כֵּן הָמוּ מֵעַי (Yirmiyahu 31:19), therefore my innards moan; נֶהֱמֶה כַדֻּבִּים כֻּלָּנוּ (Yeshayahu 59:11), we all growl like bears; כְּיוֹנֵי הַגֵּֽאָיוֹת כֻּלָּם הֹמוֹת (Yechezkel 7:16), like the doves of the valleys, all of them moaning; יָשׁוּבוּ לָעֶרֶב יֶהֱמוּ כַכָּלֶב (Tehillim 59:7), they return at evening and howl like a dog; and לִבִּי לְמוֹאָב כַּֽחֲלִלִים יֶֽהֱמֶה (Yirmiyahu 48:36), my heart sounds for Moav like flutes.

עִיר הֽוֹמִיָּה קִרְיָה עַלִּיזָה (Yeshayahu 22:2), a noisy city, a joyous town; בְּרֹאשׁ הֹֽמִיּוֹת תִּקְרָא (Mishlei 1:21), she calls at the head of the noisy streets; and מַדּוּעַ קֽוֹל־הַקִּרְיָה הוֹמָֽה (Melachim I 1:41), why is the sound of the city in an uproar.

כַּֽהֲמוֹת יַמִּים (Yeshayahu 17:12), like the roaring of seas; on other patterns הֶמְיַת נְבָלֶיךָ (Yeshayahu 14:11), the sound of your harps, and הֲמוֹן שִׁירָיִךְ (Amos 5:23), the noise of your songs. Their sense, he says, is set out under the root הִים, in its second sense.

more.h: A son's moaning, on one reading
more.t: Some explain וְאֶל־ הֲמִיתוֹ אַל־תִּשָּׂא נַפְשֶֽׁךָ (Mishlei 19:18), and to his moaning do not lift your soul, from this root. On that reading the pasuk says: chasten your son, and if he weeps and moans do not set your heart on him and do not let your soul pity him, this being the way of rebuke; and הֲמִיתוֹ, his moaning, comes from הָמָה as בְּכִיתוֹ, his weeping, comes from בָּכָה.

Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar wrote that וְלֹֽא מֵהֱמֵהֶם (Yechezkel 7:11), and none of their clamour, is of this root and this sense, a noun הָמֶה on the pattern of קָשֶׁה, hard, and יָפֶה, fair, which with the plural suffix gives המהם, as one would say קשהם, יפהם. Yonasan renders it וְלָא מִבְּנֵיהוֹן, and not of their sons.

מלל.sense: To speak or utter, with the noun מִלָּה, a word; by figure, to speak with the feet by signs. In another sense מְלִילֹת, ears of grain, rubbed out by hand.

more.t: מִי מִלֵּל לְאַבְרָהָם (Bereishis 21:7), who would have said to Avraham; בָּרוּר מִלֵּֽלוּ (Iyov 33:3), they uttered it clearly; and מִי יְמַלֵּל גְּבוּרוֹת (Tehillim 106:2), who can utter the mighty acts of Hashem. The Targum of וַיְדַבֵּר, and he spoke, is וּמַלִּיל.

אֵין מִלָּה בִּלְשׁוֹנִי (Tehillim 139:4), there is no word on my tongue. The plural in the masculine is הַֽלְהוֹכַח מִלִּים תַּחְשֹׁבוּ (Iyov 6:26), do you think to reprove with words, and אַחְבִּירָה עֲלֵיכֶם בְּמִלִּים (Iyov 16:4), I would string words together against you; and at times it comes with a nun, אֲנִי אֲשִֽׁיבְךָ מִלִּין (Iyov 35:4), I will answer you with words, and הֲלֹא־אֹזֶן מִלִּין תִּבְחָן (Iyov 12:11), does not the ear test words.

more.h: Speech, or a root of its own
more.t: Some explain קוֹל הֲמֻלָּה (Yechezkel 1:24) as though הֲמֻלָּה were מלה, a word, so that it is a sound of speech; and that is the Targum's view, which rendered it קָל מִלוּלֵיהֶן, the sound of their speech. Radak has already written it as a root of its own, under הָמַל.

From this sense, by way of figure, the light form gives מֹלֵל בְּרַגְלָו (Mishlei 6:13), he speaks with his feet, like קֹרֵץ בְּעֵינָו, he winks with his eyes, in the same pasuk: it is as though he speaks with his feet when he makes signs with them.

In another sense, וְקָֽטַפְתָּ מְלִילֹת בְּיָדֶךָ (Devarim 23:26), and you may pluck ears with your hand. The sense of מלילה, rubbing out ears, is known from the words of Chazal (Beitzah 12b): one who rubs out ears on erev Shabbos blows them the next day from one hand to the other and eats; and they said there too that one may rub out ears and crush pulse on Yom Tov.

רקם.sense: Embroidery: a garment worked in many colours, whether in the weaving or with the needle.

more.t: מַֽעֲשֵׂה רֹקֵֽם (Shemos 26:36), the work of an embroiderer; the noun is שְׁלַל צְבָעִים רִקְמָה (Shoftim 5:30), spoil of dyed stuffs, embroidered; and the plural לִרְקָמוֹת תּוּבַל (Tehillim 45:15), she is led in embroidered robes. Work of garments made of many colours, in the weaving or with the needle, is what is called רִקְמָה, embroidery.

more.h: Why the word comes in twos
more.t: צֶבַע רִקְמָתַיִם (Shoftim 5:30), dyed stuff of double embroidery, stands in the form of two because it is embroidered on two faces, this side and that alike, or in two manners after the way of embroidery. So too the pasuk speaks of the colours of the plumage, הַנּוֹצָה אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ הָֽרִקְמָה (Yechezkel 17:3), the plumage that had the embroidery.

more.h: A man embroidered in the womb
more.t: רֻקַּמְתִּי בְּֽתַחְתִּיּוֹת אָֽרֶץ (Tehillim 139:15), I was embroidered in the lowest parts of the earth: the pasuk likens the forming of a man, in sinews and bones and flesh and skin, to the work of embroidery, and likens his mother's womb to the lowest parts of the earth, a place hidden and dark.

ערשֹ.sense: A bed; the Targum's word for מטה, a bed, is עַרְסָא.

more.t: הִנֵּה עַרְשׂוֹ עֶרֶשׂ בַּרְזֶל (Devarim 3:11), his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; עַל־ עֶרֶשׂ דְּוָי (Tehillim 41:4), on a bed of sickness; אַף־ עַרְשֵׂנוּ רַֽעֲנָנָֽה (Shir HaShirim 1:16), our couch too is fresh and green; and the plural in the feminine, וּסְרֻחִים עַל־ עַרְשׂוֹתָם (Amos 6:4), sprawling on their couches. The Targum of מטה, a bed, is עַרְסָא.

עוג.sense: The עֻגָה, a cake baked on the coals, and the verb of baking it.

more.t: תְּעֻגֶנָה לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם (Yechezkel 4:12), you shall bake it before their eyes. The right form is תעוגנה with a dagesh in the nun, since the separate form is תָּעוּג אותה, you shall bake it, and the quiescent letter came in place of the dagesh. Someone has said that כִּֽי־ תִקְרֶאנָה מִלְחָמָה (Shemos 1:10), when war befalls, comes the same way, since it should have been תקראנה with a dagesh, the feminine suffix pointing at the city: that is, when war befalls the city. תעוגנה can also be read of the women, as the ones who bake. The word is of baking the cake and not of kneading it, since they dry cattle dung and kindle it and bake with it.

הָיָה עֻגָה בְּלִי הֲפוּכָֽה (Hoshea 7:8), he has become a cake not turned: a cake baked on the coals and not turned is baked on one side only and is not fit to eat. So was Ephraim, who was hasty in his counsel and did not turn it over and consider whether it was sound.

וְעֻגַת שְׂעֹרִים תֹּֽאֽכֲלֶנָּה (Yechezkel 4:12), a barley cake you shall eat, and עֻגַת רְצָפִים (Melachim I 19:6), a cake baked on coals. Another form is אִם־יֶשׁ־לִי מָעוֹג (Melachim I 17:12), if I have a cake; of these he says only that their sense is known.

Some have explained בְּחַנְפֵי לַֽעֲגֵי מָעוֹג (Tehillim 35:16) in this sense, with flatterers who mock for a cake. In Radak's own view it is a sense of mockery and idle words: with flatterers who mock in idle talk. He finds the like in the words of Chazal (Sanhedrin 90a), where Abba Shaul says: also one who pronounces the Name by its letters; and in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 101b) it was taught, ובגבולין ובלשון עגה, in the provinces and in a tongue of aggah. That is, if he mentions the Name in the provinces even at need, and in a tongue of mockery and idle words even in Yerushalayim, it is of this that Abba Shaul said he has no share in the World to Come.

עצד.sense: The מַֽעֲצָד, a craftsman's tool: the large axe, or one of two small tools, since the Mishnah and a baraisa use the word differently.

more.t: חָרַשׁ בַּרְזֶל מַֽעֲצָד (Yeshayahu 44:12), the ironsmith with his maatzad, and מַֽעֲשֵׂה יְדֵי־חָרָשׁ בַּֽמַּֽעֲצָֽד (Yirmiyahu 10:3), the work of a craftsman's hands with the maatzad. It is the קרדום, the axe, or else one of two smaller tools he names in his own vernacular.

What forced him to the two is what he found of the word in Chazal. The Mishnah (Bava Kama 10:10) has that what the craftsman brings out with a מעצד is his own and what he brings out with a כשיל is the householder's; on its reckoning the מעצד is the small tool, one of the two he names, both of them small, and the כשיל is the large axe. The Baraisa (Bava Kama 119b) has that what the craftsman brings out with a מעצד, and what is cut off with a saw, are the householder's; it did not mention the כשיל at all, because it called that tool a מעצד, so that on its reckoning the מעצד is the large axe.
What they said further (Arachin 23b), that if he was a craftsman they give him two מעצדין, is the large and the small, as Radak explained above.

בוס.sense: To trample and to befoul, as in mire or in blood; some of its forms he reads as though they were the word for despising.
