more.t: תָּבוּס נֹפֶת (Mishlei 27:7), spurns the honeycomb, which he takes as כמו תבוז, as though it were the word for spurning; יָבוּס צָרֵֽינוּ (Tehillim 60:14), He will tread down our foes; and וְעַל־הָרַי אֲבוּסֶנּוּ (Yeshayahu 14:25), and on My mountains I will trample him. So too כְּפֶגֶר מוּבָֽס (Yeshayahu 14:19), like a despised carcass, which he reads as כמו מובז, as though it were the word for one despised. Another noun is כִּי יוֹם מְהוּמָה וּמְבוּסָה (Yeshayahu 22:5), for it is a day of tumult and treading down.

וּמֵֽאֱלֹהִים הָֽיְתָה תְּבוּסַת אֲחַזְיָהוּ לָבוֹא אֶל־יוֹרָם (Divrei HaYamim II 22:7), and from Hashem was the treading down of Achazyahu, in coming to Yoram: He put it in his heart to go to Yoram, and in that going was his treading down, for Yehu did not deal with him as with a king but despised him and said to his servants גַּם־אֹתוֹ הַכֻּהוּ אֶל־הַמֶּרְכָּבָה (Melachim II 9:27), smite him too, in the chariot.

In the doubled form, בּֽוֹסְסוּ מִקְדָּשֶֽׁךָ (Yeshayahu 63:18), they have trodden down Your Mikdash, and בֹּֽסְסוּ אֶת־חֶלְקָתִי (Yirmiyahu 12:10), they have trodden my portion. These may be כמו בזזו, as though the word were the one for plundering, or they are of treading and befouling, and that, he says, is the right one.

בּוֹסִים בְּטִיט חוּצוֹת (Zecharyah 10:5) is an adjective of the light form, on the pattern of טוֹבִים, good, and בּוֹשִׁים, ashamed, and means befouled and trodden in the mire of the streets: the nations, who were as mighty men, will be trodden in the mire of the streets. Or בוסים is an adjective that takes an object, and the sense is that Israel will be as mighty men though they are weak, as it says after, וְהָיוּ כְגִבּוֹר אֶפְרַיִם (Zecharyah 10:7), and Ephraim shall be as a mighty man: they will be treading and trampling their enemies in the mire of the streets in war, since Hashem is with them, and the nations, who are the riders of horses, will be put to shame.

The reflexive is מִתְבּוֹסֶסֶת בְּדָמָיִךְ (Yechezkel 16:6), befouled in your blood. His father writes that יַעַן בּֽוֹשַׁסְכֶם עַל־דָּל (Amos 5:11), because you tread upon the poor, is of this root and this sense, with the shin interchanging with the samech, as וּבוֹלֵס שִׁקְמִֽים (Amos 7:14) stands for בולש, one who searches out sycamore figs, the Targum of וַיְחַפֵּשׂ, and he searched, being וּבְלַשׁ; and בּוֹשַׁסְכֶם would be of the four-letter form, on the pattern of כּוֹנַנְכֶם, your establishing.

סרף.sense: A man's mother's brother, where the דּוֹד is his father's brother; others take the word from burning instead.

more.t: On וּנְשָׂאוֹ דּוֹדוֹ וּמְסָרְפוֹ (Amos 6:10), his uncle and his mesarfo shall carry him, he says that the מְסָרְפוֹ is his mother's brother, since the דּוֹד is his father's brother. Some explain it from שריפה, burning. What that comes to, Radak says, is the one who burned him, to bring the bones out of the house. Yonasan renders it וְיִטְלִנֵיהּ קְרִיבֵיהּ מִיְקֵידָא, his kinsman shall take him up out of the burning.

טבל.sense: To dip, which he likens to washing with a difference: washing is to clean a thing, dipping is at times to touch it, in part or whole, to something wet.

more.t: וְטָבַל הַכֹּהֵן (Vayikra 4:6), the kohen shall dip; וַיִּטְבְּלוּ אֶת־הַכֻּתֹּנֶת בַּדָּֽם (Bereishis 37:31), they dipped the coat in the blood; וְטָבַלְתְּ פִּתֵּךְ בַּחֹמֶץ (Rus 2:14), dip your morsel in the vinegar; וְטֹבֵל בַּשֶּׁמֶן רַגְלֽוֹ (Devarim 33:24), dipping his foot in oil; and וַיֵּרֶד וַיִּטְבֹּל בַּיַּרְדֵּן שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים (Melachim II 5:14), he went down and immersed in the Yarden seven times. In the passive, נִטְבְּלוּ בִּקְצֵה הַמָּיִם (Yehoshua 3:15), they were dipped at the edge of the water.

All of them are like washing, רחיצה, in sense, but there is a difference between them: washing is to clean the thing, while dipping is at times the touching of a thing to something wet, part of it or the whole of it.

more.h: Dipped in the pit, dipped in dye
more.t: By way of figure, אָז בַּשַּׁחַת תִּטְבְּלֵנִי (Iyov 9:31), then You would dip me in the pit: that is, even had I washed in snow water, You would wash me in the pit, meaning that I would not be saved from the pit. סְרוּחֵי טְבוּלִים בְּרָאשֵׁיהֶם (Yechezkel 23:15), hanging loose and dipped, upon their heads, speaks of the turbans on their heads, which hang long and loose behind them, טְבוּלִים meaning that the turbans are dipped in dye.

ידה.sense: To cast. In another sense, to praise and give thanks, with תּוֹדָה, thanksgiving, and the name יְהוּדָה taken from it. In another, to confess.

more.t: יְדוּ אֵלֶיהָ (Yirmiyahu 50:14) is explained as השליכו, cast at her. Rabbi Yehudah said that גָּמוּל יָדוֹ הָדָה (Yeshayahu 11:8), the weaned child will cast forth his hand, is from this root, the yud exchanged for a heh. In the heavy form, לְיַדּוֹת אֶת קַרְנוֹת הַגּוֹיִם (Zecharyah 2:4), to cast down the horns of the nations, and וַיַּדּוּ אֶבֶן בִּי (Eichah 3:53), they cast a stone at me, whose proper form is וַיְיַּדּוּ. Radak's father holds that it is of the added heavy form, its proper form being וְיַיְּדּוּ.

The heavy form with the added letter is in another sense, praise and thanksgiving: הוֹדִינוּ לְּךָ (Tehillim 75:2), we give thanks to You; גַּם אֲנִי אוֹדְךָ בִכְלִי נֶבֶל (Tehillim 71:22), I too will thank You with the harp; יוֹדוּ שִׁמְךָ גָּדוֹל וְנוֹרָא (Tehillim 99:3), let them praise Your name, great and awesome; and עַל כֵּן עַמִּים יְהוֹדֻךָ (Tehillim 45:18), therefore peoples will praise You. Another noun form is תּוֹדָה וְקוֹל זִמְרָה (Yeshayahu 51:3), thanksgiving and the sound of song.

more.h: Yehudah, and why all Israel are Jews
more.t: The name is taken from it: עַל כֵּן קָרְאָה שְׁמוֹ יְהוּדָה (Bereishis 29:35), therefore she called his name Yehudah. Since the mainstay of Israel's kingship and their strong horn was Yehudah, all Israel were called יהודים, Jews: וְאֶל הַיְּהוּדִים כִּכְתָבָם (Esther 8:9), and to the Jews in their own script, and וְהֶחֱזִיקוּ בִּכְנַף אִישׁ יְהוּדִי (Zecharyah 8:23), they will take hold of the corner of a Jew's garment. The holy tongue was named for it too, וְאַל תְּדַבֵּר אֵלֵינוּ יְהוּדִית (Yeshayahu 36:11), do not speak to us in Yehudis; and a verb was built from it for turning from the nations to the faith of the Jews, וְרַבִּים מֵעַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ מִתְיַהֲדִים (Esther 8:17), and many of the peoples of the land became Jews.

Another sense is confession: וּמוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָם (Mishlei 28:13), one who confesses and forsakes will be shown mercy, and וְגַם אֲנִי אוֹדֶךָּ (Iyov 40:14), and I too will acknowledge you, though אודך there may be of the second sense. יוֹדוּךָ אַחֶיךָ (Bereishis 49:8), your brothers will acknowledge you, is: they will acknowledge to you that you are fit to rule over them. The reflexive is וְהִתְוַדָּה אֲשֶׁר חָטָא עָלֶיהָ (Vayikra 5:5), he shall confess that in which he sinned, and וְהִתְוַדּוּ אֶת חַטָּאתָם אֲשֶׁר עָשׂוּ (Bamidbar 5:7), they shall confess their sin that they did. The sense of confession is known.

From this sense is זְבַח לֵאלֹהִים תּוֹדָה (Tehillim 50:14), offer a todah to Hashem: the offering over which a man confesses his sins is called תּוֹדָה. It did not carry the law of a chatas or an asham, only that of shelamim, and the todah was eaten only for a day and a night. Though it came upon sins it was neither chatas nor asham, since those come for one particular sin, while a man brought this offering for all his sins together, when he wished to confess and return to the good way. Some say a man brought it when a nes was done for him, and that it is called תּוֹדָה because he was thanking Hashem for the nes done for him. The Torah's words are אִם עַל תּוֹדָה יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ (Vayikra 7:12), if he offers it for a todah.

שְׁתֵּי תוֹדֹת גְּדוֹלֹת (Nechemiah 12:31), two great todos, are two todah breads of chametz, as it is written, עַל חַלֹּת לֶחֶם חָמֵץ יַקְרִיב קָרְבָּנוֹ (Vayikra 7:13), with loaves of chametz bread he shall bring his offering. They are called great because of the matzah there were three kinds and of the chametz only one, so that the one kind of chametz stands against the three kinds of matzah. Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Yonah put שְׁתֵּי תוֹדֹת גְּדוֹלֹת and וְהַתּוֹדָה הַשֵּׁנִית (Nechemiah 12:38), and the second todah, in another sense, and Rabbi Yonah explained them as a term of assembly, a congregation and congregations. Chazal explained them as Radak has written: the Mishnah in the second perek of Shevuos says that the city and the azaros are added to only with a beis din of seventy-one, with two todos and with song, the beis din walking and the two todos after them, the inner one eaten and the outer burned; and the Gemara there teaches that the two todos spoken of are in their bread and not in their flesh, from the pasuk ואעמידה שתי תודות גדולות, and I set up two great todos.

חמשׁ.sense: Five, and in the larger count fifty; the fifth part, and taking it; and חֲמֻשִׁים, girded with weapons at the fifth rib.

more.t: וּמִקְצֵה אֶחָיו לָקַח חֲמִשָּׁה אֲנָשִׁים (Bereishis 47:2), from among his brothers he took five men, and in the feminine וְחָמֵשׁ צֹאן (Shmuel I 25:18), and five sheep. The larger number is שַׂר־ חֲמִשִּׁים וַֽחֲמִשָּׁיו (Melachim II 1:9), a captain of fifty and his fifty, and וְאֶת־ חֲמִשֶּׁיךָ (Melachim II 1:12), and your fifty, which he glosses חמשים שלך, the fifty that are yours.

וַֽחֲמֻשִׁים עָלוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shemos 13:18), and the Children of Yisrael went up girded: חגורי חומש בכלי זין, girded at the chomesh with weapons, which is the fifth rib. So Chazal explained (Sanhedrin 49a) on וַיַּכֵּהוּ אַבְנֵר בְּאַֽחֲרֵי הַֽחֲנִית אֶל־ הַחֹמֶשׁ (Shmuel II 2:23), and Avner struck him with the back of the spear at the chomesh, where Rabbi Yochanan said it is the fifth rib, the place where the gall and the liver hang. Some explain וַֽחֲמֻשִּׁים that each of them carried five weapons, and Radak says the first is right.

וְחִמֵּשׁ אֶת־אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם (Bereishis 41:34) is that he shall take the fifth of the land of Mitzrayim. On וְאֶת־ חֲמִֽישִׁתוֹ יוֹסֵף עָלָיו (Vayikra 5:16), and he shall add its fifth to it, Chazal explained (Bava Metzia 54a) חומשיה מלבר, its fifth is from outside; and that is a fifth of the principal. On וַֽחֲמִֽשִׁתָיו יֹסֵף עָלָיו (Vayikra 5:24), and he shall add its fifths to it, Chazal expounded (Bava Kama 108a) that many fifths may come upon one principal. Though by the rule of grammar it should be חֲמִישִׁיּוֹתָיו, in the feminine plural, we find the masculine plural alone in וַֽאֲחוֹתַיִךְ סְדֹם וּבְנוֹתֶיהָ (Yechezkel 16:55), and your sisters, Sedom and her daughters, and in נִלְאֵית בְּרֹב עֲצָתָיִךְ (Yeshayahu 47:13), you are wearied by your many counsels; or חמישיתיו may be in the masculine.

הָאַיִל מְזוּזוֹת חֲמִשִֽׁית (Melachim I 6:31), the lintel and doorposts of five: the doorposts and the lintel were of five sides, one outside the other, each set in from the next, as ornamented doorways are made today. Yonasan rendered it אֵלָהִי וְסִפּוֹהִי מְטַקְסִין, its lintel and its posts arrayed, from the sense of וַֽחֲמֻשִׁים עָלוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל, and the Children of Yisrael went up arrayed, which is a sense of readiness and arraying.

הרר.sense: A mountain: the full form of the word is הֶרֶר, and the common הַר is that same word with the doubled letter fallen away.

more.t: הֶעֱמַדְתָּה לְֽהַֽרְרִי עֹז (Tehillim 30:8), You set my mountain firm, and בְּהַֽרֲרָם שֵׂעִיר (Bereishis 14:6), in their mountain, Seir; in some sefarim the resh there has a chataf patach and in some a bare sheva. The plural of the full form is הֲרָרִים. The construct is כְּֽהַרְרֵי ־אֵל (Tehillim 36:7), like the mountains of Kel, יְסוּדָתוֹ בְּהַרְרֵי ־קֹֽדֶשׁ (Tehillim 87:1), His foundation is in the holy mountains, and וּמֵֽהֲרָרֶיהָ תַּחְצֹב נְחֽשֶׁת (Devarim 8:9), out of its mountains you will hew copper; the adjective is הֲרָרִי בַּשָּׂדֶה (Yirmiyahu 17:3), the one on the mountain in the field. With a heh added, הֶרָה נָּֽסוּ (Bereishis 14:10), they fled to the mountain. The plural of הַר is הָרִים, mountains, which would take a dagesh were it not for the resh; and the word is spoken of in the feminine, שְׁמָמָה תִֽהְיֶה הַר ־שֵׂעִיר (Yechezkel 35:15), Har Seir shall be a desolation.
הַרְכֶם צִפּֽוֹר (Tehillim 11:1) he reads as הר שלכם, your mountain; some explain that it is two words, הר and כם, the כם standing for כמו: flee to a mountain like a bird.
Some explain בְּהַֽרֲרָם שֵׂעִיר, in their mountain, Seir, as an infinitive of the doubled form. One can object to them from the patach of the heh.

Some take from this הָרוֹת הַגִּלְעָד (Amos 1:13), the mountain cities of Gilad, and וְהָרֹֽתֵיהֶם תְּבַקֵּֽעַ (Melachim II 8:12), and you will breach their mountain cities; if these words are of this root and this sense, they mean the cities fortified and set high in the mountains. So too הִֽנְנִי אֵלֶיךָ הַר הַמַּשְׁחִית (Yirmiyahu 51:25), behold, I am against you, destroying mountain, where the mountain is a fortified city, since Bavel is nothing but a plain, and Targum Yonasan rendered it כְּרַכָּא מְחַבְּלָא, the destroying city.

הוד.sense: Strength and majesty, הכח וההדר, which he gives as the sense of all its uses.

more.t: הוֹד וְהָדָר לָבָשְׁתָּ (Tehillim 104:1), You have put on majesty and glory; הוֹדוֹ עַל־אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם (Tehillim 148:13), His majesty is over earth and heaven; הוֹד נַחְרוֹ אֵימָה (Iyov 39:20), the majesty of his snorting is terror; וְלֹא־נָתְנוּ עָלָיו הוֹד מַלְכוּת (Daniel 11:21), and they did not give him the majesty of kingship; כְּסוּס הוֹדוֹ בַּמִּלְחָמָה (Zechariah 10:3), like his majestic horse in battle; וְהוּא־יִשָּׂא הוֹד וְיָשַׁב וּמָשַׁל (Zechariah 6:13), and he shall bear majesty, and sit and rule; וְנָתַתָּה מֵהוֹדְךָ עָלָיו (Bamidbar 27:20), and you shall put of your majesty upon him; הוֹי אָדוֹן וְהוֹי הֹדֹה (Yirmiyahu 22:18), alas, lord, and alas, his majesty; וִיהִי כַזַּיִת הוֹדוֹ (Hoshea 14:7), and his majesty shall be as the olive tree. The sense of all of them is strength and majesty. Rabbi Yonah brought וְלֹא־הֵד הָרִים (Yechezkel 7:7) into this sense as well, which would make it mean, and not the majesty of the mountains; Radak has already mentioned it under the root הָדַד.

ראשׁ.sense: The head. Also the top of a hill, a sum, the principal of a debt, and the beginning or first; and, the head being the body's choicest part, the choicest and the chief.

more.t: אֶת־ הָרֹאשׁ (Vayikra 1:8), the head, and רֹאשִׁי רֹאשִׁי (Melachim II 4:19), my head, my head, of which he says only that it is known. Also יָשׁוּב עֲמָלוֹ בְרֹאשׁוֹ (Tehillim 7:17), his mischief returns on his own head. וַיַּקַּף רֹאשׁ וּתְלָאָֽה (Eichah 3:5) he reads as He compassed my head, and with weariness He compassed me; some take the word there as in רֹאשׁ וְלַֽעֲנָֽה (Devarim 29:17), gall and wormwood; and he says he will write of it again under its own root. On וְהָיָה לְאַרְבָּעָה רָאשִֽׁים (Bereishis 2:10), and it became four heads, he says that things divided out of one are called ראשים, each being a head to itself once they have parted, a usage he says is known in other tongues too; Rabbi Yonah made them great rivers, and Radak holds there is no need for that. כִּי תִשָּׂא אֶת־ רֹאשׁ בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shemos 30:12), when you take the head of the children of Yisrael, is their sum, and וְטִמֵּא רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ (Bamidbar 6:9), and he defiles the head of his nezirus, is the hair of the head of his nezirus.

וַיְהִי דָוִד בָּא עַד־ הָרֹאשׁ (Shmuel II 15:32), and David was coming to the top, is the top of the hill where David used to bow and daven, and so Targum Yonasan renders it, עַד רֵישׁ טוּרַיָא, to the top of the mountains. It is said to be Har HaZeisim, from which he could look at the Beis HaMikdash, and that is what the pasuk means by David going up the ascent of the olives. Though the Beis HaMikdash did not stand then, and its own place was not yet known, Har HaMoriah was known by tradition; which spot on it was not known until Gad told David to build a mizbeach at the threshing floor of Aravnah the Yevusi.

Because the head is the choicest part of the body, the word is used of the pick of men and their chief, and of the best of the spices: בְּשָׂמִים רֹאשׁ (Shemos 30:23), which he reads as take spices, and of them take the chief and choicest. So too רֵאשִׁית שְׁמָנִים יִמְשָׁחוּ (Amos 6:6), they anoint themselves with the choicest of oils. רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק (Bamidbar 24:20), Amalek is the reishis of the nations, he reads as the Targum renders it; Rabbi Yonah reads it as the greatest and most considerable of them. Radak adds that רֵאשִׁית הַחֵרֶם (Shmuel I 15:21), the reishis of the devoted spoil, may be of the same kind, the choicest of it.

With the plural suffix the cholam turns to kamatz, רָֽאשֵׁיכֶם שִׁבְטֵיכֶם (Devarim 29:9), your heads, your tribes, and it also comes with the cholam, בְּכָל־ רֹאשָׁיו קָרְחָה (Yeshayahu 15:2), on all its heads baldness. Some books write וַֽחֲבָלִים בְּרֹאשֵׁנוּ (Melachim I 20:31), and ropes on our heads, full, with the yud of the plural, and the Mesorah there has two, one full and one defective; other books have it defective, and the Mesorah there has two and both defective, counting דָּמוֹ בְרֹאשֵׁנוּ (Yehoshua 2:19), his blood on our heads, and Rabbi Yonah too wrote that both are defective. The alef shows itself in מַרְֽאֲשׁוֹתֵיכֶם (Yirmiyahu 13:18), which Radak glosses as your greatness; in אֲשֶׁר־שָׂם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָיו (Bereishis 28:18), which he had set under his head, as he glosses the word; and מֵרַֽאֲשֹׁתֵי שָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 26:12), from by Shaul's head, comes without the added mem, for its mem is the one that means from, as its tzere shows.

וְשִׁלַּם אֹתוֹ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ (Vayikra 5:24), and he shall repay it in its ראש: the principal of a thing is called its ראש, capital in the vernacular, because it is the head and beginning of the thing and the profit comes upon it afterwards. רֹֽאשׁ ־דְּבָרְךָ אֱמֶת (Tehillim 119:160), the beginning of Your word is truth; רִֽאשֹׁנָה יִסָּֽעוּ (Bamidbar 2:9), at the first they shall travel; וַתְּהִי רֵאשִׁית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ בָּבֶל (Bereishis 10:10), the beginning of his kingdom was Bavel. בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים (Bereishis 1:1), he says, is not in the construct, and reads: at the first Hashem created the heavens and the earth, and after that what came out of them, and only then does the Torah tell that at the beginning of the earth's making it was tohu vavohu.

more.h: First in rank, first in time
more.t: הַיּשְׁבִים רִאשֹׁנָה (Esther 1:14), who sat first, is first in standing, near the king, and so מִֽיכָאֵל אַחַד הַשָּׂרִים הָֽרִאשֹׁנִים (Daniel 10:13), Michael, one of the first princes, is one of the great in rank. בָּֽרִאשׁוֹן בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ (Yechezkel 29:17), in the first, on the first of the month, is Nisan, the first of the months; but אַךְ בַּיּוֹם הָֽרִאשׁוֹן תַּשְׁבִּיתוּ שְּׂאֹר (Shemos 12:15), but on the first day you shall put away leaven, he reads as the day before it, the fourteenth, which comes before the seven days of matzah. It can also be read plainly, that on the first day the leaven be already put away, as with וַיְכַל אֱלֹהִים בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי (Bereishis 2:2), and Hashem finished on the seventh day. בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ (Yechezkel 40:1), at the head of the year, on the tenth of the month, he takes as the seventh month, which is the head of the year, on its tenth, Yom Kippur; Chazal (Arachin 12a) take the tenth day itself to be called Rosh Hashanah and the year to have been a yovel, for which year has its Rosh Hashanah on the tenth if not the yovel. On טוֹב אַֽחֲרִית דָּבָר מֵרֵֽאשִׁיתוֹ (Koheles 7:8), good is the end of a thing from its beginning, his father explains that the end of a thing is good when a man looks from its beginning to see what its end will be, or else that the good lies in the end, as Chazal say of the man who sees what is to be born.

ארשֹ.sense: To betroth; of אֲשֶׁר אֵרַשׂ אִשָּׁה, who has betrothed a woman, and its passive he says only ענינו ידוע, its sense is known.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר אֵרַשׂ אִשָּׁה וְלֹא לְקָחָהּ (Devarim 20:7), who has betrothed a woman and not taken her; and in the passive, אֲשֶׁר לֹֽא־ אֹרָשָׂה (Shemos 22:15), who was not betrothed, and הַֽנַּֽעֲרָ הַמְאֹרָשָׂה (Devarim 22:25), the betrothed girl. Of all of them he says only ענינו ידוע, its sense is known.

ארשׁ.sense: The utterance of the lips: אֲרֶשֶׁת, which he glosses מבטא שפתיו, the utterance of his lips.

more.t: וַֽאֲרֶשֶׁת שְׂפָתָיו בַּל־מָנַעְתָּ (Tehillim 21:3), and the utterance of his lips You did not withhold, which he glosses מבטא שפתיו, the utterance of his lips.

ציה.sense: צִי is a ship, and צִיִּים ships; צִיָּה is drought and wilderness, and צִיִּים are also the beasts, or the nations, that dwell in it.

more.t: וְצִי אַדִּיר לֹא יַעַבְרֶֽנּוּ (Yeshayahu 33:21), and no mighty ship shall pass it. In the plural, וְצִים מִיַּד כִּתִּים (Bamidbar 24:24), and ships from the side of Kittim, and יֵֽצְאוּ מַלְאָכִים מִלְּפָנַי בַּצִּים (Yechezkel 30:9), messengers shall go out from before Me in ships, where the yud is the plural's and the root's yud has fallen away; with the yud shown, אַשּׁוּר יְסָדָהּ לְצִיִּים (Yeshayahu 23:13), Ashur founded it for ships. Their sense is a ship, ships.

צִיָּה גַם־חֹם (Iyov 24:19), drought and heat, and לַמְרוֹת עֶלְיוֹן בַּצִּיָּֽה (Tehillim 78:17), to rebel against the Most High in the parched land. The feminine plural הָלְכוּ בַּצִּיּוֹת נָהָֽר (Tehillim 105:41), it went in the dry places a river, he reads as the water going through the parched place and the wilderness like a river. Another pattern is כְּחֹרֶב בְּצָיוֹן (Yeshayahu 25:5), as heat in a dry place, on the weight of רָצוֹן; all of them are drought and wilderness.

וְרָֽבְצוּ־שָׁם צִיִּים (Yeshayahu 13:21), and צִיִּים shall lie down there, and וּפָֽגְשׁוּ צִיִּים (Yeshayahu 34:14), and צִיִּים shall meet, are the beasts that dwell in the ציה, and Targum Yonasan renders them תַּמְוָן. לְפָנָיו יִכְרְעוּ צִיִּים (Tehillim 72:9), before him צִיִּים shall bow, Radak takes as the nations that dwell in the wilderness, or else from the first sense, the men of the ships, as the next pasuk names the kings of Tarshish.

Rabbi Moshe HaKohen takes לְעַם לְצִיִּֽים (Tehillim 74:14), to the people, to the צִיִּים, from the ships, its lamed being like the lamed of לְעַבְדְּךָ לְיַֽעֲקֹב (Bereishis 32:19), to your servant, to Yaakov, so that it means to the men of the ships. Ibn Ezra reads it of those who dwell in the wilderness: though the creature is in the sea and its strength is great, You give it as food to the dwellers of the desert.

שֹרר.sense: To rule and be master; and to make oneself a prince over others.

more.t: לִהְיוֹת כָּל־אִישׁ שׂרֵר בְּבֵיתוֹ (Esther 1:22), that every man be master in his own house, and the reflexive כִּֽי־ תִשְׂתָּרֵר עָלֵינוּ גַּם־ הִשְׂתָּרֵֽר (Bamidbar 16:13), that you make yourself a prince over us, a prince indeed. He allows that וַיָּשַׂר אֶל־מַלְאָךְ (Hoshea 12:5), and he was master over an angel, and בִּי שָׂרִים יָשׂרוּ (Mishlei 8:16), by me princes rule, may belong here, though he has already written of them under the root שֹוֹר; but וַיָּשַׂר בַּמְּגֵרָה (Divrei HaYamim I 20:3), and he sawed them with the saw, and אִם־יִתְגַּדֵּל הַמַּשּׂוֹר (Yeshayahu 10:15), shall the saw vaunt itself, he wrote under נָשַֹר, which he says is truly their root.

שׁרר.sense: The navel. In another sense, בִּשְׁרִרוּת לִבִּי is the looking of my heart and my thoughts; some explain it as strength.

more.t: שָׁרְרֵךְ אַגַּן הַסַּהַר (Shir HaShirim 7:3), your navel a round goblet; לֹֽא־כָרַּת שָׁרֵךְ (Yechezkel 16:4), your navel was not cut, where the resh takes a dagesh in place of the doubling that is missing; and in another pattern בִּשְׁרִירֵי בִטְנֽוֹ (Iyov 40:16), in the navel of his belly, the word there being the navel.

כִּי בִּשְׁרִרוּת לִבִּי אֵלֵךְ (Devarim 29:18), for I will go in the looking of my heart, where the sense is the looking of my heart and my thoughts. With it go לְמַעַן שׁוֹרְרָי (Tehillim 5:9), because of those who watch me, and יָשֹׁר עַל־אֲנָשִׁים (Iyov 33:27), he looks upon men, though he has written those at the root שׁוּר as well, there being nothing to decide between the two roots. Some explain בִּשְׁרִרוּת as strength, from the sense of שריר וקים, valid and standing, in the words of Chazal (Bava Basra 102a).

נוף.sense: Melting and sprinkling, as with spices, and נֹפֶת, a dripping; in another sense, waving to and fro, as a wave offering, a hand or a sieve; and נוֹף, a district.

more.t: נַפְתִּי מִשְׁכָּבִי (Mishlei 7:17), I have sprinkled my bed, is ענין ההתכה והזלוף בבשמים, melting and sprinkling with spices. The noun is נֹפֶת תִּטֹּפְנָה שִׂפְתוֹתַיִךְ כַּלָּה (Shir HaShirim 4:11), your lips, O bride, drip נֹפֶת, and וְנֹפֶת צוּפִֽים (Tehillim 19:11), and the dripping of the honeycombs, on the pattern of בֹּשֶׁת, shame, from בּוּשׁ, to be ashamed. Where it stands without צופים, honeycombs, or בשמים, spices, joined to it, it is elliptical, and what is left out is understood from elsewhere. Where the verb takes an object, גֶּשֶׁם נְדָבוֹת תָּנִיף אֱלֹהִים (Tehillim 68:10), a rain of bounty You shed, Elokim, that is, You make it flow and drip.

הֵנִיף אַֽהֲרֹן תְּנוּפָה (Vayikra 9:21), Aharon waved a wave offering. Chazal explain (Menachos 61a) that he would carry it forward and bring it back, and that waving is movement this way and that, while the תרומה, the raising, was a lifting upward, raising and lowering, and that is what it says, אֲשֶׁר הוּנַף וַֽאֲשֶׁר הוּרָם (Shemos 29:27), what was waved and what was raised: the waving is carrying forward and back, the raising is lifting up and down.

more.h: Waving the hand, and the call to war
more.t: וְהֵנִיף יָדוֹ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם וְאָסַף הַמְּצֹרָֽע (Melachim II 5:11), he will wave his hand toward the place and gather in the metzora, in the manner of those who whisper over a wound and wave their hand over it this way and that. אִם־יִתְגַּדֵּל הַמַּשּׂוֹר עַל־ מְנִיפוֹ (Yeshayahu 10:15), shall the saw magnify itself over the one who waves it, is said because the one who cuts with a saw waves it back and forth. יְנֹפֵף יָדוֹ (Yeshayahu 10:32), he waves his hand, is like אַֽחֲרֶיךָ רֹאשׁ הֵנִיעָה (Melachim II 19:21), she has shaken her head behind you: a man who scorns a thing waves and shakes his hand and his head at it, and so a man calling another waves his hand to him to come. In this sense it says מִפְּנֵי תְּנוּפַת יַד, because of the waving of the hand of Hashem of hosts, אֲשֶׁר־הוּא מֵנִיף, which He waves (Yeshayahu 19:16), that is, He waves His hand to those who fight against it and brings them upon it; so too הָנִיפוּ יָד וְיָבֹאוּ פִּתְחֵי נְדִיבִֽים (Yeshayahu 13:2), wave the hand and let them come into the gates of the nobles, and וּבְמִלְֽחֲמוֹת תְּנוּפָה (Yeshayahu 30:32), and in battles of waving.

לַֽהֲנָפָה גוֹיִם בְּנָפַת שָׁוְא (Yeshayahu 30:28), to wave the nations in a sieve of vanity, where לַֽהֲנָפָה is the infinitive, or else a noun. The noun is נָפָה, in construct בְּנָפַת. In the words of Chazal the sieve that flour is sifted in is a נפה, and they said (Avos 5:15) נפה שמוציאה את הקמח וקולטת את הסולת, the sieve that lets out the flour and keeps back the fine meal. It is called so because it is waved this way and that when the flour is sifted.

יְפֵה נוֹף מְשׂוֹשׂ כָּל־הָאָרֶץ (Tehillim 48:3), fair of נוֹף, the joy of all the earth, where נוֹף is מחוז או פלך, a district or a province. So too, in another pattern, כָּל־ נָפַת דֹּאר (Melachim I 4:11), all the district of Dor, and וּבְנָפוֹת דּוֹר (Yehoshua 11:2), and in the districts of Dor, which the Targum renders בְפִלְכֵי דוֹר, in the provinces of Dor; and שְׁלֹשֶׁת הַנָּֽפֶת (Yehoshua 17:11), the three districts, rendered תלתא פלכין, three provinces.

His father explains that the Creator divided His world into seven parts, the climes, which in lashon hakodesh are נופות. The air of each differs, and a man who leaves the נוף of his birth for another will most often fall ill, the change of air upsetting his own mixture. Yerushalayim was the fairest of the נופות, and whoever came to her from the rest would be sound and whole, and that is מְשׂוֹשׂ כָּל־הָאָרֶץ, the joy of all the earth.

עשֹק.sense: Harassing and contesting a claim, טרידה וערעור: the well named עֵשֶׂק, because they contended with him.

more.t: וַיִּקְרָא שֵׁם־הַבְּאֵר עֵשֶׂק (Bereishis 26:20), he called the name of the well Esek, which he notes is written with five points; and from it, in the reflexive, כִּי הִֽתְעַשְּׂקוּ עִמּֽוֹ, because they contended with him. Its sense is טרידה וערעור, harassment and the contesting of a claim, as in the words of Chazal, ויצאו עיליה עשקין (Bava Kamma 9a), claimants came out against it, which Radak explains as one who contests, saying it is mine.

עשׁק.sense: To withhold another's money that came into your hand, a deposit, a loan or a wage owed, refusing to return it; robbing, taking by force, is a different thing.

more.t: לֹא־ תַֽעֲשֹׁק אֶת־רֵֽעֲךָ וְלֹא תִגְזֹל (Vayikra 19:13), do not withhold from your fellow and do not rob, is no repetition: to withhold is where your fellow's money came into your hand as a deposit or a loan, or you came to owe him his wage, and when he asks for it you keep back the money and say you will not return it; to rob is to snatch it from him or take it from him by force. So Chazal explained it (Bava Kamma 79b), bringing proof from וַיִּגְזֹל אֶֽת־הַֽחֲנִית מִיַּד הַמִּצְרִי (Shmuel II 23:21), he wrested the spear out of the Egyptian's hand. The pasuk itself parts the two: אוֹ בְגָזֵל אוֹ עָשַׁק אֶת־עֲמִיתֽוֹ (Vayikra 5:21), or in robbery, or he has withheld from his fellow.

וְהַצִּילוּ גָזוּל מִיַּד עָשׁוֹק (Yirmiyahu 22:3), deliver the robbed out of the hand of the withholder, does not mean that all is one; it is that a robber certainly withholds as well, for once he has robbed his fellow by force, it goes without saying that he will withhold from him if his money comes into his hand. עָשׁוֹק itself is an adjective, on the weight of גָּדוֹל, great, and רָחוֹק, far.

אָדָם עָשֻׁק בְּדַם־נָפֶשׁ (Mishlei 28:17), a man ashuk in the blood of a soul: in his view this too is an adjective, like עושק, one who oppresses, for though it has a shuruk, adjectives like it with a shuruk are found; so his father explained שָׁחוּט (Yirmiyahu 9:7), said of an arrow, as an adjective like שוחט, one who slaughters. The meaning is a man who oppresses others in the blood of a soul, that is, who kills men. His father explained it otherwise: a man whose yetzer hara oppressed him so that he killed a soul, and until he goes down to Gehinnom men will not support him or help him; and יָנוּס, he flees, is said because he is in dread all his days.

עָֽשְׁקָה ־לִּי עָרְבֵֽנִי (Yeshayahu 38:14), ashkah for me, be my surety, is in his view a command, though it is not shortened, as שָֽׁמְרָה נַפְשִׁי כִּֽי־חָסִיד אָנִי (Tehillim 86:2), guard my soul, for I am devout, is not; its meaning is: give me over and above, and add to my days and my years. In the words of Chazal (Bava Metzia 51a), עשיק לגביך ושוי לכרסיך, pay over for your back and pay the value for your belly; by his explanation, to clothe yourself, buy the garment giving extra and adding to the price though it is not worth so much, but for your belly buy at its worth. He had explained it before in another sense, as a verb in the feminine, my sickness has oppressed me, be You my surety; but what he has written here is the straight and right reading in his eyes. עֲלֵיהֶם יִֽחְיוּ (Yeshayahu 38:16), upon them they live, means the years You allotted to a man, on which men can live by Your will, as I do, for my allotted days were already complete and You added fifteen years to them for me; and וּלְכָל־בָּהֶן חַיֵּי רוּחִי, and to all, in them is the life of my spirit, means: to all I will tell, and say that in them, in the added years, is the life of my spirit.

more.h: By way of figure, and the nouns
more.t: By way of figure, הֵן יַֽעֲשֹׁק נָהָר (Iyov 40:23), behold, he withholds a river, that is, he draws the whole river into his mouth as though he had withheld it. In the passive, הַֽמְעֻשָּׁקָה בְּתוּלַת בַּת־צִידוֹן (Yeshayahu 23:12), the oppressed maiden daughter of Tzidon. The noun is כִּי הָעֹשֶׁק יְהוֹלֵל חָכָם (Koheles 7:7), for oppression makes a wise man mad, and with an added mem and the feminine ending, וְרַב מַֽעֲשַׁקּוֹת (Mishlei 28:16), and great in oppressions, and מֹאֵס בְּבֶצַע מַֽעֲשַׁקּוֹת (Yeshayahu 33:15), who despises the gain of oppressions.

עמד.sense: To stand; also to stop, and to endure and hold firm. The עַמּוּד, a pillar, is what keeps a house standing; and עִמָּדִי means with me.

more.t: כִּי מִי עָמַד בְּסוֹד (Yirmiyahu 23:18), for who has stood in the counsel of Hashem, and וְאַתָּה פֹּה עֲמֹד עִמָּדִי (Devarim 5:28), and you, stand here with me. עֲמֹד פֶּתַח הָאֹהֶל (Shoftim 4:20), stand at the entrance of the tent, is the infinitive, as is וְיָֽכָלְתָּ עֲמֹד (Shemos 18:23), and you will be able to stand; and וַיָּבֹא אֵצֶל עָמְדִי (Daniel 8:17), and he came near where I stood, is that he came beside me, to the place where I was standing.
וַיַּֽעֲמֹד הַשָּֽׁמֶן (Melachim II 4:6), the oil stopped, no more of it being poured out; and וַֽתַּֽעֲמֹד מִלֶּֽדֶת (Bereishis 29:35), she ceased bearing.

וְיָרֵחַ עָמָד (Yehoshua 10:13), and the moon stood; and וַתַּֽעֲמֹד מִלְחָמָה (Divrei HaYamim I 20:4), war held on, which he glosses ותתקיים, it endured. הֲיַֽעֲמֹד לִבֵּךְ (Yechezkel 22:14), will your heart hold and be strong; וַיַּֽעֲמֹד כָּל־הָעָם בַּבְּרִֽית (Melachim II 23:3), all the people stood in the covenant, that is, they took strength in accepting the covenant to keep it; לְמַעַן יַֽעַמְדוּ יָמִים רַבִּֽים (Yirmiyahu 32:14), that they last many days; and בֵּין הָעֹֽמְדִים הָאֵֽלֶּה (Zecharyah 3:7), among these that endure, which he takes as a hint at the angels, who endure for ever.

עַמּוּדֵי שָׁמַיִם יְרוֹפָפוּ (Iyov 26:11), the pillars of heaven tremble, and וּלְעַמּוּד בַּרְזֶל (Yirmiyahu 1:18), and an iron pillar, belong here, because the pillars are what keeps the house standing, or what stands beneath it; and by the likeness of a pillar, עַמּוּד הֶֽעָנָן (Shemos 13:22), the pillar of cloud, and וְעַמּוּד הָאֵשׁ, and the pillar of fire, are so called.

וַיַּֽעֲמִידֵם לָעַד לְעוֹלָם (Tehillim 148:6), He set them to endure for ever; וְהֶֽעֱמַדְנוּ עָלֵינוּ מִצְוֹת (Nechemiah 10:33), we upheld mitzvos and took them upon ourselves. On וְהַֽעֲמַדְתָּ לָהֶם כָּל־מָתְנָֽיִם (Yechezkel 29:7), and you made all their loins stand, he says that a man who leans is bent over, and when the prop gives way he straightens up from his bending. Yonasan renders it so, וְלָא תְהֵי לְהוֹן לְבֵית סוּמְכְוָן, you will not be a house of support to them, which Radak takes to mean that you will set them on their own loins, so that they lean on you no longer; he has explained the pasuk another way under the root מעד. וּמֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה מַֽעֲמִיד בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה נֹכַח אֲרָם (Divrei HaYamim II 18:34), and the king of Yisrael held himself up in the chariot facing Aram, means that he held himself up and braced himself so that Aram should not see him wounded, and showed himself as though he had not been struck, so that Aram should not take heart against Yisrael in the battle.

לֹא תַֽעֲמֹד עַל־דַּם רֵעֶךָ (Vayikra 19:16), do not stand by your fellow's blood, means that you are not to hold back from going to save him where you can, as Chazal explained it (Sanhedrin 73a): from where do we know that one who sees his fellow drowning in a river, or robbers or a wild beast coming upon him, is bound to save him? Because the pasuk says, do not stand by your fellow's blood. Rabbi Yonah reads עֶמְדָּתֽוֹ in יִקַּח מִכֶּם עֶמְדָּתֽוֹ (Michah 1:11) as אמדתו, his estimate, from estimating. Radak says it may be read from standing, as the word is formed: he will learn his standing from you. That is, the one who dwells in Tzaanan did not go out to the mourning for Beis HaEtzel, and Beis HaEtzel will learn its standing from you: as you did not go out to mourn when your brothers went into exile, so they will not go out when you are in exile. And עִמָּדִי in בְּעוֹד שַׁדַּי עִמָּדִי (Iyov 29:4 in his edition), while Shaddai was yet with me, is as עִמִּי, with me. The word may be drawn from standing, meaning in the place where I am; and it is found only of one speaking of himself.

דוך.sense: To pound in a mortar; pounding is not as fine as grinding, and from this sense the poor man is called דַּךְ.

more.t: אוֹ דָכוּ בַּמְּדֹכָה (Bamidbar 11:8), or they pounded it in a mortar, which he explains as כתשו במכתש, they crushed it in a mortar. Pounding is not as fine as grinding, and so Chazal parted the two (Shabbos 19b): where the pounding is still wanting all agree the thing is forbidden, and they differ only where the grinding is wanting, from which it appears that grinding is the finer of the two. From this sense the poor man is called דַּךְ: אַל־יָשֹׁב דַּךְ נִכְלָם (Tehillim 74:21), let not the poor turn back ashamed.

אול.sense: A fool, אֱוִיל, whose sense he gives as שוטה; and אִוֶּלֶת, folly, read as a noun, though noun and adjective may share its pattern.

more.t: אֱוִיל הַנָּבִיא (Hoshea 9:7), the prophet is a fool; with the yud of relation, כְּלִי רֹעֶה אֱוִלִֽי (Zecharyah 11:15), the gear of a foolish shepherd; and וֶֽאֱוִילִים בַּֽחֲסַר־לֵב יָמֽוּתוּ (Mishlei 10:21), fools die for want of heart. Their sense, he says, is שוטה, שוטים, a fool and fools. וְאִוֶּלֶת בְּיָדֶיהָ תֶֽהֶרְסֶֽנּוּ (Mishlei 14:1), and folly tears it down with her hands, is explained as אשת אולת, a woman of folly, because אִוֶּלֶת is a noun and not an adjective; and so אִוֶּלֶת אָדָם תְּסַלֵּף דַּרְכּוֹ (Mishlei 19:3), a man's folly perverts his way. He allows that noun and adjective may share one weight, in which case אִוֶּלֶת בְּיָדֶיהָ would be the adjective, on the pattern of עִוֶּרֶת, blind, the chirik of the one and the patach of the other making no difference to the weight. אוּלַי, perhaps, is written under the root אלה.

ארן.sense: אֹרֶן, the name of a tree; and אָרוֹן, a chest, like a תיבה, a box, used as both masculine and feminine, mostly masculine.

more.t: נָטַע אֹרֶן (Yeshayahu 44:14), he planted an oren, the name of a tree; so too in the words of Chazal (Parah 3:8), ועצים היו מסודרין שם עצי ארזים ארנים וברושים, and wood was laid in order there, wood of cedars, oranim and cypresses. Some explain it as אל צנוב"ר in Arabic, al-sanobar.

וְעָשׂוּ אֲרוֹן עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים (Shemos 25:10), they shall make a chest of shittim wood; אֲרוֹן אֶחָד (Melachim II 12:10), one chest, which he explains as one man's chest; and וַיִּישֶׂם בָּֽאָרוֹן (Bereishis 50:26), and he was placed in the chest. Its sense is known: it is like a תיבה, a box. The word is used in both genders, mostly the masculine, and in the feminine at וַֽאֲרוֹן הָאֱלֹהִים נִלְקָֽחָה (Shmuel I 4:17), and the Aron of Elokim was taken, and אֲשֶׁר־בָּאָה אֲלֵיהֶם אֲרוֹן (Divrei HaYamim II 8:11), to which the Aron of Hashem has come.

שׁמע.sense: To hear. All of it is hearing: hearing alone, hearing to accept, and hearing that understands. Also to gather men so that they heed, and to sound an instrument.

more.t: All of them are in the sense of hearing, but some are hearing alone, some שמועה לקבלה, hearing to accept, and some שמועת הבנה, hearing that understands: דַּבֶּר־נָא אֶל־עֲבָדֶיךָ אֲרָמִית כִּי שֹֽׁמְעִים אֲנָחְנוּ (Yeshayahu 36:11), speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it; גּוֹי אֲשֶׁר לֹֽא־ תִשְׁמַע לְשֹׁנֽוֹ (Devarim 28:49), a nation whose tongue you will not understand; and לֵב שֹׁמֵעַ (Melachim I 3:9), an understanding heart. תִּשְׁמַע חֲלוֹם לִפְתֹּר אֹתוֹ (Bereishis 41:15), you hear a dream to interpret it, can also be read as of this kind.

more.h: What the verb takes after it
more.t: It is said with lamed, וַיִּשְׁמַע אַבְרָם לְקוֹל שָׂרָי (Bereishis 16:2), Avram listened to the voice of Sarai; with beis, שְׁמַע בְּקֹלִי (Bereishis 27:13), listen to my voice, and וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ בְּתוֹרָתוֹ (Yeshayahu 42:24), they did not listen to His Torah; with אל, כִּי שָׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶל קוֹל הַנַּעַר (Bereishis 21:17), for God has heard the voice of the lad; and with על, יַעַן אֲשֶׁר שְׁמַעְתֶּם עַל מִצְוַת יְהוֹנָדָב אֲבִיכֶם (Yirmiyahu 35:18), because you obeyed the command of Yonadav your father, and אַל תִּשְׁמְעוּ עַל דִּבְרֵי הַנְּבִאִים הַנִּבְּאִים לָכֶם (Yirmiyahu 23:16), do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. הִנֵּה שְׁמֹעַ מִזֶּבַח טוֹב (Shmuel I 15:22), to obey is better than a sacrifice.

In the pattern with tzeirei, אֵת כָּל הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר שָׁמֵעַ (Yirmiyahu 36:13), all the words that he had heard, and וְשָׂרָה שֹׁמַעַת (Bereishis 18:10), and Sarah was listening; the Nagid wrote that וָאֶשְׁמְעָה אֶחָד קָדוֹשׁ (Daniel 8:13), and I heard a holy one, has a kamatz chatuf. The noun כַּאֲשֶׁר שֵׁמַע לְמִצְרָיִם יָחִילוּ כְּשֵׁמַע צֹר (Yeshayahu 23:5), as at the report of Mitzrayim so they shall be in pain at the report of Tzor, has tzeirei; some come with segol, as Radak sets out in the part on grammar. In another pattern, שָׁמַעְנוּ אֶת שָׁמְעוֹ (Yirmiyahu 6:24), we have heard the report of it, and וַיְהִי שָׁמְעוֹ בְּכָל הָאָרֶץ (Yehoshua 6:27), his fame was in all the land; in another, וּבָא בַשָּׁנָה הַשְּׁמוּעָה (Yirmiyahu 51:46), and the report shall come in a year, and מִי הֶאֱמִין לִשְׁמֻעָתֵנוּ (Yeshayahu 53:1), who believed our report; and in another, וְלֹא לְמִשְׁמַע אָזְנָיו יוֹכִיחַ (Yeshayahu 11:3), nor decide by what his ears hear.

וְהַקֹּל נִשְׁמַע (Bereishis 45:16), the report was heard, and וַתִּשָּׁמַע שִׂמְחַת יְרוּשָׁלַם מֵרָחוֹק (Nechemiah 12:43), the joy of Yerushalayim was heard far off. וַיִּשָּׁמַע בְּקוֹלָם (Divrei HaYamim II 30:27), and their voice was heard, means that they were heeded and found favour. Likewise מִשְׁמַעַת is obedience: וּבְנֵי עַמּוֹן מִשְׁמַעְתָּם (Yeshayahu 11:14), and the children of Ammon their מִשְׁמַעַת, is that they will be obedient to them and under their service; so too וַיְשִׂמֵהוּ דָוִד אֶל מִשְׁמַעְתּוֹ (Shmuel II 23:23), David set him over those who obeyed him, וְסָר אֶל מִשְׁמַעְתֶּךָ (Shmuel I 22:14), and turns aside to your bidding, and לְשֵׁמַע אֹזֶן יִשָּׁמְעוּ לִי (Tehillim 18:45), at the hearing of the ear they obey me.

וַיִּשְׁמַע שָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 23:8) is אספם, וקבצם שיהיו נשמעים אליו: Shaul gathered and assembled them, that they should be obedient to him. So הַשְׁמִיעוּ אֶל בָּבֶל רַבִּים (Yirmiyahu 50:29) is gather many against Bavel, that they heed you and come to Bavel, and so הַשְׁמִיעוּ עָלֶיהָ מַמְלְכוֹת אֲרָרַט מִנִּי וְאַשְׁכְּנָז (Yirmiyahu 51:27), gather against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz. With these he lists, and gives no gloss to, הִשְׁמִיעַ אֶת מַחֲנֵה אֲרָם (Melachim II 7:6), Hashem made the camp of Aram hear, and הַשְׁמִיעוּ הַלְלוּ וְאִמְרוּ (Yirmiyahu 31:7), make it heard, praise, and say.

וְאָסָף בַּמְצִלְתַּיִם מַשְׁמִיעַ, and Asaf sounding the cymbals, is משמיע קול, making a sound heard; and וְעִמָּהֶם הֵימָן וִידוּתוּן חֲצֹצְרוֹת וּמְצִלְתַּיִם לְמַשְׁמִיעִים (Divrei HaYamim I 16:42), and with them Heiman and Yedusun, trumpets and cymbals for sounding, is to be sounding, as וְחֶרֶב אוֹיְבֶיךָ לְמַשֶּׂגֶת (Divrei HaYamim I 21:12), and the sword of your enemies overtaking, is to be overtaking. The noun is לְהַשְׁמָעוּת אָזְנָיִם (Yechezkel 24:26), for making the ears hear.

שׁכן.sense: To dwell, and to make dwell, to settle; מִשְׁכָּנוֹת, dwellings; שָׁכֵן, one whose house is beside another's, or who dwells in a place. From this, the rest of death.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר שָֽׁכַן ־שָׁם (Yehoshua 22:19), where the Mishkan of Hashem dwelt; וְשָֽׁכַנְתִּי בְּתוֹכָֽם (Shemos 25:8), I shall dwell among them; שְׁכֹן בָּאָרֶץ (Bereishis 26:2), dwell in the land; and לִשְׁכֹּן בָּֽעֲרָפֶֽל (Melachim I 8:12), to dwell in the thick darkness. לְשִׁכְנוֹ תִדְרְשׁוּ (Devarim 12:5), to His dwelling you shall seek, has a chirik, and he takes it for an infinitive on the weight of וּכְפִתְחוֹ עָֽמְדוּ כָל־הָעָֽם (Nechemiah 8:5), and when he opened it all the people stood, or else for a noun.

מִשְׁכַּן (Vayikra 17:4), the Mishkan of Hashem; מִשְׁכָּנוֹת לַֽאֲבִיר יַֽעֲקֹֽב (Tehillim 132:5), dwellings for the Mighty One of Yaakov; and וּֽמִשְׁכְּנוֹתָיו מְלֵֽחָה (Iyov 39:6), his dwellings the salt land. The masculine plural is in קְדשׁ מִשְׁכְּנֵי עֶלְיֽוֹן (Tehillim 46:5), the holiest of the dwellings of the Most High.

וּשְׁכֵנוֹ הַקָּרֹב אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ (Shemos 12:4), his neighbour nearest his house; the feminine וְשָֽׁאֲלָה אִשָּׁה מִשְּׁכֶנְתָּהּ (Shemos 3:22), and a woman shall ask of her neighbour, and the plural וַתִּקְרֶאנָה לוֹ הַשְּׁכֵנוֹת (Rus 4:17), and the neighbour women named him. A שכן, he says, is one who dwells beside a man, his house beside his house; but וּבַל־יֹאמַר שָׁכֵן חָלִיתִי (Yeshayahu 33:24), and the dweller shall not say, I am sick, is of one who dwells inside her, in Yerushalayim, as the pasuk goes on, הָעָם הַיּשֵׁב בָּהּ נְשֻׂא עָוֹֽן, the people that dwell in her are forgiven their sin; and יָגוּרוּ שְׁכַן שֹֽׁמְרוֹן (Hoshea 10:5), the dwellers of Shomron shall fear, is those who dwell in Shomron.

more.h: Settling a thing, and the rest of death
more.t: Where the verb takes an object, אֹהֶל שִׁכֵּן בָּאָדָֽם (Tehillim 78:60), the tent He set to dwell among men, and לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם (Devarim 12:11), to set His name to dwell there; וְהִשְׁכַּנְתִּי עָלֶיךָ כָּל־עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם (Yechezkel 32:4), I will settle all the birds of the sky upon you, and וּכְבוֹדִי לֶֽעָפָר יַשְׁכֵּן סֶֽלָה (Tehillim 7:6), and make my honour dwell in the dust, selah. From this sense comes יִשְׁכְּנוּ אַדִּירֶיךָ (Nachum 3:18), your mighty ones rest, which is the rest of death, and like it שָֽׁכְנָה דוּמָה נַפְשִֽׁי (Tehillim 94:17), my soul rested in silence.

שֹכן.sense: שַׂכִּין, as in וְשַׂמְתָּ שַׂכִּין בְּלֹעֶךָ (Mishlei 23:2), and you shall put a knife to your throat; of it he says only that it is known.

more.t: וְשַׂמְתָּ שַׂכִּין בְּלֹעֶךָ (Mishlei 23:2), and you shall put a knife to your throat, of which he says only ידוע, it is known; and he has already written the word in another sense under the root שֹוֹך, with לְשִׂכִּים בְּעֵינֵיכֶם (Bamidbar 33:55), thorns in your eyes.

נבל.sense: Falling: leaves that fall, the base and fallen man, a disgraceful thing, the carcass that falls. Also נֵבֶל, a skin or a potter's jug, and an instrument of music.

more.t: נָבֵֽל צִיץ (Yeshayahu 40:7), the blossom has fallen, a past verb formed like יָבֵשׁ חָצִיר, the grass has dried, in that same pasuk; כִּנְבֹל עָלֶה מִגֶּפֶן (Yeshayahu 34:4), as a leaf falls from the vine; and the adjective וְהֶֽעָלֶה נָבֵל (Yirmiyahu 8:13), and the leaf is fallen. וַנָּבֶל כֶּֽעָלֶה כֻּלָּנוּ (Yeshayahu 64:5), we have all fallen like a leaf, is the heavy form with a kamatz standing in for the dagesh, as in וַיָּזֶד יַֽעֲקֹב נָזִיד (Bereishis 25:29), Yaakov cooked a stew, whose proper form is וַיִּזֵד; or it belongs to another form, whose full shape is וַיִּנָּבֵל, the nun of the root lost and its vowel thrown onto the added nun. All of them, he says, are a sense of נפילה, falling.

כְּאֵלָה נֹבֶלֶת עָלֶהָ (Yeshayahu 1:30), like a terebinth whose leaf falls: the terebinth is called falling because its leaves fall, so that it falls on the side of its leaves. So too מְגֻלְּחֵי זָקָן (Yirmiyahu 41:5), men whose beard is shaven, and וּקְרֻעֵי בְגָדִים, whose clothes are torn; חָגוּר כְּלֵי מִלְחָמָֽה (Shoftim 18:11), whose loins are girded with weapons of war; and הָעִיר הַיֹּצֵאת אֶלֶף (Amos 5:3), the city that goes out a thousand, since it is the men of the city who go out.

From this a low and fallen man is called נבל: כִּי נָבָל נְבָלָה יְדַבֵּר (Yeshayahu 32:6), for a base man speaks baseness, and כְּאַחַד הַנְּבָלִים (Shmuel II 13:13), like one of the base; the sense of all of it is falling and descent. אִם־ נָבַלְתָּ בְהִתְנַשֵּׂא (Mishlei 30:32), if you have fallen, bear yourself high, he reads as counsel to one brought down: if you have fallen from your greatness, bear yourself with honour, and do not ask of base men or of men unworthy of your asking; hold yourself as dear as you were before, and refrain from asking of unworthy men and from doing what disgraces you. That is וְאִם־זַמּוֹתָ יָד לְפֶֽה (Mishlei 30:32), and if you have devised, a hand to the mouth: even if you thought to ask, put a hand to your mouth, neither to ask nor to do what is unfit for you.

Where the verb takes an object it lowers: אַל־ תְּנַבֵּל כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ (Yirmiyahu 14:21), do not lessen or bring down the throne of Your glory, and וַיְנַבֵּל צוּר יְשֻֽׁעָתֽוֹ (Devarim 32:15), he brought the Rock of his salvation down from His greatness, in his thought and by his deeds. וְנִבַּלְתִּיךְ (Nachum 3:6) is either I will make you foul and disgraced or I will make you like a carcass thrown out; and נְבָלָה (Iyov 42:8) is a foul and disgraceful thing, as בְּנִבְלַת שִׁקּֽוּצֵיהֶם (Yirmiyahu 16:18) is the foulness of their idols. From this the dead body, which falls, is called נְבֵלָה, וְחֵלֶב נְבֵלָה (Vayikra 7:24), the fat of a carcass; and a word of falling is said of a dead body too, מַפֶּלֶת הָאַרְיֵה (Shoftim 14:8), the fallen body of the lion, so that נְבֵלָה is of the sense of falling.

נֵבֶל יִמָּלֵא יָיִן (Yirmiyahu 13:12), a נֵבֶל will be filled with wine, is a leather skin, or a potter's jug, for so it is written כְּשֵׁבֶר נֵבֶל יֽוֹצְרִים (Yeshayahu 30:14), like the breaking of a potter's jug. It is also one of the instruments of music, בְּנֵבֶל וְכִנּֽוֹר (Tehillim 150:3), with nevel and kinnor. בִכְלִי־ נֶבֶל (Tehillim 71:22), with the instrument of the nevel, has a segol, and the Mesorah's note on it begins לית סגול, the only one with a segol. Targum Yonasan renders מִכְּלֵי הָֽאַגָּנוֹת וְעַד כָּל־כְּלֵי הַנְּבָלִֽים (Yeshayahu 22:24) as from the kohanim who wear the ephod to the Levi'im who hold the nevalim.

וְנִבְלֵי שָׁמַיִם מִי יַשְׁכִּֽיב (Iyov 38:37), who can lay down the נִבְלֵי of heaven, where they are the rains of heaven; and likewise וַיְהִי הַמַּבּוּל (Bereishis 7:17), and the flood came, since its proper form is מַנְבּוּל.

יקץ.sense: To awake; of the sense he says only that it is known: Yaakov from his sleep, Noach from his wine, and those who shake you.

more.t: Three pesukim and a note on the pointing: וַיִּיקַץ יַֽעֲקֹב מִשְּׁנָתוֹ (Bereishis 28:16), Yaakov awoke from his sleep; וַיִּיקֶץ נֹחַ מִיֵּינוֹ (Bereishis 9:24), Noach awoke from his wine; and וְיִֽקְצוּ מְזַעְזְעֶיךָ (Chavakuk 2:7), those who shake you will awake, where the yud is held by a ga'ya because the yud that is the first root letter has dropped.

כחל.sense: To adorn the eyes with kohl, which is the פּוּךְ; in Arabic it is called al-kuhl.

more.t: כָּחַלְתְּ עֵינַיִךְ (Yechezkel 23:40), you adorned your eyes with kohl: he explains it as תקנת עיניך בכוחל, you set your eyes off with kohl, and says the kohl is the פּוּךְ, and that in Arabic it is called al-kuhl.

גבל.sense: A border; to border on, and where the verb takes an object, to set a bound; the גִּבְלִים, who cut stone to a set measure, or, as others explain, men of Geval.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר גָּֽבְלוּ רִֽאשֹׁנִים (Devarim 19:14), which the earlier men set as a border; וְהַיַּרְדֵּן יִגְבֹּֽל ־אֹתוֹ (Yehoshua 18:20), and the Yarden borders it; and וְגַם־חֲמָת תִּגְבָּל ־בָּהּ (Zecharyah 9:2), and Chamas too, which he glosses as being a border to it. Where it takes an object, וְהִגְבַּלְתָּ אֶת־הָעָם (Shemos 19:12), and you shall set bounds for the people, and הַגְבֵּל אֶת־הָהָר (Shemos 19:23), set bounds about the mountain, which he glosses as setting a border.

The noun is גְּבוּל, as לֹא תַסִּיג גְּבוּל רֵעֲךָ (Devarim 19:14), do not move your fellow's border; in וּגְבוּלָהּ אֶל־שְׂפָתָהּ סָבִיב (Yechezkel 43:13), and its border at its lip round about, it is the border of the cubit, that is, the frame round about, a span wide. The adjective מִגְבָּלֹת, in מִגְבָּלֹת תַּֽעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם (Shemos 28:14), you shall make them bordered, is formed like וְהֶֽעָרִים הַמִּבְדָּלוֹת (Yehoshua 16:9), the cities set apart; the noun in the feminine is וְכֻסֶּמֶת גְּבֻלָתֽוֹ (Yeshayahu 28:25), and spelt in its border, with the plural גְּבֻלוֹת יַשִּׂיגוּ (Iyov 24:2), they move borders; and in another pattern שַֽׁרְשֹׁת גַּבְלֻת (Shemos 28:22), chains of border work, formed like עַבְדּוּת, servitude.

The גִּבְלִים, in וַיִּֽפְסְלוּ בֹּנֵי שְׁלֹמֹה וּבֹנֵי חִירוֹם וְהַגִּבְלִים (Melachim I 5:32), and the builders of Shlomo and the builders of Chirom and the גִּבְלִים hewed, are those who cut the stone by line and measure, as the corners of a house are cut by line and measure, setting a red thread at the end of their measure or ruling a line and cutting the stone from there. It is of the sense of border: they set a border to the stone's measure. Others explained גִּבְלִים as the men of Geval, who were craftsmen in stone, and so זִקְנֵי גְבַל וַֽחֲכָמֶיהָ (Yechezkel 27:9), the elders of Geval and its wise men, who were craftsmen in stone.

גרם.sense: A bone, as the Targum renders עֶצֶם, bone, גַּרְמָא; the verb, to break the bones; and גֶּרֶם הַֽמַּֽעֲלוֹת, the steps themselves or a step.

more.t: יִשָּׂשׂכָר חֲמֹר גָּרֶם (Bereishis 49:14), Yissachar is a donkey of bone, he takes as strong and big of bone, bearing a great load, and this is what the pasuk says, וַיֵּט שִׁכְמוֹ לִסְבֹּל, he bent his shoulder to bear. Rabbi Yonah takes it as broken and unable to stir from his place, from וְעַצְמֹֽתֵיהֶם יְגָרֵם (Bamidbar 24:8), he will break their bones.

וְעַצְמֹֽתֵיהֶם יְגָרֵם is he will break the bones, and in the same way יְשֹׁרָֽשׁוּ (Iyov 31:8) is he will take away the roots. In the light form, לֹא גָֽרְמוּ לַבֹּֽקֶר (Tzefaniah 3:3) is either that they did not tear prey, since a lion or a wolf in tearing breaks the bones by morning, or that they left not even the bones for morning; and by way of borrowing, וְאֶת־חֲרָשֶׂיהָ תְּגָרֵמִי (Yechezkel 23:34), you will break its shards.

אֶל־ גֶּרֶם הַֽמַּֽעֲלוֹת (Melachim II 9:13), onto the very bone of the steps, that is, onto the steps themselves; or else it is in the sense of a step. Yonasan renders it שַׁעֲיָא, meaning the step that carried a mark for the hours of the day, as he renders צֵל הַֽמַּֽעֲלוֹת (Yeshayahu 38:8), the shadow of the steps, טוּל אֶבֶן שְׁעַיָא, the shadow of the stone of the hours.

גמל.sense: To deal out good or ill, in his words the beginning of good or of evil; to wean, the nursing complete, and of fruit, to finish ripening; and the camel, which is known.

more.t: Their sense is the beginning of good or of evil: כִּי גָמַל עָלָֽי (Tehillim 13:6), for He has dealt with me; אֲשֶׁר־ גְּמָלָם כְּֽרַֽחֲמָיו (Yeshayahu 63:7), which He dealt them according to His mercies; and אֲשֶׁר גָּמַלְנוּ אֹתֽוֹ (Bereishis 50:15), which we dealt him.

הַגְּמוּל אַתֶּם מְשַׁלְּמִים (Yoel 4:4), is it a recompense you are paying; with the feminine heh, הַגְּמוּלָה הַזֹּֽאת (Shmuel II 19:37), this recompense; and in another pattern, תַּגְמוּל, כָּֽל־ תַּגְמוּלוֹהִי עָלָֽי (Tehillim 116:12), all He has dealt to me, which is like תַּגְמוּלָיו and takes a heh and a yud in the Aramaic way, as עֲלוֹהִי, upon him, and יְדוֹהִי, his hands.

וַיִּגְדַּל הַיֶּלֶד וַיִּגָּמַל (Bereishis 21:8), the child grew and was weaned, which he glosses as his nursing being completed, and so עַד יִגָּמֵל הַנַּעַר (Shmuel I 1:22), until the boy is weaned; and among the light forms גְּמוּלֵי מֵֽחָלָב (Yeshayahu 28:9), those weaned from milk. So too of the completing of the ripening of fruit: וַיִּגְמֹל שְׁקֵדִֽים (Bamidbar 17:23), it ripened almonds, and וּבֹסֶר גֹּמֵל (Yeshayahu 18:5), the sour grape ripening.

אֶת־ הַגָּמָל כִּי־מַֽעֲלֵה גֵרָה הוּא (Vayikra 11:4), the camel, for it brings up the cud, and גְּמַלִּים מֵֽינִיקוֹת (Bereishis 32:16), nursing camels. Of the animal itself he says only that it is known.

שׁוב.sense: Three senses: to return or turn back, as from sin; quieting and giving rest, as in שָׁב שְׁבוּת, following Rabbi Yehudah; and rebellion, as in מְשׁוּבָה.

more.t: וָשָׁב וְרָפָא לֽוֹ (Yeshayahu 6:10), and he turns back and is healed, is שׁב מחטאו, he turns back from his sin. Likewise וּלְשָׁבֵי פֶשַׁע בְּיַֽעֲקֹב (Yeshayahu 59:20), to those in Yaakov who turn back from transgression, and כִּֽי־אַֽחֲרֵי שׁוּבִי נִחַמְתִּי (Yirmiyahu 31:19), for after my turning back I was sorry, that is, after I had turned back from my iniquities. Cities return too: at Yechezkel 35:9, your cities will not return means they will not return to their former state.

more.h: The rain that does not return
more.t: וְשָׁמָּה לֹא יָשׁוּב כִּי אִם־הִרְוָה אֶת־הָאָרֶץ (Yeshayahu 55:10), and does not return there but waters the earth, he reads taking כִּי אִם as but rather: it does not go back there, and what does it do? It waters the earth. His father reads it as it stands: it does not return until it has watered the earth, but once it has watered it, it returns. This is the return of the rain, for the heat of the sun draws it up; and but for this the earth would have no need of rain.

In the heavy form it gives back: הֱשִׁיבֹנוּ אֵלֶיךָ (Bereishis 44:8), we brought back to you; וַיָּשֶׁב אֵת כָּל־הָֽרְכֻשׁ (Bereishis 14:16), and he brought back all the goods; וַיָּשִׁיבוּ אֹתָם דָּבָר (Bamidbar 13:26), and they brought back word to them. Reaching a third party: לָכֵן שְׂעִפַּי יְשִׁיבוּנִי (Iyov 20:2), therefore my thoughts make me answer, that is, they force me to return word to you. הֱשִׁיבוֹתָ מֵֽחֲרוֹן אַפֶּֽךָ (Tehillim 85:4) is not intransitive, he holds, but transitive in the regular way: מֵֽחֲרוֹן is an infinitive with a nun added, as though it said השיבות אפך מחרון, You turned Your anger back from burning. The verb is used of a gift and of a guilt offering, as מִנְחָה יָשִׁיבוּ (Tehillim 72:10), they will render a gift, and מָה הָֽאָשָׁם אֲשֶׁר נָשִׁיב לוֹ (Shmuel I 6:4), what is the guilt offering that we shall return to him. A gift is a returning because it repays a kindness, the one who gives it returning to his benefactor out of what he was granted; or it is given out of fear, repaying the other for not harming him. A guilt offering is a returning because the sinner who brings it is like a debtor returning his debt to its owner. What seems right to him further is that a gift is a returning because it comes time after time, as וְהֵשִׁיב לְמֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim II 3:4), and he rendered to the king of Yisrael, which he did year by year.

נַפְשִׁי יְשׁוֹבֵב (Tehillim 23:3), my soul He brings back, is that He brings it back to the good way; it can also be read as quieting, He gives it rest and quiets it. מְשׁוֹבֶבֶת מֵחֶרֶב (Yechezkel 38:8), brought back from the sword, is one that escaped the sword of the nations and came back to its land. On לְשׁוֹבֵב שָׂדֵינוּ יְחַלֵּֽק (Michah 2:4), to restore our fields, he divides: the enemy takes away the portion that was mine, and while we hope for our fields to be given back to us, they divide them among themselves. וְלִתְשׁוּבַת הַשָּׁנָה (Divrei HaYamim II 36:10), at the turn of the year, is the year's end, when the sun comes back to the point it set out from.

more.h: Quieting the exile, and a dispute
more.t: The second sense: וְשָׁב י"י אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת־שְׁבֽוּתְךָ (Devarim 30:3), Hashem your God will quiet your exile, and הִֽנְנִי־ שָׁב שְׁבוּת (Yirmiyahu 30:18), behold, I quiet the exile, are quieting and giving rest, as Rabbi Yehudah wrote. Rabbi Yonah objected: what sense is there in His quieting them in exile? Radak answers that this is no sound argument, for the navi says He will quiet the exile and give them rest from their trouble, and that cannot be except by returning them to their place, since one exiled from his land has no quiet even among great delights. What Rabbi Yehudah wrote is right, that every verb of the light form in the first sense is intransitive and not one of them transitive. The noun is בְּשׁוּבָה וָנַחַת תִּוָּשֵׁעוּן (Yeshayahu 30:15), in rest and quiet you will be saved. וְשַׁבְתִּי בְּבֵית־י"י (Tehillim 23:6), and I shall rest in the house of Hashem, can be read the same way, or in the first sense, of returning there time after time. Radak sets שׁוּבָה (Bamidbar 10:36) in this second sense; his father sets it in the first, as its Targum has it, תּוּב יְיָ שְׁרֵי בִיקָרָךְ, return, Hashem, dwell in Your glory. On that reading, through the three days the Aron went before them, taken out of the camp, Moshe said קוּמָה י"י, arise, Hashem; at their end, when it came back to its place in the middle of the camp, he said שׁוּבָה י"י רִֽבֲבוֹת אַלְפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, that is, return with the myriads of the thousands of Yisrael and go with them as at first.

The third sense is ענין המרד, rebellion: תְּיַסְּרֵךְ רָֽעָתֵךְ וּמְשֻֽׁבוֹתַיִךְ תּֽוֹכִחֻךְ (Yirmiyahu 2:19), your evil will chasten you and your rebellions will reprove you; the nouns כִּי מְשׁוּבַת פְּתָיִם תַּֽהַרְגֵם (Mishlei 1:32), for the rebelliousness of the simple will kill them, and מְשֻׁבָה נִצַּחַת (Yirmiyahu 8:5), a perpetual rebellion; the adjective שׁוּבָה מְשֻׁבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yirmiyahu 3:12), return, rebellious Yisrael, and שׁוּבוּ בָנִים שֽׁוֹבָבִים (Yirmiyahu 3:14), return, rebellious children. וְעַמִּי תְלוּאִים לִמְשֽׁוּבָתִי (Hoshea 11:7), and My people hang on their rebellion against Me: for the rebellion they commit against Me they hang in their trouble, not knowing where to turn for help; the yud of לִמְשֽׁוּבָתִי does not make it rebellion of Mine. Some explain כִּי מְשׁוּבַת פְּתָיִם as quiet, the ease of the simple, as the pasuk goes on וְשַׁלְוַת כְּסִילִים תְּאַבְּדֵֽם, and the complacency of fools will destroy them; and some explain כִּֽי־אַֽחֲרֵי שׁוּבִי נִחַמְתִּי as rebellion.

שֹוב.sense: To grow grey; and שֵׂיבָה, greyness, which is further on than old age, as the Mishnah says: sixty for old age, seventy for greyness.

more.h: Greyness, further on than old age
more.t: זָקַנְתִּי וָשַׂבְתִּי (Shmuel I 12:2), I have grown old and grey; the adjective גַּם שָׂב גַּם יָשִׁישׁ בָּנוּ (Iyov 15:10), both the grey and the aged are among us; the noun כִּי קָמוּ עֵינָיו מִשֵּׂיבוֹ (Melachim I 14:4), for his eyes had risen from his grey age; and with the feminine ending גַּם שֵׂיבָה זָרְקָה בּוֹ (Hoshea 7:9), greyness is sprinkled on him. שֵׂיבָה is further on than זקנה, old age, as the Mishnah says (Avos 5:21), sixty for old age and seventy for greyness; and so the pasuk means, I grew grey after I had grown old.

חפה.sense: To cover: a head, a house with wood or gold; and, spelled with an alef, of those who screened themselves from the Creator, saying He knows nothing of what men do.

more.t: וּפְנֵי הָמָן חָפֽוּ (Esther 7:8), and Haman's face was covered, he takes as a verb that governs nothing: his face was pressed down into the ground, for he was ashamed at what the king said to him. Some take it as a verb with an object like its fellows, that is, the king's servants covered his face, as the faces of those to be hanged are covered, since the servants sensed that the king would order him hanged, having seen how angry he was with him; therefore Charvonah said גַּם הִנֵּה־הָעֵץ (Esther 7:9), here too is the tree.

חִפָּה עֵץ בְּרוֹשִׁים (Divrei HaYamim II 3:5), he overlaid it with cypress wood, and וַיְחַפֵּהוּ זָהָב טוֹב, and overlaid it with fine gold; in the passive, כַּנְפֵי יוֹנָה נֶחְפָּה בַכֶּסֶף (Tehillim 68:14), a dove's wings covered with silver. All of it is covering, and the Targum of וַיְכַס (Shemos 10:15), and it covered, is וַחֲפָא.

From this sense and root comes וַיְחַפְּאוּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim II 17:9), where an alef stands for the last root letter: the children of Yisrael drew a screen between themselves and the Creator, saying that the deeds of men are hidden from Him and that He neither knows nor grasps anything of them, and therefore built themselves high places; the whole parsha runs so. Yeshayahu says the like of them, woe to those who go deep away from Hashem to hide their counsel, whose deeds are in the dark, who say who sees us and who knows us (Yeshayahu 29:15), and the navi says of them, for they say Hashem does not see us, Hashem has forsaken the land (Yechezkel 8:12). Chazal explained it the same way in the Yalkut on Melachim II 17:9: what did the children of Yisrael say? This pillar neither sees nor hears.

קסס.sense: To pluck, ענינו קטף; it is like יְקוֹצֵץ, spelled with a tzadi, to cut off.

more.t: One line, on יְקוֹסֵס וְיָבֵשׁ (Yechezkel 17:9), one will pluck it off, and it will wither.

אתה.sense: To come. The sense of every form is coming, as the Targum renders ויבא, and he came, as וַאֲתָא.

more.t: אָתָא בֹקֶר וְגַם־לָיְלָה (Yeshayahu 21:12), morning comes and night too, and עָדֶיךָ תֵאתֶה (Michah 4:8), it will come to you, have the alef at rest; מִצָּפוֹן זָהָב יֶֽאֱתֶה (Iyov 37:22), gold comes out of the north, and כְּסוּפָה יֶֽאֱתֶה (Mishlei 1:27), it comes like a storm, have it sounded. In הַעִירוֹתִי מִצָּפוֹן וַיַּאת (Yeshayahu 41:25), I roused one from the north and he came, the last root letter has dropped; and in וַיֵּתֶא רָאשֵׁי עָם (Devarim 33:21), and he came, the heads of the people, the alef stands for the heh that is the last root letter.

הָאֹֽתִיּוֹת שְׁאָלוּנִי (Yeshayahu 45:11), ask Me of the things to come, and הַגִּידוּ הָאֹֽתִיּוֹת לְאָחוֹר (Yeshayahu 41:23), tell what is to come hereafter. In these the last root letter shows itself turned into a yud, as it does in קָֽרְבוּ וַיֶּאֱתָיֽוּן (Yeshayahu 41:5), they drew near and came, and in כִּי פַחַד פָּחַדְתִּי וַיֶּאֱתָיֵנִי (Iyov 3:24 in his edition), what I feared has come upon me.

more.h: Come, with a heh for the alef
more.t: אֵתָיוּ אֶקְחָה־יַיִן (Yeshayahu 56:12), come, let me fetch wine; and with a heh in place of the alef that is the first root letter, הֵתָיוּ לְאָכְלָֽה (Yirmiyahu 12:9), come to devour, and לִקְרַאת צָמֵא הֵתָיוּ מָיִם (Yeshayahu 21:14), which he reads as telling the waters to come toward the thirsty man, the one wandering from his place before the sword.

תמם.sense: To come to an end, be finished; and, in a sense he calls close to it, to be whole: in body, with no limb lacking, or in views and good traits.

more.t: כִּי אִם ־תַּם הַכֶּסֶף (Bereishis 47:18), that the money is spent, and וַתִּתֹּם הַשָּׁנָה (Bereishis 47:18), and the year ended; לֹֽא־יִבּוֹל עָלֵהוּ וְלֹֽא־ יִתֹּם פִּרְיוֹ (Yechezkel 47:12), its leaf will not wither and its fruit will not come to an end; עַד־ תֹּם כָּל־הַדּוֹר (Devarim 2:14), till the whole generation was gone. Where it takes an object, עַד־ תֻּמִּי אֹתָם בְּיָדֽוֹ (Yirmiyahu 27:8), until I make an end of them by his hand. כְּתֻמָּם בָּאוּ עָלַיִךְ (Yeshayahu 47:9), at their completion they came upon you: bereavement and widowhood came upon you entire, all the evil that could come of them.

more.h: A nun for the doubled letter
more.t: תַּמְנוּ חֵפֶשׂ מְחֻפָּשׂ (Tehillim 64:7), they have completed a searched-out search: the nun stands in place of the doubled letter, the rule being תממו, and the sense is that they search out wrongs until they complete them, so that no man could think out or search out more wrong than they search. So too כִּי לֹא־ תָמְנוּ (Eichah 3:22), like תממו: the kindnesses of Hashem are not ended; or it may mean that Hashem's kindnesses are with us, for we are not ended. Like it is הַאִם תַּמְנוּ לִגְוֹֽעַ (Bamidbar 17:28), have we come to an end in perishing?

more.h: Whole in body, views and traits
more.t: תָּמִים הָיָה בְּדֹֽרֹתָיו (Bereishis 6:9), he was whole in his generations; זָכָר תָּמִים (Vayikra 1:3), a whole male; יוֹנָתִי תַמָּתִי (Shir HaShirim 5:2), my dove, my perfect one; תֹּם ־וָישֶׁר (Tehillim 25:21), wholeness and uprightness; and וְאִישׁ מָשַׁךְ בַּקֶּשֶׁת לְתֻמּוֹ (Melachim I 22:34), and a man drew the bow in his innocence, meaning that he did not aim at Achav. On פַּר בֶּן־בָּקָר תְּמִימִם (Yechezkel 46:6), a bull of the herd, whole ones, he reads the plural as meaning that the bull and the herd beast be whole. Chazal expound (Menachos 45a): since we find two bulls for the new moons, how do we know that one who did not find two brings one? The pasuk says פַּר, a bull. And it says תְּמִימִם in the plural because the obligation is two. From this root and sense are אֶת־הָֽאוּרִים וְאֶת־ הַתֻּמִּים (Shemos 28:30), the Urim and the Tumim.

more.h: The day that did not hasten
more.t: וְלֹֽא־אָץ לָבוֹא כְּיוֹם תָּמִֽים (Yehoshua 10:13), and it did not hasten to set, like a whole day: the sun stood still for Yehoshua and did not hurry to set, and the day was like the full day of the year, the day of the turn of Tammuz.

אֵֽין־ מְתֹם בִּבְשָׂרִי (Tehillim 38:4), no wholeness in my flesh, since all of it is stricken; and in אֵין־בּוֹ מְתֹם (Yeshayahu 1:6), no wholeness in it, the word רק, but, is left out: there is no wholeness in it but wound and bruise. So too אֵֽין־טוֹב בָּֽאָדָם שֶׁיֹּאכַל וְשָׁתָה (Koheles 2:24), nothing good in a man but that he eat and drink.

Radak's father writes that every form with a dagesh in the tav alone belongs to a root נָתַם, all of them a sense of ending and completing. Yonasan renders וְכֵן הֵתַֽמוּ (Shmuel II 20:18), and so they concluded, as אִם מַשְׁלְמִין, whether they make peace. Radak explains: you should have asked at Avel first whether it would make peace, as it is written כִּֽי־תִקְרַב אֶל־עִיר (Devarim 20:10), when you draw near to a city, and all the more so a city of Yisrael; which is why she said after it אנכי שלומי אמוני ישראל, I am of the peaceable and faithful of Yisrael.

רצה.sense: To be pleased with a thing and accept it. It also means to pay off in full, as the land pays off her sabbaths. A third sense is to go.

more.t: כִּֽי־ רָצוּ עֲבָדֶיךָ אֶת־אֲבָנֶיהָ (Tehillim 102:15), Your servants take pleasure in her stones; וְאֶרְצֶה ־בּוֹ (Chaggai 1:8), I shall be pleased with it; וְכִי יַֽעֲלוּ עֹלָה וּמִנְחָה אֵינֶנִּי רֹצָם (Yirmiyahu 14:12), though they bring up an olah and a minchah I do not accept them; and the one accepted, יְהִי רְצוּי אֶחָיו (Devarim 33:24), let him be acceptable to his brothers. One makes himself acceptable in וּבַמֶּה יִתְרַצֶּה זֶה אֶל־אֲדֹנָיו (Shmuel I 29:4), and with what shall this one make himself acceptable to his master; and where the verb takes an object, בָּנָיו יְרַצּוּ דַלִּים (Iyov 20:10), his sons will appease the poor. The noun is וַיָּפֶק רָצוֹן (Mishlei 8:35), he draws out favour, and וּבִרְצֹנָם עִקְּרוּ־שֽׁוֹר (Bereishis 49:6), in their will they hamstrung an ox.

אִם־תִּֽהְיֶה לְטוֹב לְהָעָם הַזֶּה וּרְצִיתָם (Divrei HaYamim II 10:7), if you will be good to this people and וּרְצִיתָם: he explains it to mean that they will be acceptable, while Rabbi Yonah takes the verb as transitive, and Radak explains him to mean that you will win them over with your good words.

more.h: What the olah makes acceptance for
more.t: וְנִרְצָה לוֹ (Vayikra 1:4), and it will be accepted for him: Chazal explain in the Sifra, on parshas Vayikra, what it makes acceptance for: not for kareisos, nor for the deaths at the hands of beis din or of heaven, nor for lashes, since the punishment of those is stated; only for a positive commandment, and for a negative that a positive puts right, whose punishment is not stated; and when a man brings an olah as a gift, though he was not commanded in it, it is accepted for him to atone for what he sinned in these.

A second sense: עַד־ רָֽצְתָה הָאָרֶץ אֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתֶיהָ (Divrei HaYamim II 36:21), until the land had paid off her sabbaths; אָז תִּרְצֶה הָאָרֶץ (Vayikra 26:34), then the land will pay off; וְהֵם יִרְצוּ אֶת־עֲוֹנָם (Vayikra 26:41 in his edition), they will pay off their sin; עַד־ יִרְצֶה כְּשָׂכִיר יוֹמֽוֹ (Iyov 14:6), until he completes his day like a hired man; and in the passive כִּי נִרְצָה עֲוֹנָהּ (Yeshayahu 40:2), her sin is paid off. Their sense is completing, and it is close to the first sense.

A third sense, which he calls going: אִם־רָאִיתָ גַנָּב וַתִּרֶץ עִמּוֹ (Tehillim 50:18), if you saw a thief you went with him, whose rule is וַתִּרְצֶה, and וְהַחַיּוֹת רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב (Yechezkel 1:14), the chayos going out and back, where an alef stands for a heh. Rabbi Yonah puts בִּרְצֹתוֹ עִם־אֱלֹהִֽים (Iyov 34:9) here too, and Radak explains him to mean his walking with Hashem, then answers that there is no need to take the word out of its plain sense. One may read ותרץ עמו itself from willing, that you wished to be with him. וּרְצִיתָם is also read from going, that you go with them after their own mind and wish.

וְאַֽחֲרֵיהֶם בְּפִיהֶם יִרְצוּ סֶֽלָה (Tehillim 49:14): those after them are their sons, and the sons of the wicked are pleased with what their father charged them concerning the oppression and the violence, which is בְּפִיהֶם, by what they say to them and charge them. It is also read from going: they go after them to death in their going, and בְּפִיהֶם stands for כפיהם, like them, as in אִישׁ כְּפִי עֲבֹֽדָתֽוֹ (Bamidbar 7:5), each man as his service, and לְפִי אָכְלוֹ (Shemos 12:4), as his eating, in both of which the word means "like".

שׁמם.sense: Desolation, שממה, all of it one sense: some of it ruin, a place lying waste, and some of it astonishment.

more.h: The two sides of the one sense
more.t: Ruin: עַל הַר־צִיּוֹן שֶׁשָּׁמֵם (Eichah 5:18), for Har Tzion that lies desolate, and שְׁמָמָה תִֽהְיֶה כָּל־הָאָרֶץ (Yirmiyahu 4:27), the whole land will be a desolation. Astonishment: כַּֽאֲשֶׁר שָֽׁמְמוּ עָלֶיךָ רַבִּים (Yeshayahu 52:14), as many were astonished at you; יָשֹׁמּוּ יְשָׁרִים עַל־זֹאת (Iyov 17:8), the upright will be astonished at this; שֹׁמּוּ שָׁמַיִם (Yirmiyahu 2:12), be astonished, heavens; and וָאֵֽשְׁבָה מְשׁוֹמֵֽם (Ezra 9:3), I sat astonished.

In Radak's view אֶשֹּׁם וְאֶשְׁאַף (Yeshayahu 42:14), I will lay waste and swallow up, is transitive, and so שַׁמּוֹת וְשָׁאֹף אֶתְכֶם מִסָּבִיב (Yechezkel 36:3), laying you waste and swallowing you from every side. מַשְׁמִים בְּתוֹכָם (Yechezkel 3:15), astonished among them, is intransitive. וְעַל כְּנַף שִׁקּוּצִים מְשֹׁמֵם (Daniel 9:27), and upon the wing of abominations one that astonishes, is transitive, astonishing those who see it; and it may be intransitive as well, that at the spreading of the abominations a man will be astonished and wondering.

שִֽׁמְמוֹת עוֹלָם אֶתֶּנְךָ (Yechezkel 35:9), I will make you everlasting desolations; מְשַׁמָּה, a desolation, as כִּֽי־מֵי נִמְרִים מְשַׁמּוֹת יִֽהְיוּ (Yeshayahu 15:6), for the waters of Nimrim will be desolations; בִּמְשׂוּרָה וּבְשִׁמָּמוֹן יִשְׁתּֽוּ (Yechezkel 4:16), they will drink by measure and in astonishment; and שַׁמָּה וְשַֽׁעֲרוּרָה (Yirmiyahu 5:30), an astonishment and a horrible thing.

more.h: A command, and how to point it
more.t: פְּנֽוּ־אֵלַי וְהָשַׁמּוּ (Iyov 21:5), turn to me and be astonished: the shin has no dagesh and the heh is read with a full kamatz, as the accurate books have it, and it is a command whose pasach under the shin stands for a tzere, its rule being וְהָשֵׁמּוּ. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the shin has a dagesh, so that the heh is read with a chataf kamatz; he too explains it as a command, and says it should have gone like הָסֵבִּי עֵינַיִךְ (Shir HaShirim 6:5), turn your eyes away.

אִם־לֹא יַשִּׁים עֲלֵיהֶם נְוֵהֶֽם (Yirmiyahu 49:20), will he not make their fold desolate over them, is of this root; his father writes that the root of ישים is יָשַׁם, and Radak has already written it there.

כִּֽי־רַבִּים בְּֽנֵי־ שׁוֹמֵמָה (Yeshayahu 54:1), for the children of the desolate one are many, that is, a woman who has no husband. The adjective is also שָׂמַנִי שֹׁמֵֽם (Eichah 3:11), He made me desolate, and הָיוּ בָנַי שֽׁוֹמֵמִים (Eichah 1:16), my children are desolate, which appears with a nun for the mem at כָּל־שְׁעָרֶיהָ שֽׁוֹמֵמִין (Eichah 1:4), all her gates are desolate.

שֹמם.sense: The שְׂמָמִית of Mishlei: to Rabbi Yonah the swallow, to some a creature kept in kings' palaces for sport; it may be the spider, and Radak argues it is not the swallow.

more.t: שְׂמָמִית בְּיָדַיִם תְּתַפֵּשׂ (Mishlei 30:28), the semamis takes hold with her hands. Rabbi Yonah wrote that it is the katuf in Arabic, which is the דרור, the swallow, called orondola in la'az. Some explain that it is the one called bugia in la'az, whose shape is like a man's shape, which takes in its hands whatever is given it and is kept in the palaces of a king to play with. And it can be explained as the aranya of la'az, the spider, the one that builds her house even in the palaces of a king.

And so in the words of Chazal (Shabbos 76b): there are five fears of the weak upon the strong, the fear of the mafgia upon the lion, of the mosquito upon the elephant, of the kilbis upon the leviathan, of the סנונית upon the eagle, and of the שממית upon the scorpion; and the שממית there is explained as aranya in la'az. Rabbeinu Hai explained the סנונית, the swallow, as the katuf in Arabic; if so, Radak concludes, the שממית is not the katuf.

סלח.sense: To forgive. He gives the word no gloss, only its forms: the verb, being forgiven, סַלָּח, forgiving, and סְלִיחָה, forgiveness.

more.t: The pesukim and nothing more: סָלַחְתִּי כִּדְבָרֶֽךָ (Bamidbar 14:20), I have forgiven according to your word; לֹֽא־יֹאבֶה י"י סְלֹחַ לוֹ (Devarim 29:19), Hashem will not be willing to forgive him; סְֽלַֽח־נָא לַֽעֲוֹן הָעָם הַזֶּה (Bamidbar 14:19), forgive, please, the sin of this people; in the passive וְנִסְלַח לֽוֹ (Vayikra 4:26), and he will be forgiven; the adjective טוֹב וְסַלָּח (Tehillim 86:5), good and forgiving; and the noun כִּי־עִמְּךָ הַסְּלִיחָה (Tehillim 130:4), for with You is forgiveness.

גרן.sense: The threshing floor; its sense, he says, is known, and he gives three pesukim for it and nothing more.

more.t: גֹּרֶן וָיֶקֶב לֹא יִרְעֵם (Hoshea 9:2), threshing floor and winepress will not feed them; וּמָֽלְאוּ הַגֳּרָנוֹת בָּר (Yoel 2:24), the threshing floors will be full of grain; and מְדֻשָׁתִי וּבֶן־ גָּרְנִי (Yeshayahu 21:10), my threshed one and the son of my threshing floor. Of all of them he says only ידוע, it is known.

דגל.sense: The דֶּגֶל, the standard that the heads of the troops raise; and a verb comes from it, which he gives without a gloss.

more.t: דֶּגֶל מַֽחֲנֵה יְהוּדָה (Bamidbar 2:3), the standard of the camp of Yehudah, pointed בשש נקדות, with six dots. He glosses it הנס שמרימין ראשי החיילות, the standard that the heads of the troops raise.

דָּגוּל מֵרְבָבָֽה (Shir HaShirim 5:10), marked out above ten thousand; וּבְשֵֽׁם־אֱלֹהֵינוּ נִדְגֹּל (Tehillim 20:6), in the name of our God we will raise our banner; and אֲיֻמָּה כַּנִּדְגָּלֽוֹת (Shir HaShirim 6:4), awesome as ranks under their banners.

כתל.sense: The wall: אַחַר כָּתְלֵנוּ (Shir HaShirim 2:9), behind our wall, which he glosses הוא הקיר, it is the wall.

אפה.sense: To bake. Baking is always said of bread; of other foods, he says, the word is cooking.

more.h: A thing named by what it becomes
more.t: וּמַצּוֹת אָפָה (Bereishis 19:3), he baked matzos, and וְאַף אָפִיתִי עַל־גֶּחָלָיו לֶחֶם (Yeshayahu 44:15), I have baked bread on its coals, are על שם סופו, after what the thing ends as, since it is not called לחם, bread, until it is baked. So too וְטַֽחֲנִי קָמַח (Yeshayahu 47:2), grind flour; וַתִּקַּח אֶת־הַבָּצֵק (Shmuel II 13:8), she took the dough and kneaded it; וּבִגְדֵי עֲרוּמִּים תַּפְשִֽׁיט (Iyov 22:6), you strip the garments of the naked; נִשְׁבְּרָה קִרְיַת־תֹּהוּ (Yeshayahu 24:10), the city of emptiness is broken; יָהֵב חָכְמְתָא לְחַכִּימִין (Daniel 2:21), He gives wisdom to the wise; יוּמַת הַמֵּת (Devarim 17:6), the dead man shall be put to death; and וְיָֽצְאוּ יְלָדֶיהָ (Shemos 21:22), her children come out, though they were not born but only fit to be children.

וַתֹּפֵהוּ מַצּֽוֹת (Shmuel I 28:24), she baked it into matzos; אֵת אֲשֶׁר־ תֹּאפוּ אֵפוּ (Shemos 16:23), bake what you will bake.
