The baker: תַנּוּר בֹּעֵרָה מֵֽאֹפֶה (Hoshea 7:4), an oven burning from the baker, that is, מצד האופה שמבעירו, from the side of the baker who kindles it, and מִחוּץ הָֽאֹפִים (Yirmiyahu 37:21), from the street of the bakers. In the passive, לֹא תֵֽאָפֶה חָמֵץ (Vayikra 6:10), it shall not be baked leavened, and חָמֵץ תֵּֽאָפֶינָה (Vayikra 23:17), they shall be baked leavened. The noun is מַֽאֲפֵה תַנּוּר (Vayikra 2:4), an oven's baking.

תֻּֽפִינֵי מִנְחַת פִּתִּים (Vayikra 6:14), the bakings of a mincha of pieces, is another pattern, the alef exchanged for a quiescent vav with a nun added at the end. It is said in the plural because the offering was baked many bakings: scalded in boiling water, then baked in the oven, then fried again in a pan.

ציר.sense: צִיר נֶאֱמָן לְשֹֽׁלְחָיו (Mishlei 25:13), a faithful envoy to those who send him. The matter is set out already at the root צוּר.

שׁגר.sense: Sending: שְׁגַר־אֲלָפֶיךָ, the sending forth of your cattle, and שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה, a beast's sending forth. Chazal made it their usual word for sending.

more.t: שְׁגַר־אֲלָפֶיךָ (Devarim 7:13), the sending forth of your cattle; and in another pattern, pointed with the six dots, וְכָל־פֶּטֶר שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה (Shemos 13:12), every firstling, a beast's sending forth. ענינם ענין שלוח, their sense is sending, as in יְשַׁלְּחוּ כַצֹּאן עֲוִֽילֵיהֶם (Iyov 21:11), they send out their little ones like a flock.

In this sense Chazal say (Bava Basra 23a) מלא שגר היונה, the full sending of a dove, which he explains as שלוח היונה והליכתה, the dove's being sent out and her going. Chazal made the word usual for sending, as they say (Bava Basra 146a) שגר אחריו, he sent after him, and much else besides.

רפסד.sense: Rafts: beams tied together and taken along the rivers and the sea; they are the דוברות named in Melachim.

more.t: רַפְסֹדוֹת עַל־יָם יָפוֹ (Divrei HaYamim II 2:15), rafts by sea to Yafo, are the דוברות named in the book of Melachim (Melachim I 5:23), הקורות שקושרין אותן ביחד, the beams that are tied together and taken along the rivers and the sea. He gives their name in the vernacular.

more.h: In the Mishnah and the Yerushalmi
more.t: The Mishnah (Berachos 4:6, 28b) has היה יושב בספינה או באסדא, one who was sitting in a boat or on a raft, and the Talmud Yerushalmi there says היא אסדא היא אכסדיא היא רפסודות, the אסדא and the אכסדיא and the רפסודות are one thing.

דוג.sense: The fisher and the fish: דַּוָּגִים, a word describing those who catch fish, and דָּג, the fish, in its several forms.

more.t: עָלָיו דַּוָּגִים (Yechezkel 47:10), fishers over it: דַּוָּגִים is a word describing those who catch fish. With a yud in place of the vav, לְדַיָּגִים (Yirmiyahu 16:16), for fishers, and in the same pasuk וְדִיגוּם, and they will fish them.
Some grammarians say it is of the heavy verb, and the yud ought to take a dagesh. He says it may rather be of the augmented form, lacking the heh of the binyan, the full form being והדיגום.

דָּג גָּדוֹל (Yonah 2:1), a great fish; written with an alef in מְבִיאִים דָּאג (Nechemiah 13:16), bringing fish; דְּגֵי הַיָּם (Bamidbar 11:22), the fish of the sea; in the feminine מִמְּעֵי הַדָּגָֽה (Yonah 2:2), from the belly of the fish; and as a collective וְהַדָּגָה אֲשֶׁר־בַּיְאֹר תָּמוּת (Shemos 7:18), the fish in the river will die, דְגַת ־יְאֹרֶיךָ (Yechezkel 29:4), the fish of your rivers, and תִּבְאַשׁ דְּגָתָם מֵאֵין מַיִם (Yeshayahu 50:2), their fish stink for want of water. He says he has already written of these at the root דָּגָה.
בְּסִירוֹת דּוּגָֽה (Amos 4:2), in fishing boats: דּוּגָה is another pattern of the word, and he does not gloss it here.

טמן.sense: To hide: all of it, he says, is the sense of concealing and putting out of sight; and מַטְמוֹן, a hidden store.

more.t: טָמַן עָצֵל יָדוֹ בַּצַּלָּחַת (Mishlei 19:24), the sluggard hides his hand in the dish; טָמְנוּ פַח לִי (Tehillim 142:4), they hid a trap for me; וּטְמַנְתָּם בַּמֶּלֶט (Yirmiyahu 43:9), and hide them in the mortar; טְמַנְתִּיו שָׁמָּה (Yirmiyahu 13:7), I had hidden it there; וַיַּךְ אֶת־הַמִּצְרִי וַיִּטְמְנֵהוּ בַּחוֹל (Shemos 2:12), he struck the Mitzri and hid him in the sand; וַיִּטְמֹן אֹתָם יַעֲקֹב תַּחַת הָאֵלָה (Bereishis 35:4), Yaakov hid them under the terebinth; טָמוּן בָּאָרֶץ חַבְלוֹ (Iyov 18:10), his cord is hidden in the ground; and לִטְמוֹן בְּחֻבִּי עֲוֹנִי (Iyov 31:33), to hide my sin in my bosom.
Another form, וְהִטָּמֵן בֶּעָפָר (Yeshayahu 2:10), hide in the dust; and the heavy form, וַיֵּלְכוּ וַיַּטְמִנוּ (Melachim II 7:8), and they went and hid.

The noun: נָתַן לָכֶם מַטְמוֹן (Bereishis 43:23), He has given you a hidden store; כִּי־יֶשׁ־לָנוּ מַטְמֹנִים בַּשָּׂדֶה (Yirmiyahu 41:8), for we have hidden stores in the field; and with a shuruk, וּמַטְמֻנֵי מִסְתָּרִים (Yeshayahu 45:3), and hoards in secret places. פְּנֵיהֶם חֲבֹשׁ בַּטָּמוּן (Iyov 40:13), bind their faces in the hidden place, means to the place where one hides them.

גנז.sense: גִּנְזֵי, like אוצרות, treasuries: a place, or vessels, into which gold and silver and precious garments are put.

more.t: אֶל־ גִּנְזֵי הַמֶּֽלֶךְ (Esther 3:9), to the king's treasuries, and וּבְגִנְזֵי בְּרֹמִים (Yechezkel 27:24), and in treasuries of beromim.

שׁמשׁ.sense: The sun; and שִׁמְשֹׁתַיִךְ, the windows that the sun comes in by.

more.t: שֶׁמֶשׁ יָרֵחַ עָמַד זְבֻלָה (Chavakuk 3:11), sun and moon stood in their dwelling: שֶׁמֶשׁ is pointed בשש נקודות, with six dots, and the phrase means שמש וירח, the sun and the moon.

יוֹמָם הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ לֹֽא־יַכֶּכָּה (Tehillim 121:6), by day the sun will not strike you; הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ יָצָא עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 19:23), the sun had come out over the earth; וְזָרַח הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ (Koheles 1:5), the sun rises; לֹֽא־יָבוֹא עוֹד שִׁמְשֵׁךְ (Yeshayahu 60:20), your sun will set no more; שֶׁמֶשׁ צְדָקָה (Malachi 3:20), a sun of righteousness; and לְעֵינֵי הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ הַזֹּֽאת (Shmuel II 12:11), before this sun.
וְשַׂמְתִּי כַּֽדְכֹד שִׁמְשֹׁתַיִךְ (Yeshayahu 54:12), and I will make your windows of kadkod, which he glosses החלונות שהשמש נכנס בהם, the windows the sun enters by.

סהר.sense: The moon: the Targum renders יָרֵחַ, the moon, with סִיהֲרָא. The women's mirrors are called שהרונים for being like it, and the prison is round in its likeness.

more.t: שָׁרְרֵךְ אַגַּן הַסַּהַר (Shir HaShirim 7:3), your navel is a bowl of the moon; and the Targum of יָרֵחַ (Tehillim 8:4), the moon, is סִיהֲרָא.

For this מראות הנשים, the women's mirrors, are called שהרונים, as in וְהַשְּׁבִיסִים וְהַשַּֽׂהֲרֹנִֽים (Yeshayahu 3:18), and the shevisim and the saharonim, because they are like the סהר, the moon. That word, he notes, is written with a sin.
בֵּית הַסֹּהַר (Bereishis 39:20), the house of the sohar, is the name of the prison, שהוא עגול בדמות הסהר, which is round in the likeness of the moon.

מנח.sense: מִנְחָה, a gift or offering, its mem perhaps of the root, perhaps added; the evening and morning olah are so called, and the prayer is named for the evening one's hour.

more.h: Whether the mem is of the root
more.t: וַיָּכִינוּ אֶת־ הַמִּנְחָה (Bereishis 43:25), and they made ready the gift, and אַל־תֵּפֶן אֶל־ מִנְחָתָם (Bamidbar 16:15), do not turn to their offering: of this word some say the mem is of the root. It may rather be added, the root being נָחָה, and that is the closer to the sense, since מנחה is of the sense of נחה, just as it is also called אֲרוּחָה, from the sense of אָרַח. But the truth cannot be settled, because the plural is not found in Scripture.

Since they read מנחות in the Mishnah with a sheva under the mem, and so it is read in every mouth, מְנָחוֹת, the mem looks to be of the root: as from גִּבְעָה you say גְּבָעוֹת, so from מִנְחָה you say מְנָחוֹת. Were the mem added, it should have carried a chirik, as מִצְוָה gives מִצְוֹת and מַחְתָּה gives מַחְתּוֹת.

The evening olah is called מנחה: הַקְטֵר אֶת־עֹֽלַת־הַבֹּקֶר וְאֶת־ מִנְחַת הָעֶרֶב (Melachim II 16:15), burn the morning olah and the evening minchah, and מַֽשְׂאַת כַּפַּי מִנְחַת ־עָֽרֶב (Tehillim 141:2), the lifting of my hands as an evening offering. וַיְהִי בַּֽעֲלוֹת הַמִּנְחָה וַיִּגַּשׁ אֵֽלִיָּהוּ הַנָּבִיא (Melachim I 18:36), and it was at the going up of the minchah that Eliyahu HaNavi came near, means at the time the מנחה went up. The morning olah too is called מנחה: וַיְהִי בַבֹּקֶר כַּֽעֲלוֹת הַמִּנְחָה, and it was in the morning, as the minchah went up, means at the hour they offer the morning minchah.

more.h: The prayer named from the hour
more.t: The prayer of מנחה is so called because it falls at the hour the evening מנחה goes up, והוא עת נטות השמש, the time the sun turns down. So וַֽאֲנִי ישֵׁב מְשׁוֹמֵם עַד לְמִנְחַת הָעָֽרֶב (Ezra 9:4), I sat appalled until the evening מנחה, and וּבְמִנְחַת הָעֶרֶב קַמְתִּי מִתַּֽעֲנִיתִי (Ezra 9:5), at the evening מנחה I rose from my fast.

נתן.sense: To give. He sets out the forms and at the end says only ענינם ידוע, their sense is known.

more.t: On וְאֹיְבַי תַּתָּה לִּי עֹרֶף (Shmuel II 22:41), and my enemies, You gave me their back, he notes בחסרון הקצוות, with the ends missing, not as the past tense usually runs. וַאֲנַחְנוּ נִתַּן ־לָךְ (Shoftim 16:5), and we will give you, carries a patach, לגזרת אֶפְעַל, for the אפעל pattern. And לְתִתֵּן שָׁם אֶת־אֲרוֹן בְּרִית (Melachim I 6:19), to set there the ark of the covenant, he calls an infinitive with the nun added.

וַיִּתֶּן ־יָד (Bereishis 38:28), he put out a hand; תְּנָה אֶת־יָדֶךָ (Melachim II 10:15), give your hand; נָתְנוּ יָד תַּחַת שְׁלֹמֹה (Divrei HaYamim I 29:24), they gave the hand under Shlomo; and מִצְרַיִם נָתַנּוּ יָד (Eichah 5:6), to Mitzrayim we gave the hand. He sets them in a row and glosses none of them.

נִתְּנָה רֹאשׁ (Bamidbar 14:4), let us set a head; וְנָתוֹן אֹתוֹ עַל כָּל־אֶרֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (Bereishis 41:43), setting him over all the land of Mitzrayim; תְּנוּ אֶת־אֲרֽוֹן־הַקֹּדֶשׁ בַּבַּיִת (Divrei HaYamim II 35:3), put the holy ark in the house; נְתֻנִים נְתֻנִים הֵמָּה לִי (Bamidbar 8:16), given, given they are to Me; and שְֽׂאוּ־זִמְרָה וּתְנוּ ־תֹף (Tehillim 81:3), raise a song and sound the drum.

כְּבוֹד הַלְּבָנוֹן נִתַּן ־לָהּ (Yeshayahu 35:2), the glory of Levanon was given her; וְהִוא לֹֽא־ נִתְּנָה לוֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה (Bereishis 38:14), and she was not given him to wife; תֶּבֶן אֵין נִתָּן לַֽעֲבָדֶיךָ (Shemos 5:16), no straw is given your servants; and הִנָּתֹן תִּנָּתֵן הָעִיר הַזֹּאת (Yirmiyahu 38:3), this city will surely be given. Where the doer is not named, וְכִי יֻֽתַּן ־מַיִם עַל־זֶרַע (Vayikra 11:38), if water be put on seed.

וּמִן־ הַנְּתִינִים שֶׁנָּתַן דָּוִיד וְהַשָּׂרִים לַֽעֲבֹדַת הַֽלְוִיִּם (Ezra 8:20), of the Nesinim whom David and the officers gave for the service of the Leviim. The nouns are מֹהַר וּמַתָּן (Bereishis 34:12), bride price and gift; תְּרוּמַת מַתָּנָם (Bamidbar 18:11), the offering of their gift; עֲבֹדַת מַתָּנָה (Bamidbar 18:7), a service of gift; אִישׁ כְּמַתְּנַת יָדוֹ (Devarim 16:17), each man according to the gift of his hand; and in another pattern וְאֶתְּנָה לְךָ מַתָּֽת (Melachim I 13:7), and I will give you a gift.

תור.sense: To search out and explore; also the turtledove; a time; and תכונה, the set measure or order of a thing, which may be the sense of the Torah itself.

more.t: תַּרְתִּי בְלִבִּי (Koheles 2:3), I searched in my heart; אֲשֶׁר תָּרוּ אֹתָהּ (Bamidbar 13:32), which they searched out; וְלֹא תָתוּרוּ אַֽחֲרֵי לְבַבְכֶם (Bamidbar 15:39), do not go searching after your heart. וַיָּתִירוּ בֵֽית־יוֹסֵף (Shoftim 1:23), the house of Yosef searched out, means חקירה וחפוש, examining and searching; and from it is יְתוּר הָרִים מִרְעֵהוּ (Iyov 39:8), the searching of the mountains is his pasture, יְתוּר being a noun on the pattern of יְקוּם, living substance, and יְבוּל, produce.

לְבַד מֵֽאַנְשֵׁי הַתָּרִים וְהַסֹּֽחֲרִים (Divrei HaYamim II 9:14), besides the men who were searchers and traders: the התרים are the lesser traders, few in goods and dealings, who search hard over what they buy and sell because their business is small, while the סוחרים are the great merchants.
By the Targum's reading, דֶּרֶךְ הָֽאֲתָרִים (Bamidbar 21:1), the way of the searchers, is from this root, the alef being added.

וְתֹר וְגוֹזָֽל (Bereishis 15:9), a turtledove and a young pigeon; וְהִקְרִיב מִן־ הַתֹּרִים (Vayikra 1:14), and he shall offer of the turtledoves; and שְׁתֵּי תֹרִים (Vayikra 5:7), two turtledoves; the bird is well known. The Torah says הָאֶחָד, the one, in the masculine, at וְעָשָׂה אֶת־הָֽאֶחָד מִן־ הַתֹּרִים (Vayikra 14:30), and he shall offer the one of the turtledoves, and שְׁתֵּי, two, in the feminine, to teach that male and female are alike fit. From this, אַל־תִּתֵּן לְחַיַּת נֶפֶשׁ תּוֹרֶךָ (Tehillim 74:19), do not give the soul of Your turtledove to the wild beast, where Knesses Yisrael is likened to a turtledove, as she is likened also to a dove.

more.h: A time, and a man's measure
more.t: תֹּר נַֽעֲרָה וְנַֽעֲרָה (Esther 2:12), the time of each girl, means a time. וּרְאִיתַנִי כְּתוֹר הָֽאָדָם הַמַּֽעֲלָה (Divrei HaYamim I 17:17), and You have seen me as the measure of the man of high degree, is כתכונת האדם, after the measure of a man: this height and greatness You have spoken of me is the measure of a great man, but what am I and what is my house? That is why the pasuk says הַמַּֽעֲלָה, of high degree: You saw me in a great measure, the measure of a great man, though I am small and lowly. So too וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הָֽאָדָם (Shmuel II 7:19), and this is the measure of a man.

more.h: The Torah, and the rows of pearls
more.t: It may be that וְזֹאת הַתּוֹרָה (Devarim 4:44), and this is the Torah, is of this root, and with it the pasuk the Torah of Hashem is perfect (Tehillim 19:8), all of them alike in this sense, since they mean תכונה, a set measure, as he explained at the root יָרָה. Near to it is נָאווּ לְחָיַיִךְ בַּתֹּרִים (Shir HaShirim 1:10), your cheeks are comely in the rows, which are the pearls joined together and set in a fixed order.

למד.sense: To learn, and to teach; and of the taught and accustomed, whose sense is learning and habit. The ox goad, מַלְמַד, is named for teaching the oxen to plough.

more.t: בַּל־ לָמַד צֶדֶק (Yeshayahu 26:10), he has not learned righteousness, which he marks מלרע, stressed on the last syllable; יִשְׁמְעוּ וְלָמְדוּ (Devarim 31:13), they will hear and learn; לְמַעַן יִלְמַד לְיִרְאָה (Devarim 17:19), so that he may learn to fear; וַיִּלְמַד לִטְרָף־טֶרֶף (Yechezkel 19:3), he learned to tear prey; and אִם־ לָמֹד יִלְמְדוּ אֶת־דַּֽרְכֵי עַמִּי (Yirmiyahu 12:16), if they will indeed learn the ways of My people.

לִמַּד ־דַּעַת (Koheles 12:9), he taught knowledge; רְאֵה לִמַּדְתִּי אֶתְכֶם (Devarim 4:5), see, I have taught you; אֲשֶׁר אָֽנֹכִי מְלַמֵּד אֶתְכֶם (Devarim 4:1), which I teach you; עֶגְלָה מְלֻמָּדָה (Hoshea 10:11), a trained heifer; מְלֻמְּדֵי מִלְחָמָה (Shir HaShirim 3:8), trained in war; and where the doer is not named, כְּעֵגֶל לֹא לֻמָּד (Yirmiyahu 31:18), like a calf untrained.

וּלְמוּדֵי מִלְחָמָה, those trained for war; פֶּרֶה לִמֻּד מִדְבָּר (Yirmiyahu 2:24), a wild donkey used to the wilderness; לְשׁוֹן לִמּוּדִים (Yeshayahu 50:4), the tongue of the taught; לִמֻּדֵי הָרֵֽעַ (Yirmiyahu 13:23), trained to do evil; and וְכָל־בָּנַיִךְ לִמּוּדֵי י"י (Yeshayahu 54:13), all your children taught of Hashem. The sense of the last four is learning and habit, and it is well known. In another pattern, כַּקָּטֹן כַּגָּדוֹל מֵבִין עִם־ תַּלְמִֽיד (Divrei HaYamim I 25:8), the small as the great, the one who understands with the learner.

אַשּׁוּר כִּלֽמַד רֹֽכַלְתֵּֽךְ (Yechezkel 27:23), Ashur, as one accustomed, was your trader: לָמֵד is of the pattern of כָּבֵד, heavy, and in the construct לְמַד, as כְבַד ־פֶּה (Shemos 4:10), heavy of mouth. His father writes that the men of Ashur were as those accustomed to come to you always in trade. Radak adds that he will write of it further at the root רָכַל.

From this the staff with the needle fixed in its head, the one called a דָּֽרְבָן, a goad, is named מלמד: בְּמַלְמַד הַבָּקָר (Shoftim 3:31), the goad of the oxen, לפי שמלמד ומורה הבקר לחרישה, because it teaches and directs the oxen to plough.

עבט.sense: The pledge, a thing seized and held back in a man's hand; from it, being held back on the way; and lending, since a loan on a pledge is called by it.

more.t: לַֽעֲבֹט עֲבֹטֽוֹ (Devarim 24:10), to seize his pledge, and יוֹצִיא אֵלֶיךָ אֶת־הָֽעֲבוֹט (Devarim 24:11), he shall bring the pledge out to you. It is the pledge, a thing seized and held back in a man's hand.

From this comes וְלֹא יְעַבְּטוּן אֹֽרְחוֹתָֽם (Yoel 2:7), they are not held back in their paths, since they run swiftly, as it says כְּגִבּוֹרִים יְרֻצוּן, they run like mighty men. So the Targum renders וְלָא מְעַכְּבִין אוֹרְחָתְהוֹן, they do not delay their paths. Some read it as not lending their paths one to another, from וְהַֽעֲבֵט תַּֽעֲבִיטֶנּוּ (Devarim 15:8), you shall surely lend him, since the pasuk says וְאִישׁ בִּדְרָכָיו יֵֽלֵכוּן, each man goes in his own ways. Others read it as not twisting or perverting, and so it is in Arabic.

וְהַֽעֲבֵט תַּֽעֲבִיטֶנּוּ (Devarim 15:8), you shall surely lend him דֵּי מַחְסֹרוֹ, enough for his need, because a loan made against a pledge is called העבט. The Targum renders אוֹזָפָא תּוֹזְפִנֵּהּ, you shall surely lend him. So too וְהַֽעֲבַטְתָּ גּוֹיִם רַבִּים (Devarim 15:6), and you will lend to many nations, and וְאַתָּה לֹא תַֽעֲבֹט (Devarim 15:6), and you will not borrow.
עַבְטִיט may be from this root, on the pattern of סַגְרִיר, steady rain, meaning a great deal of money; he has written at the root טִיט that it is a compound word.

צבה.sense: The belly swelling; of this root too צְבִי, the gazelle, and צְבִי, desire and will, for which he says Eretz Yisrael is called צבי; Chazal give another reason.

more.t: וְצָֽבְתָה בִטְנָהּ (Bamidbar 5:27), and her belly will swell; the feminine adjective, וְאֶת־בִּטְנֵךְ צָבָֽה (Bamidbar 5:21), and your belly swollen; and where the verb makes the belly swell, לַצְבּוֹת בֶּטֶן (Bamidbar 5:22), to make the belly swell, whose proper form would be לְהַצְבּוֹת, as לַנְחֹתָם (Shemos 13:21), to lead them, stands for להנחותם.

אַיָּל וּֽצְבִי (Devarim 14:5), the hart and the gazelle, and תָּאֳמֵי צְבִיָּֽה (Shir HaShirim 7:4), the twins of a gazelle. The plural כְּאַחַד הַצְּבָיִם (Shmuel II 2:18), as one of the gazelles, has lost the yud of the plural; וְכִצְבָאיִם עַל־הֶֽהָרִים לְמַהֵֽר (Divrei HaYamim I 12:8 in his edition), and like gazelles on the mountains for swiftness, is written with an alef and a yud, the alef silent and the yud sounded, and the plural's yud dropped. In the feminine plural the yud is exchanged for an alef: בִּצְבָאוֹת אוֹ בְּאַיְלוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה (Shir HaShirim 2:7), by the gazelles or by the hinds of the field. It is a known animal.

נַֽחֲלַת צְבִי (Yirmiyahu 3:19), an inheritance of desire; צְבִי הִיא לְכָל־הָֽאֲרָצֽוֹת (Yechezkel 20:6), it is the desire of all the lands; לַֽעֲטֶרֶת צְבִי (Yeshayahu 28:5), for a crown of desire; הַצְּבִי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shmuel II 1:19), the desire of Yisrael; לִצְבִי וּלְכָבוֹד (Yeshayahu 4:2), for desire and for honour: ענינם החפץ והרצון, their sense is desire and will. In Aramaic too, דִּֽי־הֲוָא צָבֵא הֲוָה קָטֵל (Daniel 5:19), whom he wished, he would kill. Some explain all of them as לשון הדר ופאר, splendour and glory. In נַֽחֲלַת צְבִי צִבְאוֹת גּוֹיִם (Yirmiyahu 3:19), an inheritance of desire, the desires of the nations, the feminine plural has its yud exchanged for an alef; though צבאות גוים may be from צָבָא.

more.h: Why Eretz Yisrael is called צבי
more.t: From this sense Eretz Yisrael is called צבי: אֶל־הַנֶּגֶב וְאֶל־הַמִּזְרָח וְאֶל־ הַצֶּֽבִי (Daniel 8:9), toward the south and toward the east and toward the land of desire; וְיַֽעֲמֹד בְּאֶֽרֶץ־ הַצְּבִי (Daniel 11:16), and he will stand in the land of desire; בֵּין יַמִּים לְהַר־ צְבִי ־קֹדֶשׁ (Daniel 11:45), between the seas and the mountain of holy desire; because it is a land of desire. Chazal (Kesubos 112a) hold that it is called צבי for another reason: as the gazelle is swifter of foot than all the beasts, so Eretz Yisrael is quicker than all lands to ripen her fruits.

עמת.sense: עָמִית, a fellow, a companion; and לְעֻמַּת, over against, opposite.

more.t: וְעַל־גֶּבֶר עֲמִיתִי (Zecharyah 13:7), against the man who is My fellow; וְכִחֵשׁ בַּעֲמִיתוֹ (Vayikra 5:21), and he deals falsely with his fellow; וְאֶל־אֵשֶׁת עֲמִיתְךָ (Vayikra 18:20), to your fellow's wife. All of them, he says, are חבר, a companion.

לְעֻמַּת הֶעָצֶה יְסִירֶנָּה (Vayikra 3:9), he shall remove it over against the backbone, is לנכח העצה, opposite the backbone, and וְקוֹל הָאוֹפַנִּים לְעֻמָּתָם (Yechezkel 3:13), and the sound of the wheels over against them, is לנכחם, opposite them. The lamed in them is a servile letter, as in לְנִכְחוֹ and לְנֶגְדּוֹ, opposite him and before him. With a cholam, לְעֻמּוֹת אַחַד הַחֲלָקִים (Yechezkel 45:7), over against one of the portions, is like לְעֻמַּת, as שְׁבֻעוֹת יָמִים מַצּוֹת יֵאָכֵל (Yechezkel 45:21), for seven days matzos shall be eaten, is like שבעת ימים.

כָּל־עֻמַּת שֶׁבָּא (Koheles 5:15), just as he came, stands without the servile lamed. Some joined כָּל to עמת in the manner of the Aramaic כָּל־קְבַל־דִּנָה, all over against this. Radak holds right what the Gaon Ibn Giat wrote: לעמת never comes without its lamed, as לְמַעַן, for the sake of, never lacks its lamed, nor בַּעֲבוּר, because of, its beis; so in this phrase the kaf is the kaf of comparison and the lamed belongs to לְעֻמַּת, and it should have been one word, כָּלְעֻמַּת, and was written apart, as many joined words are, like וְלַאֲסוּרִים פְּקַח־קוֹחַ (Yeshayahu 61:1), and to the bound, release, two words whose sense is one.

תרע.sense: A single word, תִּרְעָתִים, explained as gatekeepers, and the Targum of a gate is תַרְעָא; Radak allows that it may be the name of a family.

more.t: One line, on תִּרְעָתִים שִׁמְעָתִים (Divrei HaYamim I 2:55), the Tir'asim, the Shim'asim, where תִּרְעָתִים has been explained as gatekeepers; and the Targum of שַׁעַר (Bereishis 22:17), a gate, is תַרְעָא. Radak allows that it may be the name of a family.

מזה.sense: Burnt: מְזֵי רָעָב (Devarim 32:24) is שרופי רעב, those burnt up with hunger.

more.t: לְמֵזֵא לְאַתּוּנָא (Daniel 3:19), to heat the furnace, carries the same sense, though the mem of לְמֵזֵא is not a root letter.

צפצף.sense: To chirp: chirping in birds, he says, is as speech in man. In another sense, the צַפְצָפָה, a kind of willow, and the inferior kind.

more.t: וּפֹצֶה פֶה וּמְצַפְצֵֽף (Yeshayahu 10:14), opening the mouth and chirping; הַֽמְצַפְצְפִים וְהַמַּהְגִּים (Yeshayahu 8:19), those who chirp and those who mutter; אִמְרָתֵךְ תְּצַפְצֵֽף (Yeshayahu 29:4), your speech will chirp. כְּסוּס עָגוּר כֵּן אֲצַפְצֵף (Yeshayahu 38:14), like a sus, an agur, so I chirp, he explains as כסוס כעגור, like a sus, like an agur. Chirping in birds is as speech in man. The sense of אִמְרָתֵךְ תְּצַפְצֵֽף is like that of תִּשַּׁח אִמְרָתֵךְ (Yeshayahu 29:4), your speech will be low, in the same pasuk.

In another sense, צַפְצָפָה שָׂמֽוֹ (Yechezkel 17:5), set as a צַפְצָפָה: a kind of willow, in Arabic צפצ"ף. It is the inferior kind, as Chazal said (Sukkah 34a) that ערבי נחל, willows of the brook, excludes the צפצפה that grows among the mountains.

more.h: The pasuk as Chazal read it
more.t: Chazal read the pasuk so (Sukkah 34a): קָח עַל־מַיִם רַבִּים צַפְצָפָה שָׂמֽוֹ, taken by abundant waters and set as a צַפְצָפָה, is I made them like the willow that grows by abundant waters, and they made themselves like the צפצפה that grows among the mountains. On their reading, he says, שָׂמוֹ is Yisrael setting itself so.

Yonasan renders צַפְצָפָה שָׂמֽוֹ as גְפַּן נִצְבָא שַׁוְיֵיהּ, he made it a planted vine. Radak takes the Targum to mean that although they took seed and sowed it, he set it as a planted vine, that is, it grew quickly.

חדשׁ.sense: To renew, with חָדָשׁ, new. The חֹדֶשׁ, the month, is named for the renewal of the moon; the word means the whole thirty days, and also the first day alone.

more.t: וְחִדְּשׁוּ עָרֵי חֹרֶב (Yeshayahu 61:4), they will renew the waste cities; תְּחַדֵּשׁ עֵדֶיךָ נֶגְדִּי (Iyov 10:17), You renew Your witnesses against me; and of itself, תִּתְחַדֵּשׁ כַּנֶּשֶׁר נְעוּרָֽיְכִי (Tehillim 103:5), your youth renews itself like the eagle. The whole sense of renewal is well known.

וְאֵין כָּל־ חָדָשׁ תַּחַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (Koheles 1:9), there is nothing new under the sun; וְיָשָׁן מִפְּנֵי חָדָשׁ תּוֹצִֽיאוּ (Vayikra 26:10), you shall bring out the old before the new; and חֲדָשִׁים לַבְּקָרִים (Eichah 3:23), new every morning. וְהוּא חָגוּר חֲדָשָׁה (Shmuel II 21:16), and he was girded with a new one, means a new sword; so וּמַֽאֲכָלוֹ בְּרִאָֽה (Chavakuk 1:16), and his food is fat, means a fat sheep, and וַֽאֲנִי תְפִלָּֽה (Tehillim 109:4), and I am prayer, means a man of prayer.

כִּֽי־יִקַּח אִישׁ אִשָּׁה חֲדָשָׁה (Devarim 24:5), when a man takes a new wife, means one new to him, which leaves out a man who takes back his own divorcee; a widow, or another man's divorcee, is included.

more.h: The month, and its first day
more.t: The חֹדֶשׁ is named for the renewal of the moon, which renews itself in it, and the whole thirty days together are called חדש. The first day alone, Rosh Chodesh, is also called חדש: מָחָר חֹדֶשׁ (Shmuel I 20:18), tomorrow is Rosh Chodesh; לֹֽא־ חֹדֶשׁ וְלֹא שַׁבָּת (Melachim II 4:23), it is neither Rosh Chodesh nor Shabbos; וְהָיָה מִֽדֵּי־ חֹדֶשׁ בְּחָדְשׁוֹ (Yeshayahu 66:23), and it shall be, each Rosh Chodesh in its time; בַּשַּׁבָּתוֹת וּבֶֽחֳדָשִׁים (Yechezkel 46:3), on the Shabbosos and on Roshei Chodashim. But in בְּיֽוֹם־ הַחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי (Shmuel I 20:34), on the second day of the month, it names the whole month. His father takes לֹֽא־חֹדֶשׁ וְלֹא שַׁבָּת of the whole thirty days, that is, not yet a month has passed, nor even a week, since you saw him. חֹדֶשׁ יָמִֽים (Bamidbar 11:20), a month of days, is a full month, thirty days.

עַתָּה יֹֽאכְלֵם חֹדֶשׁ אֶת־חֶלְקֵיהֶֽם (Hoshea 5:7), now a month shall devour them with their portions, is the month decreed upon them, the month of Av; and so בְּחָדְשָׁהּ יִמְצָאֽוּנְהָ (Yirmiyahu 2:24), in her month they will find her, is the month decreed upon her, when she cannot be saved from the hand of those who seek her. His father reads בְּחָדְשָׁהּ as an infinitive, in her renewing; that is, why do none who seek her weary? Because at every time they find her renewed, as though she were only now beginning to run before them.

פרע.sense: Rebelling, keeping far off and setting aside; in another sense, uncovering, as of the head and its hair; and in a third, vengeance.

more.t: שִׁמְעוּ מוּסָר וַֽחֲכָמוּ וְאַל־ תִּפְרָֽעוּ (Mishlei 8:33), hear instruction and be wise, and do not set it aside; וַתִּפְרְעוּ כָל־עֲצָתִי (Mishlei 1:25), you set all my counsel at nothing; פּוֹרֵעַ מוּסָר (Mishlei 15:32), one who sets instruction aside; פְּרָעֵהוּ אַל־תַּֽעֲבָר־בּוֹ (Mishlei 4:15), keep far from it, do not pass through it; בְּאֵין חָזוֹן יִפָּרַֽע עָם (Mishlei 29:18), where there is no vision a people rebels; and of making others leave off, תַּפְרִיעוּ אֶת־הָעָם מִֽמַּֽעֲשָׂיו (Shemos 5:4), you make the people leave off their work. The sense of all of them, and of those like them, is המרי והריחוק והבטול, rebellion, keeping far, and setting aside.

Some take them from the usage of Chazal (Megillah 17a), one who reads the Megillah למפרע, out of its order, that is, turning a thing backwards and reversed. So לֹֽא־ אֶפְרַע וְלֹֽא־אָחוּס (Yechezkel 24:14), I will not turn back and will not spare, is that He will not go back from what He has spoken.

In another sense, כִּי פָרֻעַ הוּא כִּֽי־פְרָעֹה אַֽהֲרֹן (Shemos 32:25), for it was uncovered, for Aharon had uncovered it: exposed in its evil deeds. וּפָרַע אֶת־רֹאשׁ הָֽאִשָּׁה (Bamidbar 5:18), and he shall uncover the woman's head: he uncovers the hair of her head that is hidden under the veil. וְרֹאשׁוֹ יִהְיֶה פָרוּעַ (Vayikra 13:45), and his head shall be uncovered; אֶת־רֹאשׁוֹ לֹא יִפְרָע (Vayikra 21:10), he shall not uncover his head; רָֽאשֵׁיכֶם אַל־ תִּפְרָעוּ (Vayikra 10:6), do not uncover your heads: since a mourner's way is to uncover his head and take off his turban or his cap and his headdress. And גַּדֵּל פֶּרַע שְׂעַר רֹאשֽׁוֹ (Bamidbar 6:5), letting the hair of his head grow uncovered, the pei with a segol: when his hair grows long it is uncovered below the turban.

Some explain בִּפְרֹעַ פְּרָעוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל (Shoftim 5:2) and כִּי הִפְרִיעַ בִּֽיהוּדָה (Divrei HaYamim II 28:19) from this sense of uncovering: on that reading, when things were laid bare in Yisrael, and for he laid things bare in Yehudah.

In a third sense, מראשׁ פַּרְעוֹת אויב (Devarim 32:42), from the first of the vengeances of the enemy: the פרעות are נקמות, vengeances. So too בפרוע פרעות בישראל, when vengeances were taken in Yisrael, and in the heavy form כִּי הִפְרִיעַ בִּֽיהוּדָה, for he took vengeance in Yehudah. The Targum of נְקֹם נִקְמַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Bamidbar 31:2), avenge the vengeance of the children of Yisrael, is אִתְפְּרַע פֻּרְעֲנוּת, exact the retribution.

משׁל.sense: Two senses: to rule, with הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה, the dominion; and the מָשָׁל, the likening of one thing to another (which also holds hidden matters), with being likened.

more.t: וְיָשַׁב וּמָשַׁל עַל־כִּסְאוֹ (Zecharyah 6:13), he will sit and rule on his throne; וּמָֽשַׁלְתָּ בְּגוֹיִם רַבִּים (Devarim 15:6), and you will rule over many nations; מְשָׁל ־בָּנוּ גַּם־אַתָּה (Shoftim 8:22), rule over us, you too; משֵׁל בִּגְבוּרָתוֹ (Tehillim 66:7), He rules by His might. The noun is in וּמָשַׁל מִמְשָׁל רַב (Daniel 11:3), and he will rule a great dominion, with the mem in chirik; and with a heh or a tav added, הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה הָרִאשֹׁנָה (Michah 4:8), the first dominion, לְמֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַיּוֹם (Bereishis 1:16), for the rule of the day, and וּמֶֽמְשַׁלְתְּךָ בְּכָל־דּוֹר וָדֽוֹר (Tehillim 145:13), and Your dominion is in every generation.

Another sense: הנה כָּל־ הַמֹּשֵׁל עָלַיִךְ יִמְשֹׁל (Yechezkel 16:44), see, everyone who speaks in parables will speak one about you; עַל־כֵּן יֹֽאמְרוּ הַמּֽשְׁלִים (Bamidbar 21:27), therefore those who speak in parables say; מֹֽשְׁלֵי הָעָם הַזֶּה (Yeshayahu 28:14), the speakers of parables of this people, which Yonasan took from the first sense and rendered שִׁלְטוֹנֵי עַמָא, the rulers of the people. The noun is לְהָבִין מָשָׁל (Mishlei 1:6), to understand a parable, וַיִּשָּׂא מְשָׁלוֹ (Bamidbar 23:7), and he took up his parable, לְמָשָׁל וְלִשְׁנִינָה (Devarim 28:36 in his edition), for a parable and a byword; and where a man makes them, הֲלֹא מְמַשֵּׁל מְשָׁלִים הֽוּא (Yechezkel 21:5), is he not a maker of parables? A מָשָׁל is the likening of one thing to another, and it also holds hidden matters.

In מְשַׁל הַקַּדְמֹנִי (Shmuel I 24:13 in his edition) the word is in the construct, and it means the parable of the ancient maker of parables; or else it is another pattern and not construct at all, and הקדמוני describes it: the ancient parable.

נִמְשַׁל כַּבְּהֵמוֹת (Tehillim 49:13), he is likened to the beasts; וְנִמְשַׁלְתִּי עִם־יוֹרְדֵי בֽוֹר (Tehillim 28:1), and I will be likened to those who go down to the pit; וָֽאֶתְמַשֵּׁל כֶּֽעָפָר וָאֵֽפֶר (Iyov 30:19), and I am likened to dust and ashes; and where one likens another, וְתַמְשִׁלוּנִי וְנִדְמֶֽה (Yeshayahu 46:5), and you liken Me, that we be alike. So too in this sense זִכְרֹֽנֵיכֶם מִשְׁלֵי־אֵפֶר (Iyov 13:12), your remembrances are likenings of ash.

The adjective from this is הַמִּמְשָׁלִים לְבֵית אֲבִיהֶם (Divrei HaYamim I 26:6), those likened to their father's house, meaning like them in might, for they were mighty men of valour. The mem comes with a chirik, as in עֲתַלְיָהוּ הַמִּרְשַׁעַת (Divrei HaYamim II 24:7), Atalyahu the wicked one, and וְהֶֽעָרִים הַמִּבְדָּלוֹת (Yehoshua 16:9), and the cities set apart.

ארץ.sense: Earth, a name for the whole world or a part of it; wider than תֵּבֵל, the settled lands, since ארץ takes in the wilderness too; and, as the earth is low, a low place.

more.t: אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָֽיִם (Bereishis 2:4), earth and heaven, with its six vowel points, is known: a name for the whole world or for some of it. It is more general than תֵּבֵל, since תבל takes in all the settled lands and ארץ the wilderness and the settled together. Sometimes it is one particular land: אֶרֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם (Bereishis 41:41), the land of Egypt, and הִנֵּה אַרְצִי לְפָנֶיךָ (Bereishis 20:15), behold, my land is before you.
Some say the root of ארץ is רץ, runs, and the alef is added, and that it is called so because the sphere is over it and goes round it continually.

It is used both as masculine and as feminine, mostly feminine. Masculine: וְלֹֽא־נָשָׂא אֹתָם הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 13:6), and the land did not bear them; נֶעְתַּם אָרֶץ (Yeshayahu 9:18), the land is darkened; אַךְ־בְּגוֹרָל יֵֽחָלֵק אֶת־ הָאָרֶץ (Bamidbar 26:55), only by lot shall the land be divided; שָׁרַץ אַרְצָם צְפַרְדְּעִים (Tehillim 105:30), their land swarmed with frogs. אָבַל אֻמְלְלָה אָרֶץ (Yeshayahu 33:9), the land mourns, it languishes, has both in one. The plural: וּמֵֽאֲרָצוֹת קִבְּצָם (Tehillim 107:3), and He gathered them from the lands, and אַרְצוֹת גּוֹיִם (Tehillim 105:44), the lands of nations.

Because the earth is low, a low place is called ארץ: רֻקַּמְתִּי בְּֽתַחְתִּיּוֹת אָֽרֶץ (Tehillim 139:15), I was wrought in the lowest parts of the earth, which is the womb; and like it אוֹפַן אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ (Yechezkel 1:15), one wheel upon the earth, meaning low against the ofanim above it.

זיז.sense: זִיז, by its place like זיו, radiance; some say it is a beast of the field, others a name for every beast of the field; in Vayikra Rabbah, a great bird.

more.t: וְהִתְעַנַּגְתֶּם מִזִּיז כְּבוֹדָֽהּ (Yeshayahu 66:11), and you will delight in the radiance of her glory, where by its place the sense is like זיו, radiance. So too Yonasan renders it מַחֲמַד יְקָרָהּ, the delight of her glory.

Some say it is the name of a beast of the field, as וְזִיז שָׂדַי עִמָּדִֽי (Tehillim 50:11), and the beast of the field is with Me, and וְזִיז שָׂדַי יִרְעֶֽנָּה (Tehillim 80:14), and the beast of the field grazes on it; and some say זיז is a general name for every beast of the field.

On וְזִיז שָׂדַי עִמָּדִֽי, Rabbi Yehudah beRabbi Simon said (Vayikra Rabbah 22) that the זיז is a great bird, and when it spreads its wings it darkens the disc of the sun, as it is written המבינתך יאבר נץ יפרוש כנפיו לתימן, is it by your understanding that the hawk soars and spreads his wings toward the south. There too: why is it called זיז? Because it has in it every kind of taste, מזה ומזה, of this and of that.

סוף.sense: To come to an end; from it סוֹף, the end of a thing; סוּפָה, the storm, which too brings things to an end; and סוּף, the rush, which may be named for its quick end.

more.t: סָפוּ תַמּוּ (Tehillim 73:19), they are spent and finished; וְזִכְרָם לֹא־ יָסוּף (Esther 9:28), their memory will not come to an end; יַחְדָּו יָסֻפוּ (Yeshayahu 66:17), together they will come to an end; and where the verb takes an object, אָסֵף כֹּל (Tzefaniah 1:2), I will make an end of everything. Their sense is ענין כליה, coming to an end. In אָסֹף אֲסִיפֵם (Yirmiyahu 8:13), I will make an utter end of them, the word אָסֹף is not of this root but of אָסַף, as he wrote under the alef, though it is of their sense.

From this sense, סוֹף דָּבָר הַכֹּל נִשְׁמָע (Koheles 12:13), the end of the matter, all has been heard; סוֹף כָּל־הָאָדָם (Koheles 7:2), the end of every man; and וּמְצָאתֶם אֹתָם בְּסוֹף הַנַּחַל (Divrei HaYamim II 20:17 in his edition), and you will find them at the end of the valley. All of them mean אחרית הדבר ותכליתו, the last of a thing and its finish.

The סוּפָה does not stand outside this sense: וּכְגַלְגַּל לִפְנֵי סוּפָֽה (Yeshayahu 17:13), like a thing that whirls before the storm; וּכְמֹץ גְּנָבַתּוּ סוּפָֽה (Iyov 21:18), like chaff the storm has stolen away; וְגַלְגִּלָּיו כַּסּוּפָֽה (Yeshayahu 5:28), and its wheels like the storm; כְּסוּפוֹת בַּנֶּגֶב לַֽחֲלֹף (Yeshayahu 21:1), like storms in the south sweeping through. It too is of ending, being the winds and the quakings that move things lightly and swiftly and bring them to an end.

In another sense, וַתָּשֶׂם בַּסּוּף עַל־שְׂפַת הַיְאֹֽר (Shemos 2:3), and she set it among the rushes on the bank of the river, and קָנֶה וָסוּף קָמֵֽלוּ (Yeshayahu 19:6), reed and rush have withered. It is the plant called גמא. A larger kind grows on the sea bed at the roots of the mountains, and of it is said סוּף חָבוּשׁ לְרֹאשִֽׁי (Yonah 2:6), the rush was bound about my head. This too does not stand outside the first sense, for it may be called so because it comes quickly to an end.

שׁאן.sense: To be quiet and tranquil; the sense of every form is השקט ושלוה, quiet and tranquillity.

more.t: The verb is found with its last letter doubled: שַׁאֲנַן מוֹאָב מִנְּעוּרָיו (Yirmiyahu 48:11), Moav has been tranquil from his youth; וְשָׁקַט וְשַֽׁאֲנַן (Yirmiyahu 30:10), and he shall be quiet and tranquil; וְשַֽׁאֲנַן מִפַּחַד רָעָֽה (Mishlei 1:33), and tranquil from the dread of evil. These three he marks as verbs, as against the adjective below, since they are pointed with patach, and the first root letter with a patach as well. יַחַד אֲסִירִים שַֽׁאֲנָנוּ (Iyov 3:18), prisoners are tranquil together, is said as well, with a kamatz under the nun though it stands at no pause, because of the sheva under the alef.

The adjective has a kamatz under the nun: לְעַשְׁתּוּת שַֽׁאֲנָן (Iyov 12:5), in the thought of the tranquil, and so נָוֶה שַֽׁאֲנָן (Yeshayahu 33:20), a tranquil dwelling. The plural takes a dagesh: הַשַּֽׁאֲנַנִּים בְּצִיּוֹן (Amos 6:1), the tranquil in Tziyon, וּבִמְנוּחֹת שַֽׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת (Yeshayahu 32:18), and in tranquil resting places, and נָשִׁים שַֽׁאֲנַנּוֹת (Yeshayahu 32:9), tranquil women. וְשַֽׁאֲנַנְךָ עָלָה בְאָזְנָי (Yeshayahu 37:29), your sha'anan has come up into My ears, is taken up under the root שָׁאָה.

In כֻּלּוֹ שַׁלְֽאֲנַן וְשָׁלֵֽיו (Iyov 21:23), all of him tranquil and at peace, the lamed is added; or the word is compounded of שָׁלֵו, at peace, and שַֽׁאֲנָן, tranquil, and that is the right one.

זהר.sense: To warn and to take warning; and in another sense to shine, זֹהַר being brightness.

more.t: וְהִזְהִיר אֶת־הָעָֽם (Yechezkel 33:3), and he warns the people; וְהִזְהַרְתָּה אֶתְהֶם (Shemos 18:20), and you shall warn them; וְלֹא הִזְהַרְתּוֹ (Yechezkel 3:18), and you did not warn him; and in וְהִזְהִירֹה (Melachim II 6:10), and he warned him, a heh stands in place of a vav. Of the one warned: חָיוֹ יִֽחְיֶה כִּי נִזְהָר (Yechezkel 3:21), he shall surely live because he was warned; אֶת־קוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר וְלֹא נִזְהָר (Yechezkel 33:4), the sound of the shofar, and was not warned; וְהָעָם לֹֽא־ נִזְהָר (Yechezkel 33:6), and the people were not warned; and וְהוּא נִזְהָר נַפְשׁוֹ מִלֵּֽט (Yechezkel 33:5), had he been warned he would have saved his life. All four have a kamatz and are past forms of the passive, in the sense of one who did not know to take heed. Also וְיֹתֵר מֵהֵמָּה בְּנִי הִזָּהֵר (Koheles 12:12), and more than these, my son, be warned. All of them are the sense of warning, and it is a known one.

וְהַמַּשְׂכִּלִים יַזְהִרוּ כְּזֹהַר הָֽרָקִיעַ (Daniel 12:3), and the wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament, and כְּמַרְאֵה־ זֹהַר כְּעֵין הַחַשְׁמַֽלָה (Yechezkel 8:2), like the appearance of brightness, like the colour of the chashmal. The sense is נגה, shining.

שׁבת.sense: To cease, to leave off and stop, and to make a thing cease. The noun שַׁבָּת is the Shabbos, and it can be a week, since every week has a Shabbos in it.

more.t: אֵיךְ שָׁבַת נֹגֵשׂ (Yeshayahu 14:4), how the oppressor has ceased; שָׁבַת מְשׂוֹשׂ לִבֵּנוּ (Eichah 5:15), the joy of our heart has ceased; שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַֽשׁ (Shemos 31:17), He ceased and rested; וְיוֹם וָלַיְלָה לֹא יִשְׁבֹּֽתוּ (Bereishis 8:22), and day and night shall not cease; וַיִּשְׁבְּתוּ שְׁלשֶׁת הָֽאֲנָשִׁים הָאֵלֶּה מֵֽעֲנוֹת אֶת־אִיּוֹב (Iyov 32:1), and these three men ceased from answering Iyov. Every form here and below has one sense, הבטלה והפסק הדבר, leaving off and the stopping of a thing. The nouns are כָּבוֹד לָאִישׁ שֶׁבֶת מֵרִיב (Mishlei 20:3), it is an honour for a man to cease from strife, with six points; רַק שִׁבְתּוֹ יִתֵּן (Shemos 21:19), only for his ceasing shall he pay; and on another pattern שַׁבַּת שַׁבָּתוֹן (Vayikra 16:31), a Shabbos of ceasing.

Shabbos is sometimes feminine, as וְֽהָֽיְתָה שַׁבַּת הָאָרֶץ לָכֶם לְאָכְלָה (Vayikra 25:6), and the Shabbos of the land shall be food for you, and sometimes masculine, as שֹׁמֵר שַׁבָּת מֵֽחַלְּלוֹ (Yeshayahu 56:2), who keeps the Shabbos from profaning it, and עֹלַת שַׁבַּת בְּשַׁבַּתּוֹ (Bamidbar 28:10), the offering of each Shabbos on its Shabbos, which goes as חֹדֶשׁ בְּחָדְשׁוֹ (Yeshayahu 66:23), each month in its month, and יוֹם בְּיוֹמוֹ (Vayikra 23:37), each day on its day. The plural, שַׁבָּתוֹת, is feminine.

more.h: A week, and the seven weeks
more.t: שֶׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת (Vayikra 23:15) is seven weeks of days, and עַד מִמָּֽחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת הַשְּׁבִיעִת (Vayikra 23:16) is until the morrow of the seventh week. A week is called so because there is a Shabbos in every week; and because seven שבתות might fall without seven whole weeks of days in them, it says תְּמִימֹת תִּֽהְיֶֽינָה (Vayikra 23:15), they shall be complete, making forty-nine days. Chazal (Menachos 66a) expounded another matter from its saying תמימות; Radak holds his own explanation the right one by the plain sense of the pasuk. So too with the years of shemittah, each shemittah year being called שבת: since שֶׁבַע שַׁבְּתֹת שָׁנִים (Vayikra 25:8), seven Shabbosos of years, might hold fewer than forty-nine years, it spells it out, שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים (Vayikra 25:8), seven years seven times.

more.h: Egypt's help will cease, on one reading
more.t: A noun on yet another pattern is שָֽׁבֶת in רַהַב הֵם שָֽׁבֶת (Yeshayahu 30:7), they are strength, they will cease. The pasuk runs וּמִצְרַיִם הֶבֶל וָרִיק יַעְזֹרוּ, and Egypt will help in vain and to no purpose, and then לכן קראתי לזאת, therefore I have called this one, which Radak explains of Yerushalayim, who thinks to be helped by Egypt and that they will be רהב, strength, to them: הם שבת, they will cease and stop from helping them. He has given another explanation, better than this, in the root יָשַׁב.

more.h: What Rabbi Yonah takes from it
more.t: Rabbi Yonah explained שָׂרוֹף יִשָּֽׂרְפוּ בַּשָּֽׁבֶת (Shmuel II 23:7), they shall be utterly burned בַּשָּׁבֶת, from this sense, which Radak glosses בכליון חרוץ, with a decreed destruction, until no memory of them is left. שֶׁבֶת חָמָֽס (Amos 6:3), the שֶׁבֶת of violence, has been explained from it as well. Radak has explained both himself in the root יָשַׁב.

more.h: Putting a stop to a thing
more.t: Where the verb takes an object it is making a thing cease: אֲשֶׁר לֹא הִשְׁבִּית לָךְ גֹּאֵל הַיּוֹם (Rus 4:14), who has not left you without a redeemer today; וְהִשְׁבִּית אֶת־הַכְּמָרִים (Melachim II 23:5), and he put down the idolatrous priests; וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי חַיָּה רָעָה (Vayikra 26:6), and I will make evil beasts cease; אַשְׁבִּיתָה מֵּֽאֱנוֹשׁ זִכְרָֽם (Devarim 32:26), I would make their memory cease from men; תַּשְׁבִּיתוּ שְּׂאֹר מִבָּֽתֵּיכֶם (Shemos 12:15), you shall make leaven cease from your houses. Of the same sense are וְנִשְׁבַּת גְּאוֹן עֻזָּהּ (Yechezkel 33:28), and the pride of her strength shall cease, and the noun in שָֽׂחֲקוּ עַל מִשְׁבַּתֶּֽהָ (Eichah 1:7), they mocked at her ceasing.

פרך.sense: Hardship and crushing, בְּפֶרֶךְ; and the פָרֹכֶת, a sheet that screened the Aron off from the Ohel Moed.

more.t: וַיַּֽעֲבִדוּ מִצְרַיִם אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּפָֽרֶךְ (Shemos 1:13), Mitzrayim made the children of Yisrael work with crushing hardship, and לֹֽא־יִרְדֶּנּוּ בְּפֶרֶךְ לְעֵינֶֽיךָ (Vayikra 25:53), he shall not rule over him with crushing hardship in your sight, the second pointed with six dots. He glosses the word בקושי וברצוץ, with hardship and crushing. In the words of Chazal (Chullin 46b), שתהא נפרכת בצפורן, that it should crumble under a fingernail.

וְעָשִׂיתָ פָרֹכֶת (Shemos 26:31), and you shall make a curtain, is a sheet that screened the Aron, to divide between it and the Ohel Moed. In the words of Chazal (Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer 41), ותלה בחופת בנו פרכיות שחורות, and he hung black curtains in his son's chuppah; the פרכיות, Radak explains, are black sheets like the tents of Kedar.

שׁטר.sense: שֹׁטֵר, an officer, a word he calls known; and מִשְׁטָרוֹ, his dominion; some read it as his writ, which he takes to mean his decree and statute.

more.t: שֹׁטֵר וּמֹשֵׁל (Mishlei 6:7), officer and ruler; שֹׁפְטִים וְשֹׁטְרִים (Devarim 16:18), judges and officers; and וְשֹׁטְרִים לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶם (Devarim 1:15), officers for your tribes. The word, he says, is known.

From this root is אִם־תָּשִׂים מִשְׁטָרוֹ בָאָֽרֶץ (Iyov 38:33), can you set his dominion on the earth, where מִשְׁטָרוֹ is like ממשלתו, his dominion. Some explain it as כתבו, his writ; Radak takes that to mean his decree and his statute, drawn from Chazal's term שטר חוב, a bond of debt (Bava Metzia 1:6, 12b).

אחד.sense: One. Since one is the least of number, a small quantity is called by it, as כְּיָמִים אֲחָדִים, like a few days. Also joined into one, and keeping alone in one place.

more.h: A few, and joined into one
more.t: כְּיָמִים אֲחָדִים (Bereishis 29:20), that is, they were in his eyes like a few days. וְהָיוּ לַֽאֲחָדִים בְּיָדֶֽךָ, and they shall be as one in your hand, means מחוברים בדבר אחד, joined in one thing. Where the alef falls away, וְדִבֶּר־חַד אֶת־ אַחַד (Yechezkel 33:30), one speaking with another.
הִתְאַֽחֲדִי הֵימִנִי (Yechezkel 21:21), keep yourself alone, go to the right: that is, התבודדי באחד המקומות, take yourself off alone to one of the places.

אַל־תֵּחַד כְּבֹדִי (Bereishis 49:6), let my honour not be joined to them, has its root and its sense here, on the pattern of אֵהָב (Mishlei 8:17), I will love. אַל־ יִחַדְּ בִּימֵי שָׁנָה (Iyov 3:6), let it not be joined among the days of the year, is set here too, its doubled dalet only setting the reading right, since the word is stressed on the earlier syllable, as he wrote in the grammar; but it is good to take it from חָדָה, of joy, let it not rejoice among the days of the year, while אַל־תֵּחַד כְּבֹדִי stays with this root.

אַחַת אֶל־ אֶחָֽת (Shemos 36:12), one to another, would properly be אַחֶדֶת, the dalet dropping and the tav being the sign of the feminine. In his own view אחת is a word derived on its own and not from אחד at all, but from אח, as וְעָשָׂה אָח מֵאַחַד מֵאֵֽלֶּה (Yechezkel 18:10), and does one of any of these: אח said of the masculine and אחת of the feminine, since from אחד no feminine form is found. Yonasan rendered that pasuk as it sounds, וְיַעְבֵּד לַאֲחוּהִי מֵחֲדָא מֵאִלֵין, and does to his brother one of these.

אנך.sense: Tin, and the tin plummet a builder weighs with; also אָנֹכִי, which is like אני, I.

more.t: עַל־חוֹמַת אֲנָךְ (Amos 7:7), upon a wall of anach: he explains אנך as בדיל, tin, and says it is called so in Arabic, with the kaf doubled; the meaning is a wall built with a measuring line and with the plummet of judgment. וּבְיָדוֹ אֲנָֽךְ (Amos 7:7), and in his hand an anach, is משקלת הבדיל, the tin plummet, for the plummet the builder weighs with is made of lead or of tin, that is, פְּייומְבִּין, a plumb.

הִֽנְנִי שָׂם אֲנָךְ (Amos 7:8), behold I am setting an anach, he explains as משקלת אנך, a plummet of anach. He says Rabbi Yonah explained the matter well, taking it in the sense of וְשַׂמְתִּי מִשְׁפָּט לְקָו וּצְדָקָה לְמִשְׁקָלֶת (Yeshayahu 28:17), and I will make justice the line and righteousness the plummet.

לֹֽא־אוֹסִיף עוֹד עֲבוֹר לֽוֹ (Amos 7:8), I will not again pass him by any more, means: I will no longer pass over his sins, for I will call him to account for them in judgment, judging them by the plummet of judgment and the line of law.
אָנֹכִי הָאֵל (Bereishis 46:3), I am the Kel: אָנֹכִי is like אני, I.

נכה.sense: To strike: a man, a thing, the hand against the hand, or with the tongue; by borrowing, to tear a city down. Close to it in sense, נְכֵה רַגְלָיִם, lame in the feet.

more.t: וְהִכִּיתָ אֶת־כָּל־זְכוּרָהּ (Devarim 20:13), you shall strike every male of it; וְהִכִּיתָ בַצּוּר (Shemos 17:6), you shall strike the rock; וַיַּךְ הַבָּרָד (Shemos 9:25), the hail struck. Of hands, אַכֶּה כַפִּי אֶל־כַּפִּי (Yechezkel 21:22), I will strike My palm against My palm, and וַיַּכּוּ־כָף (Melachim II 11:12), they clapped hands. Of the tongue, לְכוּ וְנַכֵּהוּ בַלָּשׁוֹן (Yirmiyahu 18:18), let us strike him with the tongue.

וְיַךְ שָׁרָשָׁיו (Hoshea 14:6) is that it strikes its roots this way and that, meaning its roots go far off; the word is used as in וּמָחָה עַל־כֶּתֶף יָם־כִּנֶּרֶת (Bamidbar 34:11), and it shall reach to the shoulder of the sea of Kinneres.

more.h: Striking a city, not its people
more.t: וַיַּכּוּ אֶת־צִקְלַג (Shmuel I 30:1), they struck Tziklag, is a borrowed use and means they tore it down, since the pasuk speaks of the city and not the people: it says in the same place מִקָּטֹן וְעַד־גָּדוֹל לֹא הֵמִיתוּ אִישׁ, from small to great they killed no man.

Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar wrote that there is a masculine noun מַכֶּה, with a segol under the kaf, on the pattern of מַטֶּה, a staff, its plural in מִן־ הַמַּכִּים אֲשֶׁר יַכֻּהוּ אֲרַמִּים (Melachim II 8:29), from the blows that the Arameans struck him; Radak's father wrote the same. Rabbi Yonah wrote that it is rather the plural of the feminine מכה, as חִטִּים from חִטָּה, wheat, and שָׁנִים from שָׁנָה, a year.

The feminine noun is מַכָּה, a blow: מַכַּת־חֶרֶב (Esther 9:5), a blow of the sword, and מָה הַמַּכּוֹת הָאֵלֶּה (Zecharyah 13:6), what are these blows. A sense close to it is נְכֵה רַגְלָיִם (Shmuel II 4:4), lame in the feet, and נֶאֶסְפוּ עָלַי נֵכִים (Tehillim 35:15), stricken men gathered against me. A plural with an alef in place of the heh is in תֶּהְגּוּ אַךְ־ נְכָאִֽים (Yeshayahu 16:7), you shall moan, surely stricken, and another form of it is נִכְּאוּ מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ (Iyov 30:8), they were struck out of the land.
פַרְעֹה נְכֹה (Melachim II 23:29) may be of this sense, named so because he was נכה רגלים, lame in the feet; and so Targum Yonasan renders it פַּרְעֹה חֲגִירָא, Pharaoh the lame.

מצח.sense: The forehead, a sense he calls known; and מִצְחַת נְחשֶׁת, a plate of brass, named for the מצחה that girls wear on the forehead.

more.t: עַל־ מֵצַח אַֽהֲרֹן (Shemos 28:38), on Aharon's forehead; מִצְֽחֲךָ חָזָק לְעֻמַּת מִצְחָֽם (Yechezkel 3:8), your forehead strong against their forehead; עַל־ מִצְחוֹת הָֽאֲנָשִׁים (Yechezkel 9:4), on the foreheads of the men. Of the sense he says only ידוע, it is known.
וּמִצְחַת נְחשֶׁת עַל־רַגְלָיו (Shmuel I 17:6), and a mitzchas of brass on his legs, is a plate of brass, called מצחת because it was like the מצחה that girls wear on their forehead.

נזל.sense: To flow down, of water and of mountains, and to make flow. The מַזָּלוֹת, the constellations, are named from it because they flow in their course.

more.t: Taking no object: הָרִים נָֽזְלוּ (Shoftim 5:5), the mountains flowed, and מַיִם זָרִים קָרִים נוֹזְלִֽים (Yirmiyahu 18:14), strange cold flowing waters. Taking an object: וְעַפְעַפֵּינוּ יִזְּלוּ־מָֽיִם (Yirmiyahu 9:17), and our eyelids shall stream water, and וּשְׁחָקִים יִזְּלוּ־צֶדֶק (Yeshayahu 45:8), and let the skies pour down righteousness; and in the heavy form, מַיִם מִצּוּר הִזִּיל לָמוֹ (Yeshayahu 48:21), He made water flow from the rock for them. The sense of all of them is ההגרה, flowing down.

מִפָּנֶיךָ הָרִים נָזֹֽלּוּ (Yeshayahu 64:2), the mountains flowed down before You, is of this root and sense; it stands as it does because of the pause, on the pattern פָּעֹל, its dagesh only for the beauty of the word, like the dagesh of חָדֵלּוּ in פְרָזוֹן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל חָדֵלּוּ (Shoftim 5:7), the villagers ceased in Yisrael. Rabbi Yehudah wrote the word under the root זָלַל; Radak holds that is not right, since nothing of this sense is found in that root.

לַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְלַיָּרֵחַ וְלַמַּזָּלוֹת (Melachim II 23:5), to the sun and to the moon and to the constellations: they are named from this root because they flow in their course. הֲתֹצִיא מַזָּרוֹת בְּעִתּוֹ (Iyov 38:32), can you bring out the Mazaros in their season, means the same as מזלות, or else it is the name of a star.

מין.sense: Kind: what is like a thing and is of its own make, as fruit after its kind and the beast of the earth after its kind.

more.t: עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי לְמִינוֹ (Bereishis 1:11), making fruit after its kind, and אֶת־חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ לְמִינָהּ (Bereishis 1:25), the beast of the earth after its kind: the word means מה שדומה לו והוא מתכונתו, what is like it and is of its own make.

חתן.sense: To marry into a family: a wife's father is the man's חֹתֵן, her mother his חֹתֶנֶת, and he is their חָתָן, which he becomes on the day of his chupah.

more.t: וְלֹא תִתְחַתֵּן בָּם (Devarim 7:3), you shall not make marriages with them; וַיִּתְחַתֵּן לְאַחְאָֽב (Divrei HaYamim II 18:1), he made a marriage bond with Achav; וְהִֽתְחַתְּנוּ אֹתָנוּ (Bereishis 34:9), make marriages with us. The father of a man's wife is called his חֹתֵן, as חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה (Shemos 18:1), Moshe's father-in-law; her mother is his חֹתֶנֶת, as אָרוּר שֹׁכֵב עִם־חֹֽתַנְתּוֹ (Devarim 27:23), cursed is he who lies with his wife's mother; and he is called their חָתָן, as שִׁמְשׁוֹן חֲתַן הַתִּמְנִי (Shoftim 15:6), Shimshon, the Timnite's son-in-law.

Rabbi Yonah wrote that a wife's brother is called חותן to her husband, as מִבְּנֵי חֹבָב חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה (Shoftim 4:11), of the sons of Chovav, Moshe's חותן. He found וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה לְחֹבָב בֶּן רְעוּאֵל הַמִּדְיָנִי חֹתֵן מֹשֶׁה (Bamidbar 10:29), Moshe said to Chovav son of Reuel the Midianite, Moshe's חותן, and it says וַתָּבֹאנָה אֶל רְעוּאֵל אֲבִיהֶן (Shemos 2:18), they came to Reuel their father; so it seemed to him that Reuel is Yisro and Chovav is Yisro's son. Radak says it cannot be explained so, for Moshe says to him וְהָיִיתָ לָּנוּ לְעֵינָיִם (Bamidbar 10:31), and you shall be eyes for us, and it was Yisro who was with them in the wilderness, as it says וַיִּשְׁמַע יִתְרוֹ כֹהֵן מִדְיָן (Shemos 18:1), and Yisro the kohen of Midian heard. The correct view is that Chovav is Yisro and Reuel is Yisro's father, and אֲבִיהֶן there is their father's father, for so the language calls a father's father a father and a son's son a son.

בְּיוֹם חֲתֻנָּתוֹ (Shir HaShirim 3:11), on the day of his wedding, is the day of his chupah, the day a man becomes a חתן; he is called so then because of his joining to his father-in-law. So קוֹל חָתָן וְקוֹל כַּלָּה (Yirmiyahu 7:34), the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, and וְהוּא כְּחָתָן יֹצֵא מֵחֻפָּתוֹ (Tehillim 19:6), like a bridegroom going out from his chupah.

On כִּי חֲתַן־דָּמִים אַתָּה לִי (Shemos 4:25), for you are a bridegroom of blood to me: it appears by reasoning that as a man was called חתן on the day of his chupah, so a baby was called חתן on the day of his milah, for the essential sense of the word חתן is התחדשות השמחה, the renewing of joy; as joy is renewed on the day of the chupah, so it is renewed on the day of the milah.

The angel sought to kill Moshe because he had not circumcised Eliezer his son. Moshe sensed that it was the punishment for the milah, and told Tzipporah to circumcise his son, since he himself could not for the sickness already upon him. וַתַּגַּע לְרַגְלָיו (Shemos 4:25), and she touched it to his feet, is Moshe's feet, as if to say: if it is for this punishment that you are ill, here is the blood of the milah. As she circumcised her son she said כִּי חֲתַן־דָּמִים אַתָּה לִי, that is, you have become to me today a bridegroom for blood, for the killing of my husband; and when the blood of the milah reached Moshe's feet and the sickness eased from him, she said חֲתַן דָּמִים לַמּוּלֹת (Shemos 4:26), a bridegroom of blood for the circumcisions: you whom I called a bridegroom of blood are a bridegroom not for the blood of killing but for the blood of the circumcisions.

צין.sense: Its sense is that of a מצבה, a standing stone set over a grave or as a sign on the roads.

more.t: מָה הַצִּיּוּן הַלָּז (Melachim II 23:17), what is that marker; וּבָנָה אֶצְלוֹ צִיּוּן (Yechezkel 39:15), he shall build a marker beside it; and הַצִּיבִי לָךְ צִיֻּנִים (Yirmiyahu 31:20), set up markers for yourself. The word is on the pattern of חִבֻּק יָדַיִם (Mishlei 6:10), a folding of the hands.

אדן.sense: A lord or master, and the honoured Name אֲדֹנָי. In a second sense אֲדָנִים, the hollow sockets that the boards and the pillars were set into.

more.h: A plural that honours one man
more.t: לָכֵן יְשַׁלַּח הָאָדוֹן (Yeshayahu 10:16), therefore the Lord shall send; וַֽאדֹנִי זָקֵֽן (Bereishis 18:12), and my lord is old. The plural comes as a form of honour for one: אֲדֹנִים קָשֶׁה, a hard master, and אִם־אֲדֹנָיו יִתֶּן־לוֹ אִשָּׁה (Shemos 21:4), if his master gives him a wife. It comes without the yud too, יֹֽאמַר־נָא אֲדֹנֵנוּ (Shmuel I 16:16), let our lord say. The sense itself, he says, is known.

more.h: The yud of the honoured Name
more.t: The honoured Name, אֲדֹנָי, is in the plural for honour and pointed with a kamatz, carrying one sign of plural only, as וְקָרַֽע לוֹ חַלּוֹנָי (Yirmiyahu 22:14), and he cut out windows for himself; or else the yud is the yud of relation, as the yud of מוֹכִיחַ אָדָם אַֽחֲרַי (Mishlei 28:23), one who reproves a man afterward.

Where the word is secular it takes a patach, הִנֶּה נָּֽא־אֲדֹנַי (Bereishis 19:2), behold now, my lords. But in וַיֹּאמַר אֲדֹנָי אִם־נָא מָצָאתִי חֵן בְּעֵינֶיךָ (Bereishis 18:3), and he said, אֲדֹנָי, if now I have found favour in your eyes, it is kamatz, and Chazal are divided over it (Shevuos 35b): some say it is secular and was said to the greatest of them, and some say it is holy. So too of וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹט אֲלֵהֶם אַל־נָא אֲדֹנָֽי (Bereishis 19:18), and Lot said to them, not so, please, אֲדֹנָי, they say it is holy.

בִּי אֲדֹנָי בַּמָּה אוֹשִׁיעַ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shoftim 6:15), please my lord, with what shall I save Yisrael, is kamatz and yet not in pause. It may be that it took the kamatz because of the zakef, the word being secular, since Gideon did not yet know that he was an angel.

In a second sense, כִּכָּר לָאָֽדֶן (Shemos 38:27), a talent for the socket, and וּשְׁנֵי אֲדָנִים תַּחַת הַקֶּרֶשׁ הָֽאֶחָֽד (Shemos 26:25), two sockets under one board. The sockets were hollow and the tenons of the boards went into them, and so too the pillars, and the sockets held them up. So על מה אֲדָנֶיהָ הָטְבָּעוּ (Iyov 38:6), on what were its sockets sunk, which he glosses יסודותיה, its foundations.

עדן.sense: Pleasure, תענוג: whatever gives the body pleasure, good food or fine clothing; עֶדְנָה, the days of youth. Also binding, as he holds Agag's מַעֲדַנֹּת to mean.

more.t: The noun הָֽיְתָה־לִּי עֶדְנָה (Bereishis 18:12), I have had pleasure, is תענוג, pleasure, and it is the days of youth. Without the feminine heh, גַּן־בְּעֵדֶן (Bereishis 2:8), a garden in Eden, and כָּל־עֲצֵי־עֵדֶן (Yechezkel 31:16), all the trees of Eden. Four places where the word is pointed otherwise are the name of a city, which he treats in the grammar.

On הַמַּלְבִּשְׁכֶם שָׁנִי עִם־עֲדָֽנִים (Shmuel II 1:24), who clothed you in scarlet with delights, some say the pasuk is elliptical: who clothes you in scarlet and feeds you delicacies, and so the Targum has וּמוֹבִיל לְכוֹן תַּפְנוּקִין, and brings you delicacies. Rabbi Yonah read it as clothing you in scarlet in the days of delights. Radak holds, for his own part, that one may not alter what is written: עדן is said of the clothing itself, for as good food is עדן to the body, so is fine clothing, and whatever gives the body pleasure is called עדן.

With a mem added, וְיִתֵּן מַֽעֲדַנִּים לְנַפְשֶֽׁךָ (Mishlei 29:17), he will give delights to your soul, and וְהוּא יִתֵּן מַֽעֲדַנֵּי־מֶֽלֶךְ (Bereishis 49:20), he will yield the dainties of a king. The adjective is שִׁמְעִי־זֹאת עֲדִינָה (Yeshayahu 47:8), hear this, you who are given to pleasure.

וַיֵּלֶךְ אֵלָיו אֲגַג מַֽעֲדַנֹּת (Shmuel I 15:32), and Agag went to him מַעֲדַנֹּת, is explained as במעדנות, in joy and pleasure: he went to him so, for he chose his death over his life. Some explain that he went to him as one bound. Of the same kind is הַתְקַשֵּׁר מַֽעֲדַנּוֹת כִּימָה (Iyov 38:31), can you bind the מַעֲדַנּוֹת of Kimah, the knots of Kimah over the fruits. On this reading Agag went to him in the bindings and chains that were on him, and Radak says this explanation is correct; so too Chazal use the word for tying, כיון שהתיר ראשי מעדנים שלהן כשרין (Sukkah 13b), once he has untied the ends of their bindings, they are fit. Rabbi Yonah read it of pleasantness, for his many pleasures and the greatness of his kingdom.

חבצל.sense: חֲבַצֶּ֣לֶת הַשָּׁר֔וֹן (Shir HaShirim 2:1), the chavatzeles of the Sharon, which he says is what Chazal call the ורד, the rose.

more.t: The tav is the feminine tav, like the tav of שֽׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָֽעֲמָקִֽים in the same pasuk, the lily of the valleys; and it is the flower called ורד, a rose, in the language of Chazal (Sheviis 7:7), רוז"א, rosa, in the vernacular.

זיו.sense: Ziv, the month of Iyar, called so, Chazal say, for the brightness it holds for the trees; זיו in their language is brightness and shining.

more.h: Why the month is called so
more.t: בְּחֹדֶשׁ זִו (Melachim I 6:1), in the month of Ziv, is the month of Iyar. Chazal say (Rosh Hashanah 11a) that it is called so משום דאית בה זיוא לאילני, because there is brightness in it for the trees. In their language זיו is הזהר והנגה, brightness and shining; and so the Targum renders מִנֹּגַהּ נֶגְדּוֹ (Shmuel II 22:13), from the brightness before Him, as מִזִיו יְקָרֵיהּ, from the brightness of His glory.

גמד.sense: A measure: גֹּמֶד אָרְכָּהּ (Shoftim 3:16), a gomed its length, the gomed being אמה הזרוע, the cubit of the arm; and גַמָּדִים, men of short measure.

more.t: The adjective is וְגַמָּדִים בְּמִגְדְּלוֹתַיִךְ הָיוּ (Yechezkel 27:11), and dwarfs were in your towers, which he explains as ננסים, dwarfs, men of short measure.

חרם.sense: Killing, cutting off, destroying and loss; what a man devotes is as though destroyed to him. Close to this, a net; and חָרֻם, in Chazal, one whose nose is sunken.

more.t: וְאֵת כָּל־הַנְּשָׁמָה הֶֽחֱרִים (Yehoshua 10:40), he destroyed every soul; וְהַֽחֲרַמְתִּי אֶת־עָֽרֵיהֶֽם (Bamidbar 21:2), I will destroy their cities; and in the passive, זֹבֵחַ לָֽאֱלֹהִים יָֽחֳרָם (Shemos 22:19), one who sacrifices to gods is to be destroyed. The sense of them all, he says, is הריגה וכריתה והשחתה ואיבוד, killing, cutting off, destroying and loss.
אִֽישׁ־ חֶרְמִי (Melachim I 20:42), the man I doomed to destruction, may be explained from this, and Targum Yonasan has it the same way, גְבַר דְחַיָב קְטוֹל, a man liable to be put to death.

In וְהֶחֱרִים, said of אֵת לְשׁוֹן יָם־מִצְרַיִם (Yeshayahu 11:15), Hashem will cut off the tongue of the sea of Mitzrayim, the sense is cutting off and cutting apart, as in לְגֹזֵר יַם־סוּף לִגְזָרִים (Tehillim 136:13), who cut the Yam Suf into pieces.

more.h: A man already as good as dead
more.t: On כָּל־ חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יָֽחֳרַם מִן־הָֽאָדָם לֹא יִפָּדֶה (Vayikra 27:29), no one doomed from among men shall be redeemed, Chazal say (Arachin 6b) that it speaks of a man going out to be killed: if he says, my valuation is on me, or my worth is on me, or another says of him, this one's valuation or worth is on me, nothing is owed, since he is already as one dead, and a dead man has no valuation and no worth. Hence it says לֹא יִפָּדֶה מוֹת יוּמָֽת, he shall not be redeemed, he shall surely be put to death, which Radak explains: since he is to die, there is no redeeming him.

כָּל־ חֵרֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל (Bamidbar 18:14), every devoted thing in Yisrael, and what a man devotes to Hashem of all that he has: though the thing itself is not destroyed, to the one who devotes it it is as though destroyed, since he will have no benefit from it.

Close to this sense are יָצוּדוּ חֵֽרֶם (Michah 7:2), they hunt with a net, יְגֹרֵהוּ בְחֶרְמוֹ (Chavakuk 1:15), he gathers him in his net, שִׁלַּחְתָּ אֶֽת־אִֽישׁ־ חֶרְמִי (Melachim I 20:42), you sent away the man of my net, מִשְׁטַח חֲרָמִים (Yechezkel 26:5), a spreading place for nets, and מְצוֹדִים וַֽחֲרָמִים (Koheles 7:26), snares and nets: all of them nets and snares to hunt with. And אוֹ חָרֻם (Vayikra 21:18), or one who is חָרֻם, Chazal explain (Bechoros 43b) as one whose nose is sunk between his two eyes, one who paints both his eyes at once.

זנה.sense: To play the harlot, said of a woman, of a people going after foreign gods, and of the heart and the eyes; and to make another play the harlot.

more.t: כִּי זָֽנְתָה אִמָּם (Hoshea 2:7), for their mother played the harlot; וְאַתְּ זָנִית רֵעִים רַבִּים (Yirmiyahu 3:1), and you played the harlot with many companions; וַתִּזְנִים וְגַם לֹא שָׂבָֽעַתְּ (Yechezkel 16:28), where he glosses וַתִּזְנִים as ותזני עמם, and you played the harlot with them, and still you were not sated. Of the heart and the eyes, אֶת־לִבָּם הַזּוֹנֶה and וְאֵת עֵֽינֵיהֶם הַזֹּנוֹת (Yechezkel 6:9), their heart that plays the harlot and their eyes that play the harlot.

וְזָֽנְתָה אֶת־כָּל־מַמְלְכוֹת הָאָרֶץ (Yeshayahu 23:17), and she shall play the harlot with all the kingdoms of the earth: the pasuk had likened her, once the merchants ceased from her, to a forgotten harlot, and says that she will again come to her hire; that is, all the kingdoms will trade with her.

זְנוּת וְיַיִן וְתִירוֹשׁ (Hoshea 4:11), harlotry and wine and new wine, with its plural in וְנָֽשְׂאוּ אֶת־זְנֽוּתֵיכֶם (Bamidbar 14:33), and they shall bear your harlotries. With a tav added at the start, וַיִּשְׁפְּכוּ תַזְנוּתָם עָלֶֽיהָ (Yechezkel 23:8), they poured out their harlotry upon her. With a nun added in place of the tav, מֵרֹב זְנוּנֵי זוֹנָה (Nachum 3:4), from the many harlotries of the harlot; or else זנונים doubles the middle root letter of זנה, as הגיגי, my meditation, does of הגה.

הִזְנוּ וְלֹא יִפְרֹצוּ (Hoshea 4:10), they played the harlot and shall not increase, stands without an object; but אַל־תְּחַלֵּל אֶֽת־בִּתְּךָ לְהַזְנוֹתָהּ (Vayikra 19:29), do not profane your daughter to make her a harlot, and וַיֶּזֶן אֶת־יֹֽשְׁבֵי יְרֽוּשָׁלַם (Divrei HaYamim II 21:11), he made the dwellers of Yerushalayim play the harlot, take one.

שֹנא.sense: To hate, a sense he calls known; some uses are not real hatred but loving another more, as Leah was called hated.

more.t: כִּֽי־ שְׂנוּאָה לֵאָה (Bereishis 29:31), that Leah was hated: her husband did not hate her, but because he loved Rachel more, Leah was called hated. So too הָֽאַחַת אֲהוּבָה וְהָֽאַחַת שְׂנוּאָה (Devarim 21:15), the one beloved and the one hated.

The one who hates, וְיָנֻסוּ מְשַׂנְאֶיךָ מִפָּנֶיךָ (Bamidbar 10:35), and let those who hate You flee from before You; the one hated, גַּם־לְרֵעֵהוּ יִשָּׂנֵא רָשׁ (Mishlei 14:20), the poor man is hated even by his neighbour; and the adjective, הַבֵּן הַבְּכֹר לַשְּׂנִיאָה (Devarim 21:15), the firstborn son is the hated one's, built like נְבִיאָה, a prophetess.

רכשׁ.sense: רֶכֶשׁ, beasts ridden: to Rabbi Yonah good horses not many years old, to Radak perhaps another kind; and רְכוּשׁ, all a man's wealth, cattle, silver, gold, movables.

more.t: Rabbi Yonah wrote that they are the good horses over whom many years have not passed. Radak holds it may rather be some other beast we do not know, since one pasuk sets the couriers בְּיַד הָרָצִים בַּסּוּסִים רֹכְבֵי הָרֶכֶשׁ (Esther 8:10), by the hand of the runners on horses, riders of the רֶכֶשׁ, and another gives וְהַשְּׂעֹרִים וְהַתֶּבֶן לַסּוּסִים וְלָרָכֶשׁ (Melachim I 5:8), the barley and the straw for the horses and for the רֶכֶשׁ: it looks like a kind besides horses.

The noun covers all a man's money: his cattle, silver and gold, and every movable thing. So וְאֶת־כָּל־רְכֻשׁוֹ אֲשֶׁר רָכָשׁ (Bereishis 31:18), all his goods that he had gathered. And on תֶּן־לִי הַנֶּפֶשׁ וְהָרְכֻשׁ קַח־לָךְ (Bereishis 14:21), give me the souls and take the goods to yourself, he says נפש is the souls of the men, for he asked of him nothing but the people, and let him take the livestock and all the money.

רכס.sense: The רְכָסִים are the high mountains; רֻכְסֵי אִישׁ, the pride and haughtiness of men; and the verb, raising the choshen to join it to the ephod above it.

more.t: וְהָֽרְכָסִים לְבִקְעָֽה (Yeshayahu 40:4), and the high mountains into a valley, רְכָסִים being the high mountains; מֵֽרֻכְסֵי אִישׁ (Tehillim 31:21), from the pride of men and their haughtiness; and the verb from it, וְיִרְכְּסוּ אֶת־הַחֹשֶׁן (Shemos 28:28), that is, they shall raise the choshen to join it to the ephod, which is above it.

פצע.sense: Splitting, that is, a blow that brings out blood, with the noun פֶּצַע; and פְצוּעַ־דַּכָּה, one whose testicles are split.

more.t: הִכּוּנִי פְצָעוּנִי (Shir HaShirim 5:7), they struck me, they split me open; הַכֵּה וּפָצֹֽעַ (Melachim I 20:37), striking and splitting; and the noun, with segol, פֶּצַע תַּחַת פָּצַע (Shemos 21:25), a split for a split. ענינם ענין בקוע, their sense is splitting, that is, a blow that brings out blood, and he gives the word for it in the vernacular. The Targum Yerushalmi renders וַיְבַקַּע עֲצֵי עֹלָה (Bereishis 22:3), he split the wood for the offering, with ופצע קיסין לעלתא, and he split wood for the offering.
פְצוּעַ־דַּכָּה (Devarim 23:2), one split at the testicles, he explains as one whose testicles have been split open, even one of the two.

פצה.sense: Opening, the sense of all of them, of the mouth and the lips; and another sense close to it, redeeming and the opening of the prison.

more.t: וְאָנֹכִי פָּצִיתִי־פִי (Shoftim 11:35), and I have opened my mouth; אֲשֶׁר־פָּצוּ שְׂפָתָי (Tehillim 66:14), which my lips opened; הֶבֶל יִפְצֶה־פִּיהוּ (Iyov 35:16), he opens his mouth in vanity; פְּצֵה פִיךָ וֶאֱכֹל (Yechezkel 2:8), open your mouth and eat; and וּפֹצֶה פֶה וּמְצַפְצֵף (Yeshayahu 10:14), one that opens the mouth and chirps. The sense of all of them is opening.

Another sense, close to this: פְּצֵנִי וְהַצִּילֵנִי (Tehillim 144:11), redeem me and rescue me, and הַפּוֹצֶה אֶת־דָּוִד עַבְדּוֹ (Tehillim 144:10), who redeems David His servant: the sense of redemption and of the opening of the prison.

שׁלה.sense: To be at ease and quiet, with שַׁלְוָה, ease; a second sense is error and leading into error; and from the same root the שליא, the sac the unborn child stands in.

more.t: שָׁלוּ כָּל־בֹּגְדֵי בָגֶד (Yirmiyahu 12:1), all who deal treacherously are at ease; the adjective שָׁלֵו הָיִיתִי (Iyov 16:12), I was at ease; and the noun וְשַׁלְוַת כְּסִילִים תְּאַבְּדֵם (Mishlei 1:32), the ease of fools destroys them.

His father explains לְדַבֵּר אִתּוֹ בַּשֶּׁלִי (Shmuel II 3:27), to speak with him basheli, from the sense of ease, on the pattern of מְרִי: on that reading he was speaking with him in peace, and killed him. Or it means suddenly, and so Onkelos renders בְּפֶתַע פִּתְאֹם (Bamidbar 6:9), suddenly, unawares, as בִּתְכֵף שָׁלוּ, with this word. In Radak's own reading it belongs to the second sense: in error and deceit he took him aside to speak with him, and struck him.

לֹא תַשְׁלֶה אֹתִי (Melachim II 4:28), do not mislead me, that is, do not lead me into error; and the Targum of שְׁגָגָה (Bamidbar 15:25), an unwitting error, is שָׁלוּתָא. So וַיַּכֵּהוּ שָׁם הָאֱלֹהִים עַל־הַשַּׁל (Shmuel II 6:7), and God struck him there for the שַׁל: that is, for the error he made in laying hold of the Aron when the oxen shook it, for even the Levi'im were given it to carry only on poles, and he took hold of it; and besides, he was no Levi. Chazal darshened that Hakadosh Baruch Hu said: it carries those who carry it, all the more itself. Some explain וְשַׁלְוַת כְּסִילִים תְּאַבְּדֵֽם (Mishlei 1:32) from this sense too: the error of fools destroys them.

In the second sense, בָּנַי עַתָּה אַל־תִּשָּׁלוּ (Divrei HaYamim II 29:11) is my sons, do not now fall into error: let there be no forgetting and no error among you in purifying the house of Hashem. Rabbi Yonah wrote it in the first sense, do not now be at ease, which would mean: do not rest and do not be quiet until you have finished the purifying.

From this root too, וּבְשִׁלְיָתָהּ הַיּוֹצֵת מִבֵּין רַגְלֶיהָ (Devarim 28:57), and her שליא that comes out from between her legs. In the words of Chazal (Chullin 4:6), one who slaughters a beast and finds a שליא in it, a man of hearty appetite may eat it. The שליא, Radak says, is the sac in which the child stands in its mother's womb, and it may be that the pasuk means by it the little children, as though they were in the שליא still; and so the Targum says, וּבִזְעֵר בְּנָהָא, and the youngest of her children. Rabbi Yonah explained לֹא תַשְׁלֶה אֹתִי from this sense, and Radak holds that far-fetched.

שׁקט.sense: To be quiet and still, with שֶׁקֶט for quiet; and where the verb takes an object, to give quiet. The sense he gives is rest and repose.

more.t: אֶרֶץ יָֽרְאָה וְשָׁקָֽטָה (Tehillim 76:9), the land feared and grew quiet, he explains as fearing Hashem and growing quiet from making war on Yisrael, as it says there, מִגַּֽעֲרָתְךָ אֱלֹהֵי יַֽעֲקֹב נִרְדָּם וְרֶכֶב וָסֽוּס (Tehillim 76:7), at Your rebuke, God of Yaakov, chariot and horse fell into a dead sleep.

Where the verb takes an object it gives quiet: וְאֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם יַשְׁקִיט רִֽיב (Mishlei 15:18), one slow to anger quiets strife, and לְהַשְׁקִיט לוֹ מִימֵי רָע (Tehillim 94:13), to give him quiet from the days of evil. Their sense, he says, is rest and repose.

תער.sense: תַּעַר, a razor, which he calls known and does not gloss; and תַּעַר again for the sheath, the case of the sword.

more.t: Of the first he says nothing but ידוע, it is known: וְהֶעֱבִירוּ תַעַר (Bamidbar 8:7), let them pass a razor over, תַּעַר הַגַּלָּבִים (Yechezkel 5:1), the barbers' razor, and יִקְרָעֶהָ בְּתַעַר הַסֹּפֵר (Yirmiyahu 36:23), he cut it with the scribe's blade. The other is the נדן, the sheath: וַיִּשְׁלְפָהּ מִתַּעְרָהּ (Shmuel I 17:51), he drew it from its sheath.

ערה.sense: Pouring out; uncovering, and nakedness; joining, as shields joined to a wall; and עָרוֹת, the moist greens and grasses.

more.t: תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱרָה לַמָּוֶת נַפְשׁוֹ (Yeshayahu 53:12), because he poured out his soul to death; אַל־ תְּעַר נַפְשִֽׁי (Tehillim 141:8), do not pour out my soul; וַתְּעַר כַּדָּהּ (Bereishis 24:20), and she poured out her pitcher; and וִיעָרוּ אֶת־הָאָרוֹן (Divrei HaYamim II 24:11), and they poured out the chest: a sense of pouring out and pouring. It may be that תִּשְׁכְּרִי וְתִתְעָרִֽי (Eichah 4:21), you will be drunk and pour out, is of this sense, since it is the way of a drunkard to vomit after he has drunk much. Radak also lists it under uncovering, as laying oneself bare, after the manner of וישכר וַיִּתְגַּל בְּתוֹךְ אָֽהֳלֹֽה (Bereishis 9:21), and he was drunk and uncovered himself within his tent.

Another sense: את מקרה הֶֽעֱרָה (Vayikra 20:18), he has laid bare her source; עָרוֹת יְסוֹד עַד־צַוָּאר (Chavakuk 3:13), laying bare the foundation to the neck; עָרוּ עָרוּ עַד הַיְסוֹד בָּֽהּ (Tehillim 137:7), lay it bare, lay it bare, to the foundation in her. The nouns: עֶרְוַת אָבִיךָ וְעֶרְוַת אִמְּךָ לֹא תְגַלֵּה (Vayikra 18:7), the nakedness of your father and the nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover; כִּֽי־ עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ בָּאתֶם לִרְאֽוֹת (Bereishis 42:12), for you have come to see the nakedness of the land; and in another form וְהַרְאֵיתִי גוֹיִם מַעְרֵךְ (Nachum 3:5), and I will show nations your nakedness, with כְּמַֽעַר ־אִישׁ (Melachim I 7:36), like the bareness of each. The sense of all of these is uncovering.

On וְאַתְּ עֵרֹם וְעֶרְיָֽה (Yechezkel 16:7), and you were naked and bare, he explains the pair as nouns, בערום ובעריה, in nakedness and in bareness, and so וְהִנִּיחוּךְ עֵירֹם וְעֶרְיָֽה (Yechezkel 16:39), and they will leave you naked and bare. Or else they are adjectives, and when the text speaks of Knesses Yisrael it speaks now in the masculine and now in the feminine, as he set out in his grammar; and that is the correct reading.

Rabbi Yonah explained כמער איש as מצד, from the side, and Radak explains him to mean that the figures went round every side of each board, as it says מֵעֵבֶר אִישׁ לֹיֽוֹת, wreaths at the side of each. And so Rabbi Yonah explained מִמַּֽעֲרֵה ־גָֽבַע (Shoftim 20:33) as מצר הגבעה, from the side of the hill, where Targum Yonasan has מִמֵישַׁר גִבְעָתָא, from the plain of the hill. It seems that Chazal explained כמער איש from the sense of joining, for they said (Yoma 54a) that Rabbah bar Shila said כאיש המעורה בלויה שלו, like a man joined to his companion, which Radak explains as a man cleaving to his wife face against face.

וְקִיר עֵרָה מָגֵֽן (Yeshayahu 22:6), and the shield was joined to the wall, is a sense of joining: the shields were joined to the wall to fight against the city. And so Targum Yonasan renders it וְעַל שׁוּר דְבַקוּ תְרֵיסִין, and on the wall they joined shields. Like it in the words of Chazal is מעורה בטרפשין (Chullin 46a), that is, attached at the diaphragm, and אם היו מעורות בגידין אסורות (Beitzah 7a), if they were attached by the sinews they are forbidden. Rabbi Yehudah put עד יֵֽעָרֶה עלינו, on his view until a spirit is joined to us, in the sense of וְקִיר עֵרָה מָגֵֽן. Radak's own view is that עַד־ יֵֽעָרֶה עָלֵינוּ רוּחַ מִמָּרוֹם (Yeshayahu 32:15) may be of the uncovering sense, until a spirit from on high is revealed upon us, or of the first sense, until it is poured out upon us, after the manner of אֶשְׁפּוֹךְ אֶת־רוּחִי (Yoel 3:1), I will pour out My spirit.

עָרוֹת עַל־יְאוֹר (Yeshayahu 19:7), the moist greens by the river, is an adjective for moist greens and grasses, in the pattern of בָּלוֹת וּמְטֻלָּאוֹת (Yehoshua 9:5), worn out and patched. And so מִמַּֽעֲרֵה־גָֽבַע means a place near the hill where there were grasses and herbs, called so for the moistness of the grasses in it; and וּמִתְעָרֶה כְּאֶזְרָח רַֽעֲנָֽן (Tehillim 37:35), growing moist like a fresh native tree, is of this sense too: מתלחלח, becoming moist.

ישׁר.sense: Straight, and right in one's eyes; the upright, יְשָׁרִים; level ground, מִישׁוֹר; and the verb, to make straight.

more.t: לַאֲשֶׁר יָשַׁר בְּעֵינָי (Yirmiyahu 27:5), to whom it was right in My eyes; כַּאֲשֶׁר יָשַׁר בְּעֵינֵי הַיּוֹצֵר (Yirmiyahu 18:4), as it was right in the potter's eyes; כִּי־הִיא יָשְׁרָה בְעֵינָי (Shoftim 14:3), for she is right in my eyes. And of going straight on, וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה הַפָּרוֹת (Shmuel I 6:12), the cows went straight.

more.h: The upright rule in the morning
more.t: On וַיִּרְדּוּ בָם יְשָׁרִים לַבֹּקֶר (Tehillim 49:15), the upright shall rule over them in the morning: the upright have rule and greatness over the foolish rich who love this world, of whom it says נִמְשַׁל כַּבְּהֵמוֹת נִדְמוּ (Tehillim 49:13), he is likened to the beasts that perish. In this world the fools rule the upright, as עָשִׁיר בְּרָשִׁים יִמְשׁוֹל (Mishlei 22:7), the rich rules over the poor; in the World to Come the upright are the rulers, and that is morning for them and evening for the rich. The rich wear away in Sheol when they die and leave the dwelling they had; the upright do not, for though the bodily form decays, the form of their soul stands forever.
