וְהָיָה הֶֽעָקֹב לְמִישׁוֹר (Yeshayahu 40:4), the crooked shall become level ground. הוֹלֵךְ לְדוֹדִי לְמֵישָׁרִים (Shir HaShirim 7:10), going to my beloved in straightness, because good wine goes straight and is very pleasant to a man; and so יִתְהַלֵּךְ בְּמֵישָׁרִֽים (Mishlei 23:31), it goes along in straightness.

Where the verb takes an object it makes straight: יַשְּׁרוּ בָּֽעֲרָבָה מְסִלָּה (Yeshayahu 40:3), make a highway straight in the plain; הַֽמְיַשְּׁרִים אֹֽרְחוֹתָֽם (Mishlei 9:15), those who make their paths straight. In another heavy form, with the first root letter sounded against the usual way, וְעַפְעַפֶּיךָ יַיְשִׁרוּ נֶגְדֶּֽךָ (Mishlei 4:25), let your eyelids look straight before you.

פדן.sense: His palace, אַפַּדְנוֹ, the alef added. פדן ארם is named so because two places were called Aram, פדן being two in Chazal's words; some take it as the field of Aram.

more.t: וְיִטַּע אָֽהֳלֵי אַפַּדְנוֹ (Daniel 11:45), and he will plant the tents of his palace: the alef is an addition and the word means his palace, and in the words of Chazal a palace is called אפדנא (Bava Metzia 35a). His father writes that the alef is a root letter and the nun the addition, from וְאָֽפַדְתָּ לוֹ (Shemos 29:5), and you shall gird it on him, and files the pasuk under the root אפד.

מִפַּדַּן אֲרָם (Bereishis 25:20), from Paddan Aram, and פַּדֶּנָֽה אֲרָם (Bereishis 28:2), to Paddan Aram: it is called so because there were two places called Aram, Aram Naharayim and Aram Tzovah. In the words of Chazal פדן is two: ההוא גברא דגזל פדנא דתורי מחבריה (Bava Kama 96b), that man who stole a פדנא of oxen from his fellow, which Radak explains as a yoke of oxen. And the Targum of וַיִּקַּח צֶמֶד בָּקָר (Shmuel I 11:7), and he took a yoke of oxen, is פַּדַן תּוֹרַיָא, a pair of oxen. There are also Aram Damesek and Aram Beis Rechov, but two of these lie near one another, and so it pairs those two; and the Aram across the river is Aram Naharayim.
Some explain פדן ארם as the field of Aram, and in the tongue of Yishmael a field is called פדן; his father writes so as well.

עבד.sense: To serve: service to men, divine service, and working the land. עֶבֶד is a servant; the land's produce is named for the work, and the word can mean deeds.

more.h: Who serves and who is worked
more.t: The plain verb is said both of the one who serves and of the one who is worked, but the one worked is joined to it with a beis, as לֹא־ תַֽעֲבֹד בּוֹ (Vayikra 25:39), you shall not work him. So of the servant you say עובד אותו, he serves him, and of the master עובד בו, he works him. Onkelos takes וַֽעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אֹתָם (Bereishis 15:13), and they shall serve them and they shall afflict them, as though it read ועבדו בם, they shall work them, and so rendered וְיִפְלְחוּן בְּהוֹן, they shall work them. It can also be read as it sounds, with the serving said of Israel and the afflicting of Egypt.
עֲבֹדַת עֲבֹדָה (Bamidbar 4:47), the service of service, is the song, which is the service of the korban.

וְעָבַדְתָּ לּוֹ אֶת־הָֽאֲדָמָה (Shmuel II 9:10), you shall till the land for him, and עֹבֵד אֲדָמָֽה (Bereishis 4:2), a tiller of the ground. Because a man's need of the land is so great, and he must be busy with it always, he stands to it as a servant before his master. In וְנִֽהְיֶה אֲנַחְנוּ וְאַדְמָתֵנוּ עֲבָדִים לְפַרְעֹה (Bereishis 47:19), and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh, the land is as a servant to its owners. The land's produce is named for the work done on it, וַֽעֲבֻדָּה רַבָּה מְאֹד (Iyov 1:3), a very great yield.

מֶלֶךְ לְשָׂדֶה נֶעֱבָֽד (Koheles 5:8) is read two ways. Either the field, from the constancy of a man's work in it, is called נעבד, worked, though it is itself the one serving, as in וְנֶעֱבַדְתֶּם וְנִזְרַעְתֶּֽם (Yechezkel 36:9), you shall be tilled and sown; or the lamed of לשדה means for the sake of, and its meaning is that even the king is served only for the sake of the field, out of which comes what he gives and what feeds his armies. That second reading, Radak says, is the correct one.

וַיַּֽעֲבִדוּ מִצְרַיִם אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shemos 1:13), the Egyptians made the Children of Israel serve, and וְהַֽעֲבַדְתִּיךָ אֶת־אֹיְבֶיךָ (Yirmiyahu 17:4), I will make you serve your enemies. לֹא הֶעֱבַדְתִּיךָ בְּמִנְחָה (Yeshayahu 43:23) means: I did not force you to pass before Me with a meal offering.

לָכֵן יַכִּיר מַעְבָּֽדֵיהֶם (Iyov 34:25), therefore He knows their deeds: מַעְבָּֽדֵיהֶם is their deeds, as the Targum renders מעשה, a deed, by עוּבְדָא; and without the added mem, וַֽעֲבָדֵיהֶם בְּיַד הָאֱלֹהִים (Koheles 9:1), their deeds are in Hashem's hand.

שׁרת.sense: To minister and attend; he gives no gloss of the sense, only the pesukim and notes on their forms.

more.t: וְשֵׁרֵת אֶת־אֶחָיו (Bamidbar 8:26), he shall minister with his brothers; וְשֵׁרְתוּ אֹתוֹ (Bamidbar 3:6), and they shall minister to him; וַיְשָׁרֶת אֹתָם (Bereishis 40:4), and he attended them; וּמְשָׁרְתִים אֶת־הַבָּיִת (Yechezkel 44:11), and ministering to the house; אֵילֵי נְבָיוֹת יְשָׁרְתוּנֶךְ (Yeshayahu 60:7), the rams of Nevayos shall serve you, and וּמַלְכֵיהֶם יְשָׁרְתוּנֶךְ (Yeshayahu 60:10), and their kings shall serve you, where in both the esnachta falls on the tav and the nun is therefore pointed with a segol; לְשָׁרֵת בְּשֵׁם־י"י (Devarim 18:5), to minister in the name of Hashem; לִפְנֵי הָעֵדָה לְשָׁרְתָם (Bamidbar 16:9), before the congregation to minister to them; מְשָׁרֵת מֹשֶׁה (Bamidbar 11:28), the attendant of Moshe, with וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ מְשָׁרְתוֹ (Shemos 24:13), and Yehoshua his attendant; and of a woman, מְשָׁרַת אֶת־הַמֶּלֶךְ (Melachim I 1:15), attending the king, where by rule the form should be משרתת. The noun: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת (Divrei HaYamim II 24:14), vessels of service, and אֶת־כָּל־כְּלֵי הַשָּׁרֵת (Bamidbar 4:12), all the vessels of the service.

שֹרת.sense: The מַשְׂרֵת, a pan: the Targum's word for מַחֲבַת, a pan, is מַסְרִיתָא, and in the vernacular it is sarten.

more.t: One line: וַתִּקַּח אֶת־הַמַּשְׂרֵת (Shmuel II 13:9), and she took the pan; the Targum of מַּֽחֲבַת (Vayikra 2:5), a pan, is מַסְרִיתָא, in the vernacular שרט"ן, sarten.

גוח.sense: To bring out, and to go out. Groaning belongs here, a groan being breath brought out, and the river גִיחוֹן may be named for going out.

more.t: כִּי־אַתָּה גֹחִי מִבָּטֶן (Tehillim 22:10), for You are my bringer-forth from the womb, a description built like גוֹזִי. Where the verb takes an object it brings out: כִּי־יָגִיחַ יַרְדֵּן אֶל־פִּיהוּ (Iyov 40:23), that he brings the Yarden out to his mouth, and מֵגִיחַ מִמְּקֹמוֹ (Shoftim 20:33), bringing out from its place, though some say the word stands of itself and means going out from its place. Going out: בְּגִיחוֹ מֵרֶחֶם יֵצֵא (Iyov 38:8), in its going out from the womb it came forth, and וַתָּגַח בְּנַהֲרוֹתֶיךָ (Yechezkel 32:2), and you went out in your rivers.

The river גִיחוֹן may be named from this, because it goes out and spreads far, being a great river, as it says הַסּוֹבֵב אֵת כָּל־אֶרֶץ כּוּשׁ (Bereishis 2:13), that goes round the whole land of Kush. His father writes that it is the Nile of Egypt, called גִיחוֹן because it goes out and waters the land. The one near Jerusalem is also called so, small though it is, and it is the one called שִׁלֹחַ, for Targum Yonasan renders אֶל־גִּחוֹן (Melachim I 1:33), to Gichon, by לְשִׁילוּחָא, to the Shiloach. It may be called Gichon because it goes out to the gardens to water them.

חוּלִי וָגֹחִי בַּת־צִיּוֹן כַּיּוֹלֵדָה (Michah 4:10), writhe and groan, daughter of Tzion, like a woman giving birth, where וגחי is והאנחי, and groan; this too belongs to the first sense, since a groan is the bringing out of breath.

נגח.sense: Pushing and striking with the horn, which he gives as the sense of every form, from the ox that pushes a man to שׁוֹר נַגָּח, a pushing ox.

more.t: וְכִֽי־יִגַּח שׁוֹר אֶת־אִישׁ (Shemos 21:28), and if an ox pushes a man. The heavy form: וּבְקַרְנֵיכֶם תְּנַגְּחוּ כָּל־הַנַּחְלוֹת (Yechezkel 34:21), and with your horns you push all the sickly; בָּהֶם עַמִּים יְנַגַּח (Devarim 33:17), with them he pushes nations; בְּךָ צָרֵינוּ נְנַגֵּחַ (Tehillim 44:6), through You we push our foes; מְנַגֵּחַ יָמָּה וְצָפוֹנָה וָנֶגְבָּה (Daniel 8:4), pushing westward and northward and southward. The adjective: וְאִם שׁוֹר נַגָּח הוּא (Shemos 21:29), and if it is a pushing ox. The reflexive: וּבְעֵת קֵץ יִתְנַגַּח עִמּוֹ מֶלֶךְ הַנֶּגֶב (Daniel 11:40), and at the time of the end the king of the south will push with him. ענינם ענין ההדיפה והמכה בקרן, their sense is pushing and striking with the horn.

חטם.sense: A single word, אֶחֱטָם: I will lengthen My nose toward you, as the same pasuk says I will lengthen My anger; for anger and wrath are also called חוטם, nose.

more.t: One line, on וּתְהִלָּתִי אֶחֱטָם־לָךְ (Yeshayahu 48:9), which he reads as, for the sake of My praise I will lengthen My nose toward you, as the same pasuk says אַאֲרִיךְ אַפִּי, I will lengthen My anger, since anger, אף, and wrath are also called חוטם, nose.

שׁמד.sense: To be destroyed, and where the verb takes an object, to destroy; of the sense itself he says only that it is known.

more.t: A list of uses: וְנִשְׁמַד כָּל־הֲמוֹנָֽהּ (Yechezkel 32:12), all her multitude is destroyed, and וְלֹֽא־יִשָּׁמֵד שְׁמוֹ מִלְּפָנָֽי (Yeshayahu 48:19), his name shall not be destroyed from before Me; and in the heavy form, וְהִשְׁמַדְתִּי אֶת־בָּמֹֽתֵיכֶם (Vayikra 26:30), I will destroy your high places, and בְּמַטְֽאֲטֵא הַשְׁמֵד (Yeshayahu 14:23), with the besom of destruction. Of all of them he says only ידוע, it is known.

רגל.sense: The foot, and going on foot; רְגָלִים, times; being accustomed. Also to slander, which may come from the foot, and near to it, to spy out a land.

more.t: לֹֽא־ רָגַל עַל־לְשֹׁנוֹ (Tehillim 15:3), he does not slander with his tongue, and וַיְרַגֵּל בְּעַבְדְּךָ (Shmuel II 19:28), he slandered your servant: the sense is informing and talebearing. It may be from רֶגֶל, the foot, since the talebearer is always going about and carrying words from this one to that one. Near to it is עֲלוּ וְרַגְּלוּ אֶת־הָאָרֶץ (Yehoshua 7:2), go up and spy out the land, which he likens to וַיָּתֻרוּ אֶת־הָאָרֶץ (Bamidbar 13:21), and they searched out the land.

שֵׁשׁ־מֵאוֹת אֶלֶף רַגְלִי (Bamidbar 11:21), six hundred thousand on foot, meaning that they went on their feet. בָּעֵמֶק שֻׁלַּח בְּרַגְלָיו (Shoftim 5:15), into the valley he was sent on his feet, means that he did not ask for a beast to ride on, from the greatness of his running and his desire for the war; and likewise וַיֵּצֵא הַמֶּלֶךְ וְכָל־הָעָם בְּרַגְלָיו (Shmuel II 15:17), the king went out, and all the people, on foot, from the greatness of the fear and the worry. וְכָל־הָעָם אֲשֶׁר־ בְּרַגְלֶיךָ (Shemos 11:8), and all the people at your feet, is those who go with you at your foot, and וּלְרֶגֶל הַיְלָדִים (Bereishis 33:14), at the foot of the children, is at their slow pace, their feet not being in a run.

וְלֹֽא־עָשָׂה רַגְלָיו (Shmuel II 19:25), and he had not done his feet, is a way of naming the hair of the nakedness, as it says וְשַׂעַר הָֽרַגְלָיִם (Yeshayahu 7:20), the hair of the feet; and likewise לְהָסֵךְ אֶת־ רַגְלָיו (Shmuel I 24:3 in his edition), to cover his feet, is a way of naming the passing of water. Targum Yonasan takes וְלֹֽא־עָשָׂה רַגְלָיו as it sounds, rendering וְלָא שְׁטַף רַגְלוֹהִי, he did not wash his feet.

more.h: A good foot, and a count of times
more.t: Hashem blessed אֹֽתְךָ לְרַגְלִי (Bereishis 30:30), you at my foot: it is like what people say, רגל טובה לפלוני, so-and-so has a good foot. שָׁלֹשׁ רְגָלִים תָּחֹג לִי בַּשָּׁנָֽה (Shemos 23:14), three times you shall keep a feast to Me in the year, and כִּי הִכִּיתָנִי זֶה שָׁלשׁ רְגָלִֽים (Bamidbar 22:28), that you have struck me these three times: both mean times, and the two are one expression.

וְאָֽנֹכִי תִרְגַּלְתִּי לְאֶפְרַיִם (Hoshea 11:3), and I accustomed Efraim, has been explained as הרגלתי, I accustomed, with a tav in place of a heh; the sense of accustoming is known from the words of Chazal (Yevamos 85b), and it is like custom. עֵין רֹגֵֽל (Melachim I 1:9) Targum Yonasan renders עֵין קַצְרָא, the launderer's spring, and the sense of רֹגֵֽל is from רֶגֶל, the foot, because those who wash clothes rub them with their feet.

עשׁת.sense: Bright and clear, as burnished iron or ivory; in another sense thought, from which, he holds, eleven is named, as the counter's first thought after ten.

more.t: שָֽׁמְנוּ עָֽשְׁתוּ (Yirmiyahu 5:28), they grew fat, they grew bright: he glosses עָֽשְׁתוּ as צחו וזכו, they became bright and clear. בַּרְזֶל עָשׁוֹת (Yechezkel 27:19) is iron that is clear and burnished, עָשׁוֹת being a description of the iron weighed like רָחוֹק, far, and קָרוֹב, near. It is the metal called in la'az אציי"ר, or the iron called in Arabic הינד"י. Yonasan renders בְּעַרְקִין דְבַרְזֶל, meaning שבטי ברזל, rods of iron, like וְגִיד בַּרְזֶל עָרְפֶּךָ (Yeshayahu 48:4), your neck a sinew of iron; and so in the words of Chazal (Yoma 34b), עששית של ברזל היו מחמין מערב יום הכפורים, they would heat a piece of iron from erev Yom Kippur.

עֶשֶׁת שֵׁן (Shir HaShirim 5:14), which he takes as like the clearness of ivory. On another pattern, לְעַשְׁתּוּת שַֽׁאֲנָן (Iyov 12:5), weighed like עַבְדּוּת, servitude: Iyov says of himself that he is לַפִּיד בּוּז, a torch of contempt, and that before this he was for the clearness and pleasantness of the quiet and untroubled, and now he is נָכוֹן לְמוֹעֲדֵי רָֽגֶל, ready for those whose foot slips.

אוּלַי יִתְעַשֵּׁת הָֽאֱלֹהִים לָנוּ (Yonah 1:6), perhaps Elokim will take thought for us: He will be appeased and take thought for us, for the will lies in the thought. אָבְדוּ עֶשְׁתֹּנֹתָֽיו (Tehillim 146:4), his thoughts perish; like it in Aramaic is וּמַלְכָּא עֲשִׁית לַֽהֲקָמוּתֵהּ (Daniel 6:4), and the king thought and wished to set him up; and the Targum of כִּי־אַֽחֲרֵי מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵינוּ (Yirmiyahu 18:12), for after our thoughts, is בָתַר עַשְׁתּוֹנָתָא נְהַךְ, after the thoughts we will go.

more.h: Why eleven is named from thinking
more.t: לְעַשְׁתֵּֽי ־עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ (Zecharyah 1:7), the eleventh month, and עַשְׁתֵּֽי ־עֶשְׂרֵה יְרִיעֹת (Shemos 26:7), eleven curtains: eleven is called so because it is the counter's thought, the first thing that rises in his heart to count after ten, ten being the end of the number. Rabbi Yonah explained the word from שתי, two, and Radak says he has already broken Rabbi Yonah's words in the part on grammar.

שֹום.sense: To put or set: a mouth for man, the heart to a matter, battle ranks against a city, paint in the eyes; and a putting of the hand, a partnership.

more.t: מִי שָׂם פֶּה לָֽאָדָם (Shemos 4:11), who set a mouth for man, and כִּֽי־ שָׂמוּ אֹתִי בַּבּֽוֹר (Bereishis 40:15), that they put me in the pit, the second accented on its last syllable, not in the usual way. וְשָׂם דֶּרֶךְ (Tehillim 50:23), and one who sets a way, is one who sets his way in the ways of Hashem; and אֲשֶׁר־ שָׂם לוֹ בַּדֶּרֶךְ (Shmuel I 15:2), that he set against him on the way, is that he set his forces and his battle ranks to fight with Yisrael.

אֽוֹ־ בִתְשׂוּמֶת יָד (Vayikra 5:21), or in a putting of the hand, means a partnership, each of them putting his money into the business; the mem is pointed with a segol, not in the usual way, and it is as though it had a patach, and in the Hilali sefer in Toledo it is written with a patach. And שִֽׂימָה ־נָּא עָרְבֵנִי עִמָּךְ (Iyov 17:3) means: place now a pledge, and be my surety with you; or place now a guarantor on your own behalf, as it says there, מִי הוּא לְיָדִי יִתָּקֵֽעַ, who is he that will strike hands with me?

more.h: Setting the heart to a thing
more.t: אַל־ תָּשֶׂם אֶת־לִבְּךָ לָהֶם (Shmuel I 9:20), do not set your heart to them, and מִבְּלִי מֵשִׂים לָנֶצַח יֹאבֵֽדוּ (Iyov 4:20), without one who sets, they perish forever, which means without one setting it to heart. So too וְיָשִׂימוּ וְיַשְׂכִּילוּ יַחְדָּו (Yeshayahu 41:20), that they may set and understand together, means that they set the heart, as it says הַגִּידוּ וְנָשִׂימָה לִבֵּנוּ (Yeshayahu 41:22), tell, and let us set our heart.

וְֽחַנְפֵי־לֵב יָשִׂימוּ אָף (Iyov 36:13), and the hypocrites of heart set anger, is not in the sense of lengthening it, as Rabbi Yonah wrote, since one who lengthens his anger is appeased and leaves his anger, as is said of the attributes of Hashem, אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם (Shemos 34:6), slow to anger. It means rather that they grow angry and enraged when Hakadosh Baruch Hu brings suffering upon them, and they do not cry out and turn back from their evil way.

more.h: Ranks, and paint on the eyes
more.t: וַיָּשִׂימוּ עַל־הָעִֽיר (Melachim I 20:12), and they set against the city, means that they set their battle ranks and their battles against the city; and שִׂים ־לְךָ אֹרֵב (Yehoshua 8:2), set an ambush for yourself. וַתָּשֶׂם בַּפּוּךְ עֵינֶיהָ (Melachim II 9:30), she set her eyes in paint, means that she put paint in her eyes, what should come first set later, as in וְאֶת־הָעִיר שִׁלְּחוּ בָאֵֽשׁ (Shoftim 1:8), and the city they sent into fire. Some explain it as she adorned, and שִׁית זוֹנָה (Mishlei 7:10), a harlot's adornment, is of that kind; all of them are one sense.

more.h: Where the one who placed is not named
more.t: וַיִּישֶׂם בָּֽאָרוֹן (Bereishis 50:26), he was put in the coffin: its regular form would be וַיּוּשַֹם, and a small patach, the segol, has come in place of a great one, and the chirik in place of the shuruk. Some explain that it is another root, יָשֹם, and means that the one who placed him placed him in the coffin. Likewise וַיֹּאמֶר לְיוֹסֵף (Bereishis 48:1), and one said to Yosef, lacks the one who said, and there are others besides.

יבם.sense: To take one's brother's wife in yibum: he is her יָבָם and she his יְבָמָה; and the wife of the יָבָם is called her יְבָמָה too, on account of her husband.

more.t: בֹּא אֶל־אֵשֶׁת אָחִיךָ וְיַבֵּם אֹתָהּ (Bereishis 38:8), come to your brother's wife and take her in yibum, and לֹא אָבָה יַבְּמִֽי (Devarim 25:7), he does not consent to take me in yibum. The one who takes his yevamah, who is his brother's wife, is called מיבם, one who does yibum; he is called יָבָם to her, and she is יְבָמָה to him: מֵאֵן יְבָמִי (Devarim 25:7), my yavam refuses, and וְנִגְּשָׁה יְבִמְתּוֹ (Devarim 25:9), and his yevamah shall come near. The wife of the yavam is likewise called yevamah to her, on account of her husband: הִנֵּה שָׁבָה יְבִמְתֵּךְ (Rus 1:15), your sister-in-law has returned.

more.h: The form the possessive is built on
more.t: יְבִמְתּוֹ and יְבִמְתֵּךְ, his and your sister-in-law, are not joined from יְבָמָה but from יְבֶמֶת, as he set out in the grammar.

צבא.sense: The gathering of a host: to gather as a host against a place, and צָבָא, the host; in another sense an end and a set time, as a man's set time on earth.

more.t: אֲשֶׁר צָבְאוּ עַל־יְרֽוּשָׁלָם (Zecharyah 14:12), who gathered as a host against Yerushalayim, and וַֽיִּצְבְּאוּ עַל־מִדְיָן (Bamidbar 31:7), and they gathered as a host against Midyan. In לִצְבֹא צָבָא (Bamidbar 4:23), to gather into the host, the noun is added only to make it plainer, since לִצְבֹא alone would have been enough, as in וַתַּשְׁרֵשׁ שָׁרָשֶׁיהָ (Tehillim 80:10), it took root with its roots. The noun is כָּל־יֹצֵא צָבָא (Bamidbar 1:3), all who go out in the host. Where the verb takes an object, הַמַּצְבִּא אֶת־עַם הָאָרֶץ (Yirmiyahu 52:25), who gathered the people of the land into the host; and all of them are the gathering of a host.

more.h: The women who gathered at the Ohel Moed
more.t: בְּמַרְאֹת הַצֹּבְאֹת אֲשֶׁר צָֽבְאוּ פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵֽד (Shemos 38:8), with the mirrors of the women who gathered at the entrance of the Ohel Moed: the daughters of Yisrael would gather at the entrance of the Ohel Moed and bring in their hands even their own mirrors for the donation of the Mishkan.

אֱלֹהֵי הַצְּבָאוֹת (Hoshea 12:6), the God of the hosts, meaning the hosts above and the hosts below. Though strength and force lie with hosts when they agree in one heart and gather together, even so He is master and ruler over them all, and they succeed not by their own strength but by His strength and His will.

more.h: A set time and its end
more.t: הֲלֹֽא־ צָבָא לֶאֱנוֹשׁ עֲֽלֵ [עֲֽלֵי] ־אָרֶץ (Iyov 7:1), has man not a set time upon the earth; כָּל־יְמֵי צְבָאִי אֲיַחֵל (Iyov 14:14), all the days of my set time I will wait; כִּי מָֽלְאָה צְבָאָהּ (Yeshayahu 40:2), that her time is fulfilled; וֶֽאֱמֶת הַדָּבָר וְצָבָא גָדוֹל (Daniel 10:1), and the word is true, and the set time great; and וְצָבָא תִּנָּתֵן עַל־הַתָּמִיד בְּפָשַׁע (Daniel 8:12), and a set time shall be given upon the daily offering in transgression: the sense of all of it is an end and a time. Some explain צָבָא in וְצָבָא גָדוֹל as desire, from the Aramaic דִּֽי־הֲוָא צָבֵא הֲוָה קָטֵל (Daniel 5:19), whom he wished he would kill; and the chacham Rabbi Avraham Ibn Ezra explains it from the first sense. Radak spells that out: a great host appeared to Daniel in the visions of the night.

בצק.sense: Dough (עיסה); and of the foot, going bare without a shoe, which is from the sense of dough, since when the shoe wears out the foot grows doughy with mud.

more.t: אֶת־בְּצֵקוֹ טֶרֶם יֶחְמָץ (Shemos 12:34), its dough before it was leavened, and לָשׁוֹת בָּצֵק (Yirmiyahu 7:18), to knead dough, which he glosses עיסה, dough. וְרַגְלְךָ לֹא בָצֵקָה (Devarim 8:4), and your foot did not go bare, and וְרַגְלֵיהֶם לֹא בָצֵֽקוּ (Nechemiah 9:21), and their feet did not go bare, speak of a foot bare without a shoe. It is from the sense of dough, because when the shoe is worn away the foot grows doughy with mud.

עסס.sense: To tread down and pound. From it is named עָסִיס, the liquid that comes out by squeezing and pounding.

more.t: וְעַסּוֹתֶם רְשָׁעִים (Malachi 3:21), and you shall tread down the wicked: the sense is treading and pounding. From it עָסִיס is named, as יִטְּפוּ הֶֽהָרִים עָסִיס (Yoel 4:18), the mountains shall drip juice; וְכֶֽעָסִיס דָּמָם יִשְׁכָּרוּן (Yeshayahu 49:26), and as with juice they shall be drunk with their own blood; and מֵֽעֲסִיס רִמֹּנִֽי (Shir HaShirim 8:2), of the juice of my pomegranate. It is the liquid that comes out by squeezing and pounding.

פגר.sense: A corpse, which is the body without spirit; and as a verb, to be weakened and weary, unable to go on, or, on one reading, to make oneself out so.

more.t: רַב הַפֶּגֶר (Amos 8:3), many a corpse, כְּפֶגֶר מוּבָֽס (Yeshayahu 14:19), like a trampled carcass, and עַל־ פִּגְרֵי גִּלּֽוּלֵיכֶם (Vayikra 26:30), upon the carcasses of your idols. The sense is known: הפגר הוא הגוף בלא רוח, the corpse is the body without spirit.

more.h: Why the pasuk adds the word you
more.t: On וּפִגְרֵיכֶם אַתֶּם יִפְּלוּ (Bamidbar 14:32), your own carcasses shall fall, he says the word אַתֶּם, you, is there to make the thing clear: had it said your carcasses alone, one would have understood the carcasses of their children.

more.h: Faint from going, or feigning it
more.t: אֲשֶֽׁר־ פִּגְּרוּ מִלֶּכֶת אַֽחֲרֵי דָוִד (Shmuel I 30:21), who were too faint to go after David: they were weakened and weary and could not walk. פגרו may be like וּפִתְּחוּ שְׁעָרַיִךְ (Yeshayahu 60:11), and your gates shall be opened, where the chirik stands in place of a shuruk; or it may be the heavy form itself, and intransitive; or it may be transitive, and then the sense is that they made themselves faint, showing themselves weak although they were not, so as not to go, since they were afraid and chose to sit by the baggage rather than go.

more.h: The day the talmidim were spent
more.t: Like it in the words of Chazal (Shabbos 129b) is יומא דמפגרי רבנן אמרי האידנא יומא דשפמי, on the day the rabbanan are faint they say, today is a day of the moustache. Radak explains: on the day the talmidim were weak and weary from their learning and could not come to the beis midrash, they would call it by way of a figure יומא דשפמי, a day of the moustache, that is, a day of idleness, like one who shaves the moustache, which is idle work, since he takes no wage for trimming the moustache alone but only for the head or the beard.

בלה.sense: To wear out, and to wear down; בְּלוֹיֵ, worn rags; and בַּלָּהוֹת, terrors, like בהלות, panics, with the letters turned about.

more.t: לֹֽא־ בָלוּ שַׂלְמֹֽתֵיכֶם (Devarim 29:4), your garments did not wear out, and אַֽחֲרֵי בְלֹתִי (Bereishis 18:12), after I am worn with age. Where the verb takes an object, בִּלָּה בְשָׂרִי וְעוֹרִי (Eichah 3:4), He has worn away my flesh and my skin, and וְלֹֽא־יוֹסִיפוּ בְנֵֽי־עַוְלָה לְבַלֹּתוֹ (Divrei HaYamim I 17:9), the sons of wickedness shall wear him away no more. The description is בָּלֶה, worn, weighed like רָוֶה, sated, as שַׂקִּים בָּלִים (Yehoshua 9:4), worn sacks. Of this sense too he takes חָשַׁקְתָּ נַפְשִׁי מִשַּׁחַת בְּלִי (Yeshayahu 38:17), בְּלִי being a noun weighed like שְׁבִי, captivity.

בְּלוֹיֵ מְלָחִים, worn rags, is written with one yud only, the yud of the last root letter, the yud of the plural being wanting in the writing; and with an alef, בְּלוֹאֵי הַסְּחָבוֹת וְהַמְּלָחִים (Yirmiyahu 38:12). Of their sense he says only that it is known.

לְעֵת עֶרֶב וְהִנֵּה בַלָּהָה (Yeshayahu 17:14), at evening time, and behold, terror, and בַּלָּהוֹת אֶתְּנֵךְ וְאֵינֵךְ (Yechezkel 26:21), I will make you terrors and you shall be no more. In the construct, בַּלְהוֹת צַלְמָוֶת, terrors of the shadow of death, the lamed is lightened; and the word is like the reverse of בהלה and בהלות, panic and panics.

שׁחר.sense: Black, and שְׁחוֹר, the black that is charcoal. In another sense the dawn: youth is named from it, and so is seeking, since the eager rise at dawn. Also brightness.

more.t: עוֹרִי שָׁחַר מֵֽעָלָי (Iyov 30:30), my skin has turned black upon me; the adjective in וְשֵׂעָר שָׁחֹר צָֽמַח־בּוֹ (Vayikra 13:37), black hair has grown in it, and שְׁחוֹרָה אֲנִי (Shir HaShirim 1:5), I am black; and doubled, שְׁחַרְחֹרֶת (Shir HaShirim 1:6), swarthy. The noun is in חָשַׁךְ מִשְּׁחוֹר תָּֽאֳרָם (Eichah 4:8), their form is darker than שְׁחוֹר, meaning more than black, and the שחור is charcoal. So in the words of Chazal (Gittin 19a; Shabbos 104b), one may write with anything, with שחור and with שיחור: the שחור being charcoal, and the שיחור being קנקנתום, called אוורדמנ"ט in the vernacular, or ויטריאול"ה, vitriol.

In another sense, וּכְמוֹ הַשַּׁחַר עָלָה (Bereishis 19:15), and as the dawn rose, and כְּשַׁחַר פָּרֻשׂ עַל־הֶֽהָרִים (Yoel 2:2), like dawn spread over the mountains. From this youth is called שחרות, as כִּֽי־הַיַּלְדוּת וְהַֽשַּֽׁחֲרוּת הָֽבֶל (Koheles 11:10), for childhood and youth are vanity, since the days of youth are likened to the morning as the days of old age are likened to the evening.

וְשָׁבוּ וְשִֽׁחֲרוּ ־אֵֽל (Tehillim 78:34), they returned and sought God, and אֵלִי אַתָּה אֲֽשַֽׁחֲרֶךָּ (Tehillim 63:2), You are my God, I seek You, and מְשַֽׁחֲרֵי לַטָּרֶף (Iyov 24:5), those who seek after prey. Some explain all of them as seeking and searching out. Even so, Radak says, they belong to the sense of dawn, because at dawn a man seeks and searches and takes account, since one who is eager for a thing rises early at dawn; and you will find them all in this sense. So too, from the sense of morning, it says וּלְבַקֵּר בְּהֵיכָלֽוֹ (Tehillim 27:4), and to inquire in His sanctuary.

more.h: Brightness, and a trouble not foreseen
more.t: אֲשֶׁר אֵין־לוֹ שָֽׁחַר (Yeshayahu 8:20), that has no שחר, means that it has no brightness and no clearness. לֹא תֵֽדְעִי שַׁחְרָהּ (Yeshayahu 47:11), you will not know its dawn, means that you will not know the time of its coming, for it comes suddenly, like a thing that comes at dawn, which a man does not feel until he sees it; and it says the same in בַּשַּׁחַר נִדְמֹה נִדְמָה (Hoshea 10:15), at dawn the king of Yisrael is utterly cut off. Rabbi Yonah explains לֹא תֵֽדְעִי שַׁחְרָהּ as that the way of its healing and of escape from it will not be made clear to you. Radak's father reads חָשַׁךְ מִשְּׁחוֹר תָּֽאֳרָם from this same sense: on that reading מִשְּׁחוֹר is a noun on the pattern of מִזְמוֹר, a song, with a dagesh for beauty like the dagesh of מִקְּדָשׁ (Shemos 15:17), a sanctuary, and the phrase means that the brightness of their form has grown dark.

קרץ.sense: Cutting off and decreeing; and so too the moving of the eyes or the lips in mockery and scorn, as though one were cutting and breaking them.

more.t: קֶרֶץ מִצָּפֹון (Yirmiyahu 46:20), a cutting from the north: the sense is cutting off and decreeing. So too the passive, מֵחֹמֶר קֹרַצְתִּי גַם־אָֽנִי (Iyov 33:6), I too was cut from clay, which he glosses נגזרתי, I was cut. So too in the Mishnah (Yoma 3:4), הביאו לו את התמיד קרצו, they brought him the tamid and he cut it, that is, slaughtered it.

So too of the moving of the eyes and the lips in mockery and scorn, as though one were cutting and breaking them: יִקְרְצוּ ־עָֽיִן (Tehillim 35:19), they move the eye, קֹרֵץ בְּעֵינָו (Mishlei 6:13), moving with his eyes, and קֹרֵץ שְׂפָתָיו (Mishlei 16:30), moving his lips.

חמד.sense: To desire, to covet. Its nouns name what is desired and of worth: garments of worth, the delight of the eyes, a land of desire, vineyards of delight.

more.t: חָמַד רָשָׁע מְצוֹד (Mishlei 12:12), the wicked desires the net, and וְחָֽמְדוּ שָׂדוֹת וְגָזָלוּ (Michah 2:2), they covet fields and rob them, and לֹא תַחְמֹד בֵּית רֵעֶךָ (Shemos 20:14), do not covet your fellow's house. In the passive it is נֶחְמָד לְמַרְאֶה (Bereishis 2:9), desirable to the sight, and הַנֶּחֱמָדִים מִזָּהָב (Tehillim 19:11), more desirable than gold.

אֶת־בִּגְדֵי עֵשָׂו בְּנָהּ הַגָּדֹל הַֽחֲמֻדֹת (Bereishis 27:15), the חמודות garments of Esav her elder son, are garments of worth and desirable ones; and כִּי חֲמוּדוֹת אָתָּה (Daniel 9:23), for you are חמודות, means a man of חמודות, that is, one who holds great excellences and good qualities. The nouns: מַחְמַד עֵינֶיךָ (Yechezkel 24:16), the delight of your eyes; אֶרֶץ חֶמְדָּה (Yirmiyahu 3:19), a land of desire; and כַּרְמֵי־ חֶמֶד נְטַעְתֶּם (Amos 5:11), you have planted vineyards of delight.

more.h: Bread of worth, or hot bread
more.t: לֶחֶם חֲמֻדוֹת (Daniel 10:3) is bread of worth and desirable. Rabbeinu Hai explained it as להם חם, bread that is hot, and like it in the words of the Chachamim (Chullin 56a), נפלה לאור ונחמדו בני מעיה, it fell into the fire and its innards were נחמדו, that is, נתחממו, they grew hot. So they too explained lechem chamudos (Yoma 76b): what is lechem chamudos? Rabbi Yehudah the son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilach said in the name of Rav, even warm wheat bread with olives they did not eat.

נפשׁ.sense: The soul; at times the body; the will and the desire; the dead, so called because death is the soul's parting from the body; the breath; and as a verb, to rest.

more.t: Sometimes it comes in the masculine, when the body is meant by it: אֶחָד נֶפֶשׁ מֵֽחֲמֵשׁ הַמֵּאוֹת (Bamidbar 31:28), one soul out of five hundred, and כָּל־ נֶפֶשׁ אַרְבָּעָה עָשָֽׂר (Bereishis 46:22), all the souls, fourteen. בַּרְזֶל בָּאָה נַפְשֽׁוֹ (Tehillim 105:18), the iron entered his soul, is said so because the soul is afflicted by the affliction of the body; and so בְּגֹעַל נַפְשֵׁךְ (Yechezkel 16:5), in the loathing of your soul, where the soul is your body.

The dead are called nefesh because the cause of death is the parting of the soul from the body: וְעַל כָּל־ נַפְשֹׁת מֵת לֹא יָבֹא (Vayikra 21:11), he shall not come upon any souls of the dead, and הַנֹּגֵעַ בְּמֵת לְכָל־ נֶפֶשׁ (Bamidbar 19:11), one who touches the dead of any soul. So too מֵֽאֲשֶׁר חָטָא עַל־ הַנָּפֶשׁ (Bamidbar 6:11), for that he sinned by the soul, that is, by the dead. Some of Chazal (Nazir 19a) explained that same phrase of his having pained himself by keeping from wine: he sinned against the soul that desires, withholding its desire from wine altogether.

Because the soul is the mistress of the will and the desire, the sin and the trespass are hung upon her: נֶפֶשׁ כִּֽי־תִמְעֹל (Vayikra 5:15), a soul that commits a trespass, and וְנֶפֶשׁ כִּי־תֶֽחֱטָא (Vayikra 5:1), and a soul that sins; and the touching of the body likewise, נֶפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר תִּֽגַּֽע (Vayikra 22:6), a soul that touches, since the body acts in partnership with her. So too אַֽל־תִּתְּנֵנִי בְּנֶפֶשׁ צָרָי (Tehillim 27:12), do not give me over to the soul of my adversaries, that is, to their will and their desire, and לֶאְסֹר שָׂרָיו בְּנַפְשׁוֹ (Tehillim 105:22), to bind his princes at his soul, that is, by his own will, without leave of the king.

It is said of the breath and the vapour that goes out from the mouth, נַפְשׁוֹ גֶּחָלִים תְּלַהֵט (Iyov 41:13), his breath kindles coals; and Ibn Ezra explained לָכֵן הִרְחִיבָה שְּׁאוֹל נַפְשָׁהּ (Yeshayahu 5:14) the same way, therefore the grave has widened her breath. The verb is שָׁבַת וַיִּנָּפַֽשׁ (Shemos 31:17), He ceased and rested, and וְיִנָּפֵשׁ בֶּן־אֲמָֽתְךָ (Shemos 23:12), and the son of your handmaid may rest, that is, that his soul may rest.

more.h: Her own; and the soul as a figure
more.t: וְשִׁלַּחְתָּהּ לְנַפְשָׁהּ (Devarim 21:14), you shall send her away to herself, is that she is to belong to herself and not stand in another's authority. And by way of a figure it says that Hashem swore בְּנַפְשׁוֹ (Amos 6:8), by His soul, and so אֲשֶׁר לֹא־נָשָׂא לַשָּׁוְא נַפְשִׁי (Tehillim 24:4), who has not taken My soul in vain, and וְנַפְשׁוֹ אִוְּתָה וַיָּֽעַשׂ (Iyov 23:13), and His soul desired, and He did it.

בוא.sense: To come, and where it takes an object, to bring. Of the sun, its setting; a respectful term for marital relations; and תְּבוּאָה, produce, named for the coming year.

more.t: בָּא אָחִיךָ בְּמִרְמָה (Bereishis 27:35), your brother came with guile. Where the verb takes an object it is bringing: וְהֵֽבֵאתִי עֲלֵיכֶם (Vayikra 26:25), I will bring upon you, and וְהֵבִיאוּ בָנַיִךְ בְּחֹצֶן (Yeshayahu 49:22), they shall bring your sons in the bosom; and in the passive, כִּי הֽוּבְאוּ בֵּית יוֹסֵף (Bereishis 43:18), that they were brought to Yosef's house. The word is also used as a way of honour for what passes between man and wife, as וַיָּבֹא אֶל־הָגָר (Bereishis 16:4), and he came to Hagar.

more.h: A hired beast comes for its wage
more.t: בָּא בִּשְׂכָרֽוֹ (Shemos 22:14), it came for its hire: it came to the work for its wage and not for nothing as with a borrower, and therefore the one who hired it does not pay if it was broken or died, as a borrower does.

more.h: The suffix that means to him
more.t: בָּהֶם תְּֽבוֹאָתְךָ טוֹבָֽה (Iyov 22:21) is by them good will come to you, אַל־ תְּבוֹאֵנִי רֶגֶל גַּֽאֲוָה (Tehillim 36:12) is let not the foot of pride come to me, and כָּל־יַד עָמֵל תְּבֹאֶֽנּוּ (Iyov 20:22) is every hand of the toiler will come to him: so through the whole simple form of this root, the suffix is read with a lamed, to. And in בֹּֽאֲכָה אַשּׁוּרָה (Bereishis 25:18), as you come toward Ashur, the kaf is not an added letter, as many have thought, but is addressed to one who knows the place; were the kaf an added letter, the Mikra would not say בואכה with it in every place it does.

וּבָא הַשָּׁמֶשׁ (Koheles 1:5), and the sun comes in, and לֹֽא־ יָבוֹא עוֹד שִׁמְשֵׁךְ (Yeshayahu 60:20), your sun shall go in no more: the sense is the sun's entering and its going in. So קוּמִי אוֹרִי כִּֽי־ בָא אוֹרֵךְ (Yeshayahu 60:1), arise, shine, for your light has come in, is that the light you were led by until now has set, and from here on the glory of Hashem shines upon you. And where the verb takes an object, וְהֵבֵאתִי הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בַּצָּהֳרָיִם (Amos 8:9), I will bring the sun in at noon.

His father explains כִּֽי־ יָבוֹא כַנָּהָר צָר (Yeshayahu 59:19), for the adversary shall come in like the river, from this sense: like the river that goes into the sea and is seen no more. It may also be taken as it sounds: when the adversary comes to make war on Yisrael, like a river that comes in a rush, the spirit of Hashem drives against him and destroys him.

וַֽאֲכַלְתֶּם מִן־ הַתְּבוּאָה יָשָׁן (Vayikra 25:22), you shall eat of the old produce, and כִּתְבוּאַת גֹּרֶן וְכִתְבוּאַת יָֽקֶב (Bamidbar 18:30), like the produce of the threshing floor and of the winepress: it is a name that covers every fruit fit for food, and is called so because it belongs to the year that is coming, while that of the year gone by is called עָבוּר. Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar takes from this sense וְהֵבֵאתָ (Shmuel II 9:10), and you shall bring in, which is accented on the syllable before the last although the word is a future, and likewise אִישׁ יָבִא בְּפִרְיוֹ (Shir HaShirim 8:11), each would bring in for its fruit, in the sense of produce; and Radak says there is no need to take them out of their own sense.

אמר.sense: To say, with אֹמֶר and אִמְרָה for what is said, and at times saying in the heart, that is, thinking; in another sense אָמִיר, the topmost bough, and from it, to exalt.

more.t: כֹּה אָמַר (Shemos 11:4), thus said Hashem, and אַתָּה אֹמֵר אֵלַי (Shemos 33:12), you say to me. וְלֶחֶם אָמַר לוֹ (Melachim I 11:18), and bread he said to him, means he said to give him bread. The nouns are אֵין אֹמֶר וְאֵין דְּבָרִים (Tehillim 19:4), there is no speech and there are no words, and אֲמָרַי הַֽאֲזִינָה (Tehillim 5:2), give ear to my words, and with an added mem, וְאֶת־ מַֽאֲמַר מָרְדֳּכַי (Esther 2:20), the word of Mordechai; and in another form, הַשֹּׁלֵחַ אִמְרָתוֹ אָרֶץ (Tehillim 147:15), who sends His word to the earth. Their sense, he says, is known.

In the words אֶל־מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹֽר (Shemos 6:10), to Moshe, saying, the saying means to say it to Yisrael. But אֶמֶשׁ אָמַר אֵלַי לֵאמֹר (Bereishis 31:29), last night he said to me, saying, is the infinitive doubled upon the verb to strengthen the matter, and the more so where it comes after; and so אֹֽמְרִים אָמוֹר לִמְנַֽאֲצַי (Yirmiyahu 23:17), they keep saying to those who despise Me.

הַֽלְהָרְגֵנִי אַתָּה אֹמֵר (Shemos 2:14), are you saying to kill me, that is, are you thinking of it; and וַיֹּאמֶר לְהַכּוֹת אֶת־דָּוִֽד (Shmuel II 21:16), and he said to strike David, is that he purposed to kill him. So too הָאֹֽמְרָה בִּלְבָבָהּ (Yeshayahu 47:8), she that says in her heart, and אָמַרְתִּי אֲנִי בְּלִבִּי (Koheles 2:1), I said in my heart.

בְּרֹאשׁ אָמִיר (Yeshayahu 17:6), at the top of the amir, which is the uppermost bough. From this sense are הֶֽאֱמַרְתָּ (Devarim 26:17), that is, you have raised Him up and made Him great, and הֶֽאֱמִֽירְךָ (Devarim 26:18), He has raised you up; and so יִֽתְאַמְּרוּ כָּל־פֹּֽעֲלֵי אָֽוֶן (Tehillim 94:4), all the workers of iniquity raise themselves up and grow haughty. It may be that וּבִכְבוֹדָם תִּתְיַמָּֽרוּ (Yeshayahu 61:6), and in their glory you shall raise yourselves up, belongs here too, with the alef changed for a yud.

Some explain אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי־טוֹב (Yeshayahu 3:10) from the sense of exalting; Radak holds it right to take it from saying, say of the righteous that it is well. It may be that הֶֽאֱמַרְתָּ and הֶֽאֱמִֽירְךָ are from saying too: you brought it about that He said He would be a God to you, and He brought it about that you said to Him that you would be a people to Him and walk in His ways.

נחר.sense: The nostrils, the two openings of the nose; and sneezing, as of horses, is named for them.

more.t: מִנְּחִירָיו יֵצֵא עָשָׁן (Iyov 41:12), from his nostrils smoke goes out: they are שני נקבי האף, the two openings of the nose. Sneezing, העטישה, is named for the nostrils: נַחְרַת סוּסָיו (Yirmiyahu 8:16), the sneezing of his horses, and הוֹד נַחְרוֹ אֵימָה (Iyov 39:20), the majesty of his sneezing is terror.

ריק.sense: To empty out, said of the vessel and of what comes out of it alike; empty, and for nothing; and, another sense, arming for war, said of sword and spear and of men.

more.h: Emptying, and what it is not
more.t: הֵם מְרִיקִים שַׂקֵּיהֶם (Bereishis 42:35), they were emptying their sacks, and עַל־הָאָרֶץ יָרִיקוּ (Koheles 11:3), they empty themselves upon the earth. This word is used both of the vessel and of what comes out of it, and in that it differs from הצקה, pouring, which is said only of what comes out of the vessel.

וְלֹא־הוּרַק מִכְּלִי אֶל־כֶּלִי (Yirmiyahu 48:11), he was not emptied from vessel to vessel. Of שֶׁמֶן תּוּרַק שְׁמֶךָ (Shir HaShirim 1:3), your name is oil poured out, he says the word may be a descriptive form with an added tav, and though its vowel is a patach we find others like it: יִסַּד בְּצִיּוֹן (Yeshayahu 28:16), laying in Tzion, and לֵב הוּתַל (Yeshayahu 44:20), a deceived heart.

כֵּלִים רֵקִים (Melachim II 4:3), empty vessels, and הַשִּׁבֳּלִים הָרֵקוֹת (Bereishis 41:27), the empty ears of grain. As a noun, וְתַם לָרִיק כֹּחֲכֶם (Vayikra 26:20), your strength spent for nothing, and וּלְאֻמִּים יֶהְגוּ־רִיק (Tehillim 2:1), peoples murmuring emptiness. With an added mem, רֵיקָם שִׁלַּחְתָּנִי (Bereishis 31:42), you would have sent me away empty handed, one form serving male and female alike.

וְחֶרֶב אָרִיק אַחֲרֵיהֶם (Yechezkel 5:2), I will draw out a sword after them, וְהָרֵק חֲנִית (Tehillim 35:3), draw out the spear, and וַיָּרֶק אֶת־חֲנִיכָיו (Bereishis 14:14), he armed his trained men, are another sense, arming for war. It can be read as near the first sense, since taking a sword out of its sheath is like emptying a vessel, and perhaps some spears too are made with a sheath; on that reading וַיָּרֶק אֶת־חֲנִיכָיו is said because the men empty out the swords.

more.h: Like the mire of the streets
more.t: On אֲרִיקֵם in כְּטִיט חוּצוֹת אֲרִיקֵם (Tehillim 18:43), like the mire of the streets, his own view is that the quiescent letter stands in place of a dagesh the word should have had, and that it is of the sense of רקק in the words of Chazal (Chullin 27b), where a bird created מן הרקק, from the mire, is made fit by one sign; and the רקק is soft mud. Or the word may belong with וְרַקּוֹת בָּשָׂר (Bereishis 41:19), lean of flesh, and וּרְקִיקֵי מַצּוֹת (Shemos 29:2), thin matzah wafers, which is a sense of poorness.

בחר.sense: To choose; נִבְחָר, choice; and בָּחוּר, a young man, so called because he is chosen for any work or for war more than an old man is.

more.t: כִּי־יַעֲקֹב בָּחַר לוֹ (Tehillim 135:4), for Yaakov He chose for Himself, and הַבֹּחֵר בִּירוּשָׁלָם (Zecharyah 3:2), who chooses Yerushalayim; and where a man chooses, כִּי־בֹחֵר אַתָּה לְבֶן־יִשַׁי (Shmuel I 20:30), you are choosing the son of Yishai.

On בְּחַרְתִּיךָ בְּכוּר עֹנִי (Yeshayahu 48:10), I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction, Rabbi Yonah explained the word as בחנתיך, I have tested you. Radak sees no need for that: a man chooses the gold out from the dross in the furnace.

more.h: The choice thing, and the young man
more.t: In the passive, וְנִבְחַר מָוֶת מֵחַיִּים (Yirmiyahu 8:3), death will be chosen over life, and כֶּסֶף נִבְחָר (Mishlei 10:20), choice silver, a form Rabbi Yonah did not record. One young in days is called בָּחוּר because he is chosen for anything, for any work or for war, more than an old man: בָּחוּר וּבְתוּלָה (Yechezkel 9:6), young man and maiden. The noun is youth: מְשָׁרֵת מֹשֶׁה מִבְּחֻרָיו (Bamidbar 11:28), Moshe's attendant from his youth, as מנעוריו. With an added mem, מִבְחַר, as בְּמִבְחַר קְבָרֵינוּ (Bereishis 23:6), in the choicest of our graves.

מִבְחַר וְטוֹב־לְבָנוֹן (Yechezkel 31:16), the choicest and best of Levanon, stands as one construct upon another, as אֶת־מִסְפַּר מִפְקַד־הָעָם (Shmuel II 24:9), the number of the mustering of the people, and חַכְמֵי יֹעֲצֵי פַרְעֹה (Yeshayahu 19:11), the wise men of Pharaoh's counsellors.

תלע.sense: A worm, and Israel likened to one in exile; crimson, named for the worm, or else תולע itself means colour; another sense, the thick teeth, with letters transposed.

more.t: כִּי תֹֽאכְלֶנּוּ הַתֹּלָֽעַת (Devarim 28:39), for the worm will eat it, and וַיָּרֻם תּֽוֹלָעִים (Shemos 16:20), it bred worms. By way of figure, אַל־תִּֽירְאִי תּוֹלַעַת יַֽעֲקֹב (Yeshayahu 41:14), fear not, worm of Yaakov, because they are weak in exile like a worm; and the Midrash Yelamdenu says that as the worm's whole strength is only in its mouth, so Israel's whole strength is in prayer.

אִם־יַאְדִּימוּ כַתּוֹלָע (Yeshayahu 1:18), though they be red as crimson, and וְתוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי (Shemos 25:4), and crimson. Radak has already explained that the שני is the כרמ"ז, the kermes, and it is called by the word for a worm because of how much of the worm is in it. Or תולע may mean colour, so that תולעת שני says a red colour, and שְׁנִי הַתּוֹלַעַת (Vayikra 14:6) says red of colour, that is, the fine colour, which is the kermes.

Because the colour is well known and finer than the rest, the word תולע is used without שני, and it is as though שני were said: האמונים עֲלֵי תוֹלָע (Eichah 4:5), those brought up on crimson. From it, אַנְשֵׁי־חַיִל מְתֻלָּעִים (Nachum 2:4), men of valour clothed in crimson, that is, dressed in garments of שני.

Another sense: וָֽאֲשַׁבְּרָה מְתַלְּעוֹת עַוָּל (Iyov 29:17), I broke the thick teeth of the wrongdoer. The word is מַלְתְּעוֹת with its letters transposed, as in מַלְתְּעוֹת כְּפִירִים (Tehillim 58:7), the teeth of young lions, and they are the thick teeth.

לתע.sense: The large teeth, מַלְתְּעוֹת; and from this a verb for those teeth being uprooted and falling out.

more.t: מַלְתְּעוֹת כְּפִירִים (Tehillim 58:7), the מלתעות of young lions, which are the large teeth. From this, in the passive, וְשִׁנֵּי כְפִירִים נִתָּֽעוּ (Iyov 4:10), and the teeth of young lions are uprooted, where the form by rights is נִלְתָּעוּ; it means the uprooting of the מלתעות and their falling out, as יְשַׁרֵשׁ is the uprooting of a root.
בְּעַד הָֽאֶשְׁנָב (Shoftim 5:28), through the window, and בְּעַד אֶשְׁנַבִּי נִשְׁקָֽפְתִּי (Mishlei 7:6), through my window I looked out: פירושו חלון, its meaning is a window.

נשׁב.sense: Of the wind, to blow upon a thing; to make the wind blow, and to make a thing fly off. The sense, he says, is ההפרחה והריחוף, making fly and hovering.

more.t: נָשְׁבָה בּוֹ (Yeshayahu 40:7), said of the wind of Hashem that blew upon it. Where the verb takes an object, יַשֵּׁב רוּחוֹ יִזְּלוּ־מָיִם (Tehillim 147:18), He makes His wind blow and the waters flow, and וַיַּשֵּׁב אֹתָם אַבְרָם (Bereishis 15:11), and Avram made them fly off. ענין ההפרחה והריחוף, the sense of making fly away and hovering.

אבר.sense: Two senses: might and strength, said of the mighty and of strong horses; and the wing, with a verb for flying.

more.t: אַבִּירֵי בָשָׁן (Tehillim 22:13), the mighty ones of Bashan, and אֶשְׁתּוֹלְלוּ אַבִּירֵי לֵב (Tehillim 76:6), the stout of heart were despoiled: these and their like are לשון עוצם וחוזק, a word of might and strength. דַּהֲרוֹת אַבִּירָיו (Shoftim 5:22), the galloping of his mighty ones, he explains as the strong horses.

לֶחֶם אַבִּירִים אָכַל אִישׁ (Tehillim 78:25), a man ate the bread of the mighty, he explains of the mon that came down to them from the heavens, the heavens being the mighty ones, as is said of them חֲזָקִים כִּרְאִי מוּצָק (Iyov 37:18), strong as a molten mirror.

מִי־יִתֶּן־לִּי אֵבֶר כַּיּוֹנָה (Tehillim 55:7), who would give me a wing like a dove's, אֶרֶךְ הָאֵבֶר (Yechezkel 17:3), long of pinion, and בְּאֶבְרָתוֹ יָסֶךְ לָךְ (Tehillim 91:4), under His pinion He shelters you. Their sense and the like of them is כנף, a wing.

הֲמִבִּינָתְךָ יַאֲבֶר־נֵץ (Iyov 39:26), does the hawk fly by your understanding, which he glosses יעוף, it flies; and the sense is given by what stands beside it in the pasuk, יפרוש כנפיו לתימן, he spreads his wings toward the south.

His father takes הָבֵרוּ הַחִצִּים (Yirmiyahu 51:11), feather the arrows, from this root, its form by rights הַאֲבֵרוּ, with the alef falling quiet as it does; it says to set a feather on the arrows so as to make them straight.

אגף.sense: His father takes the alef in אֲגַפָּיו as added and the word as his wings; that is, Radak explains, his troops, which are like wings.

more.t: אַתָּה וְכָל־אֲגַפֶּיךָ (Yechezkel 39:4), you and all your bands, and וְכָל־אֲגַפָּיו אֱזָרֶה לְכָל־רוּחַ (Yechezkel 12:14), and all his bands I will scatter to every wind. His father wrote that the alef is added and that the word means his wings. That is, Radak goes on, his troops, which are like wings, and the term has been said of troops already, as וְהָיָה מֻטּוֹת כְּנָפָיו (Yeshayahu 8:8), and the spreading of his wings shall be. It is like Aramaic, which calls wings גַּפִּין, the dagesh standing for a missing dalet; Chazal have it with the dalet, פרח גדפא ויתיב ליה ברישיה (Kesubos 105b), a wing flew and settled on his head. The alef is an addition, and Chazal have the word so as well, עד בין אגפים (Chullin 46a), as far as between the wings.

מנה.sense: To count. The מָנֶה, a weight of sixty shekels, is named for the known number in it. In a second sense, to appoint or assign, and a מָנָה is a portion.

more.t: מוֹנֶה מִסְפָּר לַכּוֹכָבִים (Tehillim 147:4), counting the number of the stars, and וּמָנִיתִי אֶתְכֶם לַחֶרֶב (Yeshayahu 65:12), I will count you out to the sword. In לִמְנוֹת יָמֵינוּ כֵּן הוֹדַע (Tehillim 90:12), to count our days, so make known, he takes the word as an infinitive; Rabbi Yonah wrote that it is a noun.

more.h: The maneh, a weight and a number
more.t: Rabbi Yehudah set הַמָּנֶה יִהְיֶה לָכֶם (Yechezkel 45:12), the maneh shall be yours, under this sense, and Rabbi Yonah objected to it. Radak answers that even if a maneh is a weight, as he has explained it, as in שְׁלֹשֶׁת מָנִים זָהָב (Melachim I 10:17), three maneh of gold, there is still a known number in it: the maneh is sixty shekels and the shekel twenty gerah, and every weight has its known count of how many ounces are in it.

Chazal use מנה sometimes of a weight, the litra, saying מנה דבילה, a maneh of pressed figs, and sometimes of a number, בתולה גובה מאתים ואלמנה מנה (Kesubos 5:1), a virgin collects two hundred and a widow a maneh, which is a hundred zuz. It is one thing either way, since a weight is called a maneh only for the known number in it, those places reckoning a litra at twenty zuz.
עֲשֶׂרֶת מֹנִים (Bereishis 31:41), ten times, which he glosses פעמים, times, the word being used because they are a count.

אֲשֶׁר מִנָּה אֶת־מַאֲכַלְכֶם (Daniel 1:10), who appointed your food, וַיְמַן לָהֶם הַמֶּלֶךְ (Daniel 1:5), the king appointed for them, and וְלֵילוֹת עָמָל מִנּוּ־לִי (Iyov 7:3), nights of toil were assigned to me: all of them ענין הזמנה ומתנה, appointing and giving. The noun is a gift and portion, מְנָת־חֶלְקִי וְכוֹסִי (Tehillim 16:5), the portion of my lot and my cup, and וּמִשְׁלוֹחַ מָנוֹת (Esther 9:19), the sending of portions.

more.h: Why the mon is so named
more.t: וַיִּקְרְאוּ בֵית־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־שְׁמוֹ מָן (Shemos 16:31), the house of Israel called its name mon, and וּמַנְךָ לֹא־מָנַעְתָּ מִפִּיהֶם (Nechemiah 9:20), You did not withhold Your mon from their mouth. Since they knew no name for it they called it מַן, that is, a gift and a portion from Hashem.

פקד.sense: To remember and watch over a thing; to lack, or be missing; to number and count; to command; to store a thing away; and to appoint a man over a charge.

more.t: פָּקַד אֶת־שָׂרָה (Bereishis 21:1), He remembered Sarah, פָּקֹד פָּקַדְתִּי אֶתְכֶם (Shemos 3:16), I have surely remembered you, and וְאֶת־אַחֶיךָ תִּפְקֹד לְשָׁלוֹם (Shmuel I 17:18), see to your brothers' welfare. It is said of sin too: פֹּקֵד עֲוֹן אָבֹת (Shemos 20:5), who remembers the sin of fathers, and עַד־פָּקְדִי אֹתוֹ (Yirmiyahu 32:5) he reads as: until I remember him and take My vengeance of him. The sense of all of them is ענין זכירה והשגחה, remembering and watching over a thing. וְאֶל־יוֹשְׁבֵי פְּקוֹד (Yirmiyahu 50:21), and to the dwellers of Pekod, is Bavel, called so because the time had come to remember her sin. Yonasan left it untranslated, perhaps holding it to be the name of a city of Bavel; and likewise פְּקוֹד וְשׁוֹעַ וְקוֹעַ (Yechezkel 23:23), Pekod and Shoa and Koa, which on Yonasan's view are names of provinces.

וְלֹא־נִפְקַד מִמֶּנּוּ אִישׁ (Bamidbar 31:49), not a man of us is missing, וְלֹא־נִפְקַד לָהֶם מְאוּמָה (Shmuel I 25:7), nothing of theirs was missing, and פֻּקַּדְתִּי יֶתֶר שְׁנוֹתָי (Yeshayahu 38:10), I am deprived of the rest of my years: the sense of all of them is חסרון, lack. כִּי יִפָּקֵד מוֹשָׁבֶךָ (Shmuel I 20:18) is because your seat will be lacking, you not being there; and וְנִפְקַדְתָּ is: you will be remembered, that is, my father will remember you when he sees your seat empty of anyone sitting in it.

more.h: Lest the enemy remember, or a leaf lack
more.t: פֶּן יִפְקֹד עָלֶיהָ לַיְלָה וָיוֹם אֶצֳּרֶנָּה (Yeshayahu 27:3) he reads of the enemy: lest the enemy remember her and set his face to fight against her, night and day I will guard her. Dunash ben Labrat reads פֶּן יִפְקֹד עָלֶיהָ in the sense of lacking; on that reading, with לרגעים אשקנה, every moment I water it, it means lest even her leaf be missing, all the more her fruit.

וַיִּפְקֹד שָׁאוּל אֶת־הָעָם (Shmuel I 13:15), Shaul counted the people, תִּפְקְדוּ אֹתָם לְצִבְאֹתָם (Bamidbar 1:3), you shall number them by their hosts, and אֵלֶּה פְקוּדֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן (Shemos 38:21), these are the reckonings of the Mishkan: the sense of all of them is ענין מספר ומנין, number and count.

הוּא פָקַד עָלַי לִבְנוֹת־לוֹ בַיִת (Ezra 1:2), He commanded me to build Him a house: its sense is צוה, commanded, as the Targum renders it. With a mem added, בְּמִפְקַד יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ (Divrei HaYamim II 31:13) is by the command of Chizkiyahu the king. In another sense it is storing a thing away: וַיִּקַּח מִיָּדָם וַיִּפְקֹד בַּבָּיִת (Melachim II 5:24), he took it from their hand and laid it up in the house, הַפִּקָּדוֹן (Vayikra 5:23), the deposit, and וְהָיָה הָאֹכֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן (Bereishis 41:36), the food shall be a store: a sense of גניזה והנחה, putting away and laying up.

וּפָקְדוּ שָׂרֵי צְבָאוֹת (Devarim 20:9), they shall appoint commanders of hosts, and the man so appointed, פָקִיד עַל־אַנְשֵׁי הַמִּלְחָמָה (Yirmiyahu 52:25), an officer over the men of war: the sense of all of them is מנוי וגזברות, appointment and stewardship. Rabbi Yonah wrote וַיַּפְקֵד אֹתוֹ לְכָל־סֵבֶל בֵּית יוֹסֵף (Melachim I 11:28), he set him over all the burden of the house of Yosef, under the light form; Radak found it in the accurate books in the heavy form, and the Mesorah notes two such, this one and וַיַּפְקֵד עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת־גְּדַלְיָהוּ (Melachim II 25:22), he set Gedaliah over them. In Radak's own view פְּקֻדָּתוֹ יִקַּח אַחֵר (Tehillim 109:8), let another take his charge, belongs to this sense: what he is set and appointed over, meaning his wife or his property.

קרה.sense: To lay the beams of a house and cover it with them, with קוֹרָה, a beam. A second sense is קִרְיָה, a city; a third, to happen or befall, with מִקְרֶה, a happening.

more.t: הֵמָּה קֵרוּהוּ (Nechemiah 3:3), they laid its beams, and הַמְקָרֶה בַמַּיִם עֲלִיּוֹתָיו (Tehillim 104:3), who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters: their sense is תקון הקורות, setting the beams in place, and covering the house with them. Then the beam itself: קוֹרָה אֶחָת (Melachim II 6:2), one beam, and בְּצֵל קֹרָתִי (Bereishis 19:8), in the shadow of my beam.

יִמַּךְ הַמְּקָרֶה (Koheles 10:18), the beamed roof sinks: מְקָרֶה is a name for the whole of what is beamed over, on the pattern of מְכַסֶּה, a covering, in וְלִמְכַסֶּה עָתִיק (Yeshayahu 23:18), which reads: and for a thick and costly covering. That is, the beams sink low and lean to fall because of the drip that keeps at them.

In another sense, קִרְיַת חָנָה דָוִד (Yeshayahu 29:1), the city where David encamped: it may be a construct whose second word is missing, or the tav may stand in place of a heh. In קָרֶת a tav stands for the feminine heh or for the third root letter: לְפִי־קָרֶת (Mishlei 8:3), at the mouth of the city, and בְּצֵאתִי שַׁעַר עֲלֵי־קָרֶת (Iyov 29:7), when I went out to the gate by the city. The Targum of עִיר (Bereishis 4:17), a city, is קַרְתָּא. The heavy verb from this is וְהִקְרִיתֶם לָכֶם עָרִים (Bamidbar 35:11), you shall set up cities for yourselves.

more.h: Two cities, or a city's name
more.t: The dual is נִלְכְּדָה קִרְיָתָיִם (Yirmiyahu 48:1), the two cities are taken; it may be the name of a city of Moav, and it is named among the cities of Moav in וְעַל קִרְיָתַיִם וְעַל־בֵּית גָּמוּל (Yirmiyahu 48:23), and upon Kiryasayim and upon Beis Gamul. The plural is נִלְכְּדָה הַקְּרִיֹּות (Yirmiyahu 48:41), the cities are taken, meaning each one of the cities; it too may be the name of a city of Moav, named among them in וְעַל־קְרִיֹּות וְעַל־בָּצְרָה (Yirmiyahu 48:24), and upon Kerios and upon Batzrah. The definite heh on it is no bar to that, as with הָעַי (Yehoshua 7:2), the Ai, בַּקַּרְקֹר (Shoftim 8:10), in the Karkor, and בַּשִּׁטִּים (Bamidbar 25:1), in the Shittim.

Another sense: אֲשֶׁר קָרְךָ בַּדֶּרֶךְ (Devarim 25:18), what befell you on the way, וְקָרָהוּ אָסוֹן (Bereishis 44:29), and harm befall him, and וַיִּקֶר מִקְרֶהָ (Rus 2:3), and her chance fell out. The noun: כִּי מִקְרֶה בְנֵי־הָאָדָם וּמִקְרֶה הַבְּהֵמָה (Koheles 3:19), for the sons of man are a happening and the beast is a happening, meaning that the sons of man are a happening in the world, and so is the beast, and one happening is theirs in their death. In another form, וְאִם־תֵּלְכוּ עִמִּי קֶרִי (Vayikra 26:21), and if you walk with Me by chance: that is, you say the sufferings He brings on you come by way of chance and are not the requital of your sins.

מצא.sense: To find and to be found; to befall, of the happenings that meet a man; to suffice; and, where the verb takes an object, to bring a thing to hand.

more.t: מָצָא חֵן בַּמִּדְבָּר (Yirmiyahu 31:2), found favour in the wilderness, וְלֹא־מָצְאָה הַיּוֹנָה מָנוֹחַ (Bereishis 8:9), and the dove found no resting place, and כִּי־חַיִּים הֵם לְמֹצְאֵיהֶם (Mishlei 4:22), for they are life to those who find them.

אֵין־בְּשׂוֹרָה מֹצֵאת (Shmuel II 18:22) has the alef quiet, against כְּמוֹצְאֵת שָׁלוֹם (Shir HaShirim 8:10), as one who finds peace, where it keeps its vowel. He explains it: the tidings find you no place now to bring news this day. Yonasan renders וְלָךְ לֵית בְּסוֹרָא מִתְיְהַב, and to you no tidings are given. By the sense of bringing to hand it can also be read מזדמנת, coming to hand: no reward will come your way by this news.

In אִם אֶת־כָּל־דְּגֵי הַיָּם יֵאָסֵף לָהֶם וּמָצָא לָהֶם (Bamidbar 11:22), if all the fish of the sea be gathered for them, he explains וּמָצָא לָהֶם as and it will be found for them, or else its sense may be and it will suffice them. So too לֹא־יִמָּצֵא לָנוּ הָהָר (Yehoshua 17:16), the hill will not suffice us.

more.h: What his father says of the meat
more.t: His father reads it so: when they craved, they had flocks and herds in plenty, but could not eat of them until they were brought to the door of the Ohel Moed for the sprinkling of the blood and the burning of the fats, and none of a man's household who was tamei could eat. Moshe was saying that were flocks and herds slaughtered for them so that they might slaughter anywhere, it would truly suffice them, and so all the fish of the sea; but with that not so, how were they to eat meat enough? He was answered (Bamidbar 11:23) that Hashem's hand is not short, and that He would give them meat enough besides flocks, herds and fish.

אֵת כָּל־הַתְּלָאָה אֲשֶׁר מְצָאָתַם בַּדֶּרֶךְ (Shemos 18:8), all the hardship that befell them on the way, וּמְצָאֻהוּ רָעוֹת רַבּוֹת (Devarim 31:17), many evils will befall him, and אֵת כָּל־הַמֹּצְאוֹת אוֹתָם (Yehoshua 2:23), all that had met them, which he glosses הקורות המוצאות אותם, the happenings that met them.

וְהִנֵּה אָנֹכִי מַמְצִיא אֶת־הָאָדָם אִישׁ בְּיַד־רֵעֵהוּ (Zecharyah 11:6), and behold, I am bringing men each into the hand of his fellow, and וְאֶת־הָעֹלָה הִמְצִיאוּ אֵלָיו לִנְתָחֶיהָ (Vayikra 9:13), and they brought the olah to him in its pieces. All of them are ענין המציאה, finding, which is like הזמנה, bringing a thing to hand.

פרח.sense: To blossom, and the blossom; close to it, a thing showing itself and spreading, as tzaraas on the skin; the young of birds and of men; and to fly.

more.t: פָּרַח מַטֵּה־אַהֲרֹן (Bamidbar 17:23), Aharon's staff blossomed, and צַדִּיק כַּתָּמָר יִפְרָח (Tehillim 92:13), the righteous blossoms like a palm; the noun, פֶּרַח שׁוֹשָׁן (Melachim I 7:26), a lily blossom, and כַּפְתֹּרֶיהָ וּפְרָחֶיהָ (Shemos 25:31), its knobs and its blossoms. The heavy form stands without an object in מֵרֵיחַ מַיִם יַפְרִחַ (Iyov 14:9), at the scent of water it will blossom, and takes one in וְהִפְרַחְתִּי עֵץ יָבֵשׁ (Yechezkel 17:24), I will make a dry tree blossom. Of the sense itself he says only הענין ידוע, it is known.

וַיֹּצֵא פֶרַח וַיָּצֵץ צִיץ (Bamidbar 17:23), it brought forth a פֶּרַח and budded a bud: פֶּרַח here is the leaves coming out first and the bud after, which is the reverse of the almond tree's nature, and it was so to make the miracle greater.

A sense near the first, of a thing showing itself and spreading: וְאִם־פָּרוֹחַ תִּפְרַח הַצָּרַעַת (Vayikra 13:12), if the tzaraas breaks out, בַּשְּׁחִין פָּרָחָה (Vayikra 13:20), it broke out in the boil, and פֹּרֵחַ בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה (Shemos 9:10), breaking out on man and beast.

עַל־יָמִין פִּרְחַח יָקוּמוּ (Iyov 30:12), the young rise at my right: the small ones and the youths, rising at his right to mock him. So too the young of birds are called אפרוחים, as אֶפְרֹחִים אוֹ בֵיצִים (Devarim 22:6), fledglings or eggs, and Chazal say פרחי כהונה (Yoma 1:7), the young sons of the kohanim. Others take פרחח for a compound word whose form is פֶּרַח חָח, the blossom of a thorn, pointing at men who are base and despised, likened to the blossom of thorn and brier, which has nothing of substance in it.

אֲשֶׁר אַתֵּנָה מְצֹֽדְדוֹת שָׁם אֶת־הַנְּפָשׁוֹת לְפֹרְחוֹת (Yechezkel 13:20), where you hunt the souls to make them fly: לְפֹרְחוֹת is מעופפות, flying. The Targum of יְעוֹפֵף עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 1:20), let it fly over the earth, is יְפָרַח עַל אַרְעָא, let it fly over the land. The pasuk means that you hunt them to kill them, so that their souls fly off and are gone.

נפל.sense: To fall, its many uses one sense, each read by its context; also to be less than another. The nouns: the refuse of grain, a miscarried child, and the giants.

more.h: Falling, one sense read by context
more.t: לֹֽא־ נָפַל דָּבָר אֶחָד (Yehoshua 23:14), not one thing has failed; וְכִֽי־ נָפְלָה אֵֽימַתְכֶם עָלֵינוּ (Yehoshua 2:9), and that your dread has fallen upon us; לְכוּ וְנִפְּלָה אֶל־מַֽחֲנֵה אֲרָם (Melachim II 7:4), come, let us go over to the camp of Aram; אֶל־הַכַּשְׂדִּים אַתָּה נֹפֵֽל (Yirmiyahu 37:13), you are going over to the Kasdim. After a further run, among them וַתִּפֹּל מֵעַל הַגָּמָֽל (Bereishis 24:64), she fell from the camel, and חֲשֵׁכָה גְדֹלָה נֹפֶלֶת עָלָֽיו (Bereishis 15:12), a great darkness falling upon him, he says that all of them are one sense, and each is read by the context it stands in.

לֹֽא־ נֹפֵל אָֽנֹכִי מִכֶּם (Iyov 12:3), I am not less than you, that is, פחות, lesser; and so וַיִּפְּלוּ מְאֹד בְּעֵֽינֵיהֶם (Nechemiah 6:16), they fell greatly in their own eyes, that is, they were fallen and much lowered in their own eyes against us, since they saw the wall built against their will.

וְנָפַל חָלָל בְּתֽוֹכְכֶם (Yechezkel 6:7), and the slain shall fall among you; and so, with the lamed doubled, וְנִפְֽלַל חָלָל בְּתוֹכָהּ (Yechezkel 28:23), and the slain shall fall in her midst, as Yonasan renders it, כַּד יִתְרְמוּן קְטִילִין בְּגַוָהּ, when the slain are cast down in her midst. Or it may be from the root of פְּלִילִים and of its sense, as Rabbi Yehudah wrote.

more.h: His lot fell, or he dwelt
more.t: עַל־פְּנֵי כָל־אֶחָיו נָפָֽל (Bereishis 25:18), over against all his brothers he fell: that is, his lot fell there; or it is in the sense of שָׁכֵן, dwelling. And so נֹֽפְלִים בָּעֵמֶק (Shoftim 7:12), dwelling in the valley. וְאִם־ יִפּוֹל עֵץ (Koheles 11:3), and if a tree falls, may be read like them.

וּמַפַּל בַּר (Amos 8:6), the refuse of the grain, what falls out of it in the sieve; מַפֶּלֶת הָאַרְיֵה (Shoftim 14:8), the carcass of the lion, at the place where it fell; and טוֹב מִמֶּנּוּ הַנָּֽפֶל (Koheles 6:3), better than he is the miscarried child, the unborn child a woman miscarries, called so because it falls dead.

הַנְּפִלִים הָיוּ בָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 6:4), the giants were in the land: men of great stature, called so because a man falls from fear of them, they are so tall; and in this sense, he says, the name האֵימים, the dread ones, was given likewise. And so הַר־ נוֹפֵל יִבּוֹל (Iyov 14:18), a high mountain crumbles, נוֹפֵל being גבוה ותלול, high and steep.

דרג.sense: Steps, by way of the Targum, which renders going up בְמַעֲלֹת, by steps, as בְּדַרְגִּין; he gives no gloss of his own.

more.t: בְּסֵתֶר הַמַּדְרֵגָה (Shir HaShirim 2:14), in the covert of the steps, and וְנָפְלוּ הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת (Yechezkel 38:20), the steps will fall. He glosses neither; what he adds is that the Targum of וְלֹא־תַעֲלֶה בְמַעֲלֹת (Shemos 20:23), you shall not go up by steps, is וְלָא תִסַּק בְּדַרְגִּין, the same in Aramaic, with דַרְגִּין for steps.

זרח.sense: To rise, as the sun does, its rising being its uncovering. Where it rises is called מִזְרָח, the east, and אֶזְרָח is the settled native, uncovered and known to all.

more.t: שֶׁמֶשׁ זָרְחָה וְנוֹדַד (Nachum 3:17), the sun rose and it fled, and הָאֹמֵר לַחֶרֶס וְלֹא יִזְרָח (Iyov 9:7), who speaks to the sun and it does not rise, which he reads as said of the night, and the rest of the pasuk, that He seals up the stars, as said of the day. The quarter where the sun rises is called מִזְרָח, as מִמִּזְרַח שֶׁמֶשׁ עַד מְבוֹאוֹ (Tehillim 113:3), from the rising of the sun to its setting, and the noun is לְנֹגַהּ זַרְחֵךְ (Yeshayahu 60:3), to the brightness of your rising.

more.h: Why the tzaraas is said to shine
more.t: וְהַצָּרַעַת זָרְחָה בְמִצְחוֹ (Divrei HaYamim II 26:19) he glosses as its being uncovered, since the rising of the sun is the uncovering of it: until it rises it is hidden, and in rising it is uncovered and seen. Or else, he offers, it says זרחה because the tzaraas was bright as the sun, which is why it is called בַהֶרֶת.

more.h: Why a native is called אזרח
more.t: כְּאֶזְרָח מִכֶּם יִהְיֶה לָכֶם (Vayikra 19:34): he is the settled man, long in the city, because he is uncovered to all and it is known who he is and whose family; but the stranger is covered, and no man knows who he is or whose family. By the same figure כְּאֶזְרָח רַעֲנָן (Tehillim 37:35) is the green and sappy tree, uncovered and seen in its beauty and its freshness.
וַיִּתֵּן עַל־פָּנָיו מַסְוֶֽה (Shemos 34:33), and he put a veil on his face: the מַסְוֶֽה is הצעיף, the veil, called וויל"ו in the vernacular.

סלם.sense: A ladder; of the sense he says only that it is known.

more.t: One line, on וְהִנֵּה סֻלָּם מֻצָּב אַרְצָה (Bereishis 28:12), and behold a ladder set on the ground. Of it he says only ידוע, it is known.

חוט.sense: A thread; of the sense he says only that it is known.

more.t: כְּחוּט הַשָּׁנִי שִׂפְתֹתַיִךְ (Shir HaShirim 4:3), your lips are like a thread of scarlet; and the Targum renders פְּתִיל תְּכֵלֶת (Bamidbar 15:38), a cord of techeiles, as חוּטָא דִתְכֶלְתָּא, a thread of techeiles.

גרל.sense: The lot; of the sense he says only that it is known.

more.t: גּוֹרָל אֶחָד, one lot, for Hashem, וְגוֹרָל אֶחָד לַֽעֲזָאזֵֽל, and one lot for Azazel, and עַל־שְׁנֵי הַשְּׂעִירִם גֹּֽרָלוֹת, lots on the two goats (Vayikra 16:8); וַיִּפֹּל הַגּוֹרָל עַל־יוֹנָֽה (Yonah 1:7), and the lot fell on Yonah; אַתָּה תּוֹמִיךְ גּוֹרָלִֽי (Tehillim 16:5), You uphold my lot. Of all of them he says only ידוע, it is known.

רמך.sense: Mares, in his father's reading: בְּנֵי הָרַמָּכִים (Esther 8:10) are sons of the mares, since in Arabic a mare is called רמכה.

more.t: His father wrote that בְּנֵי הָֽרַמָּכִֽים (Esther 8:10), sons of the ramachim, are בני הסוסיות, sons of the mares, since in Arabic a mare is called רמכה.

His father goes on to explain אחשרתרנים as a large beast of two kinds, from a horse and from a donkey, since אח"ש is large in Persian, and to say that perhaps they were large mules, sons of the mares.

טבר.sense: The navel; and because the navel is the middle of the body, the middle and high point of the earth is called טַבּוּר הָאָרֶץ.

more.t: In Aramaic the word is a known one for the navel, the שורר; and Chazal use it much, as פיו סתום וטבורו פתוח (Niddah 30b), its mouth closed and its navel open.

Since the navel is the middle of the body, a place that is the earth's middle and its height is called by the word: מֵעִם טַבּוּר הָאָרֶץ (Shoftim 9:37), from the middle of the land, and יֹשְׁבֵי עַל טַבּוּר הָאָרֶץ (Yechezkel 38:12), those dwelling on the middle of the earth.

כבל.sense: A fetter, and in the plural chains of iron; the land called אֶרֶץ כָּבוּל is explained from the foot sinking into it and being held fast.

more.t: עִנּוּ בַכֶּבֶל (Tehillim 105:18), they afflicted his foot with the fetter; and בְּכַבְלֵי בַרְזֶל (Tehillim 149:8), with fetters of iron, which he glosses שלשלאות של ברזל, chains of iron.

more.h: Why the land is called כָּבוּל
more.t: On אֶרֶץ כָּבוּל (Melachim I 9:13) it is explained that the land is so named because the foot sinks into it and is held fast from all the mud there, or else that it was sand. So Chazal say (Shabbos 54a) that it is ארץ שאינה עושה פירות, a land that brings out no fruit; and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says ארץ חמטון היתה, it was a land of chamtun, and why is it called כבול? דמשתקעא כרעא בגוה כי כבלא, because the foot sinks into it as into a fetter. Radak explains חמטון as sand.

חלשׁ.sense: To grow weak; and with an object, to break and crush. Radak takes חוֹלֵשׁ עַל־גּוֹיִם as crushing nations; Chazal read it in the sense of a lot.

more.t: וְגֶבֶר יָמוּת וַיֶּחֱלָשׁ (Iyov 14:10), a man dies and grows weak, a verb without an object, which he reads as: he had already weakened, since before he dies he falls ill.

With an object, וַיַּחֲלשׁ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ (Shemos 17:13), Yehoshua weakened them, that is, he broke them and crushed them; and so חוֹלֵשׁ עַל גּוֹיִם (Yeshayahu 14:12), who crushed the nations, where עַל stands as though added, the sense holding without it.
הַחַלָּשׁ יֹאמַר גִּבּוֹר אָנִי (Yoel 4:10), let the weak one say I am mighty; and the noun קוֹל עֲנוֹת חֲלוּשָׁה (Shemos 32:18), a sound of crying of weakness.

Chazal explain חוֹלֵשׁ עַל גּוֹיִם in the sense of a lot, which Radak takes to mean one who casts his lot over them, as Chazal said מטילין חלשים על הקדשים ביום טוב (Shabbos 148b), that lots are cast over the holy portions on Yom Tov, אבל לא על המנות, but not over the portions; and at Shabbos 149b the Gemara asks what shows that חלשים is the language of a lot, answering from this very pasuk.

שׁקל.sense: To weigh: the mountains in a balance, silver weighed out, a man's vexation weighed; מִשְׁקָל, weight, in several forms; and the שֶׁקֶל, the shekel.

more.t: וְשָׁקַל בַּפֶּלֶס הָרִים (Yeshayahu 40:12), and weighed the mountains in a balance; כֶּסֶף יִשְׁקֹל (Shemos 22:16), he shall weigh out silver; וָאֶשְׁקֲלָה לּוֹ אֶת הַכֶּסֶף (Yirmiyahu 32:9), and I weighed out the silver to him. In the passive, נִשְׁקַל הַכֶּסֶף (Ezra 8:33), the silver was weighed; וְלֹא יִשָּׁקֵל כֶּסֶף מְחִירָהּ (Iyov 28:15), and silver shall not be weighed out as her price; and לוּ שָׁקוֹל יִשָּׁקֵל כַּעְשִׂי (Iyov 6:2), if only my vexation were weighed.

וָאֶשְׁקֲלָה לּוֹ (Yirmiyahu 32:9), and I weighed out to him, and וָאֶשְׁקֲלָה עַל יָדָם (Ezra 8:26), and I weighed out into their hand, both carry a shva and a pasach under the kuf; וָאֶשְׁקֳלָה לָהֶם אֶת הַכֶּסֶף (Ezra 8:25), and I weighed out the silver to them, carries a kamatz chatuf instead.

מֹאזְנֵי מִשְׁקָל (Yechezkel 5:1), scales for weighing; בֶּקַע מִשְׁקָלוֹ (Bereishis 24:22), a beka in weight. Another form, with a tav, וּצְדָקָה לְמִשְׁקָלֶת (Yeshayahu 28:17), and righteousness for a weight; with a cholam, בְּמִשְׁקוֹל עֶשְׂרִים שֶׁקֶל לַיּוֹם (Yechezkel 4:10), by weight, twenty shekels a day; and with the tav, וְאֶת־ מִשְׁקֹלֶת בֵּית אַחְאָב (Melachim II 21:13), and the weight of the house of Achav. Then the שֶׁקֶל, with six points, two segols: בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ (Shemos 30:13), by the holy shekel, and עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הַשֶּׁקֶל (Shemos 30:13), the shekel is twenty gerah.

רמם.sense: To be high and to rise; and where the verb takes an object, to exalt and magnify. Also רִמָּה, the worm, and a verb from it, to breed worms.

more.t: רֹאשׁ כּֽוֹכָבִים כִּי־ רָֽמּוּ (Iyov 22:12), the head of the stars, that they are high; וַיָּרָם כְּבֽוֹד, the glory of Hashem rose from off the keruv (Yechezkel 10:4); וַיֵּרֹמּוּ הַכְּרוּבִים (Yechezkel 10:15), the keruvim were lifted; הֵרֹמּוּ מִתּוֹךְ הָֽעֵדָה הַזֹּאת (Bamidbar 17:10), be lifted up from among this congregation. רוֹמּוּ מְעַט וְֽאֵינֶנּוּ (Iyov 24:24) he reads of the wicked: they grew proud and rose a little, and are gone, for in a moment they perish.

וְרוֹמַם תַּחַת לְשׁוֹנִֽי (Tehillim 66:17), meaning what is under my tongue exalts and magnifies Him, a hint at the heart. יַחַד לֹא יְרוֹמֵֽם (Hoshea 11:7): together not one of them exalts HaKadosh Baruch Hu or magnifies Him, though the prophets rebuke them and call them to return to the Most High and exalt Him in their prayer; so the prophets' rebukes avail nothing.

more.h: The three words take an object
more.t: עַל־כֵּן לֹא תְרוֹמֵֽם (Iyov 17:4) he joins to the pasuk beside it, as a prayer to Hashem: do not exalt one who tells his fellows smooth things and will not rebuke him truly for his transgressions, for even those among Iyov's fellows who know the truth is with him speak smooth words with their fellows to condemn him unjustly. These three words, he says, take an object, and are not intransitive as Rabbi Yonah holds; and Radak allows that all three may instead belong to the roots weak in the middle letter.

וְרִמָּה תְּכַסֶּה עֲלֵיהֶֽם (Iyov 21:26), the worm covers them; תַּחְתֶּיךָ יֻצַּע רִמָּה (Yeshayahu 14:11), the worm is spread beneath you; מְתָקוֹ רִמָּה (Iyov 24:20), the worm finds him sweet. Of these he says only that the sense is known.

A verb from it: וַיָּרֻם תּֽוֹלָעִים וַיִּבְאַשׁ (Shemos 16:20), it bred worms and stank, pointed with a shuruk to hold it apart from וַיָּרָם כְּבֽוֹד, the rising of the glory of Hashem (Yechezkel 10:4).

טבח.sense: To slaughter, ענין זביחה: טַבָּח, the slaughterer; טֶבַח, טִבְחָה and מַטְבֵּחַ, slaughter. Rabbi Yonah took some as cooking; Radak reads them all as slaughter.

more.t: וּטְבָחוֹ אוֹ מְכָרוֹ (Shemos 21:37), he slaughtered it or sold it; שׁוֹרְךָ טָבוּחַ לְעֵינֶיךָ (Devarim 28:31), your ox slaughtered before your eyes; וּטְבֹחַ טֶבַח וְהָכֵן (Bereishis 43:16), slaughter a slaughtering and make ready; טָבַחְתָּ לֹא חָמָלְתָּ (Eichah 2:21), You slaughtered and did not pity; יוּבַל לִטְבוֹחַ (Yirmiyahu 11:19), led to be slaughtered.

וַיָּרֶם הַטַּבָּח אֶת הַשּׁוֹק (Shmuel I 9:24), the slaughterer lifted the thigh; שַׂר הַטַּבָּחִים (Bereishis 39:1), the chief of the slaughterers; and in the feminine לְרַקָּחוֹת וּלְטַבָּחוֹת (Shmuel I 8:13), as perfumers and as slaughterers.

כַּשֶּׂה לַטֶּבַח יוּבָל (Yeshayahu 53:7), led like a lamb to the slaughter; טָֽבְחָה טִבְחָהּ (Mishlei 9:2), she has slaughtered her slaughter; with the hei of the feminine, כְּצֹאן טִבְחָֽה (Tehillim 44:23), like sheep for slaughter, and וְאֵת טִבְחָתִי אֲשֶׁר טָבַחְתִּי לְגֹֽזְזָי (Shmuel I 25:11), and my slaughter that I slaughtered for my shearers; and in another pattern הָכִינוּ לְבָנָיו מַטְבֵּחַ (Yeshayahu 14:21), prepare a slaughter for his sons. All of them, he says, are ענין זביחה, slaughter.

Rabbi Yonah divided some of them off to the sense of cooking, and most of the commentators did the same, likening them to Arabic, which calls one who cooks meat טב"ך, the ches being a kaf in Arabic. Radak holds there is no need for that, since every one of them can be explained as slaughter.

שׁחט.sense: To slaughter. The word means drawing: shechitah is done by drawing the knife forward and back, and fine gold drawn thin is זָהָב שָׁחוּט, drawn gold.

more.t: וְשָׁחַט אֶת בֶּן הַבָּקָר (Vayikra 1:5), he shall slaughter the young bull; שׁוֹחֵט הַשּׁוֹר (Yeshayahu 66:3), one who slaughters the ox; in the passive הֲצֹאן וּבָקָר יִשָּׁחֵט לָהֶם (Bamidbar 11:22), shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them; and the noun שְׁחִיטַת הַפְּסָחִים (Divrei HaYamim II 30:17), the slaughtering of the pesachim.

Rabbi Yonah made וּֽבְשַֽׁחֲטָם אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶם (Yechezkel 23:39), when they slaughtered their children, belong to the heavy form. Radak holds it right that it be an infinitive of the light form, like וְשַֽׁחֲטָה שֵׂטִים הֶעְמִיקוּ (Hoshea 5:2), and in slaughtering, those who turn aside have gone deep.

Shechitah is done by carrying the knife forward and back, because the word is the language of drawing, as חץ שחוט (Yirmiyahu 9:7), a drawn arrow. Chazal said (Chullin 30b) that if he severed the head at one stroke it is invalid, and asked from where this is learned; the answer is that the pasuk says חץ שחוט. Radak adds: that is, so must a man draw the knife over the neck, carrying it forward and back. The Sifra on parshas Tzav says there is no language of shechitah but the language of drawing, as it says זָהָב שָׁחוּט, drawn gold. His father wrote that חץ שחט is a describing word like שׁוֹחֵט, slaughtering; Radak adds: that is, a killing arrow.

זָהָב שָׁחוּט (Divrei HaYamim II 9:16), drawn gold, so called because fine gold is soft enough from its great worth to be drawn out and spread; and Chazal say (Chullin 30b) זהב השחוט שהיה נמשך כשעוה, the drawn gold that stretched like wax.

שֹחט.sense: To press, ענין עצור: I pressed them into Pharaoh's cup; and in the Mishnah, of squeezing to bring the liquid out.

more.t: וָאֶשְׂחַט אֹתָם אֶל כּוֹס פַּרְעֹה (Bereishis 40:11), I pressed them into Pharaoh's cup; and in the Mishnah (Shabbos 22:1; 143b), אין סוחטין, one does not squeeze, להוציא מהן משקין, to bring the liquid out of them. The sense is ענין עצור, pressing.

בקע.sense: To split or cleave open. From this sense בֶּקַע, the half shekel, split from the shekel; and בִּקְעָה, level ground as against the mountains, is of the same sense.

more.t: בָּקַע יָם וַיַּעֲבִירֵם (Tehillim 78:13), He split the sea and brought them across; יְבַקַּע צֻרִים בַּמִּדְבָּר (Tehillim 78:15), He splits rocks in the wilderness. Of men breaking into a camp or a city, וַיִּבְקְעוּ שְׁלשֶׁת הַגִּבֹּרִים בְּמַחֲנֵה פְלִשְׁתִּים (Shmuel II 23:16), the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Pelishtim, and in the passive הָבְקְעָה הָעִיר (Yirmiyahu 39:2), the city was breached.

נִבְקְעוּ כָּל מַעְיְנוֹת תְּהוֹם רַבָּה (Bereishis 7:11), all the springs of the great deep were split open; כִּי נִבְקְעוּ בַמִּדְבָּר מַיִם (Yeshayahu 35:6), waters broke open in the wilderness; אָז יִבָּקַע כַּשַּׁחַר אוֹרֶךָ (Yeshayahu 58:8), then your light will break open like the dawn.

In וּבָֽקְעָה וְדָֽגְרָה בְצִלָּהּ (Yeshayahu 34:15), and she hatches and broods in her shade, the splitting is the chick's coming out of the egg, and likewise בֵּיצֵי צִפְעוֹנִי בִּקֵּעוּ (Yeshayahu 59:5), they hatched adders' eggs.
בֶּקַע לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת (Shemos 38:26), a beka a head, is half a shekel, and carries the name because it is split off from the shekel.

יֹֽצְאִים בַּבִּקְעָה וּבָהָֽר (Devarim 8:7), going out in plain and hill; וְהָֽרְכָסִים לְבִקְעָֽה (Yeshayahu 40:4), the ridges made a plain; וַיִּמְצְאוּ בִקְעָה (Bereishis 11:2), they found a plain. It is a level place, as against the mountains, and these too are of the first sense.
