פעם.sense: A time, as this time or seven times. Also breaking and crushing, from which the bell is called פעמון; and the feet, and in the feminine plural, corners.

more.t: פַּעַם חוּץ פַּעַם בָּרְחֹבוֹת (Mishlei 7:12), one time outside, one time in the streets; זֹאת הַפַּעַם (Bereishis 2:23), this time; אַךְ הַפַּעַם הַזֶּה (Shoftim 16:28), only this once.

Rabbi Yonah reads לְפַעֲמוֹ (Shoftim 13:25) from that first sense: prophecy began to come to him a first time. Or it is to break and crush him, from וַתִּפָּעֶם רוּחוֹ (Bereishis 41:8), his spirit was broken, and נִפְעַמְתִּי וְלֹא אֲדַבֵּר (Tehillim 77:5), I am broken and cannot speak, a language of breaking and crushing; and that, Radak says, is the right one. So too וַתִּתְפָּעֶם רוּחוֹ (Daniel 2:1), his spirit was broken.

אֶת הוֹלֶם פָּעַם (Yeshayahu 41:7) is the breaking of the blow or the blow that breaks; or פעם is the name of the tool one strikes with, the hammer, as the Targum renders it דִמְטַפַּח בְקוּרְנְסָא, one who strikes with a hammer. From the same the bell is called פעמון, since it rattles and is struck by the clapper inside it: וַיִּתְּנוּ אֶת הַפַּעֲמֹנִים בְּתוֹךְ הָרִמֹּנִים (Shemos 39:25), a bell set between one pomegranate and the next. Chazal read לְפַעֲמוֹ likewise (Sotah 9b), the spirit of prophecy ringing before him like a bell.

מַה יָּפוּ פְעָמַיִךְ (Shir HaShirim 7:2), how beautiful your feet; הָרִימָה פְעָמֶיךָ (Tehillim 74:3), lift up your steps; פַּעֲמֵי דַלִּים (Yeshayahu 26:6), the feet of the poor. Some read הָרִימָה פְעָמֶיךָ instead as מהלמותיך, your blows. From the sense of feet is explained also צֵלָע אֶל צֵלָע שָׁלוֹשׁ וּשְׁלֹשִׁים פְּעָמִים (Yechezkel 41:6), chamber against chamber, thirty-three, with פְּעָמִים as feet; Yonasan rendered it thirty-three, eleven to a row.
עַל אַרְבַּע פַּעֲמֹתָיו (Shemos 25:12), which he takes as its four corners.

עקב.sense: Deceit and cunning; the heel, and in the plural, goings; from the heel, the end of a thing, and reward, since reward is the end of the deed.

more.t: עָקֹב הַלֵּב מִכֹּל (Yirmiyahu 17:9), the heart is deceitful above all; כָל־אָח עָקוֹב יַעְקֹב (Yirmiyahu 9:3), every brother deals deceitfully; וַֽיַּעְקְבֵנִי זֶה פַֽעֲמַיִם (Bereishis 27:36), he has deceived me these two times; and the noun, וְיֵהוּא עָשָׂה בְעָקְבָּה (Melachim II 10:19), and Yehu acted with cunning. The sense of them all is trickery and cunning. Beside these, וְהָיָה הֶֽעָקֹב לְמִישׁוֹר (Yeshayahu 40:4), and the crooked shall become level, the crooked being the winding road that is hard to climb.

The feminine adjective is עֲקֻבָּה מִדָּֽם (Hoshea 6:8), cunning with blood, and so Chazal explain it: שהיו עוקבין להרוג נפשות (Makkos 10a), that they were עוקבין to take lives, which Radak explains as acting craftily. In another place they explain עקבה as מלוכלכת, soiled: the Yerushalmi rules אם יש בו עקבת יין אסור, if there is עקבת יין on it, it is forbidden, and asks what עקבת יין is; the answer is דההוא דמלכלך, that which soils, as it is written עֲקֻבָּה מִדָּֽם, soiled with blood.

וְיָדוֹ אֹחֶזֶת בַּֽעֲקֵב עֵשָׂו (Bereishis 25:26), and his hand holding Esav's heel; וְאַתָּה תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ עָקֵֽב (Bereishis 3:15), and you will bruise his heel; הִגְדִּיל עָלַי עָקֵֽב (Tehillim 41:10), he has made his heel great over me, as though I were under his foot; and the verb from this, בַּבֶּטֶן עָקַב (Hoshea 12:4), in the womb he took hold of his heel. In the plural the word is goings: צְֽאִי־לָךְ בְּעִקְבֵי הַצֹּאן (Shir HaShirim 1:8), go out in the goings of the flock, and וְעִקְּבוֹתֶיךָ לֹא נֹדָֽעוּ (Tehillim 77:20), and Your goings were not known, meaning the place of Your goings.

From the heel comes the end, since the heel is the end of the body: נָטִיתִי לִבִּי לַֽעֲשׂוֹת חֻקֶּיךָ לְעוֹלָם עֵֽקֶב (Tehillim 119:112), I have inclined my heart to do Your statutes forever, to the end of the world; וְאֶצְּרֶנָּה עֵֽקֶב (Tehillim 119:33), and I will keep it to the end of the world, meaning all the days of my life; וְהוּא יָגֻד עָקֵֽב (Bereishis 49:19), and he will raid at the end. From it too comes the verb וְלֹא יְעַקְּבֵם כִּֽי־יִשָּׁמַע קוֹלֽוֹ (Iyov 37:4), and He does not delay them when His voice is heard: He does not put them off to the end, but brings the thunder straight after the lightning.

Reward too is called עקב, since reward is the end of the deed: וְהָיָה עֵקֶב תִּשְׁמְעוּן (Devarim 7:12), in reward for your listening; יָשׁוּבוּ עַל־ עֵקֶב בָּשְׁתָּם (Tehillim 70:4), in reward of their shame they will turn back; בְּשָׁמְרָם עֵקֶב רָֽב (Tehillim 19:12), in keeping them there is great reward; עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר־שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם (Bereishis 26:5), in reward for Avraham's listening; and עֵקֶב הָֽיְתָה רוּחַ אַחֶרֶת עִמּוֹ (Bamidbar 14:24), in reward for there being another spirit with him. In the same way reward is called אחרית, the end: כִּי אִם־יֵשׁ אַֽחֲרִית וְתִקְוָתְךָ לֹא תִכָּרֵֽת (Mishlei 23:18), for there is surely a reward, and your hope will not be cut off.

His father explains in the same way: לָמָּה אִירָא בִּימֵי רָע עֲוֹן עֲקֵבַי יְסוּבֵּֽנִי (Tehillim 49:6), why should I fear in the days of evil, when the reward of sin at my end surrounds me? In the days of punishment, the evil reward that is to be mine at my end surrounds me now; if so, why should I fear, since I am receiving the reward of my deeds now. עֲוֹן there is the reward of sin, as in כִּי לֹֽא־שָׁלֵם עֲוֹן הָֽאֱמֹרִי (Bereishis 15:16), for the reward of the Emori's sin is not yet complete. וְאֶת־ עֲקֵבוֹ מִיָּם לָעִיר (Yehoshua 8:13), and its heel west of the city, is read as its end; his father takes it from the sense of וַֽיַּעְקְבֵנִי, which the Targum renders וְחַכְּמַנִי, a word of ambush, that is, its ambush was west of the city. The Targum renders this pasuk the same way, וְיַת כְּמָנֵיהּ מַעֲרַב לְקַרְתָּא, and its ambush west of the city.

אוה.sense: Desire and longing; another sense, beauty and comeliness, as נָאוָה, which may belong to the root נאה; and a third, a boundary.

more.h: With my soul I desired You
more.t: On נַפְשִׁי אִוִּיתִיךָ בַּלַּיְלָה (Yeshayahu 26:9), my soul, I desired You at night, Rabbi Yonah said the word is like אִוָּֽתְךָ, my soul desired You. Radak answers that there is no need: its sense is with my soul I desired You, and so the pasuk goes on, אַף־רוּחִי בְקִרְבִּי אֲשַֽׁחֲרֶךָּ, with my spirit too within me I seek You. So too אֵפוֹד יָרַד בְּיָדֽוֹ (Shmuel I 23:6), whose sense is with an ephod he came down, in his hand, and אַתָּה יָדְךָ גּוֹיִם הוֹרַשְׁתָּ (Tehillim 44:3), whose sense is with Your hand You drove out nations; though for אֵפוֹד יָרַד בְּיָדֽוֹ Radak has a sound explanation of his own, which he gives at the root ירד. Radak's father explains נַפְשִׁי אִוִּיתִיךָ בַּלַּיְלָה as it stands, and the words after it as: while רוּחִי בְקִרְבִּי, my spirit is within me, אֲשַֽׁחֲרֶךָּ, I seek You; and it says at night because then the heart is free of the world's business.

more.h: Or the sense leans on the suffix
more.t: Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar wrote in Sefer HaShalem that the sense attaches to the suffix, the yud of נַפְשִׁי and the yud of רוּחִי: though soul and spirit are named, the sense rests on the suffix, as if the pasuk had said, I desired You. Many are like it, and so וְצַפַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶן לֹא חָסֵר (Melachim I 17:16), and the jar of oil did not fail, where the failing falls on the oil and not on the jar.

אִוָּהּ לְמוֹשָׁב לֽוֹ (Tehillim 132:13), He desired it for His dwelling; the noun בְּכָל־ אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ (Devarim 12:15), with all your soul's desire, and in another form תַּֽאֲוָה נִהְיָה (Mishlei 13:19), a desire fulfilled; the sense of all of them is desire and longing. In Radak's view לְבֵיתְךָ נָֽאֲוָה ־קֹדֶשׁ (Tehillim 93:5) is of this sense too: the alef is sounded with a chataf patach and the word is a past passive, so that its sense is that holiness is desired for Your house. The reflexive is וְלֹא תִתְאַוֶּה בֵּית רֵעֶךָ (Devarim 5:18), you shall not desire your fellow's house, the desiring being in the heart. The noun in another form is מַֽאֲוַיֵּי רָשָׁע (Tehillim 140:9), the desires of a wicked man, with a dagesh; Rabbi Yonah wrote it without one.

Another sense: נָאווּ לְחָיַיִךְ (Shir HaShirim 1:10), your cheeks are comely; מַה־ נָּאווּ עַל־הֶהָרִים רַגְלֵי מְבַשֵּׂר (Yeshayahu 52:7), how beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the herald; לֹֽא־ נָאוֶה לִכְסִיל כָּבֽוֹד (Mishlei 26:1), honour is not comely for a fool; שְׁחוֹרָה אֲנִי וְֽנָאוָה (Shir HaShirim 1:5), I am black and comely. In all of them the alef is quiescent, and they are the sense of beauty and comeliness.

Rabbi Yehudah brought הַנָּוָה וְהַמְּעֻנָּגָה (Yirmiyahu 6:2), the comely and delicate one, in with them, perhaps having found it written with an alef; Radak has not found it so. Rabbi Yonah too wrote it without an alef, and faulted Rabbi Yehudah for bringing it; Radak answers that there is nothing to fault, since even where the alef is not written it is quiescent after the kamatz. The noun is תַּֽאֲוַת אָדָם חַסְדּוֹ (Mishlei 19:22), that is, a man's beauty, and what is comely for him to do, is his kindness. It may be that these belong to the root נאה, the last root letter showing, on the pattern of גַּאֲוָה, pride. Chazal use the word regularly in the root נאה, and it seems that was its root for them, as when they say (Shabbos 133b) לולב נאה, a beautiful lulav, and התנאה לפניו במצות, make yourself beautiful before Him with mitzvos.

A third sense: עַֽד־ תַּֽאֲוַת גִּבְעֹת עוֹלָם (Bereishis 49:26), to the boundary of the everlasting hills, וְהִתְאַוִּיתֶם לָכֶם (Bamidbar 34:10), and you shall mark out your boundary, and תְּתָאוּ לְבֹא (Bamidbar 34:8), you shall mark the boundary to the entrance; their sense is a boundary. עַֽד־תַּֽאֲוַת גִּבְעֹת עוֹלָם is explained: as long as the boundary of the everlasting hills stands, the blessings will be on Yosef's head. תְּתָאוּ ought by rule to be תְּתַאֲווּ, and it is well to place it in this root, so that it has companions in the sense, וְהִתְאַוִּיתֶם לָכֶם and עַֽד־תַּֽאֲוַת גִּבְעֹת עוֹלָם; or it is from the root תָּאָה or תָּוָה, and then it stands alone in its root in this sense. And it is likely that its root is תוה, from וְהִתְוִיתָ תָּו (Yechezkel 9:4), and you shall set a mark, whose sense is close to a boundary, the alef standing in place of a vav.

זכר.sense: To remember; a second sense, זָכָר, the male; a third, smell, as the אַזְכָּרָה, the part burned; smell and memory may be one sense, since smell brings a thing to mind.

more.t: וְלֹֽא־ זָכַר שַׂר־הַמַּשְׁקִים (Bereishis 40:23), the chief of the cupbearers did not remember; זָכַרְנוּ אֶת־הַדָּגָה (Bamidbar 11:5), we remember the fish. זְכָרָנוּ יְבָרֵךְ (Tehillim 115:12) means that Hashem, who has always remembered us in His pity, will bless His people, and the pasuk then names in particular whom He will bless.

כִּי זְכֹר אֲנִי וָאַתָּה (Melachim II 9:25) may be a command: remember when I and you were riding in pairs. Rabbi Yitzchak Giat wrote that it is an infinitive bound to the word אֲנִי, I, as are וְשַׁבֵּחַ אֲנִי (Koheles 4:2), and I praise, and אֲנִי פִּי־מֶלֶךְ שְׁמוֹר (Koheles 8:2), I keep the king's mouth; all three, he wrote, are infinitives. Radak has written that וְשַׁבֵּחַ is an adjective, and that פִּי־מֶלֶךְ שְׁמוֹר may be a command: I warn you, keep the king's mouth.

זִכָּרוֹן לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shemos 39:7), a remembrance for the children of Israel; אֵין זִכְרוֹן לָרִֽאשֹׁנִים (Koheles 1:11), there is no remembrance of the former ones; סֵפֶר הַזִּכְרֹנוֹת (Esther 6:1), the book of records; תִּמְחֶה אֶת־ זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק (Devarim 25:19), you shall blot out the memory of Amalek. מַזְכֶּרֶת עָוֹֽן (Bamidbar 5:15), recalling iniquity, may be a verb rather than a noun: the minchah was making her sin remembered, if she had one.

more.h: Against Rabbi Yonah on two forms
more.t: יַעַן הִזָּכֶרְכֶם בַּכַּף תִּתָּפֵֽשׂוּ (Yechezkel 21:29) does not govern an object, as Rabbi Yonah wrote it does, but stands alone as the rule is: since you are remembered before Me, that is, since I remember who you are, full of sin as you are, you will be caught in the palm. So too in the sense of the male, וְכָֽל־מִקְנְךָ תִּזָּכָר (Shemos 34:19), and all your cattle: the cattle is spoken of here in the feminine, and תִּזָּכָר means that its males are to be set apart from it. This does not govern an object either, as Rabbi Yonah wrote it does, for a nifal governing an object is never found, only one standing alone.

זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בְּרָאָם (Bereishis 5:2), male and female He created them; יֵֽרָאֶה כָּל־ זְכוּרְךָ (Shemos 34:23), all your males shall appear. Some read זְכָרָנוּ יְבָרֵךְ (Tehillim 115:12) from here, He will bless our males, and then the house of Israel for the females. Radak rejects that, since בית ישראל, the house of Israel, is a general term taking in males and females alike, and so is the house of Aharon; in his own view the males are named on their own because they were the ones going up for the festival and coming to the Beis HaMikdash.

A third sense is smell: זִכְרוֹ כְּיֵין לְבָנֽוֹן (Hoshea 14:8), its scent is like the wine of Levanon, and the אַזְכָּרָה, as וְהָֽיְתָה לַלֶּחֶם לְאַזְכָּרָה (Vayikra 24:7), and it shall be the bread's אַזְכָּרָה, the alef standing for a hei. נַזְכִּירָה דֹדֶיךָ מִיַּיִן (Shir HaShirim 1:4), we will savour your love more than wine, and מַזְכִּיר לְבֹנָה (Yeshayahu 66:3), one who makes levonah give its savour, carry the sense of smell and of a thing gladly received. כִּזְכֹּר בְּנֵיהֶם מִזְבְּחוֹתָם (Yirmiyahu 17:2) is in this sense on the view of many, that is, that they used to offer their children on their altars; it can also be read from the first sense, and that is Yonasan's view, who renders כְּאִדְכָּרָא בְנֵיהוֹן אֱגוֹרֵיהוֹן, like the remembering of their children, their altars. Yet Yonasan too may mean burning, since Onkelos renders אַזְכָּרָה with the same word, אִדְכַּרְתָּא. It may be that all of it is one sense, since a smell brings the thing to mind. Read as remembering, the pasuk means that the remembering of their altars, spoken of always in the matter of their offerings, was as sweet to them as the remembering of their children, who were very dear to them. Rabbi Yonah kept אַזְכָּֽרָתָהּ (Vayikra 5:12), its אַזְכָּרָה, away from smell and set it under remembrance; that is not right, for even where that minchah had no levonah, a small fistful of the flour was burned. Rabbi Yonah also held that the bread's אַזְכָּרָה suits remembrance very well, saying that its levonah was never burned; that is not right either, for the levonah set on the bread was in fact burned on the coming Shabbos when the bread was removed, and with its burning the loaves were permitted to the kohanim; the levonah was burned for the bread, since nothing of the bread itself went up on high.

צבע.sense: Dyeing; the bird called צָבוּעַ for its many colours, as though dyed; the צבוע, a beast Chazal name; and, from this root, אֶצְבַּע, a finger, its alef added.

more.t: צֶבַע רִקְמָתַיִם (Shoftim 5:30), dyed embroidery, with a segol under the tzadi, and שְׁלַל צְבָעִים (Shoftim 5:30), a spoil of dyed stuffs. The sense of dyeing is known in the words of Chazal (Bava Kamma 9:4): one who gives wool to a dyer to dye red for him, and he dyed it black.

הַעַיִט צָבוּעַ נַֽחֲלָתִי לִי (Yirmiyahu 12:9), my inheritance is to me a bird of prey of many colours, called so because it is of one colour and another, as though it had been dyed. They say it is a certain bird that all the other birds gather round to eat because they hate it. Some explain עוף צבוע, a dyed bird, as one rolled in blood, to which the other birds gather.

הַנִּשְׁקָף עַל־גֵּי הַצְּבֹעִים הַמִּדְבָּֽרָה (Shmuel I 13:18), that looks out over the valley of Tzevoim toward the wilderness. The צבוע is a beast Chazal name (Bava Kamma 16a), where Rabbi Meir says, even the צבוע; and they said צבוע זה אפא, this צבוע is the אפא. Radak explains that אפא is אפעה, since it is their way to hide the guttural letters; and so Targum Yonasan renders the valley לְחֵילַת אַפְעַיָא, to the plain of the אפעה. The Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 7) says this beast comes from a drop of white and has three hundred and sixty five kinds of colour, the number of the days of the sun.

אֶצְבַּע אֱלֹהִים הִוא (Shemos 8:15), it is the finger of Hashem, and אֶצְבָּעוֹ הַיְמָנִית (Vayikra 14:16), his right finger, are from this root, the alef being added; for so it is found in the Mishnah, used as a verb in the heavy form (Yoma 2:1): if the two were equal, the appointed one says to them הצביעו, put out your fingers. The Gemara (Yoma 22b) explains it with a braisa, הוציאו אצבעותיכם למנין, put out your fingers for the count.

עין.sense: The eye, and looking, whether in hatred or in hope; the look a thing has; a spring of water; and in Chazal's usage, something after the manner of another.

more.t: כִּי עַיִן בְּעַיִן יִרְאוּ (Yeshayahu 52:8), for they shall see eye to eye, and עֵינַיִם לָהֶם וְלֹא יִרְאֽוּ (Tehillim 115:5), they have eyes and do not see. The word is feminine, עַיִן תִּֽלְעַג לְאָב (Mishlei 30:17), an eye that mocks a father, and עֵינֶיךָ תִרְאֶינָה יְרֽוּשָׁלַם (Yeshayahu 33:20), your eyes shall see Yerushalayim, but its plural comes in the masculine too, עֵינֶיךָ לְנֹכַח יַבִּיטוּ (Mishlei 4:25), your eyes shall look straight before you. שִׁבְעָה עֵינָיִם (Zecharyah 3:9), seven eyes, are explained by the pasuk further on (Zecharyah 4:10), where these seven are the eyes of Hashem ranging over all the earth: that is, Hashem's eyes will guard the building so that Israel's adversaries cannot stop the work, and seven stands for many guardings, as שבע יפול צדיק וקם, seven times the righteous falls and rises. In לַמְרוֹת עֵנֵי כְבוֹדֽוֹ (Yeshayahu 3:8), to defy the eyes of His glory, the sense is that they rebel even openly, as the next pasuk says that they told their sin and did not hide it (Yeshayahu 3:9), having no shame that would make them hide it; the form עני lacks the yod, which is the root's middle letter.

כִּי לַֽי"י עֵין אָדָם (Zecharyah 9:1), for the eye of man is to Hashem, that is, their looking and their hope is to Hashem and to Him they lift their eyes. וַיְהִי שָׁאוּל עוֵֹן (Shmuel I 18:9), Shaul was eyeing David, that is, setting his eyes on him and looking at him with the look of hatred. Radak holds that the look of hope is said the same way: כָּֽל־ מַעְיָנַי בָּֽךְ (Tehillim 87:7), all my looking and my hope is in You. Chazal used the word much in the doubled form (Bava Basra 115a and 89a). And וְהָיִיתָ לָּנוּ לְעֵינָֽיִם (Bamidbar 10:31), you shall be to us for eyes, is that he will show them the good road as the eyes show a man his way, or that they will have him always before their eyes and be able to repay him with good. וַתֵּשֶׁב בְּפֶתַח עֵינַיִם (Bereishis 38:14), and she sat at the opening of eyes, and הִוא בָֽעֵינַיִם (Bereishis 38:21), she at the eyes, both mean an opening in the open and in public, where passers-by came and went, as it says there, עַל־הַדָּרֶךְ, by the road.

וְעֵינוֹ כְּעֵין הַבְּדֹֽלַח (Bamidbar 11:7), its look was as the look of bdolach, and כְּעֵין תַּרְשִׁישׁ (Yechezkel 1:16), like tarshish in its look. כִּֽי־יִתֵּן בַּכֹּיס (Mishlei 23:31), when it gives its eye in the cup: its eye is its look and its shine. So of a mark: וְאִם־ בְּעֵינָיו עָמַד הַנֶּתֶק (Vayikra 13:37), if the netek has stayed in its look, and לֹֽא־הָפַךְ הַנֶּגַע אֶת־ עֵינוֹ (Vayikra 13:55), the mark has not changed its look, the look it had at first. Some take יָצָא מֵחֵלֶב עֵינֵמוֹ (Tehillim 73:7) here too, their eye went out from fat, that is, their look shines from all their fat; they read יָצָא as shone, like הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ יָצָא עַל־הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 19:23), the sun shone out over the earth.

עַל־עֵין הַמַּיִם (Bereishis 16:7), by the spring of water. It is feminine: עַל־כֵּן קָרָא שְׁמָהּ עֵין הַקּוֹרֵא (Shoftim 15:19), therefore he called its name Ein HaKorei, and אֶל־ עֵין מִשְׁפָּט הִוא קָדֵשׁ (Bereishis 14:7), to Ein Mishpat, which is Kadesh. The plural is עֲיָנֹת וּתְהֹמֹת (Devarim 8:7), springs and deeps. With an added mem the word is מַעְיָן, as מַעְיָן נִרְפָּשׂ (Mishlei 25:26), a muddied spring, and מִמַּֽעַיְנֵי הַיְשׁוּעָֽה (Yeshayahu 12:3), from the springs of salvation. עֵין יַֽעֲקֹב (Devarim 33:28), the spring of Yaakov, is in the manner of מִמְּקוֹר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (Tehillim 68:27), from the source of Israel. Rabbi Yonah counted כָּֽל־ מַעְיָנַי בָּֽךְ (Tehillim 87:7) among these, all my springs are in You; and it can also be read as all my looking and my watching is in You.

more.h: After the manner of a thing
more.t: Chazal use the word much this way: מעין שמנה עשרה (Berachos 28b), something after the manner of the eighteen blessings, and מעין כל ברכה (Berachos 29a), after the manner of every blessing, which Radak explains as מענין כל ברכה, of the matter of every blessing. From this Onkelos renders עֵין יַֽעֲקֹב (Devarim 33:28) as כְּעֵין בִּרְכְּתָא דִבָרֵכִנּוּן, after the manner of the blessing with which he blessed them; that is, Radak explains, as he blessed them, so their lot and portion fell to them in the land, and each dwelt secure in the portion that fell to him.

הִנֵּה הוּא־לָךְ כְּסוּת עֵינַיִם (Bereishis 20:16), behold, it is to you a covering of eyes: the thousand of silver I gave your brother is for him to buy you with it a fine garment, made עינים עינים, eyes upon eyes, and Bereishis Rabbah (52) explains it the same way. On בְּעֵינִי (Shmuel II 16:12), upon my eye, some say that the yod standing between the ayin and the nun belongs after them, and the word is properly בְּעָנְיִי, upon my affliction; Yonasan renders it דִמְעַת עֵינִי, the tear of my eye; and it may be read as upon my matter, the one I am in now.

קשׁה.sense: Hardness, a sense he calls known: to be hard; to make hard a heart, a neck or a birth; a hard master; and the Menorah's מִקְשָׁה, which Rashi takes from striking.

more.t: לֹֽא־ יִקְשֶׁה בְעֵינֶךָ (Devarim 15:18), let it not be hard in your eyes, and וַיִּקֶשׁ דְּבַר־אִישׁ יְהוּדָה (Shmuel II 19:44), the word of the men of Yehudah was the harder. The adjective is אֲדֹנִים קָשֶׁה (Yeshayahu 19:4), a hard master; the noun, אֶל־ קְשִׁי הָעָם הַזֶּה (Devarim 9:27), the hardness of this people, with a sheva alone; and in the passive, וְעָבַר בָּהּ נִקְשֶׁה וְרָעֵב (Yeshayahu 8:21), one hardened and hungry passes through it.

כִּי עַם־ קְשֵׁה ־עֹרֶף אָֽתָּה (Devarim 9:6), for you are a people stiff of neck, and וְאֶֽת־עָרְפְּךָ הַקָּשֶׁה (Devarim 31:26), your stiff neck; the phrase means they do not turn to the one who calls them. Its build is like נֹבֶלֶת עָלֶהָ (Yeshayahu 1:30), whose leaf withers, and קְרוּעֵי בְגָדִים (Yeshayahu 36:22), with garments rent.

כִּֽי־ הִקְשָׁה פַרְעֹה לְשַׁלְּחֵנוּ (Shemos 13:15), when Pharaoh hardened against letting us go, which he explains as hardening his heart; likewise מי הִקְשָׁה אליו (Iyov 9:4), who hardened toward Him, hardened his heart; וַיֶּקֶשׁ אֶת־עָרְפּוֹ (Divrei HaYamim II 36:13), he stiffened his neck; וּמַקְשֶׁה לִבּוֹ (Mishlei 28:14), one who hardens his heart.

וַיְהִי בְהַקְשֹׁתָהּ בְּלִדְתָּהּ (Bereishis 35:17), and it was, when she made it hard in her giving birth, which he explains as her making the birth hard upon herself; and וַתְּקַשׁ בְּלִדְתָּֽהּ (Bereishis 35:16), and she made it hard in her giving birth, another heavy form, is likewise a verb that acts on something, in the sense he has explained.

מִקְשָׁה תַּֽעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם (Shemos 25:18), you shall make them miksha, מִקְשָׁה תֵּֽיעָשֶׂה הַמְּנוֹרָה (Shemos 25:31), the Menorah shall be made miksha, and כְּתֹמֶר מִקְשָׁה הֵמָּה וְלֹא יְדַבֵּרוּ (Yirmiyahu 10:5), they are miksha like a palm tree, and do not speak, all carry one sense. So too, in another form, וְתַחַת מַֽעֲשֶׂה מִקְשֶׁה (Yeshayahu 3:24), and instead of work miksheh, means work and miksheh, since מעשה, work, is not in construct, being pointed with a segol; its sense is instead of the dressing and the evening, that is, instead of the dressing of the hair, which was fair and even, there is now baldness. Or it may be that מקשה describes the מעשה: the even dressing of the hair. Rashi explained the two pesukim of מִקְשָׁה from דָּא לְדָא נָֽקְשָֽׁן (Daniel 5:6), the one knocking against the other, a matter of striking; Radak spells out what that means: one struck with a hammer and spread the yerechim, the branches, this way and that, and all was one body, the branches and the knobs not made by themselves and joined to the Menorah afterward.

קשֹה.sense: He gives no sense here: of קְשׂוֹת הַנָּסֶךְ, the kesos of the covering, and the forms beside it, he says he has explained them at the roots נסך and נקה.

more.t: וּקְשׂוֹתָיו וּמְנַקִיֹתָיו (Shemos 25:29), its kesos and its menakiyos, and וְאֵת קְשׂוֹת הַנָּסֶךְ (Bamidbar 4:7), and the kesos of the covering; with the root's last letter showing, וְאֶת־ הַקְּשָׂוֹת אֲשֶׁר יֻסַּךְ בָּהֵן (Shemos 37:16), and the kesos with which it is covered, a form like יֹשְבֵי קְצָוֹת (Tehillim 65:9), those who dwell at the ends. He says he has explained them already at the roots נסך and נקה.

קשׁח.sense: To be cruel and hard of heart: dealing hardly with one's young, and a heart hardened away from the fear of Hashem.

more.t: הִקְשִׁיחַ בָּנֶיהָ לְּלֹא־לָהּ (Iyov 39:16), she deals hardly with her young as though they were not hers, and תַּקְשִׁיחַ לִבֵּנוּ מִיִּרְאָתֶךָ (Yeshayahu 63:17), You harden our heart away from fearing You: the sense is cruelty and hardness of heart.

On the pasuk in Yeshayahu: seeing the ease of the wicked, the length of our exile and our being trampled by them, our heart hardens over it, as though You were the one making us stray from Your ways and hardening our heart away from Your fear, when we see that the ease has lasted long for them, and the exile and the troubles for us.

נגב.sense: The south, and waste, parched land; in the Targum and in Chazal, to dry. The south itself is called נֶגֶב, he says, for the drought of that quarter and its heat.

more.t: מֶֽלֶךְ־ הַנֶּגֶב (Daniel 11:5), the king of the south, with six points, and צָפֹנָה וָנֶגְבָּה (Bereishis 13:14), northward and southward: it is the south.

כִּי אֶרֶץ הַנֶּגֶב נְתַתָּנִי (Yehoshua 15:19), for you have given me a land of the Negev, which he explains as ארץ חרבה וחררה, a waste and parched land; and likewise כַּֽאֲפִיקִים בַּנֶּֽגֶב (Tehillim 126:4), like streams in the dry land, כְּסוּפוֹת בַּנֶּגֶב (Yeshayahu 21:1), like whirlwinds in the dry land, and מַשָּׂא בַּֽהֲמוֹת נֶגֶב (Yeshayahu 30:6), the burden of the beasts of the dry land.

more.h: Drying, in Targum and in Chazal
more.t: חָֽרְבוּ פְּנֵי הָֽאֲדָמָֽה (Bereishis 8:13), the face of the ground was dry, which the Targum renders נְגוּבוּ אַפֵּי אַרְעָא, the face of the land dried; and Chazal (Taharos 10:8) say מנגבן והן טהורין, he wipes them dry and they are clean. They use the word much besides.

more.h: Which sense, in Shmuel and Yirmiyahu
more.t: וְדָוִד קָם מֵאֵצֶל הַנֶּגֶב (Shmuel I 20:41), and David rose from beside the Negev, נֶגֶב יְהוּדָה (Shmuel I 27:10), the Negev of Yehudah, and אֶל־ נֶגֶב וְאֶל־צִקְלַג (Shmuel I 30:1), to the Negev and to Tziklag, may all be the wilderness and the place of waste and dryness, or they may be the south; so too עָרֵי הַנֶּגֶב סֻגְּרוּ (Yirmiyahu 13:19), the cities of the Negev are shut up. Or these may mean level ground, since the wilderness too is level. The south itself is called נֶגֶב because that quarter has much drought and no settlement as the others have, for its heat.

יבשׁ.sense: To dry up, and to dry a thing up, with יַבָּשָׁה, the dry land; another sense is shame, and two pesukim in Yoel can be read in either sense.

more.t: כִּי יָֽבְשׁוּ אֲפִיקֵי מָיִם (Yoel 1:20), the water channels are dried up; יָֽבְשׁוּ עַצְמוֹתֵינוּ (Yechezkel 37:11), our bones are dried; יָֽבְשָׁה הָאָֽרֶץ (Bereishis 8:14), the earth was dry; וַיִּיבַשׁ הַנָּחַל (Melachim I 17:7), the brook dried up. The sense is known: it is dryness.

On הֵן יַעְצֹר בַּמַּיִם וְיִבָשׁוּ (Iyov 12:15), He holds back the waters and they dry up, Rabbi Yonah wrote that the vav takes a chirik and the yod is quiescent. Radak did not find it so in the accurate books, but with a sheva under the vav and a chirik under the yod.

אֲשֶׁר־ הוֹבִישׁ (Yehoshua 2:10), how Hashem dried up the waters of Yam Suf; הוֹבַשׁתִּי עֵץ לָח (Yechezkel 17:24), I dried up the green tree; וְהֹבִישׁוּ כֹּל מְצוּלוֹת יְאֹר (Zecharyah 10:11), and they shall dry up all the depths of the river, which is also a verb that takes an object. Rabbi Yonah set that last as a word standing alone, and Radak says there is no need, for the pasuk means: a wind of trouble shall pass through the sea and strike the waves of the sea, and the winds shall dry up all the depths of the river. Of another heavy form, תְּיַבֶּשׁ ־גָּֽרֶם (Mishlei 17:22), it dries the bone, and גּוֹעֵר בַּיָּם וַיַּבְּשֵׁהוּ (Nachum 1:4), He rebukes the sea and dries it up. By rule that is וַיְיַּבְּשֵׁהוּ: the written yod is the prefix, the root's own yod has dropped, and when it dropped its vowel stayed on the added yod. Rabbi Yehudah said the reverse; and some say it is of the same heavy form as הוֹבִישׁ, which is also the view of Radak's father.

וְנוֹזְלִים עַל־ יַבָּשָׁה (Yeshayahu 44:3), streams on the dry ground, and וְתֵֽרָאֶה הַיַּבָּשָׁה (Bereishis 1:9), let the dry land appear, which may be a noun or an adjective; with a tav for the heh, וְיַבֶּשֶׁת יָדָיו יָצָֽרוּ (Tehillim 95:5), His hands formed the dry land. In another pattern the adjective: עֵץ יָבֵשׁ (Yechezkel 17:24), a dry tree, and נַפְשֵׁנוּ יְבֵשָׁה (Bamidbar 11:6), our soul is dried up.

לֹֽא־עַתָּה יֵבוֹשׁ יַֽעֲקֹב (Yeshayahu 29:22), Yaakov shall not now be shamed; גַּם־ בּוֹשׁ לֹֽא־ יֵבוֹשׁוּ (Yirmiyahu 6:15), they are not ashamed at all; יֵבשׁוּ רֹֽדְפַי (Yirmiyahu 17:18), let my pursuers be shamed; and where it takes an object, הֹבַשְׁתָּ הַיּוֹם אֶת־פְּנֵי כָל־עֲבָדֶיךָ (Shmuel II 19:6), today you have shamed the face of all your servants.

Intransitive: הֹבִישׁוּ אִכָּרִים (Yoel 1:11), the farmers are ashamed, and הַגֶּפֶן הוֹבִישָׁה (Yoel 1:12), the vine is ashamed, by way of figure, as though the vine had shame when it does not give its fruit as it should. So too הוֹבִישׁ תִּירוֹשׁ (Yoel 1:10), the new wine is ashamed, and הֹבִישׁוּ חֲכָמִים (Yirmiyahu 8:9), the wise are ashamed; all of them are the sense of shame. But הַגֶּפֶן הוֹבִישָׁה and הוֹבִישׁ תִּירוֹשׁ can be read instead as the sense of drying and ceasing.

נעם.sense: To be pleasant; pleasantness is a known sense, of the kind that is beauty: pleasant words, ways of pleasantness, the one pleasant in Yisrael's songs.

more.t: נָעַמְתָּ לִּי מְאֹד (Shmuel II 1:26), you were very pleasant to me; וְשָׁמְעוּ אֲמָרַי כִּי נָעֵֽמוּ (Tehillim 141:6), they shall hear my words, for they are pleasant; וְדַעַת לְֽנַפְשְׁךָ יִנְעָֽם (Mishlei 2:10), knowledge shall be pleasant to your soul.

נְעִמוֹת בִּימִינְךָ נֶֽצַח (Tehillim 16:11), pleasant things at Your right hand for ever; כָּל־הוֹן יָקָר וְנָעִֽים (Mishlei 24:4), all precious and pleasant wealth; וּנְעִים זְמִרוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (Shmuel II 23:1), the one pleasant in Yisrael's songs; הַנֶּאֱהָבִים וְהַנְּעִימִם (Shmuel II 1:23), the beloved and the pleasant; נִטְעֵי נַֽעֲמָנִים (Yeshayahu 17:10), pleasant plantings; דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי־ נֹעַם (Mishlei 3:16 in his edition), her ways are ways of pleasantness; and וּבַל־אֶלְחַם בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם (Tehillim 141:4), and let me not eat of their pleasant things. The sense of pleasantness is known, of the kind that is beauty.

כִּֽי־ נָעִים כִּֽי־תִשְׁמְרֵם בְּבִטְנֶךָ (Mishlei 22:18), for it is pleasant that you keep them in your belly, can also be read from נָע וָנָד (Bereishis 4:12), moving and wandering: that is, if you do not keep them in your belly, they will soon be on the move and go off.

מתק.sense: To be sweet and to make sweet: sweetness of lips, sweeter than honey, the labourer's sweet sleep; and by a borrowing, evil sweet in the mouth, and sweet light.

more.t: מָֽתְקוּ ־לוֹ רִגְבֵי נָחַל (Iyov 21:33), the clods of the valley are sweet to him, and מְתָקוֹ רִמָּה (Iyov 24:20), which he reads either as the worm being sweet to him or as the worm's mouth being sweetened from him.

אִם־ תַּמְתִּיק בְּפִיו רָעָה (Iyov 20:12), though evil be sweet in his mouth, which is a borrowed use, and intransitive; and so אֲשֶׁר יַחְדָּו נַמְתִּיק סוֹד (Tehillim 55:15), with whom we sweetened counsel together, which is transitive.

וּמֶתֶק שְׂפָתַיִם יֹסִיף לֶֽקַח (Mishlei 16:21), sweetness of lips adds learning; הֶֽחֳדַלְתִּי אֶת־ מָתְקִי (Shoftim 9:11), shall I leave my sweetness; חִכּוֹ מַֽמְתַּקִּים (Shir HaShirim 5:16), his palate is sweetness; מַה־ מָּתוֹק מִדְּבַשׁ (Shoftim 14:18), what is sweeter than honey; וַתְּהִי בְפִי כִּדְבַשׁ לְמָתֽוֹק (Yechezkel 3:3), and it was in my mouth like honey for sweetness, which he explains: as honey is sweet to a man, so it was sweet in my mouth; מְתוּקָה שְׁנַת הָֽעֹבֵד (Koheles 5:11), sweet is the sleep of the labourer, and וּמְתוּקִים מִדְּבַשׁ (Tehillim 19:11), and sweeter than honey; and by a borrowing, וּמָתוֹק הָאוֹר (Koheles 11:7), and the light is sweet.

סבא.sense: Drinking and drunkenness; wine is named for it, and so the wine-seller is called סובא; and סְבָאִים, a nation of the sons of Kush.

more.t: וְנִסְבְּאָה שֵׁכָר (Yeshayahu 56:12), let us fill ourselves with strong drink; זוֹלֵל וְסֹבֵֽא (Devarim 21:20), a glutton and a drunkard; אַל־תְּהִי בְסֹֽבְאֵי ־יָיִן (Mishlei 23:20), be not among the drinkers of wine; וּכְסָבְאָם סְבוּאִים (Nachum 1:10), and drunken as with their drink. The adjective is מֽוּבָאִים סָבָאִים מִמִּדְבָּר (Yechezkel 23:42), drunkards brought from the wilderness, that is, men who have drunk and are drunk.

Wine itself is named for it: סָבְאֵךְ מָהוּל בַּמָּֽיִם (Yeshayahu 1:22), your wine is mixed with water. And so the wine-seller was called סובא, as the poet has it, and so Chazal (Avodah Zarah 70b) speak of a woman who sells wine: ההיא מסוביתא דמסרה מפתחא לגויה, that wine-seller who handed the key to a gentile.

כּוּשׁ וּסְבָאִים אַנְשֵׁי מִדָּה (Yeshayahu 45:14), Kush and the Sevaim, men of stature, where it is the name of a nation of the sons of Kush; and מֽוּבָאִים סָבָאִים מִמִּדְבָּר (Yechezkel 23:42) can be read that way too, Sevaim brought from the wilderness.

זלל.sense: A glutton, one who eats much meat, as a drunkard is one who drinks much wine; and in another sense, lightness and contempt.

more.t: זוֹלֵל וְסֹבֵֽא (Devarim 21:20), a glutton and a drunkard, and בְּזֹֽלְלֵי בָשָׂר לָֽמוֹ (Mishlei 23:20), among those who eat much meat for themselves: one who eats much meat is called זולל, a glutton, as one who drinks much wine is called סובא, a drunkard.

וְאִם־תּוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל (Yirmiyahu 15:19), if you bring out the precious from the vile, and כִּי הָיִיתִי זוֹלֵלָֽה (Eichah 1:11), for I have become despised. The noun is כְּרֻם זֻלֻּת לִבְנֵי אָדָֽם (Tehillim 12:9), which he reads as: when the wicked are lifted high, there is contempt for the sons of men. Rabbi Yonah put הָרִים נָזֹֽלּוּ (Yeshayahu 64:2), the mountains flowed down, under this root; Radak holds that the right root is נזל, flowing.

איב.sense: To be an enemy, and the noun אֵיבָה, enmity; the sense is hatred.

more.t: וְאָֽיַבְתִּי אֶת־אֹיְבֶיךָ (Shemos 23:22), and I will be an enemy to your enemies, and the noun וְאֵיבָה אָשִׁית (Bereishis 3:15), and I will put enmity: the sense is hatred.

צרר.sense: To harass, to be an enemy, with the noun הַמֵּצַֽר, the strait; to bind up, with צְרוֹר, a bundle; and צְרוֹר, a stone, which is like צוּר, a rock.

more.t: וְצָֽרְרוּ אֶתְכֶם (Bamidbar 33:55), they shall harass you; צָרוֹר אֶת־הַמִּדְיָנִים (Bamidbar 25:17), harass the Midianites; כי צֹֽרֲרִים הֵם לָכֶם (Bamidbar 25:18), for they harass you; and וְצַרְתִּי אֶת־ צֹֽרְרֶֽיךָ (Shemos 23:22), I will harass those who harass you. It may be that וִֽיהוּדָה לֹֽא־ יָצֹר אֶת־אֶפְרָֽיִם (Yeshayahu 11:13), Yehudah shall not harass Efraim, is from this root.

מִן־ הַמֵּצַֽר (Tehillim 118:5), out of the strait, and בֵּין הַמְּצָרִֽים (Eichah 1:3), between the straits. Rabbi Yehudah put וְהֵצַר לְךָ (Devarim 28:52), it shall press you, and וַֽהֲצֵרֹתִי לָֽאָדָם (Tzefaniah 1:17), I will press men hard, under this root; Radak has already written them at צוּר, along with צַר וְאוֹיֵב (Esther 7:6), an adversary and an enemy, and צַר ־לִי מְאֹד (Shmuel II 24:14), I am in great straits, and it may be that the root of them all is צָרַר.

Rabbi Yehudah set in another sense וְכִֽעֲסַתָּה צָֽרָתָהּ (Shmuel I 1:6), her rival vexed her, and לִצְרֹר לְגַלּוֹת עֶרְוָתָהּ (Vayikra 18:18), to take a rival and uncover her nakedness, the second of which Radak lists with the harassing; he has explained צרתה, her rival, at צוּר.

מִי צָֽרַר ־מַיִם בַּשִּׂמְלָה (Mishlei 30:4), who has bound up water in a garment; צֹֽרֵר ־מַיִם בְּעָבָיו (Iyov 26:8), He binds up water in His clouds; כִּצְרוֹר אֶבֶן (Mishlei 26:8), like binding a stone; and in the passive, וּמְבֻקָּעִים וּמְצֹֽרָרִֽים (Yehoshua 9:4), split and bound up. The noun is צְֽרוֹר ־הַכֶּסֶף לָקַח בְּיָדוֹ (Mishlei 7:20), he took the bundle of silver in his hand, and צְרוֹר הַמֹּר דּוֹדִי לִי (Shir HaShirim 1:13), my beloved is a bundle of myrrh to me: their sense is binding.

וַתִּֽהְיֶינָה צְרֻרוֹת (Shmuel II 20:3), and they were bound, he first lists with the harassing, but holds that it is rightly from this sense of binding: as though they were bound until the day of their death and not loosed to marry a man. And וְלֹֽא־יִפּוֹל צְרוֹר אָֽרֶץ (Amos 9:9), not a stone shall fall to the ground, and אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹֽא־נִמְצָא שָׁם גַּם־ צְרֽוֹר (Shmuel II 17:13), where not even a stone was found: צְרוֹר there means a stone, and it is like צוּר, a rock, צוּר and צָרַר being of one sense.

מיר.sense: Exchanging one thing for another, with the noun תמורה, what is given in exchange. In one pasuk the word may also carry a second sense, magnifying.

more.t: הֵמִיר כְּבוֹדוֹ (Yirmiyahu 2:11), he exchanged his glory; וְלֹֽא־יָמִיר אֹתוֹ (Vayikra 27:10), he shall not exchange it; וְלֹא יָמֵר (Yechezkel 48:14), he shall not exchange, said of the first of the land; and the noun, וְהָֽיָה־הוּא וּתְמֽוּרָתוֹ (Vayikra 27:10), it and what is exchanged for it. Their sense is the exchanging of one thing for another.

more.h: Perhaps two senses in one word
more.t: הַֽהֵימִיר גּוֹי אֱלֹהִים (Yirmiyahu 2:11), has a nation exchanged gods: the yod written between the heh and the first root letter is the quiescent letter of הֵקִים, he raised up, and הֵשִׁיב, he brought back, and in this word it is written against the usual way. The word may be meant to join two senses. One is exchange: whether a nation has exchanged gods for other gods, although they are no gods. The other comes from וּבִכְבוֹדָם תִּתְיַמָּֽרוּ (Yeshayahu 61:6), and in their glory you shall be magnified; then הֵימִיר would follow the pattern of הֵיטִיב, he did good, and the sense would be: has a nation magnified other gods that are not its own, though they are no gods, neither the one nor the other.

חלף.sense: To pass on and be gone; to change or renew, and changes of garments; in place of; and a sense close to these, cutting off, from which knives are called מַֽחֲלָפִים.

more.t: חָלַף הָלַךְ לֽוֹ (Shir HaShirim 2:11), it has passed and gone; וְחָֽלַפְתָּ מִשָּׁם וָהָלְאָה (Shmuel I 10:3), you shall pass on from there; וְיַֽחֲלֹף וְֽלֹא־אָבִין לֽוֹ (Iyov 9:11), He passes by and I do not perceive Him; כְּסוּפוֹת בַּנֶּגֶב לַֽחֲלֹף (Yeshayahu 21:1), like whirlwinds in the Negev, passing through; חָלְפוּ חֹק (Yeshayahu 24:5), they passed over the statute. All of them are the sense of passing. Beside them stand בַּבֹּקֶר יָצִיץ וְחָלָף (Tehillim 90:6), in the morning it blossoms and passes, and בַּבֹּקֶר כֶּחָצִיר יַֽחֲלֹֽף (Tehillim 90:5), in the morning like grass it passes.

וְהַֽחֲלִיפוּ שִׂמְלֹֽתֵיכֶֽם (Bereishis 35:2), change your garments; וַתַּֽחֲלֵף אֶת־מַשְׂכֻּרְתִּי (Bereishis 31:41), you changed my wages; כַּלְּבוּשׁ תַּֽחֲלִיפֵם וְֽיַֽחֲלֹֽפוּ (Tehillim 102:27), You change them like a garment and they are changed; אִֽם־יִכָּרֵת וְעוֹד יַֽחֲלִיף (Iyov 14:7), though it be cut down it will yet renew, meaning it will renew its shoots; וְקַשְׁתִּי בְּיָדִי תַֽחֲלִֽיף (Iyov 29:20), my bow renews in my hand, which he explains as my strength and my might renewing my honour for me; and יַֽחֲלִיפוּ כֹחַ (Yeshayahu 40:31), they shall renew strength.

more.h: A change of garments, and in place of
more.t: וַיְגַלַּח וַיְחַלֵּף שִׂמְלֹתָיו (Bereishis 41:14), he shaved and changed his garments; חֲלִפוֹת שְׂמָלֹת (Bereishis 45:22), changes of raiment; וּשְׁלשִׁים חֲלִפֹת בְּגָדִֽים (Shoftim 14:12), thirty changes of garments: all in the sense of renewal and exchange. One thing coming in another's place is עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים בַּחֹדֶשׁ חֲלִיפוֹת (Melachim I 5:28), ten thousand a month by courses, these going and those coming. חֵלֶף עֲבֹֽדַתְכֶם (Bamidbar 18:31), in return for your service, is pointed with six dots; and the Targum renders תַּחַת (Bereishis 4:25), in place of, as חֲלַף.

more.h: Cutting off, a sense close by
more.t: Another sense, close to this one: אִם־ יַֽחֲלֹף וְיַסְגִּיר (Iyov 11:10), if He cuts off and shuts up; וְהָאֱלִילִים כָּלִיל יַֽחֲלֹֽף (Yeshayahu 2:18), and the idols shall be wholly cut off; תַּחְלְפֵהוּ קֶשֶׁת נְחוּשָֽׁה (Iyov 20:24), a bow of brass shall cut him down; and the nouns עַד־בּוֹא חֲלִיפָתִֽי (Iyov 14:14), until my cutting off comes, אֲשֶׁר אֵין חֲלִיפוֹת לָמוֹ (Tehillim 55:20), who have no cutting off, and כָּל־בְּנֵי חֲלֽוֹף (Mishlei 31:8), all the sons of cutting off. All of these are the sense of cutting off, and the people of the world are called בני חלוף because death and cutting off from the world come upon them.

His father explains כֶּחָצִיר יַֽחֲלֹֽף (Tehillim 90:5), like grass it is cut off, from this sense, citing זְרַמְתָּם שֵׁנָה יִהְיוּ בַּבֹּקֶר כֶּחָצִיר יַֽחֲלֹֽף, You flood them away, they are as a sleep; in the morning, like grass, it is cut off. Radak glosses it: if they are there at night they are not there in the morning, for like grass it is cut off, the word standing alone in that sense. And if בַּבֹּקֶר יָצִיץ וְחָלָף (Tehillim 90:6), in the morning it blossoms and is renewed, is like וְעוֹד יַֽחֲלִיף (Iyov 14:7), it will yet renew, then by evening it is cut down and dried.

From this sense knives are called מחלפים, מַֽחֲלָפִים תִּשְׁעָה וְעֶשְׂרִֽים (Ezra 1:9), twenty-nine knives, because they cut; and אֶת־שֶׁבַע מַחְלְפוֹת רֹאשִׁי (Shoftim 16:13), the seven locks of my head, are the curls of the hair, called so because they are like knives, or because change and exchange come over them when they whiten in old age.

שׁפח.sense: The שִׁפְחָה, a maidservant, a word with no masculine; and in another sense the מִשְׁפָּחָה, a family, a name given also to a tribe and to a nation.

more.t: כְּעֵינֵי שִׁפְחָה אֶל־יַד גְּבִרְתָּהּ (Tehillim 123:2), as the eyes of a maid to the hand of her mistress; עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת (Koheles 2:7), menservants and maidservants; אֵין לְשִׁפְחָֽתְךָ כֹל (Melachim II 4:2), your maidservant has nothing. No masculine noun is formed from it: for the male one says עֶבֶד, a servant, and for the female אָמָה or שפחה, a maid.

מִשְׁפָּחָה וּמִשְׁפָּחָה (Esther 9:28), every single family, and לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתֵיהֶם יָֽצְאוּ מִן־הַתֵּבָֽה (Bereishis 8:19), they went out of the ark by their families; the tribe that Hashem takes יִקְרַב לַמִּשְׁפָּחוֹת (Yehoshua 7:14), shall come near by families. The tribe itself is also called מִשְׁפָּחָה: וַיַּקְרֵב אֶת־ מִשְׁפַּחַת יְהוּדָה (Yehoshua 7:17), he brought near the family of Yehudah.

A nation is called מִשְׁפָּחָה: וְאִם־ מִשְׁפַּחַת מִצְרַיִם (Zecharyah 14:18), and if the family of Mitzrayim; עַל כָּל־ הַמִּשְׁפָּחָה אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱלֵיתִי מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם (Amos 3:1), against the whole family I brought up from the land of Mitzrayim; מִכֹּל מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הָֽאֲדָמָה (Amos 3:2), of all the families of the earth. And by way of borrowing, וּפָֽקַדְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶם אַרְבַּע מִשְׁפָּחוֹת (Yirmiyahu 15:3), I will appoint over them four families.

שֹפח.sense: He gives no sense here. The entry is one pasuk of Yeshayahu, with a note that the word is treated at the letter samech.

more.t: The one pasuk is Yeshayahu 3:17, on קָדְקֹד בְּנוֹת צִיּוֹן, the crown of the daughters of Tzion. Of the word itself he says nothing here, only that he has already treated it at the letter samech.

אמה.sense: A maidservant; but at וַתִּשְׁלַח אֶת־ אֲמָתָהּ, which he reads as she sent her maid, some read אַמָּתָהּ with a dagesh, her arm, as Rav Saadiah Gaon explained it.

more.t: וְגַם אֶת־בֶּן־ הָֽאָמָה (Bereishis 21:10 in his edition), and also the son of the maidservant: the heh at the end is the feminine ending, and the heh that is the root's last letter drops, showing in וְאַמְהֹתָיו וַיֵּלֵֽדוּ (Bereishis 20:17), and his maidservants, and they bore. Their sense is known, that they are maidservants.

So too וַתִּשְׁלַח אֶת־ אֲמָתָהּ (Shemos 2:5), she sent her maidservant, שפחתה. It is said that the reading of this word is disputed: some read it with a dagesh, אַמָּתָהּ, from אַמָּה אָרְכּוֹ (Shemos 30:2), a cubit its length; and so Rav Saadiah Gaon explained it in his Arabic commentary, whose words mean ותשלח זרועה, and she put out her arm.

צום.sense: To fast, and צוֹם, a fast. His father wrote that the צוֹם called over Navos is a gathering; so too any calling of a צוֹם that is not a matter of teshuvah.

more.t: לָמָּה צַּמְנוּ וְלֹא רָאִיתָ (Yeshayahu 58:3), why have we fasted and You did not see, וַיָּצֻמוּ שִׁבְעַת יָמִֽים (Shmuel I 31:13), they fasted seven days, וַיָּצָם דָּוִד צוֹם (Shmuel II 12:16), and David fasted a fast, and וְצוּמוּ עָלַי וְאַל־תֹּאכְלוּ וְאַל־תִּשְׁתּוּ (Esther 4:16), fast for me and do not eat and do not drink. The noun is וַיִּקְרְאוּ ־צוֹם (Yonah 3:5), they called a fast, with the feminine plural דִּבְרֵי הַצֹּמוֹת (Esther 9:31), the matters of the fasts, of which he says only that it is known.

הֲצוֹם צַמְתֻּנִי אָֽנִי (Zecharyah 7:5), did you fast for Me, Me, is explained: did you fast on My account? Did I command you to fast? It was for your fathers' sins that the House was destroyed. And what do you give Me by your fasting, or by your eating and drinking? This is in the way of אִם־צָדַקְתָּ מַה־תִּתֶּן־לוֹ (Iyov 35:7), if you are righteous, what do you give Him? And the meaning is: if you do justice, truth, kindness and mercy, you will not fast, for the House you fast over will be built, and you will rejoice in its building, and eat and drink.

On קִרְאוּ־ צוֹם וְהֹשִׁיבוּ אֶת־נָבוֹת בְּרֹאשׁ הָעָֽם (Melachim I 21:9), call a tzom and seat Navos at the head of the people, his father wrote that it is not a word for fasting but for gathering, from צומת הגידין in the Talmud (Chullin 76a), the meeting place of the sinews. So too every calling of a צוֹם that is not a matter of teshuvah, and so בְּיוֹם צוֹם (Yirmiyahu 36:6), on a day of tzom, is on a day of gathering.

צמת.sense: To cut off, the sense of כריתה, cutting off; some read one form, נִצְמָתוּ, as being joined together, from a word in Chazal.

more.t: צָמְתוּ בַבּוֹר חַיָּי (Eichah 3:53), they cut off my life in the pit. In the passive, בְּעֵת יְזֹרְבוּ נִצְמָתוּ (Iyov 6:17), when they grow hot they are cut off; and some explain that one as נתחברו, they were joined together, from צומת הגידין, the junction of the sinews, in the words of Chazal (Chullin 4:6, 76a). The noun is לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ (Vayikra 25:30), cut off to the one who bought it.

more.h: Where the verb takes an object
more.t: צִמְּתַתְנִי קִנְאָתִי (Tehillim 119:139), my zeal has cut me off, בִּעוּתֶיךָ צִמְּתוּתֻנִי (Tehillim 88:17), Your terrors have cut me off, אוֹתוֹ אַצְמִית (Tehillim 101:5), him will I cut off, הִצְמַתָּה כָּל זוֹנֶה מִמֶּךָּ (Tehillim 73:27), You have cut off everyone who strays from You, וּמְשַׂנְאַי אַצְמִיתֵם (Tehillim 18:41), I will cut off those who hate me, and יַצְמִיתֵם י"י אֱלֹהֵינוּ (Tehillim 94:23), Hashem our God will cut them off. All of them are the sense of cutting off.

נצח.sense: The text here breaks off after מְנַצְּחִים לְהַֽעֲבִיד אֶת־הָעָֽם, overseeing, to make the people work, and runs on into words of reaching.

more.h: What the rest of it holds
more.t: What follows speaks of reaching: כלם ענין ההדבקה וההגעה, all of them the sense of cleaving to a thing and reaching it. The noun is in כִּֽי־שִׂיחַ וְכִי־ שִׂיג לוֹ (Melachim I 18:27), for he is in talk, or in pursuit, that is, he has some matter with another, or is overtaking his enemies in war. שִׂיג is a noun with its nun missing, as שִׂיא is in אִם־יַֽעֲלֶה לַשָּׁמַיִם שִׂיאוֹ (Iyov 20:6), though his loftiness mount to the heavens. Like them, though written with a samech, is וְתַסֵּג וְלֹא תַפְלִיט (Michah 6:14), and you will reach but not bring out safely: that is, you reach pregnancy and do not bring it out, but miscarry it.

סלה.sense: To tread down and trample, as it may be read from מסלה, a highway, though the two are separate roots; and in another sense, to be valued.

more.h: Treading down, as it may be read
more.t: סָלִיתָ כָּל שׁוֹגִים מֵחֻקֶּיךָ (Tehillim 119:118) and סִלָּה כָל אַבִּירַי (Eichah 1:15). Their sense may be taken from מסלה, a highway, even though the two are separate roots: you have trodden and trampled all who stray from Your statutes, and he trod and trampled all my mighty ones in my midst.

Another sense: לֹא תְסֻלֶּה בְּכֶתֶם אוֹפִיר (Iyov 28:16), it is not to be valued against the fine gold of Ophir, where the sense is לא תעריך, it cannot be appraised. He has mentioned it already at the root סָלָא.

רבע.sense: Four-square, with its sides equal; אַרְבָּעָה, four; רֶבַע and רְבִיעִת, a fourth part; and רְבִיעִי, fourth.

more.t: רָבוּעַ יִהְיֶה הַמִּזְבֵּחַ (Shemos 27:1), the altar shall be four-square, that is, its sides equal, its length as its breadth. So of the whole terumah, בַּחֲמִשָּׁה וְעֶשְׂרִים אָלֶף רְבִיעִית, by twenty-five thousand, four-square, that is, it shall be squared, its length as its breadth; and מְזוּזוֹת עֲצֵי־שָׁמֶן מֵאֵת רְבִעִית (Melachim I 6:33), doorposts of oil-wood, four-square, that is, they were squared on all its sides, which Targum Yonasan renders מִן אַרְבְּעָה סִטְרֵיהוֹן מְרַבְּעִין, squared from their four sides. In the heavy form, מְרֻבַּע סָבִיב (Yechezkel 45:2), squared round about, and וְרֹחַב מֵאָה אַמָּה מְרֻבָּעַת (Yechezkel 40:47), and a hundred cubits broad, squared.

more.h: The number, and the fourth part
more.t: The number takes an added alef: לְאַרְבָּעָה רָאשִׁים (Bereishis 2:10), to four heads, and אֶל־אַרְבַּעַת מִקְצוֹעֵי הֶחָצֵר (Yechezkel 46:21), to the four corners of the court; for the feminine, without a heh, וְאַרְבַּע־צֹאן (Shemos 21:37), and four sheep. וְאֶת־הַכִּבְשָׂה יְשַׁלֵּם אַרְבַּעְתָּיִם (Shmuel II 12:6), and he shall pay for the ewe-lamb אַרְבַּעְתָּיִם, is two times four, double what the law prescribes, since of one who steals a sheep it is said, וארבע צאן תחת השה, four sheep in place of the one. The name for a fourth part is רֶבַע הַהִין (Shemos 29:40), a quarter of a hin, with a segol under the reish; so אֶל אַרְבַּעַת רְבָעָיו (Yechezkel 43:16), to its four quarters; and in other patterns, וּמִסְפָּר אֶת־רֹבַע יִשְׂרָאֵל (Bamidbar 23:10), and the number of the fourth part of Yisrael, and רְבִיעִת הַהִין (Shemos 29:40), a fourth of a hin.
יוֹם רְבִיעִי (Bereishis 1:19), a fourth day, בְּנֵי רְבִעִים (Melachim II 10:30), sons of the fourth generation, and in another pattern וְעַל־רִבֵּעִים (Shemos 34:7), and upon the fourth generation.

Rabbi Yonah wrote that among what derives from this sense is לְרִבְעָהּ תֶּבֶל הוּא (Vayikra 18:23), to couple with her, it is perversion, and with it the heavy form לֹא־תַרְבִּיעַ כִּלְאַיִם (Vayikra 19:19), you shall not let two kinds couple. Radak holds it right that they are of the sense of אָרְחִי וְרִבְעִי (Tehillim 139:3), my path and my lying down, רבע being the Targum of וַתִּרְבַּץ תַּחַת בִּלְעָם (Bamidbar 22:27), and she lay down under Bilam, which it renders וּרְבַעַת.

שׁכל.sense: To be bereaved of children, and where the verb takes an object, to bereave; and in another sense אֶשְׁכּוֹל, a cluster.

more.t: כַּאֲשֶׁר שָׁכֹלְתִּי שָׁכָלְתִּי (Bereishis 43:14), as I have been bereaved, I am bereaved; לָמָה אֶשְׁכַּל גַּם שְׁנֵיכֶם (Bereishis 27:45), which he reads as why should I be bereaved of both of you, or on account of both of you; and כֵּן תִּשְׁכַּל מִנָּשִׁים (Shmuel I 15:33), so shall she be bereaved more than the rest of the women, as he reads it. The adjective is וַאֲנִי שְׁכוּלָה וְגַלְמוּדָה (Yeshayahu 49:21), and I am bereaved and alone, and the nouns וְלֹא אֵדַע שְׁכוֹל (Yeshayahu 47:8), I shall not know bereavement, שְׁכוֹל לְנַפְשִׁי (Tehillim 35:12), bereavement to my soul, and שְׁכוֹל וְאַלְמֹן (Yeshayahu 47:9), bereavement and widowhood.

רְחֵלֶיךָ וְעִזֶּיךָ לֹא שִׁכֵּלוּ (Bereishis 31:38), your ewes and your she-goats did not lose their young, תְּפַלֵּט פָּרָתוֹ וְלֹא תְשַׁכֵּל (Iyov 21:10), his cow calves and does not lose her calf, וְלֹא תְשַׁכֵּל לָכֶם הַגֶּפֶן (Malachi 3:11), the vine will not cast its fruit for you, and מְשַׁכֵּלָה וַעֲקָרָה (Shemos 23:26), one that loses her young and one that is barren. The adjective is כְּדֹב שַׁכּוּל (Hoshea 13:8), a bereaved bear, and וְשַׁכֻּלָה אֵין בָּהֶם (Shir HaShirim 4:2), and none among them is bereaved, with a patach under the shin; the noun is שִׁכּוּל, bereavement, with the plural בְּנֵי שִׁכֻּלָיִךְ (Yeshayahu 49:20), the children of your bereavement, the shin there carrying a chirik.

more.h: Where the verb takes an object
more.t: שִׁכַּלְתִּי אִבַּדְתִּי אֶת עַמִּי (Yirmiyahu 15:7), I have bereaved, I have destroyed My people; כַּאֲשֶׁר שִׁכְּלָה נָשִׁים חַרְבֶּךָ (Shmuel I 15:33), as your sword has bereaved women; אֹתִי שִׁכַּלְתֶּם (Bereishis 42:36), you have bereaved me; מִחוּץ תְּשַׁכֶּל חֶרֶב (Devarim 32:25), outside, the sword shall bereave; אַעֲבִיר בָּאָרֶץ וְשִׁכְּלָתָּה (Yechezkel 14:15), I send it through the land and it bereaves the land, said of an evil beast; וְחַיָּה רָעָה וְשִׁכְּלֻךְ (Yechezkel 5:17), and an evil beast, and they will bereave you; and וְהָאָרֶץ מְשַׁכָּלֶת (Melachim II 2:19), the land bereaving. Apart from these, and set under another heavy form, stand רֶחֶם מַשְׁכִּיל (Hoshea 9:14), a womb that bereaves, and כְּגִבּוֹר מַשְׁכִּיל (Yirmiyahu 50:9), like a warrior who bereaves; he glosses neither.

On וְלֹא יִהְיֶה מִשָּׁם עוֹד מָוֶת וּמְשַׁכָּלֶת, there shall be from there no more death or bereaving, he says the verb of being, stated once, stands for two, the sense being that she will not be bereaving; or else משכלות is a noun. He weighs too whether in וְהָאָרֶץ מְשַׁכָּלֶת the verb passes to one other only, like מְשַׁכֵּלָה וַעֲקָרָה, one that loses her young and one that is barren; and so of וּמְשַׁכֶּלֶת (Yechezkel 36:13), bereaving.

אֵין אֶשְׁכּוֹל לֶאֱכוֹל (Michah 7:1), no cluster to eat, וְאֶשְׁכּוֹל עֲנָבִים אֶחָד (Bamidbar 13:23), one cluster of grapes, and אֶשְׁכֹּל הַכֹּפֶר (Shir HaShirim 1:14), a cluster of henna. The plurals are וְשָׁדַיִךְ לְאַשְׁכֹּלוֹת (Shir HaShirim 7:8), and your breasts like clusters, with a patach under the alef, כְּאֶשְׁכְּלוֹת הַגֶּפֶן (Shir HaShirim 7:9), like clusters of the vine, with a segol, אַשְׁכְּלֹת מְרֹרֹת (Devarim 32:32), clusters of bitterness, and הִבְשִׁילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶיהָ עֲנָבִים (Bereishis 40:10), its clusters ripened into grapes. The single berries are called עֲנָבִים, grapes, and what holds them is called an אֶשְׁכּוֹל, for which he gives the name in his own vernacular.

נצר.sense: To guard and keep, and from it the נוֹצְרִים, lookouts in a tower; another sense, ruin; and a third, נֵצֶר, a young shoot or a branch.

more.t: עֵדֹתֶיךָ נָצָרְתִּי (Tehillim 119:22), I have kept Your testimonies, נֹצֵר תְּאֵנָה יֹאכַל פִּרְיָהּ (Mishlei 27:18), one who guards a fig tree eats its fruit, לְנֹצְרֵי בְרִיתוֹ (Tehillim 25:10), to those who keep His covenant, נְצֹר לְשׁוֹנְךָ מֵרָע (Tehillim 34:14), guard your tongue from evil, and וּבְרִיתְךָ יִנְצֹרוּ (Devarim 33:9), and they keep Your covenant; the sense of all of them is guarding. With the first root letter dropped, צוֹר תְּעוּדָה (Yeshayahu 8:16), keep the testimony, which Targum Yonasan renders נְבִיָא טַר סַהֲדוּתָא, prophet, keep the testimony.

more.h: What is kept out of reach
more.t: וּנְצֻרוֹת וְלֹא יְדַעְתָּם (Yeshayahu 48:6), kept things, and you did not know them, are things kept, too lofty to be reached and known; וְהַנִּשְׁאָר וְהַנָּצוּר (Yechezkel 6:12), the one who is left and the one who is kept, is one kept from being reached; and שִׁית זוֹנָה וּנְצֻרַת לֵב (Mishlei 7:10), in a harlot's attire and guarded of heart, is שמורת לב, guarded of heart, meaning that no man can take her and entice her, but she entices men.

From this sense comes מִמִּגְדַּל נוֹצְרִים (Melachim II 17:9), from the tower of the watchers: they are the lookouts who stand in the tower, a tower not for settlement but for the lookout to stand in. So too קראו נֹֽצְרִים בְּהַר אֶפְרָיִם (Yirmiyahu 31:6), watchmen call out on Mount Efraim: the lookouts and keepers call out קומו ונעלה ציון, arise and let us go up to Tzion. Or נצרים there may be a people called after their place, but the first is the right one. Rabbi Yonah explained נֹצְרִים בָּאִים מֵאֶרֶץ הַמֶּרְחָק (Yirmiyahu 4:16), נֹצְרִים come from a distant land, as a people called after Nevuchadnetzar, and Radak's father explained it so as well.

וּבַנְּצוּרִים יָלִינוּ (Yeshayahu 65:4), and they lodge among the ruins, and כְּעִיר נְצוּרָה (Yeshayahu 1:8), like a ruined city, are of the sense of חרבה, ruin. From this sense his father explains וּנְצֻרַת לב, that is, חרבת דעת, ruined of understanding; he wrote that so it stands in the words of the philosopher, ישבו עולמם בחרבן שכלם, they settle their world in the ruin of their intellect, and his father said it of the harlot, that she is חרבת שכל, ruined of mind.

In another sense, וְנֵצֶר מִשָּׁרָשָׁיו יִפְרֶה (Yeshayahu 11:1), and a shoot from his roots will bear fruit, and כְּנֵצֶר נִתְעָב (Yeshayahu 14:19), like a loathsome shoot; their sense is יונק או ענף, a sucker or a branch. כְּנֵצֶר נִתְעָב means: as a man throws away the loathsome shoot that does not thrive, pulling it out of its pit and casting it off, so you were cast out of your grave.

נטר.sense: To keep; from this sense, the מַטָּרָה, a mark set up to shoot arrows at, and the court and the gate of the guard.

more.t: הֲיִנְטֹר לְעוֹלָם (Yirmiyahu 3:5), will He keep it forever, וְנוֹטֵר הוּא לְאֹיְבָיו (Nachum 1:2), He keeps it for His enemies, לֹא אֶטּוֹר לְעוֹלָם (Yirmiyahu 3:12), I will not keep it forever, לֹא־תִקֹּם וְלֹא־תִטֹּר (Vayikra 19:18), do not take revenge and do not keep it, and שָׂמֻנִי נֹטֵרָה אֶת־הַכְּרָמִים (Shir HaShirim 1:6), they set me to keep the vineyards; all of them are keeping. The Targum renders וַיִּשְׁמֹר (Bereishis 26:5), and he kept, as וּנְטַר, and he kept.

From this sense the thing set up for arrows to be shot at is called a מַטָּרָה: וַיְקִימֵנִי לוֹ לְמַטָּרָה (Iyov 16:12), He set me up for Himself as a mark, and with an alef in place of the heh, כַּמַּטָּרָא לַחֵץ (Eichah 3:12), like a mark for the arrow. Likewise derived from this sense is בַּחֲצַר הַמַּטָּרָה (Yirmiyahu 32:2), in the court of the guard, as the same sense is put in וַיֶּאֱסֹף אֹתָם אֶל־מִשְׁמָר (Bereishis 42:17), he gathered them into ward; and likewise בְּשַׁעַר הַמַּטָּרָה (Nechemiah 12:39), at the gate of the guard, where the guards used to stand.

מסך.sense: Mixture and confusion; so too the mixing of water with wine, and the nouns מֶסֶךְ and מִמְסָךְ, a mixture.

more.t: מָסַךְ בְּקִרְבָּהּ רוּחַ עִוְעִים (Yeshayahu 19:14), has mixed within her a spirit of perversity: the sense is תערובות ובלבול, mixture and confusion. So too of tempering, which is the mixing of water with wine: מָסְכָה יֵינָהּ (Mishlei 9:2), she has mixed her wine, and וּשְׁתוּ בְּיַיִן מָסָכְתִּי (Mishlei 9:5), and drink of the wine I have mixed.

מָלֵא מֶסֶךְ (Tehillim 75:9), full of mixture, pointed with six dots; and on another pattern, לַחְקוֹר מִמְסָךְ (Mishlei 23:30), to search out the mixture, and לַמְנִי מִמְסָךְ (Yeshayahu 65:11), a mixture for Meni.

Rabbi Yonah put כָּל־אֶבֶן יְקָרָה מְסֻכָתֶךָ (Yechezkel 28:13) under this root in one of its senses, and Radak spells out what that comes to: every precious stone mixed in with you. The right account, Radak says, is that it is from the root שֹוךְ, of the sense of הָסֵר מְשׂוּכָּתוֹ (Yeshayahu 5:5), remove its hedge; and though the one is written with a samech and the other with a shin they are one, the sense being that your hedge is of precious stones.

אשׁר.sense: אֲשֶׁר, whose sense he calls known, standing also for if, so, in order that, and for and; אֲשֵׁרָה, a worshipped tree; אַשְׁרֵי, happy; and אֲשֻׁרַי, ways or feet.

more.t: הָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַח מֹשֶׁה (Bamidbar 13:16), the men whom Moshe sent, and וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר (Vayikra 25:30), the house that is in the city shall stand: of these he says only that their sense is known. It stands in place of אִם, if: אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא (Vayikra 4:22) and אֶת הַבְּרָכָה אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׁמְעוּ (Devarim 11:27) are if a ruler sins, and the blessing, if you listen. In place of כֵּן, so, in Shaul's words to Shmuel, אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּקוֹל (Shmuel I 15:20), so I have listened to the voice. In place of לְמַעַן, in order that: אֲשֶׁר יִיטַב לְךָ וּלְבָנֶיךָ אַחֲרֶיךָ (Devarim 4:40), that it may go well with you and with your children after you. And in place of a vav: טוֹב אֲשֶׁר יָפֶה (Koheles 5:17) and עָוֹן אֲשֶׁר חֵטְא (Hoshea 12:9) are good and fair, iniquity and sin.

more.h: אֲשֶׁר with a letter before it
more.t: The kaf of likeness is added to it, כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה (Vayikra 8:34), as he did, and so in many places; sometimes it is missing, and אֲשֶׁר רְאִיתֶם אֶת מִצְרַיִם (Shemos 14:13) stands for כאשר ראיתם, as you have seen Mitzrayim. A beis comes on it for because: בַּאֲשֶׁר אַתְּ אִשְׁתּוֹ (Bereishis 39:9), because you are his wife. And a beis comes on it to point at a place: בַּאֲשֶׁר כָּרַע שָׁם נָפַל שָׁדוּד (Shoftim 5:26 in his edition), where he sank, there he fell slain, and וּבַאֲשֶׁר חֲלָלִים שָׁם הוּא (Iyov 39:30), and where the slain are, there it is.

לֹא תִטַּע לְךָ אֲשֵׁרָה כָּל עֵץ (Devarim 16:21), you shall not plant yourself an asheirah, any tree: any tree that they serve, or that they plant in honour of the one they serve, is called an אֲשֵׁרָה. Its plural takes the masculine ending, בָּמוֹת וּמַצֵּבוֹת וַאֲשֵׁרִים (Melachim I 14:23), high places and pillars and asheirim, and so וְאֶת אֲשֵׁרָיו תִּכְרֹתוּן (Shemos 34:13), and you shall cut down its asheirim, and וַאֲשֵׁרֵיהֶם תִּשְׂרְפוּן בָּאֵשׁ (Devarim 12:3), and their asheirim you shall burn in fire.

more.h: אַשְׁרֵי, and calling a man happy
more.t: אַשְׁרֵי הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא הָלַךְ (Tehillim 1:1), happy is the man who has not walked, and אַשְׁרֶיךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִי כָמוֹךָ (Devarim 33:29), happy are you, Yisrael, who is like you. It is a plural noun on the weight of אַחֲלֵי אֲדֹנִי (Melachim II 5:3), would that my master, except that its alef is of the root while the alef of אחלי is added. The verb is to say of someone that he is happy: בְּאָשְׁרִי כִּי אִשְּׁרוּנִי בָּנוֹת (Bereishis 30:13), in my happiness, for daughters have called me happy, which he glosses as their saying אשרי, happy; כִּי אֹזֶן שָׁמְעָה וַתְּאַשְּׁרֵנִי (Iyov 29:11), for an ear heard and called me happy; רָאוּהָ בָנוֹת וַיְאַשְּׁרוּהָ (Shir HaShirim 6:9), daughters saw her and called her happy; and וְתֹמְכֶיהָ מְאֻשָּׁר (Mishlei 3:18), and each who holds her is called happy, of whom they say אשריו, happy is he.

תָּמֹךְ אֲשֻׁרַי (Tehillim 17:5), hold up my אֲשֻׁרַי, which he explains as דרכי או רגלי, my ways or my feet; so בַּאֲשֻׁרוֹ אָחֲזָה רַגְלִי (Iyov 23:11), my foot has held to his way, and לֹא תִמְעַד אֲשֻׁרָיו (Tehillim 37:31), his ways will not slip, not even one of them, the word being feminine like רגל, a foot. In another pattern, with a dagesh, אִם תִּטֶּה אַשֻּׁרִי מִנִי הַדָּרֶךְ (Iyov 31:7), if my track has turned aside from the way; all such, he says, have the sense of נתיב ודרך, track and way. The simple verb has וְאִשְׁרוּ בְּדֶרֶךְ בִּינָה (Mishlei 9:6), and walk in the way of understanding. In the heavy form, וְאַל תְּאַשֵּׁר בְּדֶרֶךְ רָעִים (Mishlei 4:14), which he glosses אל תדרך, do not tread in the way of the wicked; וְאַשֵּׁר בַּדֶּרֶךְ לִבֶּךָ (Mishlei 23:19), and guide your heart in the way, which he glosses as the known way that I taught you, the way of wisdom; מְאַשְּׁרֵי הָעָם הַזֶּה (Yeshayahu 9:15), those who guide this people, and אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ (Yeshayahu 1:17), guide the oppressed. Or in these two the alef stands for a yud, מְיַשְּׁרֵי, those who set this people straight, and set the oppressed straight.

עַל דֶּרֶךְ אָשׁוּר (Hoshea 13:7), on the road אָשׁוּר, is the simple verb of this root. It can also be read from אֲשׁוּרֶנּוּ וְלֹא קָרוֹב (Bamidbar 24:17), I behold him but not near, its alef marking the one speaking: as a leopard is ready to tear, so I watch and look to tear them, as it says אֶפְגְּשֵׁם כְּדֹב שַׁכּוּל (Hoshea 13:8), I will meet them like a bereaved bear. תִּדְהָר וּתְאַשּׁוּר (Yeshayahu 41:19), the tidhar and the te'ashur: the te'ashur is עץ ממין ארז, a tree of the cedar kind; Rabbi Yonah wrote that in Arabic it is called שורבי"ן, and the Targum says אֶשְׁכְּרוֹעִין. Rabbi Yonah wrote as well that this tree is called בקס, with a shin, in Arabic, and that it is said to be what is called בוס"ו in the vernacular. Targum Yonasan puts קַרְשֵׁךְ עָשׂוּ שֵׁן בַּת אֲשֻׁרִים (Yechezkel 27:6), your boards they made of ivory, בַּת אֲשֻׁרִים, as דַפִּין דְאֶשְׁכְּרוֹעִין מְכַבְשִׁין בְּשֵׁן דְפִיל, planks of eshkero'in pressed with elephant's ivory, taking בַּת אֲשֻׁרִים as one word, though it is two.

קום.sense: To rise, and to rise against; to stand and endure, and to confirm; קוֹמָה, stature; קָמָה, standing grain; יְקוּם, every living thing; and מָקוֹם, a place.

more.t: וְלֹא קָם נָבִיא עוֹד (Devarim 34:10), no prophet arose again, קוּם הִתְהַלֵּךְ בָּאָרֶץ (Bereishis 13:17), arise and walk about the land, יָקֻם אָבִי וְיֹאכַל (Bereishis 27:31), let my father rise and eat, קוּם נָא שְׁבָה (Bereishis 27:19), rise, please, sit, and וַיָּקָם הָעָם כָּל הַיּוֹם הַהוּא (Bamidbar 11:32), the people rose all that day. In וְקָאם שָׁאוֹן בְּעַמֶּךָ (Hoshea 10:14), and a tumult shall rise among your people, a quiescent alef is written for the middle letter of the root.

more.h: When eyes are said to rise
more.t: וְעֵינָיו קָמָה (Shmuel I 4:15), his eyes had risen, and כִּי קָמוּ עֵינָיו מִשֵּׂיבוֹ (Melachim I 14:4), for his eyes had risen from his old age: rising is said of the eye because when a man's eyes dim in old age the cords of the eye pucker, and the eye rises and draws in upward. Some read it by its context as a wasting of the eyes. Targum Yonasan renders כָּלוּ עֵינֵיהֶם (Yirmiyahu 14:6), their eyes failed, as קָמָא עֵינֵיהוֹן, with this same word, and renders both of these pesukim with קָמָה as well.

more.h: Those who rise against a man
more.t: כָּל הַקָּמִים עָלֶיךָ (Shmuel II 18:31), all who rise against you, שְׁאוֹן קָמֶיךָ (Tehillim 74:23), the tumult of those who rise against You, and in another pattern וּמִכַּף מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל הַקּוֹמִים עָלָי (Melachim II 16:7), and from the hand of the king of Yisrael, who are rising against me. Enemies are called קמים because they rise against the one opposite them for harm. וְאֶל יֹשְׁבֵי לֵב קָמָי (Yirmiyahu 51:1), and against those who dwell in לֵב קָמָי, has been read by the alphabet reversed, alef for tav and beis for shin, as כשדים, Kasdim, as though it said יֹשְׁבֵי כַשְׂדִּים (Yirmiyahu 51:35), the dwellers of Kasdim. It can also be read with ארץ כשדים, the land of Kasdim, left unsaid, the reader being trusted to supply it since Bavel has been named, and with לֵב קָמָי in its plain sense, the heart of my enemies, as in תַּהֲרֹס קָמֶיךָ (Shemos 15:7), You overthrow those who rise against You, and לְשִׁמְצָה בְּקָמֵיהֶם (Shemos 32:25), for a disgrace among those who rise against them: and against the heart of my enemies, the dwellers of the land of Kasdim.

The noun: וְרָמֵי הַקּוֹמָה גְּדוּעִים (Yeshayahu 10:33), the high of stature hewn down, and like it וְאֶכְרֹת קוֹמַת אֲרָזָיו (Yeshayahu 37:24), I will cut down the height of its cedars, meaning the tallest of its cedars, as it says מִבְחוֹר בְּרֹשָׁיו, the choicest of its cypresses; it is a figure for the great men and the officers. Also זֹאת קוֹמָתֵךְ דָּמְתָה לְתָמָר (Shir HaShirim 7:8), this stature of yours is like a palm tree, and וַיִּפֹּל מְלֹא קוֹמָתוֹ (Shmuel I 28:20), he fell his full height. Grain standing before it is reaped is called קָמָה because it stands, all of it together: מִגָּדִישׁ וְעַד קָמָה (Shoftim 15:5), from the stacked sheaves to the standing grain, and בְּקָמוֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּים (Shoftim 15:5), into the standing grain of the Pelishtim.

וְקָמָה בְּיָדְךָ מַמְלֶכֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shmuel I 24:21), the kingdom of Yisrael shall stand in your hand, is that it will stand and endure; so לֹא תָקוּם וְלֹא תִהְיֶה (Yeshayahu 7:7), it shall not stand and shall not be, וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר (Vayikra 25:30), the house in the city shall stand, כִּי קוֹם יָקוּמוּ דְבָרַי עֲלֵיכֶם לְרָעָה (Yirmiyahu 44:29), that My words shall surely stand against you for harm, the קוֹם written with cholam, and וַיָּקָם שְׂדֵה עֶפְרוֹן (Bereishis 23:17), the field of Efron stood, that is, it stood and was made good in his hand. Where the verb takes an object it confirms: וּמַאֲמַר אֶסְתֵּר קִיַּם (Esther 9:32), Esther's word confirmed it, קַיְּמֵנִי כִּדְבָרֶךָ (Tehillim 119:28), confirm me according to Your word, and הֲקִימֹתִי אֶת דְּבַר (Shmuel I 15:13), I have established the word of Hashem. יָקֵם סְעָרָה לִדְמָמָה (Tehillim 107:29) is that the storm He raised He will turn to calm; and in וְחָרְבוֹתֶיהָ אֲקוֹמֵם (Yeshayahu 44:26), I will raise up her ruins. The noun וָאוֹלֵךְ אֶתְכֶם קוֹמְמִיּוּת (Vayikra 26:13), I led you קוֹמְמִיּוּת, is with an upright stature, fearing no man, on the way of יֹצְאִים בְּיָד רָמָה (Shemos 14:8), going out with a high hand; and in another pattern, וְלֹא תִהְיֶה לָכֶם תְּקוּמָה (Vayikra 26:37), you shall have no standing.

וַיִּמַח אֶת כָּל הַיְקוּם (Bereishis 7:23), He blotted out every living thing, and וְאֵת כָּל הַיְקוּם אֲשֶׁר בְּרַגְלֵיהֶם (Devarim 11:6), and every living thing at their feet: יְקוּם is a general name for everything alive on the earth. אִם לֹא נִכְחַד קִימָנוּ (Iyov 22:20) is like קִימֵנוּ with tzeirei, meaning יְקוּמֵנוּ: in truth our living stock was not cut off altogether in the mabul, since Noach and his sons were left; and וְיִתְרָם אָכְלָה אֵשׁ, and fire consumed their remnant, is the rest of the wicked, those who were afterwards in Sedom and Amorah. The place is מָקוֹם: וְשַׂמְתִּי לְךָ מָקוֹם (Shemos 21:13), I will set you a place, mostly masculine, feminine in וְלֹא עוֹד תְּשׁוּרֶנּוּ מְקוֹמוֹ (Iyov 20:9), and his place shall see him no more, with the plural בְּאַחַד הַמְּקוֹמֹת (Shmuel II 17:9), in one of the places, so that it is masculine but takes a feminine plural. וְזֶה מְקוֹם לֹא יָדַע אֵל (Iyov 18:21), and this is the place of one who did not know Hashem, lacks the word it is bound to: the place of a man who did not know Hashem. Chazal (Bereishis Rabbah 68) called the Holy One by the name מָקוֹם, since He is the place of the world and the world is not His place, as He is also called מעון, a dwelling, in מְעֹנָה אֱלֹהֵי קֶדֶם (Devarim 33:27), the God of old is a dwelling. Some read רֶוַח וְהַצָּלָה יַעֲמוֹד לַיְּהוּדִים מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר (Esther 4:14), relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place, as a hint at Him, since they did not wish to write the Name in the Megillah, it being written together with the books of Madai and Paras.

נחל.sense: To take as a possession, and to give one; נַחֲלָה, an inheritance. In another sense, נַחַל, the valley the water runs in, called so even when it is dry.

more.t: וְאֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר נָחֲלוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yehoshua 14:1), and these are what the children of Yisrael took as a possession, כִּי לֹא נִנְחַל אִתָּם (Bamidbar 32:19), for we will not take a possession with them, and לִנְחֹל אֶת הָאָרֶץ (Bamidbar 34:18), to take the land as a possession. The simple verb, he says, takes one object only, the inheritance itself, so that יִנְחֲלוּ לָכֶם אֶת הָאָרֶץ (Bamidbar 34:17) is that they take the land as a possession on your behalf.

וְסָלַחְתָּ לַעֲוֹנֵנוּ וּלְחַטָּאתֵנוּ וּנְחַלְתָּנוּ (Shemos 34:9), and pardon our iniquity and our sin and take us as a possession, means take us for Your own, that we be Your inheritance, as וְהֵם עַמְּךָ וְנַחֲלָתֶךָ (Devarim 9:29), they are Your people and Your inheritance. So of Yehudah, אֶת־יְהֹוּדָה חֶלְקוֹ (Zecharyah 2:16), Yehudah His portion: Yehudah will be Hashem's inheritance forever on the holy soil. כִּי אַתָּה תִנְחַל בְּכָל הַגּוֹיִם (Tehillim 82:8), for You take possession among all the nations, he reads with what the mizmor says at its opening, עַד מָתַי תִּשְׁפְּטוּ עָוֶל, how long will you judge wrongly, and with קוּמָה אֱלֹהִים שָׁפְטָה הָאָרֶץ, arise, Elokim, judge the land: take the judgment of the poor and of those who cry out against violence from the hands of the wicked, the unjust judges, for You take the poor as Your possession among all the nations. In whatever nation the poor and the robbed are found, they are Your people and Your inheritance, and You will take them for Your own and save them from the hand of their oppressors.

אֵלֶּה אֲשֶׁר נִחַל מֹשֶׁה בְּעַרְבוֹת מוֹאָב (Yehoshua 13:32), these are what Moshe gave as inheritances in the plains of Moav, and כִּי אַתָּה תַּנְחִיל אֶת הָעָם הַזֶּה (Yehoshua 1:6), for you will give this people its inheritance; so בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת בָּנָיו (Devarim 21:16), on the day he gives his sons their inheritance, and בְּהַנְחֵל עֶלְיוֹן גּוֹיִם (Devarim 32:8), when the Most High gave the nations their inheritance. In the passive, כֵּן הָנְחַלְתִּי לִי יַרְחֵי שָׁוְא (Iyov 7:3), so months of emptiness were given me for a portion; and turned back on itself, וְהִתְנַחַלְתֶּם אֹתָם (Vayikra 25:46), where he reads אֹתָם as מהם: you shall take a possession from them, like הֵם יָצְאוּ אֶת הָעִיר (Bereishis 44:4), they had gone out from the city.

וְנִחַלְתְּ בָּךְ לְעֵינֵי גוֹיִם (Yechezkel 22:16) may be taken from this root, though he explained it at חָלַל; its proper form would then be וְנִנְחַלְתְּ, and but for the ches it would carry a dagesh. Taken so, it means: until now you were My inheritance, but since you have sinned you are not; you will be inherited by yourself and not by Me, in the sight of the nations.

פָּרַץ נַחַל (Iyov 28:4), a stream breaks out, וְהָיָה מֵהַנַּחַל תִּשְׁתֶּה (Melachim I 17:4), you will drink from the נַחַל, with the dual אֶל כָּל אֲשֶׁר יָבוֹא שָׁם נַחֲלַיִם יִחְיֶה (Yechezkel 47:9), everything to which the two streams come will live, and the plural כָּל הַנְּחָלִים הֹלְכִים אֶל הַיָּם (Koheles 1:7), all the streams go to the sea. The valley in which the waters run is called a נַחַל, and even when there is no water in it, it is still called so, since the place is what bears the name, as וְהָעִיר אֲשֶׁר בַּנַּחַל (Devarim 2:36), and the city that is in the valley. אֶל נַחַל אֵיתָן (Devarim 21:4), to a strong נַחַל, had water in it, since it is written there that they wash their hands; and so וּצְדָקָה כְּנַחַל אֵיתָן (Amos 5:24), and righteousness like a strong נַחַל, is one whose waters sweep down with force. In נַהֲרֵי נַחֲלֵי דְּבַשׁ וְחֶמְאָה (Iyov 20:17), rivers of streams of honey and butter, one construct comes upon another.

לַמְנַצֵּחַ אֶל הַנְּחִילוֹת (Tehillim 5:1), for the conductor, on the נְחִילוֹת, is the name of a tune they knew. Rabbeinu Hai explained the word from נחיל של דבורים (Bava Kamma 10:2), a swarm of bees; that is, its tune was like the whistling of bees.

יאר.sense: Water drawn off from a river in channels onto the fields; the Nilus is called so, its waters running over the fields, and so is the Chidekel. For Onkelos, the river.

more.h: River, or channel from a river
more.t: עַל־שְׂפַת הַיְאֹֽר (Shemos 2:3), on the bank of the יאור, כָּל־הַמַּיִם אֲשֶׁר־ בַּיְאֹר (Shemos 7:20), all the water in the יאור, and עַל־ יְאֹֽרֵיהֶם וְעַל־אַגְמֵיהֶם (Shemos 7:19), over their channels and over their pools. By Onkelos the יאור is the river itself, since he renders יְאֹר as נַהֲרָא, river; but יְאֹֽרֵיהֶם he renders with another word, because in that pasuk it stands next to their rivers; and the יאור is the water that flows and is drawn off in channels from the river to the fields.

Because the waters of the Nilus are drawn off and run over the fields to water them, it is called a יאור; and so the Chidekel is called a יאור, אֶחָד הֵנָּה לִשְׂפַת הַיְאֹר וְאֶחָד הֵנָּה לִשְׂפַת הַיְאֹֽר (Daniel 12:5), one on this side at the bank of the יאור and one on that side at the bank of the יאור. In וְעָֽלְתָה כָאֹר כֻּלָּהּ (Amos 8:8), and all of it shall rise like the יאור, the yud is hidden, and the word stands for כיאור, like the יאור.

אחז.sense: To take hold, to grasp. From this sense an inheritance is called אֲחֻזָּה, because a man takes hold in the place and is held secure there on its account.

more.t: חִיל אָחַז (Shemos 15:14), trembling took hold, אָחַזְתָּ שְׁמֻרוֹת עֵינָי (Tehillim 77:5), You held my eyelids, לֶאֱחֹז בְּכַנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ (Iyov 38:13), to take hold of the corners of the earth, וָאֹחֵז בְּפִילַגְשִׁי (Shoftim 20:6), and I took hold of my concubine, and וֶאֱחֹז לְךָ אֶחָד מֵהַנְּעָרִים (Shmuel II 2:21), and take hold for yourself of one of the young men. In the passive, נֶאֱחַז בַּסְּבַךְ (Bereishis 22:13), caught in the thicket, כַּדָּגִים שֶׁנֶּאֱחָזִים (Koheles 9:12), like fish that are caught, and וַיֵּאָחֲזוּ בָהּ, and they took hold in it. Also וְכֶבֶשׁ בַּזָּהָב לַכִּסֵּא מָאֳחָזִים (Divrei HaYamim II 9:18), and a footstool of gold fastened to the throne, and מְאַחֵז פְּנֵי כִסֵּה (Iyov 26:9), He holds fast the face of the throne.

אֲחֻזֵי חֶרֶב (Shir HaShirim 3:8), holding the sword, has the form of what is acted upon, in the way of חָגוּר כְּלֵי מִלְחָמָה (Shoftim 18:11), girded with weapons of war, and לָבוּשׁ בַּדִּים (Yechezkel 9:2), clothed in linen.

more.h: The beams that hold the walls
more.t: וַיֶּאֱחֹז אֶת הַבַּיִת (Melachim I 6:10), and he held the house, means that he roofed it with cedar beams, and so Targum Yonasan renders it, וְטַלֵיל יַת בֵּיתָא, and he roofed the house; the pasuk uses a word of taking hold because the beams take hold of this wall and of the wall opposite, as it also says לְבִלְתִּי אֲחֹז בְּקִירוֹת הַבָּיִת (Melachim I 6:6), so as not to take hold in the walls of the house.

From this sense comes אֲחֻזָּה: תְּנוּ לִי אֲחֻזַּת קֶבֶר (Bereishis 23:4), give me a holding for a burial place, and וְהָיוּ לָכֶם לַאֲחֻזָּה (Vayikra 25:45), and they shall be yours as a holding. An inheritance is called so because a man takes hold in the place and is held secure there on its account, as וַיֵּאָחֲזוּ בָהּ, and they took hold in it, and וְנֹאחֲזוּ בְתֹכְכֶם (Bamidbar 32:30), and they shall take hold among you.

וַאֲחֻזַּת מֵרֵעֵהוּ (Bereishis 26:26), and Achuzzas his friend, is a man's name, and the Mesorah marks it לית שום בר נש, unique as a personal name. The Targum's view is וְסִיעַת מְרַחֲמוֹהִי, the company of his friends; on that view a man's company is called an אחוזה because they hold to him and do not part from him in his going out and his coming in.

כנר.sense: כִּנּוֹר, the kinnor, named in the pesukim with the ugav and the nevel; its sense is known. It takes a plural, and a plural in the feminine form.
