Rabbi Yonah explained וְיָבֹאוּ פִּתְחֵי נְדִיבִים (Yeshayahu 13:2), and let the פִּתְחֵי of nobles come, as swords like these; and in one of his ways he explained חֶרֶב חֶרֶב פְּתוּחָה (Yechezkel 21:33), a sword, a sword, פתוחה, and חֶרֶב פָּתְחוּ רְשָׁעִים (Tehillim 37:14), the wicked פתחו a sword, as polishing and sharpening. Radak says there is no need: their sense is only drawing the sword from its sheath, as פתוח is said of bringing a prisoner out of confinement and loosing him.

הדס.sense: The myrtle; of its sense he says only ידוע, it is known.

more.t: וַהֲדַס וְעֵץ שָׁמֶן (Yeshayahu 41:19), myrtle and oil tree; יַעֲלֶה הֲדַס (Yeshayahu 55:13), a myrtle will come up; עֹמֵד בֵּין הַהֲדַסִּים (Zecharyah 1:8), standing among the myrtles. Of these he says only ידוע, it is known.

סבב.sense: Going round a thing and encircling it. Every word of the root is this one sense, since there is no rolling, returning or reversing without a going round.

more.t: וְסָבַב בֵּֽית־אֵל (Shmuel I 7:16), he went round to Beis El; סֹבּוּ צִיּוֹן וְהַקִּיפוּהָ (Tehillim 48:13), go round Tzion and encircle her; סוֹבֵב סֹבֵב הוֹלֵךְ הָרוּחַ (Koheles 1:6), round and round goes the wind; and וְהִנֵּה תְסֻבֶּינָה אֲלֻמֹּתֵיכֶם (Bereishis 37:7), your sheaves came round about.

וַיַּסֵּב אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הָעָם (Shemos 13:18), He led the people round about; וַיַּסֵּב חִזְקִיָּהוּ פָּנָיו אֶל־הַקִּיר (Yeshayahu 38:2), Chizkiyahu turned his face to the wall; וַתִּסֹּב הַמְּלוּכָה (Melachim I 2:15), the kingship turned about; and כִּֽי־הָֽיְתָה סִבָּה (Melachim I 12:15), for it was a turn of events.

Rabbi Yonah divided the root into three senses and answered Rabbi Yehudah, who wrote them all as one. Radak holds Rabbi Yehudah's view straight and right, that they are all one sense: of the pesukim that seemed strange to Rabbi Yonah, so that he took them out of the sense of going round and encircling, not one escapes it, since there is no rolling, returning or reversing without going round and encircling.

Rabbi Yonah's claim that עַד־שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ בִּמְסִבּוֹ (Shir HaShirim 1:12), while the king was in his circle, and רֹאשׁ מְסִבָּי (Tehillim 140:10), the head of those round me, are a sense apart, reclining, drawn from Chazal's saying that one does not eat until he reclines (Pesachim 99b), Radak says is not so. Reclining in Chazal's language is itself a word of going round: they used to sit round about at the food and drink, and while eating and drinking they leaned to the left as a mark of standing, so they called the leaning too by that name; no other leaning in the world is called by it, only at eating and drinking, when they sat round. And so the Targum renders וַיֵּֽשְׁבוּ לֶֽאֱכָל־לֶחֶם (Bereishis 37:25), they sat down to eat bread, with a word of going round.

more.h: A woman shall go round a man
more.t: נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵֽב גָּֽבֶר (Yirmiyahu 31:21 in his edition), a woman shall go round a man, is a figure: Knesses Yisrael is likened to a woman seeking her husband, as it says elsewhere that they will seek Hashem their God and David their king (Hoshea 3:5).

סעד.sense: To support, to prop up: bread supports the heart, a right hand upholds a man, kindness upholds a throne. From this Chazal called a meal סעודה.

more.t: וְלֶחֶם לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ יִסְעָד (Tehillim 104:15), and bread supports a man's heart, has its one object. וְסַעֲדוּ לִבְּכֶם (Bereishis 18:5), support your hearts, carries a second with it, since the sense is support your hearts with bread, the bread being what supports the heart; and likewise סְעָד לִבְּךָ פַּת לֶחֶם (Shoftim 19:5), support your heart with a morsel of bread.

more.h: Where the word for a meal comes from
more.t: בֹּֽאָה־אִתִּי הַבַּיְתָה וּֽסֳעָדָה (Melachim I 13:7), come home with me and support yourself: from this, he says, Chazal called a meal סעודה (Shabbos 117b).

סְעָדֵנִי וְאִוָּשֵׁעָה (Tehillim 119:117), hold me up and I will be saved; וִימִינְךָ תִסְעָדֵנִי (Tehillim 18:36), and Your right hand upholds me; וְסָעַד בַּחֶסֶד כִּסְאוֹ (Mishlei 20:28), and he upholds his throne with kindness. The מִסְעָד of Melachim I 10:12 he has already explained in his entry on סלל. The sense of them all is support and propping up.

שׁכח.sense: To forget; to be forgotten; to make forgotten; and, said of the righteous, to make themselves forgotten, hiding from the wicked.

more.t: וְשָׁכַחְתָּ עֹמֶר בַּשָּׂדֶה (Devarim 24:19), and you forget a sheaf in the field; שְׁכֵחֻנִי עַמִּי (Yirmiyahu 18:15), My people have forgotten Me; בִּינוּ נָא זֹאת שֹׁכְחֵי אֱלוֹהַּ (Tehillim 50:22), understand this, you who forget God; and in the passive כִּי נִשְׁכַּח זִכְרָם (Koheles 9:5), for their memory is forgotten, with נִשְׁכַּחְתִּי כְּמֵת מִלֵּב (Tehillim 31:13), I am forgotten like a dead man out of mind. The adjective is שָׁכֵחַ, formed like שָׂמֵחַ, glad, found in the plural: הַשְּׁכֵחִים אֶת־הַר קָדְשִׁי (Yeshayahu 65:11), who forget My holy mountain, and כָּל־גּוֹיִם שְׁכֵחֵי אֱלֹהִים (Tehillim 9:18), all the nations forgetful of God. It is said of making forgotten too: שִׁכַּח י"י בְּצִיּוֹן (Eichah 2:6), Hashem has made forgotten in Tzion, and לְהַשְׁכִּיחַ אֶת עַמִּי שְׁמִי (Yirmiyahu 23:27), to make My people forget My name.

תִּשְׁכַּח יְמִינִי (Tehillim 137:5), let my right hand forget, has its object missing, and the object is the playing, since the right hand moves the strings of the harp. The pasuk means: when the men of Bavel told them to sing they would answer, how shall we sing, and each of the singers would say, if I forget you, Yerushalayim, and play while you lie in ruin, let my right hand forget the playing.

וְיִשְׁתַּכְּחוּ בָעִיר אֲשֶׁר כֵּן עָשׂוּ (Koheles 8:10), and those who had done right make themselves forgotten in the city, he reads of the righteous. When the wicked die others come in their place, as it says וּמֵעָפָר אַחֵר יִצְמָחוּ (Iyov 8:19), and from the dust others will spring up; those who are from a holy place, the righteous, go off and are driven away, so as not to be seen before the wicked, because of the violence done to them; and the men who did what was true and upright hide from them and make themselves forgotten and hidden.

נשׁם.sense: Breath: every living thing's, it seems to him, though Ibn Ezra finds the word only of man. Also the תִּנְשֶׁמֶת, a kind of bird and a creeping thing.

more.h: Breath of every living thing, it seems
more.t: It seems to him that the spirit of every living thing is called נשמה, which is why the word stands joined to רוּחַ, spirit: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁמַת־רוּחַ חַיִּים בְּאַפָּיו (Bereishis 7:22), all in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, that is, everything that has breathing of spirit, which is to say movement.

וַיְהִי חָלְיוֹ חָזָק מְאֹד עַד אֲשֶׁר לֹא־נֽוֹתְרָה־בּוֹ נְשָׁמָֽה (Melachim I 17:17), his sickness was so heavy that no breath was left in him: he had no breathing, his movement came to nothing and his breath was stopped. At Daniel 10:17, where no breath was left in me, he says the words are put strongly beyond their measure, since the one saying them was speaking.

Ibn Ezra writes on כֹּל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁמַת־רוּחַ חַיִּים (Bereishis 7:22), all that has the breath of the spirit of life, that it goes back to man, since we find the word of no one but man. Ibn Ezra adds that many said it is called so because it comes from the heavens; and if those are two roots, there are many like it.

more.h: The bird and the creeping thing
more.t: וְאֶת־ הַתִּנְשֶׁמֶת וְאֶת־הַקָּאָת (Vayikra 11:18), and the tinshemes and the ka'as: the tinshemes is one of the kinds of birds, and they said it is named so because whoever sees it is appalled. Rashi writes that it is the one called צואיט"א. The same name is among the creeping things, וְהַחֹמֶט וְהַתִּנְשָֽׁמֶת (Vayikra 11:30), and the chomet and the tinshemes, and Rashi writes that this one is called in la'az טלפ"א.

יחד.sense: The sense of one: the only one, the soul as the single one, and many joined together so that they look like one; and to make one.

more.t: רַךְ וְיָחִיד לִפְנֵי אִמִּֽי (Mishlei 4:3), tender and an only child before my mother, and וְרַק הִיא יְחִידָה (Shoftim 11:34), she was his only child. Both belong, he says, to the sense of one.

more.h: The soul as the single one
more.t: The soul is called יְחִידָה, מִיַּד־כֶּלֶב יְחִידָתִֽי (Tehillim 22:21), my only one from the power of the dog, because it stands single over against the parts and powers of the body, which are many and are not of its kind.

יַּחַד יָבֹאוּ גְדוּדָיו (Iyov 19:12), his troops come on together, is also from one, since many joined look like a single thing. His own view is that the vav of יַחְדָּו is the mark of the plural set over a singular, as in עָלָיו, upon him, and אֵלָיו, to him. Though יחדו mostly has no yod, עָלָו [עָלָיו] בַּשָּׁמַיִם יַרְעֵם (Shmuel I 2:10), upon him He thunders in heaven, is found without one too, and three places have יַחְדָּיו with a yod (Yirmiyahu 46:12, 46:21 and 49:3); it is said so, he writes, because singleness and plurality are gathered together in it.
יַחֵד לְבָבִי לְיִרְאָה שְׁמֶֽךָ (Tehillim 86:11), make my heart one to fear Your name.

מהל.sense: Mixed, as wine mixed with water. His entry under these letters holds that alone, and nothing of circumcision.

more.t: סָבְאֵךְ מָהוּל בַּמָּֽיִם (Yeshayahu 1:22), your wine is mixed with water: the sense is מזוג, mixed. His father brings proof for it from the Arabic, which says of a thing that has been mingled מהל"א מהל"י.

מול.sense: To circumcise; all its forms, he says, are the sense of cutting; and מוּל, over against, facing.

more.t: וּמַלְתֶּם אֵת עָרְלַת לְבַבְכֶם (Devarim 10:16), circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and וַיָּמָל אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yehoshua 5:3), he circumcised the children of Yisrael. The form that is done to a man: וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי יִמּוֹל בְּשַׂר עָרְלָתֽוֹ (Vayikra 12:3), on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.

עַל־כָּל־ מוּל בְּעָרְלָֽה (Yirmiyahu 9:24) he reads as two things at once: upon everyone circumcised and upon everyone who is in his foreskin, that is, upon Yisrael who are circumcised and upon those who are not.

יְמוֹלֵל וְיָבֵֽשׁ (Tehillim 90:6), it is cut down and dries up, is either an intransitive verb or one whose doer is left unsaid, the wind, as in רוּחַ עָֽבְרָה־בּוֹ וְאֵינֶנּוּ (Tehillim 103:16), the wind passes over it and it is gone. So too כְּמוֹ יִתְמֹלָֽלוּ (Tehillim 58:8), as though they were cut off. The sense of all of them is cutting.

מוּל means over against: מוּל הָֽאֱלֹהִים (Shemos 18:19), which he glosses as facing Hashem, and וַיִּסֹּב מֵֽאֶצְלוֹ אֶל־ מוּל אַחֵר (Shmuel I 17:30), he turned away from him toward another, which he reads as toward another place. It comes with a cholam in place of the shuruk, מוֹל סוּף (Devarim 1:1), over against Suf, and with a quiescent alef after the vav, הַֽהוֹלֶכֶת לְמוֹאל (Nechemiah 12:38), that went over against. The sense of all of them is facing and over against.

רפא.sense: To heal, and to be healed; figuratively, to mend what is broken and to forgive. In other senses of the root, רְפָאִים are the mighty men of the giants, and the dead.

more.t: רְפֻאוֹת תְּעָלָה אֵין לָֽךְ (Yirmiyahu 30:13), you have no healing medicines; רִפְאוּת תְּהִי לְשָׁרֶּךָ (Mishlei 3:8), it will be a healing to your body; and מַרְפֵּא, a cure, לְאֵין מַרְפֵּֽא (Divrei HaYamim II 36:16), past all cure.

וְרַפֹּא יְרַפֵּֽא (Shemos 21:19), and he shall surely have him healed, reaches past the one healed to a third: the man who struck hires the doctor for him. So the Targum has וְאֲגַר אָסְיָא יְשַׁלֵּם, he shall pay the doctor's fee. And so the Chachamim taught (Bava Kama 88a) that if the one who struck is himself a doctor and wants to do the healing, he is not listened to, since the injured man may tell him that he is as a lion lying in wait for him.

By way of figure the word is used of repair: וַיְרַפֵּא אֶת־מִזְבַּח (Melachim I 18:30), and he healed the mizbe'ach of Hashem that was torn down, and כַּֽאֲשֶׁר יִשְׁבֹּר אֶת־כְּלִי הַיּוֹצֵר אֲשֶׁר לֹֽא־יוּכַל לְהֵֽרָפֵה עוֹד (Yirmiyahu 19:11), as one breaks a potter's vessel that can never be healed again. And, again by way of figure, of forgiveness: רְפָאָה נַפְשִׁי כִּי־חָטָאתִי לָֽךְ (Tehillim 41:5), heal my soul, for I have sinned against You.

From this root in another sense, נִשְׁאַר מִיֶּתֶר הָֽרְפָאִים (Devarim 3:11), left of the remnant of the Refaim, where the sense is the mighty men of the giants. The singular is נוֹלַד לְהָֽרָפָֽא (Divrei HaYamim I 20:6), born to the Rafa, where the heh is the definite article kept after the lamed of service. The two places in Divrei HaYamim are written with an alef; in Shmuel the same word is written with a heh standing in the alef's place.

In yet another sense, אִם־ רְפָאִים יָקוּמוּ (Tehillim 88:11), shall the dead rise, and כִּֽי־ רְפָאִים שָׁם (Mishlei 9:18), the dead are there. Some read הָֽרְפָאִים יְחוֹלָלוּ (Iyov 26:5), the dead are brought forth, as a hint to the grains of seed, which lie under the ground like the dead and afterwards live and are brought forth; and on that reading מִתַּחַת מַיִם, beneath the waters, is said because the waters are the cause of the moisture of the earth from which the seeds grow.

אבן.sense: A stone. A weight and the builder's plummet are called אבן, being made of stone; the potter's implement; and הָֽאָבְנָיִם of a birth, which he takes as the womb itself.

more.t: מִשָּׁם רֹעֶה אֶבֶן יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (Bereishis 49:24), from there, the shepherd, the stone of Yisrael, means all of Yisrael: a stone is one body, so Yisrael spoken of as one is called a stone; or else, since Yisrael are the foundation of the world's building, they are called a stone as a figure. Rabbi Yonah read it as the head of Yisrael. Radak answers that we do not find a head called אֶבֶן unless the pasuk explains itself afterwards, as at אֶבֶן בֹּחַן פִּנַּת יִקְרַת מוּסָד (Yeshayahu 28:16), a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a foundation.

תִּשְׁתַּפֵּכְנָה אַבְנֵי ־קֹדֶשׁ (Eichah 4:1), the holy stones are poured out, means the princes and the great men. אַבְנֵי ־אֵשׁ הִתְהַלָּֽכְתָּ (Yechezkel 28:14), among stones of fire you walked, is as though among the angels. His father takes it as among אבני אקדח, which Radak explains as gems shining like lamps, among which the one addressed would walk at night. Targum Yonasan rendered it בְעַמָא קַדִישָׁא סְבַרְתָּא לְמִשְׁלַט, among the holy people you thought to rule, and so, Radak says, the meaning appears to be, since afterwards it says וָֽאַבֶּדְךָ כְּרוּב הַסֹּכֵךְ מִתּוֹךְ אַבְנֵי ־אֵֽשׁ (Yechezkel 28:16), and I destroyed you, the covering keruv, from among the stones of fire: these are Yisrael, called so because they are holy.

וְכָֽבְשׁוּ אַבְנֵי ־קֶלַע (Zecharyah 9:15), and they shall tread down the sling stones: the sling stones are the officers of Greece. Since the kings of the house of the Chashmonaim were likened to crown stones for their greatness, the officers of Greece are likened to sling stones for their lowness.

Weights are made of stone, so a weight is called אבן: לֹא־יִֽהְיֶה לְךָ בְּכִֽיסְךָ אֶבֶן וָאָבֶן (Devarim 25:13), you shall not have in your bag two sorts of weight, and בְּאֶבֶן הַמֶּֽלֶךְ (Shmuel II 14:26), by the king's weight. So too the plummet the builder weighs with is called אבן, being of stone: וְנָטָה עָלֶיהָ קַו־תֹהוּ וְאַבְנֵי ־בֹֽהוּ (Yeshayahu 34:11), and He will stretch over it the line of emptiness and the plummets of void. Even when it is of tin or of lead it is still called a stone: אֶת־ הָאֶבֶן הַבְּדִיל (Zecharyah 4:10), the stone of tin, and אֶבֶן הָֽעוֹפֶרֶת (Zecharyah 5:8), the stone of lead.

עֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה עַל־ הָֽאָבְנָֽיִם (Yirmiyahu 18:3), doing work on the אבנים, is the potter's implement on which he makes his earthenware, well known to the men of that trade and called in laaz סיל"א. It is said that it is like a pair of millstones, and that is why the name is put as two; but in these lands it is not so, only one round piece of wood shaped like a millstone, on which the potter does his work. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the kind which is two, like a lower and an upper millstone with the upper smaller, is the tool of the potters of the east. Radak's father holds the alef here is added and the word belongs to building.

Rabbi Yonah takes וּרְאִיתֶן עַל־ הָֽאָבְנָיִם (Shemos 1:16), and you shall look upon the אבנים, as the place where the child falls from its mother's womb, which is called משבר, and derives the word from בן and בנים, son and sons, with an added alef. Radak holds it is the womb itself, named אָבְנַיִם for the בנים, the children, and called משבר for the breaking of the woman in labour and her pangs. Were it the place the child falls after coming out, why would the pasuk say you shall look upon the אבנים, when before the child is wholly out of the womb one can already see whether it is male or female, since the male faces downward and the female upward (Sotah 11b)? And why would a place of falling be called משבר? The pasuk הַֽאֲנִי אַשְׁבִּיר וְלֹא אוֹלִיד (Yeshayahu 66:9), shall I bring to the breaking and not cause to bear, shows that the משבר comes before the birth. It is named as two for the צירים at the opening of the womb, which are two like the two hinges of a door; and so the Chachamim taught (Bechoros 45a) in a braisa, Rabbi Eliezer saying that as a house has hinges so has a woman, as it says כִּֽי־נֶֽהֶפְכוּ עָלֶיהָ צִרֶֽיהָ (Shmuel I 4:19), for her צירים turned upon her. צירים is a shared name, said of the hinges of a door and of the pangs of birth.

צור.sense: To besiege; close to it, straits and pain: pangs, the enemy, the rival wife; close to that, binding up. Also an envoy, a hinge, a rock, sharpness, a form; the neck.

more.t: וְצַרְתָּ עָלֶֽיהָ (Devarim 20:12), you shall besiege it, and the noun וּבָנִיתָ מָצוֹר (Devarim 20:20), you shall build a siege work. A fortified city is itself called מָצוֹר, he says, because no man takes it by force but only by a siege built against it, with men standing about it until it falls from hunger and thirst: וַתִּבֶן צֹר מָצוֹר לָהּ (Zecharyah 9:3), and Tzor built herself a stronghold.

more.h: Straits, the enemy, the rival wife
more.t: Another sense close to it is pressure: צַר ־לִי הַמָּקוֹם (Yeshayahu 49:20), the place is too narrow for me, with the noun צָרָה, distress. The enemy is called צַר, אִישׁ צַר וְאוֹיֵב (Esther 7:6), a man who is an adversary and an enemy, and the enemy belongs to this sense because an enemy pains and presses. And since two or more wives of one man each hate and envy the other and their place is narrow for them, each is called her fellow's צָרָה, וְכִֽעֲסַתָּה צָֽרָתָהּ (Shmuel I 1:6), her rival provoked her. This whole sense of pressure, he holds, is close to the first, since one who sits in a siege is in straits and distress there; and it may all belong to the root צָרַר.

צִירִים אֲחָזוּנִי כְּצִירֵי יֽוֹלֵדָה (Yeshayahu 21:3), pangs took hold of me like the pangs of a woman giving birth; in this sense images too are called צירים, חָֽרָשֵׁי צִירִֽים (Yeshayahu 45:16), makers of images, as they are also called עצבים, idols. So too כְּלֵב אִשָׁה מְצֵרָֽה (Yirmiyahu 48:41), like the heart of a woman in distress, that is, in pain and in straits. All of these and their like, he says, are the sense of pain and pressure. A ציר is also one sent, צִיר נֶאֱמָן לְשֹֽׁלְחָיו (Mishlei 25:13), a faithful envoy to those who send him, the sense being that of being sent. And it is the pivot of a door, הַדֶּלֶת תִּסּוֹב עַל־ צִירָהּ (Mishlei 26:14), the door turns upon its hinge, which he says is the door's foot that it turns on. Some say it is the hollow in the threshold that the door's foot enters; he holds they are wrong, that hollow being called צנור, as the Mishnah has it.

וְצַרְתָּ הַכֶּסֶף (Devarim 14:25), you shall bind up the money, and וְצַרְתָּ אוֹתָם בִּכְנָפֶֽיךָ (Yechezkel 5:3), bind them in your skirts: the putting away of money or of anything else in a purse and the like, with the tying of it. וַיָּצֻרוּ וַיִּמְנוּ (Melachim II 12:11), they bound up and counted, he explains as their having counted it first and bound it up after. He calls this sense close to the sense of pressure, since those who tie a thing up press it.

וְצוּר יֶעְתַּק מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ (Iyov 14:18), a rock is moved from its place, and עַל־ הַצּוּר (Shemos 17:6), upon the rock: the sense is סלע, a crag. חֶלְקַת הַצֻּרִים (Shmuel II 2:16) he explains as the portion of the strong ones, for those young men were strong like rocks, standing against each other with neither side overcoming the other, but all falling together. For the strength of rocks Hashem is called צוּר, by way of transfer, since He may be likened to nothing but His own works: הַצּוּר תָּמִים פָּֽעֳלוֹ (Devarim 32:4), the Rock, His work is perfect, and צוּר עֽוֹלָמִֽים (Yeshayahu 26:4), the everlasting Rock. וְיֶעְתַּק־צוּר מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ (Iyov 18:4) can be read the same way, shall the Rock be moved from His place, that is, from the place of His judgment. Rabbi Yonah takes וַתִּבֶן צֹר מָצוֹר לָהּ, Tzor built herself a stronghold, and its like as belonging to this sense, meaning strength, and so Targum Yonasan rendered.

In the sense of sharpness: אַף־תָּשִׁיב צוּר חַרְבּוֹ (Tehillim 89:44), You also turn back the sharpness of his sword, and חַֽרְבוֹת צֻרִים (Yehoshua 5:2), swords of sharpness, that is, swords that have an edge; or else צוּר and צֻרִים are describing words, his sharp sword and sharp swords. Targum Yonasan renders חֶלְקַת הַצֻּרִים from this sense, אַחֲסָנַת קְטִלַיָא, the possession of the slain. Another sense is the shaping of a form: וַיָּצַר אֹתוֹ בַּחֶרֶט (Shemos 32:4), he formed it with a graving tool, and צוּרַת הַבַּיִת (Yechezkel 43:11), the form of the house. וַיָּצֻרוּ וַיִּמְנוּ (Melachim II 12:11) can also be read of this sense, that they made the silver into coin to give it out to the craftsmen, to buy timber and stones; and such is the view of Chazal on the word וְצַרְתָּ הַכֶּסֶף (Devarim 14:25), who said, a thing that has a form (Berachos 46b). From this root too is the neck: וַיָּשֶׂם רְבִד הַזָּהָב עַל־ צַוָּארֽוֹ (Bereishis 41:42), he put the gold chain upon his neck, spoken of at times as two, for its right side and its left.

חלמשׁ.sense: Strength, said of rock: מִצּוּר הַחַלָּמִישׁ, from the strong and mighty rock; מֵחַלְמִישׁ צוּר, from the strength of the rocks. It is said of nothing but a rock.

more.t: מִצּוּר הַֽחַלָּמִֽישׁ (Devarim 8:15) he glosses as from the strong and mighty rock, and מֵֽחַלְמִישׁ צֽוּר (Devarim 32:13), in construct, as from the strength of the rocks. It is like תּוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי (Shemos 28:6), worm of scarlet, and וּשְׁנִי תוֹלַעַת (Vayikra 14:4), and scarlet of worm.

Since the word falls on nothing but a rock, the pasuk can use it with no rock named beside it: בַּֽחַלָּמִישׁ שָׁלַח יָדוֹ (Iyov 28:9), he puts forth his hand upon the strong rock, and שַׂמְתִּי פָנַי כַּֽחַלָּמִישׁ (Yeshayahu 50:7), I have set my face like the strong rock.

פשֹע.sense: To step, to stride; פֶּשַׂע, a step, meaning a small thing; and מִפְשָׂעָה, a covered name for the private parts.

more.t: אֶפְשֳׂעָה בָהּ (Yeshayahu 27:4) he glosses as I will stride in it, and כִּי כְפֶשַׂע בֵּינִי וּבֵין הַמָּֽוֶת (Shmuel I 20:3), for there is but a step between me and death, he takes as a pace, meaning a small thing. The usage is common in the words of Chazal (Shabbos 113b and Taanis 10b), who say that פסיעה גסה, a wide stride, takes away one five-hundredth of a man's eyesight.

The private parts are called by a covered name using this word: עַד־ הַמִּפְשָׂעָה (Divrei HaYamim I 19:4), up to the stride, as the pesukim also cover the same with רגלים, feet: וְלֹֽא־עָשָׂה רַגְלָיו (Shmuel II 19:25), and he had not dressed his feet, and אַךְ מֵסִיךְ הוּא אֶת־רַגְלָיו (Shoftim 3:24), he is only covering his feet.

פשׁע.sense: Rebellion, going out from under the authority of a master, or of whoever charged him with the matter.

more.t: מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב פָּשַׁע בִּי (Melachim II 3:7), the king of Moav has rebelled against me, and אָז תִּפְשַׁע לִבְנָה בָּעֵת הַהִֽיא (Melachim II 8:22), then Livnah rebelled at that time; so too וְהֵם פָּשְׁעוּ בִֽי (Yeshayahu 1:2), and they have rebelled against Me. אָח נִפְשָׁע מִקִּרְיַת־עֹז (Mishlei 18:19) means a brother rebelled against is harder than a strong city.

So too the Chachamim taught (Yoma 36b): עונות are the wilful sins, as it says הִכָּרֵת תִּכָּרֵת הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַהִוא עֲוֹנָה בָֽהּ (Bamidbar 15:31), that soul shall surely be cut off, its iniquity upon it; פשעים are the rebellions, as it says מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב פָּשַׁע בִּי, the king of Moav rebelled against me; and חטאים are the errors, as it says נֶפֶשׁ כִּי־תֶֽחֱטָא בִשְׁגָגָה (Vayikra 4:2), a soul that sins in error.

more.h: The bailee who is called a rebel
more.t: עַֽל־כָּל־דְּבַר־ פֶּשַׁע (Shemos 22:8), for every matter of rebellion, said of a deposit, means a bailee careless with the deposit, who did not guard it as guardians do. There is no rebellion here and he does not destroy it with his own hands, and still he is called a פושע, a rebel: once he does not put his eyes and his heart and his watching upon what was left with him, it is as though he rebels against the man who deposited it and goes out from under the command of the one who charged him to guard it, which he took upon himself and did not keep.

כְּהָתֵם הַפּֽשְׁעִים (Daniel 8:23), when the פשעים are complete: Rabbi Yonah wrote that the word is a noun, meaning, as Radak takes him, the punishments that had passed over them. Ibn Ezra reads it plainly, as those who do the deed, the rebels; on that reading the sense is that because the rebels of Yisrael were many, they were sold into the hand of the Greeks.

חטא.sense: To sin; to make another sin, or a stone miss. The offering for a sin is called חַטָּאת after it, and its service takes sin away; it can also mean sin's punishment.

more.t: אֶל־הַֽשַּׂעֲרָה וְלֹא יַחֲטִֽא (Shoftim 20:16), at a hair and not miss, which he explains as not making the stone miss.

וְֽחֹֽטְאִי חֹמֵס נַפְשׁוֹ (Mishlei 8:36), he who sins against me wrongs his own soul: וְֽחֹֽטְאִי is one who sins against me. שְׁאוֹל חָטָֽאוּ (Iyov 24:19) he reads as they sinned as far as the grave, that is, until they die. And וְהָיִיתִי אֲנִי וּבְנִי שְׁלֹמֹה חַטָּאִֽים (Melachim I 1:21), I and my son Shlomo will be offenders, he takes to mean that it will seem we are offenders before you, having nothing to do with the kingship. Some explain it as a word put for David out of respect, meaning that the sin would be David's.

פֶּן־ יַֽחֲטִיאוּ אֹֽתְךָ לִי (Shemos 23:33), lest they make you sin against Me, and אֲשֶׁר־ הֶֽחֱטִיא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim II 3:3), who made Yisrael sin. In another form, אָֽנֹכִי אֲחַטֶּנָּה (Bereishis 31:39), which he explains: the fault of it would be on me, and I would pay you its like.

וְחִטְּאוּ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ (Yechezkel 43:22) he explains as removing a man's sin through the service of the mizbe'ach, and הַכֹּהֵן הַֽמְחַטֵּא אֹתָהּ (Vayikra 6:19) is the kohen who performs its service, so that the offering is made by his hand and he removes a man's sin with it. In the same way הוּא יִתְחַטָּא ־בוֹ (Bamidbar 19:12), which Radak reads as removing his sin by its sprinkling.

more.h: Where the word is the punishment
more.t: זֹאת תִּֽהְיֶה חַטַּאת מִצְרָיִם (Zecharyah 14:19), this will be the חַטַּאת of Mitzrayim, he explains as the punishment of the sin they sinned; and in the same way כִּי לֹֽא־שָׁלֵם עֲוֹן הָֽאֱמֹרִי עַד־הֵֽנָּה (Bereishis 15:16), for the עֲוֹן of the Emori is not yet full, where it is the punishment of the iniquity.

עוה.sense: Twisting, the sense of every form: to be bent awry, to act perversely. עָוֹן is iniquity, and at times the punishment for iniquity.

more.t: The sense of all of them is עוות, twisting, and it is well known: נַֽעֲוֵיתִי שַׁחֹתִי עַד־מְאֹד (Tehillim 38:7), I am bent awry, I am bowed very low; וְנַֽעֲוֵה לב (Mishlei 12:8), one twisted of heart; אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱוָה עַבְדְּךָ (Shmuel II 19:20), what your servant did perversely; וְהֶֽעֱוִינוּ רָשָֽׁעְנוּ (Melachim I 8:47), we have done perversely, we have done wickedly; וְעִוָּה פָנֶיהָ (Yeshayahu 24:1), and He twists its face about. From this root and its first sense is also רוּחַ עִוְעִים (Yeshayahu 19:14), a spirit of distortion, with its first letter doubled.

more.h: Which root Vashti's word belongs to
more.t: עָוְתָה וַשְׁתִּי הַמַּלְכָּה (Esther 1:16), Vashti the queen has done wrong, many put under this root; his own view is that it belongs to עות. His father wrote it under עָוַת, together with נַֽעֲוַת הַמַּרְדּוּת (Shmuel I 20:30), perverse in rebellion, and מְעֻוָּת לֹֽא־יוּכַל לִתְקֹן (Koheles 1:15), what is twisted cannot be made straight.

more.h: Whether that word is male or female
more.t: נַֽעֲוַת המרדות may belong here, as a feminine form whose heh has turned into a tav because it is in construct; what compels Radak to this is that the word בֶּן, son, before it is pointed with a segol, as words in construct are, for so he found it. His father explained נַֽעֲוַת from the root עָוַת and called it a masculine form; Radak suggests his father may have found בֵּן pointed with a tzere.

The noun עָוֹן is on the pattern of גָּאוֹן, pride, from גָּאָה. Sometimes it is not the sin but its punishment: גָּדוֹל עֲוֹנִי מִנְּשֽׂוֹא (Bereishis 4:13), my punishment is greater than I can bear it and carry it, and כִּי לֹֽא־שָׁלֵם עֲוֹן הָֽאֱמֹרִי עַד־הֵֽנָּה (Bereishis 15:16), for the Emori's punishment is not yet complete, meaning that the time of the Emori's punishment, to drive them out of their land, had not come until the four hundred years were done. The Emori is named because he is the greatest of the seven nations. So too תְּֽנָה־ עָוֹן עַל־ עֲוֹנָם (Tehillim 69:28), lay punishment upon their iniquity.

לחץ.sense: To press, whether a people oppressed or a foot pressed against a wall; and the noun, oppression. All of it, he says, is the sense of pressure.

more.t: וְהוּא לָחַץ אֶת־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּחָזְקָה (Shoftim 4:3), and he oppressed Bnei Yisrael harshly; וְגֵר לֹא תִלְחָץ (Shemos 23:9), and you shall not oppress a stranger; מפני לֹֽחֲצֵיהֶם (Shoftim 2:18), because of their oppressors; and הַלֹּֽחֲצִים אֶתְכֶֽם (Shmuel I 10:18), those who oppress you.

וּלְחַצְתֶּם אֹתוֹ בַּדֶּלֶת (Melachim II 6:32), and press him back with the door; וַתִּלְחַץ אֶת־רֶגֶל בִּלְעָם (Bamidbar 22:25), and she pressed Bilaam's foot; and, in the same pasuk, וַתִּלָּחֵץ אֶל־הַקִּיר, and she pressed herself against the wall.
וְגַם־רָאִיתִי אֶת־הַלַּחַץ (Shemos 3:9), and I have also seen the oppression, and לֶחֶם צָר וּמַיִם לָחַץ (Yeshayahu 30:20), bread of straits and water of oppression.

דחק.sense: To press; the Targum's word for לָחַץ, oppressing, is דוֹחֲקָא, pressing.

more.t: וְאִישׁ אָחִיו לֹא יִדְחָקוּן (Yoel 2:8), and they do not press one another, and מִפְּנֵי לֹחֲצֵיהֶם וְדֹחֲקֵיהֶם (Shoftim 2:18), before their oppressors and those who pressed them; and the Targum renders לָחַץ (Melachim II 13:4), oppressing, as דוֹחֲקָא, pressing.

אלץ.sense: To press: וַתְּאַֽלֲצֵהוּ he explains as ותלחצהו, and she pressed him.

more.t: One line, on כָּל־הַיָּמִים וַתְּאַֽלֲצֵהוּ (Shoftim 16:16), all the days, and she pressed him, which he glosses ותלחצהו, she pressed him, noting that by rights the lamed takes a dagesh.

נקף.sense: Breaking and cutting: of a head cut off, of forest thickets cut down with iron, and of the cutting of an olive tree.

more.t: חַגִּים יִנְקֹֽפוּ (Yeshayahu 29:1), the festivals will be cut off, that is, their head will be cut off. The Targum renders וַֽעֲרַפְתּוֹ (Shemos 13:13), and you shall break its neck, with וּתְנַקְפֵיהּ, of this root, and הָֽעֲרוּפָה (Devarim 21:6), the one whose neck was broken, with דִנְקִיפָא.

וְנִשְׁאַר־בּוֹ עֽוֹלֵלֹת כְּנֹקֶף זַיִת (Yeshayahu 17:6), and gleanings will be left in it as at the cutting of an olive tree, and on another pattern וְתַחַת חֲגוֹרָה נִקְפָּה (Yeshayahu 3:24), and instead of a girdle, a rent.

וְנִקַּף סִֽבְכֵי הַיַּעַר בַּבַּרְזֶל (Yeshayahu 10:34), the thickets of the forest are cut down with iron, and וְאַחַר עוֹרִֽי נִקְּפוּ ־זֹאת (Iyov 19:26), and after my skin they have broken this, which he explains as the worms having broken and bored into this, the word this standing for the bone. All of them are the sense of breaking and cutting.

more.h: In the words of the Chachamim
more.t: Chazal speak of המנקף בראש הזית, one who cuts at the top of an olive tree, and they said (Chullin 7b) that a man does not so much as cut his finger below unless it has been declared of him above, and that the blood of such a cut is accepted like the blood of an olah.
וּמְצוּדוֹ עָלַי הִקִּֽיף (Iyov 19:6), and has closed His net around me, and כִּי הִקִּיפוּ יְמֵי הַמִּשְׁתֶּה (Iyov 1:5), when the days of the feast had gone round, are written under the root יָקַף.

כחשׁ.sense: To deny and to lie; by borrowing, of a crop that belies the hope of those who wait on it; and in another sense, to grow lean.

more.t: וְכִחֵשׁ בַּֽעֲמִיתוֹ (Vayikra 5:21), he deals falsely with his fellow; וַתְּכַחֵשׁ שָׂרָה (Bereishis 18:15), and Sarah denied it; אָלֹה וְכַחֵשׁ (Hoshea 4:2), swearing and lying. The adjective is בָּנִים כֶּֽחָשִׁים (Yeshayahu 30:9), sons who deal falsely, and the noun is in סְבָבֻנִי בְכַחַשׁ (Hoshea 12:1), they have ringed me round with falsehood, and וּבְכַֽחֲשֵׁיהֶם שָׂרִֽים (Hoshea 7:3), and the princes with their lies. All of them mean denial and falsehood.

כִּחֵשׁ מַֽעֲשֵׂה־זַיִת (Chavakuk 3:17), the work of the olive has lied, is a borrowed use: it belies the hope of those who wait on it. So too וְתִירוֹשׁ יְכַחֶשׁ בָּֽהּ (Hoshea 9:2), and the new wine will lie to her, that is, it will belie their hope. The last word is one of two where one would suppose בָּם and the Mesorah has it read בָּהּ.

In another sense the word means lean: וּבְשָׂרִי כָּחַשׁ מִשָּֽׁמֶן (Tehillim 109:24), my flesh has grown lean and lost its fat, and so Chazal speak of a בהמה כחושה, a lean animal (Bava Kamma 65b). The noun is וַיָּקָם בִּי כַֽחֲשִׁי (Iyov 16:8), my leanness rises up against me; and וְיִכָּֽחֲשׁוּ אֹֽיְבֶיךָ לָךְ (Devarim 33:29) means your enemies will be lean and poor and humbled before you.

more.h: Strangers who submit, or who deny
more.t: בְּנֵי נֵכָר יִתְכַּֽחֲשׁוּ ־לִי (Shmuel II 22:45) he leaves open between the two senses. It may belong with the lean and the humbled, strangers who grow lean and submit before me; or it may be from the first sense, as he wrote above, that out of great dread they will deny what they did and the evil they did, and say they never did it.

נקב.sense: To bore and pierce; מַקֶּבֶת is the hammer that bores, and נְקֵבָה, female, derives from this sense. In another sense, to name, and to spell out the Name and curse.

more.t: וּבָא בְכַפּוֹ וּנְקָבָהּ (Yeshayahu 36:6), and it goes into his palm and pierces it; אֶל־צְרוֹר נָקֽוּב (Chaggai 1:6), into a bag with a hole in it; וַיִּקֹּב חֹר (Melachim II 12:10), and he bored a hole; בְּמֽוֹקְשִׁים יִנְקָב ־אָֽף (Iyov 40:24), with snares his nose is pierced.

וְאֶל־ מַקֶּבֶת בּוֹר (Yeshayahu 51:1), and to the bored pit, is the pit you were quarried from. The tool with which stones are dressed and bored is likewise called מקבת: a hammer with one end sharp for boring and dressing, while with the other end they strike and pound, in work of iron and copper and the like. וַתָּשֶׂם אֶת־ הַמַּקֶּבֶת בְּיָדָהּ (Shoftim 4:21), and she put the hammer in her hand; וּמַקָּבוֹת וְהַגַּרְזֶן (Melachim I 6:7), hammers and the axe; וּבְמַקָּבוֹת יְחַזְּקוּם (Yirmiyahu 10:4), and with hammers they fasten them.
From this sense of piercing he derives זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה (Bereishis 1:27), male and female.

The other sense: נָקְבָה שְׂכָֽרְךָ עָלַי (Bereishis 30:28), name your wage to me; נְקֻבֵי רֵאשִׁית הַגּוֹיִם (Amos 6:1), those named first of the nations; אֲשֶׁר פִּי י"י יִקֳּבֶֽנּוּ (Yeshayahu 62:2), which the mouth of Hashem will name. וַיִּקֹּב בֶּן־הָֽאִשָּׁה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית (Vayikra 24:11), and the son of the Yisraelite woman spelled out, means that he spelled out the Name in its letters and cursed; and together with the sense of cursing, וְנֹקֵב שֵׁם (Vayikra 24:16), one who spells out the Name, means one who spells it out and curses, for he is not liable until he spells it out and curses. And יִקְּבֻהוּ אֹֽרְרֵי־יוֹם (Iyov 3:8), let those who curse the day curse it; יִקְּבֻהוּ לְאוֹם (Mishlei 11:26), the people curse him; and וָֽאֶקּוֹב נָוֵהוּ פִתְאֹֽם (Iyov 5:3), and I cursed his dwelling suddenly.

פטשׁ.sense: A big hammer: the large מקבת.

more.t: וּכְפַטִּישׁ יְפֹצֵֽץ סָֽלַע (Yirmiyahu 23:29), and like a hammer that shatters rock: it is the large מקבת, the big hammer.

ארג.sense: To weave; and the noun אֶרֶג, the weaver's implement.

more.t: אִם־תַּאַרְגִי אֶת־שֶׁבַע מַחְלְפוֹת רֹאשִׁי (Shoftim 16:13), if you weave the seven locks of my head, and מַעֲשֵׂה אֹרֵג (Shemos 28:32), the work of a weaver. The sense, he says, is known.

אֶת־הַיְתַד הָאֶרֶג (Shoftim 16:14), the pin of the אֶרֶג, names the implement on which the weaver folds the cloth before him as he weaves. The two words stand as a construct with the governing noun left out, the pin, the pin of the implement; or else as a construct that keeps the definite article, as in הַלִּשְׁכוֹת הַקֹּדֶשׁ (Yechezkel 46:19), the chambers of the holy. So Yonasan renders it, as the weavers' implement, and he renders כִּמְנוֹר אֹרְגִים (Shmuel II 21:19), like a weavers' beam, the same way.

יָמַי קַלּוּ מִנִּי־אָרֶג (Iyov 7:6), my days are swifter than the אָרֶג. That is the implement that carries the weft thread, and the comparison holds because the weaver drives it at a run from one edge of the cloth to the other.

סגל.sense: The setting apart of silver and gold and precious stones in a treasury.

more.t: וִהְיִיתֶם לִי סְגֻלָּה (Shemos 19:5), and you shall be to Me a treasure set apart, and וּסְגֻלַּת מְלָכִים (Koheles 2:8), and the set-apart treasure of kings. The sense, he says, is the setting apart of silver and gold and precious stones in a treasury.

ים.sense: The sea; and the west, called so because the Great Sea lies west of Eretz Yisrael. Another sense of the root: הַיֵּמִם, the mules.

more.t: כַּמַּיִם לַיָּם מְכַסִּים (Yeshayahu 11:9), as the waters cover the sea, with the plural יַמִּים, seas (Bereishis 1:10). Because the Great Sea lies to the west of Eretz Yisrael, the west itself is called by the word: יָם וְדָרוֹם יְרָשָׁה (Devarim 33:23), possess the west and the south.

The word is sometimes referred to in the feminine: וְאֶת־הַיָּם הוֹרִד מֵעַל הַבָּקָר הַנְּחֹשֶׁת אֲשֶׁר תַּחְתֶּיהָ (Melachim II 16:17), he took the sea down off the brazen oxen that were beneath it, where the word for beneath it is a feminine one.

The root may be יָמַם, the doubled letter in the suffixed and plural forms proving it; or it may be יוֹם, the doubling standing in place of the quiescent letter, the proof there being the kamatz, since every one of them has a kamatz save יַם סוּף, the Yam Suf. He does not decide between them.

more.h: The mules found in the wilderness
more.t: אֲשֶׁר מָצָא אֶת־ הַיֵּמִם בַּמִּדְבָּר (Bereishis 36:24), who found the yemim in the wilderness: these are the mules, bred of two kinds, the horse and the donkey. אֲשֶׁר מָצָא, who found, means he found it while herding: he was herding the donkeys, and it came into his mind to breed the horse on the she-donkey, and he brought this kind into the world. Chazal (Pesachim 54a) say Anah was himself of invalid birth and brought invalid creatures into the world; the reason given is that he was the son of Tzivon, his own brother, who came upon his mother and fathered Anah by her.

דרם.sense: The south: it is התימן, Teiman, and it is הנגב, Negev, for it is called by these names.

more.t: וְדָרוֹם יְרָשָׁה (Devarim 33:23), possess the south. It is התימן, Teiman, and it is הנגב, Negev, for it is called by these names.

ימן.sense: The right hand and the right side; since a man's strength is on his right, strength; and the south, which is on a man's right when he faces east.

more.t: אִם־הַשְּׂמֹאל וְאֵימִנָה (Bereishis 13:9), if you go left I will go to the right side. The adjective names the right of a thing: וּפְנֵי אַרְיֵה אֶל־הַיָּמִין (Yechezkel 1:10), the lion's face to the right; יַד־יְמִינוֹ (Bereishis 48:17), the hand of his right side; עַל יֶרֶךְ יְמִינוֹ (Shoftim 3:16), on the thigh of his right side. The hand is at times spoken of in the masculine, as in וְהִנֵּה־יָד שְׁלוּחָה אֵלָי וְהִנֵּה־בוֹ מְגִלַּת־סֵֽפֶר (Yechezkel 2:9), and behold, a hand sent out to me, and behold, in it a scroll of a book, and so נִצָּב יְמִינוֹ כְּצָר (Eichah 2:4), His right hand stood as a foe; or that is the hand of his right side.

Since a man's strength is in his right side, the word stands for strength: וִימִינָם יְמִין שָׁקֶר (Tehillim 144:11), their strength and their might is a lie. Rabbi Adonim took it for an oath instead, from the Arabic, since the pasuk has already said אשר פיהם דבר שוא, whose mouth speaks falsehood, so that the second half runs: and their oath is a false oath.

אֶת־אֶצְבָּעוֹ הַיְמָנִית (Vayikra 14:16), his right finger, and וְעַל־בֹּהֶן יָדוֹ הַיְמָנִית (Vayikra 14:14), on the thumb of his right hand, come with kamatz under the mem. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the kamatz keeps the word apart from the one that belongs to the tribe of Binyamin, אִישׁ יְמִינִי (Esther 2:5), a Binyaminite. Rabbi Yehudah wrote the same; and שמאלי, left, was treated the same way, with kamatz under the mem, the one standing opposite the other, though שמאלי needs no such parting. Radak says they wrote well.

The Mishnah (Parah 1:1) parts two meanings of one word the same way. Rabbi Yehoshua said he had heard only שלשית, and when asked what the word meant, said he had heard it so and no more. Ben Azzai explained: said one way, שלשית is שלישית, third to the others in a count; said the other way, it is three years old. So with כרם רבעי, a vineyard of the fourth: רביעי is fourth to the others in a count, and רבעי is of four years.

וְאָבִיו קָרָא־לוֹ בִנְיָמִין (Bereishis 35:18), and his father called him Binyamin, he reads as בן ימין, son of the right. The right is more honoured and beloved to a man than the left, and the youngest of the sons is the dearest, so the name says: my son who is dear and honoured to me. His tribesmen are called after him with the full name, בֶּן־יְמִינִי (Shmuel I 9:21), a Binyaminite, and with ימין alone, אִישׁ יְמִינִי (Shmuel I 9:2 in his edition), a man of Binyamin.

The south quarter is called יָמִין because it is on a man's right when his face is to the east, the east being called פנים, the front, as the west is called אחור, the back: צָפוֹן וְיָמִין אַתָּה בְרָאתָם (Tehillim 89:13), north and south, You created them. With a tav added it is תימן: אֱלוֹהַּ מִתֵּימָן יָבוֹא (Chavakuk 3:3), Hashem will come from the south. The south is also called נֶגֶב, and the two are set side by side in נֶגְבָּה תֵימָנָה (Shemos 26:18), to the south, southward, though both are one, as in אַדְמַת־עָפָר (Daniel 12:2), earth of dust; or else the second is there for plainness, תֵימָנָה being the clearer of the two.

דגן.sense: The name of wheat, barley, or another of the five kinds, once it has been smoothed.

more.h: Wheat, barley, or another of the five
more.t: דָּגָן תִּירוֹשׁ וְיִצְהָר (Devarim 28:51), grain, wine and oil, and וְאָֽסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ (Devarim 11:14), and you shall gather in your grain. It is the name of the wheat or the barley or another of the five kinds, after it has been smoothed.

זון.sense: To feed: זַן are the kinds that feed a man, מָזוֹן is food, and Rachav הַזּוֹנָה a seller of food. Rabbi Yonah takes זַן as a kind.

more.h: The kinds that feed a man
more.t: מְפִיקִים מִזַּן אֶל־זַן (Tehillim 144:13), yielding from זַן to זַן: זַן describes the kinds that feed, the wheat and the barley and the sorts of pulse and the like, which feed a man. The Mishnah uses the verb so (Kesubos 101b), of one who marries a woman and undertakes with her to feed her daughter three years; and besides this they use the verb much. The noun is בָּר וָלֶחֶם וּמָזוֹן (Bereishis 45:23), grain and bread and food.

רָחָב הַזּוֹנָה (Yehoshua 6:25), Rachav the זוֹנָה, he takes as an adjective on the pattern of טוֹבָה, and its sense is one who sells food; and so Targum Yonasan renders it, פּוּנְדְקִיתָא, an innkeeper. Rabbi Yonah read וַיִּתְּנוּ הַיֶּלֶד בַּזּוֹנָה (Yoel 4:3), and they gave a boy for a זוֹנָה, the same way; and it may be, Radak adds, from זנה, of the sense of harlotry.

Rabbi Yonah read מזן אל זן as from one kind to another, taking it from the Targum of לְמִינוֹ (Bereishis 1:11), after its kind, which is לִזְנֵיהּ. So too, on that reading, בְּשָׂמִים וּזְנִים מְרֻקָּחִים (Divrei HaYamim II 16:14), spices and kinds compounded; but Radak holds the sounder grammar to make וזנים there a word of the roots whose last letter is weak, on the pattern of מְתִים.

In another sense, וְיָתֵד תִּהְיֶה לְךָ עַל־אֲזֵנֶךָ (Devarim 23:14), and you shall have a peg upon your weapon: the alef is added, and it is a kind of weapon, what Chazal call כלי זין. וְהַזֹּנוֹת רָחָצוּ (Melachim I 22:38), and the זֹנוֹת washed, goes on the pattern of קוֹמוֹת and קוֹמָה, of the roots whose middle letter is weak; he joins it to אֲזֵנֶךָ with וכן, likewise, but gives it no gloss of its own.

נוב.sense: Fruit and herbage coming out and growing; likewise wealth increasing, and speech, which is the fruit of the tongue.

more.t: חַיִל כִּי יָנוּב (Tehillim 62:11), when wealth increases, and עוֹד יְנוּבוּן (Tehillim 92:15), they will still bear fruit in old age. The noun is מִתְּנוּבֹת שָׂדָֽי (Eichah 4:9), from the yield of the field, and the sense of them all is fruit and herbage coming out and growing. The word is used likewise of the increase of wealth and delight and good, which is like the growth of plants, going on and growing, as in חַיִל כִּי יָנוּב and עוֹד יְנוּבוּן.

פִּֽי־צַדִּיק יָנוּב חָכְמָה (Mishlei 10:31), the mouth of a tzaddik brings forth wisdom: the word is used likewise of speech, which is the fruit of the tongue. The noun is ניב שפתים (Yeshayahu 57:19), the speech of the lips, and וְנִיבוֹ נִבְזֶה אָכְלֽוֹ (Malachi 1:12), its speech, its food, is despised.

more.h: What the new wine does to the young
more.t: וְתִירוֹשׁ יְנוֹבֵב בְּתֻלֽוֹת (Zecharyah 9:17), and new wine יְנוֹבֵב the maidens, can be read from growing, as his father explains it: כִּי מַה־טּוּבוֹ וּמַה־יָפְיוֹ, how great is its goodness and its beauty, is how good the grain and the wine that make those young men and those maidens grow, when they ask rain of Hashem and He gives grass in the field to every man (Zecharyah 10:1); so from Hashem's help and from the plenty of grain and wine the young men and maidens are fair and strong. In the four-letter form, a verb that passes on to a third, it is read otherwise: the grain and the wine gladden the young men and the maidens and make them bring forth songs and melodies, that is, they will eat and drink and rejoice on the day of that deliverance.

זוז.sense: מְזוּזָה, the doorpost; doorposts, he says, are the cheeks of the gateways. Its mem is added and its final heh marks the feminine.

more.t: In מְזוּזָה the mem is an addition and the final heh is the feminine ending: וּמְזוּזָתָם אֵצֶל מְזוּזָתִי (Yechezkel 43:8), their doorpost beside My doorpost, and in the plural וּכְתַבְתָּם עַל־מְזֻזוֹת בֵּיתֶךָ (Devarim 6:9), you shall write them on the doorposts of your house. They are the cheeks of the gateways.

more.h: At the post, or on the sill
more.t: וְעָמַד עַל־מְזוּזַת הַשַּׁעַר (Yechezkel 46:2), and he shall stand by the doorpost of the gate, means next to the doorpost of the gate. But Targum Yonasan renders it as a threshold, ויקום על סקיפת תרעא, and he shall stand on the sill of the gate. So too עַל־מְזוּזַת הֵיכַל י"י (Shmuel I 1:9), by the doorpost of the Heichal of Hashem, means next to the doorpost of the gate; and so Targum Yonasan renders it, בִּסְטַר סִיפָא דְהֵיכְלָא דַיְיָ, at the side of the threshold of the Heichal of Hashem.

כסף.sense: To desire and long for, ענין תאוה וחשק; and כֶּסֶף, silver, which he calls known.

more.t: כְּאַרְיֵה יִכְסוֹף לִטְרוֹף (Tehillim 17:12), like a lion longing to tear, and לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיךָ תִכְסֹף (Iyov 14:15), You will long for the work of Your hands. So נִכְסְפָה וְגַם־כָּלְתָה נַפְשִׁי (Tehillim 84:3), my soul longed and pined, and כִּי־נִכְסֹף נִכְסַפְתָּה לְבֵית אָבִיךָ (Bereishis 31:30), you longed sorely for your father's house. Their sense is desire and longing.

הַגּוֹי לֹא נִכְסָף (Tzefaniah 2:1) he puts with the rest, a nation that does not long. His father reads it otherwise, a nation that has no shame in it, from the word the Gemara uses (Bava Basra 111a) for a man ashamed.

זָהָב וָכֶסֶף (Shemos 25:3), gold and silver, and the plural כספים in וּלְהָשִׁיב כַּסְפֵּיהֶם אִישׁ אֶל־שַׂקּוֹ (Bereishis 42:25), to put back each man's money into his sack. The sense, he says, is known.

מכר.sense: To sell, and to be sold; also of one who sells himself to do evil. The nouns מֶכֶר and מִמְכָּר are the thing sold.

more.t: כִּי־מָכְרוּ מִצְרַיִם (Bereishis 47:20), for the Egyptians sold; וְכִי־יִמְכֹּר אִישׁ (Shemos 21:7), if a man sells; וַיִּמְכְּרֵם בְּיַד כּוּשַׁן רִשְׁעָתַיִם (Shoftim 3:8), He sold them into the hand of Kushan Rishasayim; מִכְרָה כַיּוֹם (Bereishis 25:31), sell, this very day. Of being sold: הֵן בַּעֲוֹנֹתֵיכֶם נִמְכַּרְתֶּם (Yeshayahu 50:1), behold, for your sins you were sold, and כִּי נִמְכַּרְנוּ אֲנִי וְעַמִּי (Esther 7:4), for we are sold, I and my people.

אֲשֶׁר הִתְמַכֵּר לַעֲשׂוֹת הָרַע (Melachim I 21:25), who sold himself to do evil, and הִתְמַכֶּרְךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת הָרַע (Melachim I 21:20), your selling yourself to do evil, are still the sense of selling: from how greatly he exerted himself at the work of sins, it is as though he had sold himself to that work. So also וְהִתְמַכַּרְתֶּם שָׁם לְאֹיְבֶיךָ (Devarim 28:68), and there you will put yourselves up for sale to your enemies.

לְבַד מִמְכָּרָיו עַל־הָאָבוֹת (Devarim 18:8), apart from his sales by the fathers, means apart from what the fathers sold one to another in the days of David and Shmuel, when the watches were fixed and they traded among themselves: you take your week and I will take mine.

In כְּלֵי חָמָס מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶם (Bereishis 49:5), instruments of violence, the last word has been explained as their dwellings, as though it were מגורותיהם, like מְכֹרֹתַיִךְ וּמֹלְדֹתַיִךְ (Yechezkel 16:3), your dwellings and your births, and like בְּאֶרֶץ מְכֻרוֹתַיִךְ (Yechezkel 21:35), in the land of your dwellings. The Targum goes that way: בַּאֲרַע תּוֹתָבוּתְכוֹן אֶתְפְּרַע מִנְכוֹן, in the land of your dwelling I will exact retribution from you. Yelamdenu, on Vayechi, says instead that in this phrase the word is Greek, for they call swords מכיר"י.

רוח.sense: Relief, the opposite of distress. And רוּחַ: spirit, of prophecy or an angel; will; air; the wind, and from it a side; the soul; and breath.

more.t: וְרָוַח לְשָׁאוּל (Shmuel I 16:23), and Shaul had relief, and אֲדַבְּרָה וְיִרְוַח לִי (Iyov 32:20), let me speak and find relief. The noun is רֶוַח וְהַצָּלָה (Esther 4:14), relief and rescue, and וְרֶוַח תָּשִׂימוּ (Bereishis 32:17), and you shall put a space; another form is כִּי הָיְתָה הָרְוָחָה (Shemos 8:11), that there was respite, and לְרַוְחָתִי לְשַׁוְעָתִי (Eichah 3:56), for my relief, to my cry, which he explains: do not hide Your ear from my cry, that I cry to You for my relief. In the heavy form, וַעֲלִיּוֹת מְרֻוָּחִים (Yirmiyahu 22:14), and spacious upper rooms. The sense, he says, is known: it is the opposite of distress.

more.h: At the רוּחַ of the day
more.t: Rabbi Yonah wrote לְרוּחַ הַיּוֹם (Bereishis 3:8), at the רוּחַ of the day, from this sense, which Radak explains: at the time of the day's רוח, that is, the coolness of its air. It may also be read from the wind that blows, in its plain sense: at the turn of the day, when the wind blows; and מתהלך, going about, in the pasuk then goes back to the wind or to the voice, as in קוֹלָהּ כַּנָּחָשׁ יֵלֵךְ (Yirmiyahu 46:22), her voice goes like a serpent.

more.h: Wind, and what is winnowed by it
more.t: It is air: וְרוּחַ לֹא יָבוֹא בֵינֵיהֶם (Iyov 41:8), and air shall not come between them. It is the wind that blows: וְרוּחַ גְּדוֹלָה וְחָזָק (Melachim I 19:11), a great and strong wind, and רוּחַ קָדִים (Shemos 10:13), an east wind. From this comes אֲשֶׁר זֹרֶה בָרַחַת (Yeshayahu 30:24), winnowed with the רַחַת, the tool grain is winnowed with, because it is waved into the wind. Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar wrote וְהוֹרַדְתִּי בָרִיחִים כֻּלָּם (Yeshayahu 43:14), and I will bring them all down בריחים, from this sense: they are ships, called so because they go by the wind; and so Yonasan renders it, וְאַחֲתֵית בִּמְשׁוֹטִין כּוּלְהוֹן, and I brought them all down with oars. וַעֲלִיּוֹת מְרֻוָּחִים (Yirmiyahu 22:14) may also be read from this: upper rooms the wind enters, made for the days of summer, which is why it says וְקָרַע לוֹ חַלּוֹנָי, and he cuts him out windows.

more.h: The four winds and the four sides
more.t: והבאתי אל עילם ארבע רוּחוֹת (Yirmiyahu 49:36), and I will bring four winds upon Eilam, is explained as four kingdoms: the navi likens them to wind, as a strong wind wrecks and breaks the high cedars, and he means truly four, since evil will come on them from every side and every corner. From this sense a side is called רוּחַ, there being four winds to the four sides: מָדַד רוּחַ הַצָּפוֹן (Yechezkel 42:17), he measured the north side, and לְאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת מְדָדוֹ (Yechezkel 42:20), he measured it on the four sides. Some explain from this סוֹבֵב סֹבֵב הוֹלֵךְ הָרוּחַ (Koheles 1:6), round and round goes the רוּחַ, as said of the sun, which circles and goes along the side.

Another sense: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר הָיָה בָרוּחַ עִמּוֹ (Divrei HaYamim I 28:12), all that was in the spirit with him, and וְרוּחֲךָ הַטּוֹבָה נָתַתָּ לְהַשְׂכִּילָם (Nechemiah 9:20), You gave Your good spirit to instruct them. וַיֵּצֵא הָרוּחַ וַיַּעֲמֹד (Melachim I 22:21), the spirit went out and stood, is the spirit of prophecy or an angel; so וְסוּסֵיהֶם בָּשָׂר וְלֹא רוּחַ (Yeshayahu 31:3), their horses are flesh and not spirit, means not an angel, since an angel is a thing of spirit; and so שְׁלָחַנִי וְרוּחוֹ (Yeshayahu 48:16), He has sent me, and His spirit, means and His angel.

It is will: וְרוּחַ לָבְשָׁה אֶת עֲמָשַׂי (Divrei HaYamim I 12:19), a spirit clothed Amasai, is the spirit of will and desire; so עֵקֶב הָיְתָה רוּחַ אַחֶרֶת עִמּוֹ (Bamidbar 14:24), because another spirit was with him, and עַד יֵעָרֶה עָלֵינוּ רוּחַ מִמָּרוֹם (Yeshayahu 32:15), until a spirit is poured upon us from on high, the will of the Creator. It is the soul: וְהָרוּחַ תָּשׁוּב אֶל הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר נְתָנָהּ (Koheles 12:7), and the spirit returns to Hashem who gave it, the name being given sometimes to each of the three souls and sometimes to the neshamah, the highest, alone; or to the one seated in the heart, which is where anger lives, so it says אַל תְּבַהֵל בְּרוּחֲךָ לִכְעוֹס (Koheles 7:9), do not be hasty in your spirit to anger; and כָּל רוּחוֹ יוֹצִיא כְסִיל (Mishlei 29:11), a fool lets out all his spirit, that is, all his will. It is also said of breathing: רוּחִי זָרָה לְאִשְׁתִּי (Iyov 19:17), my breath is strange to my wife; and וּבְרוּחַ שְׂפָתָיו יָמִית רָשָׁע (Yeshayahu 11:4), with the breath of his lips he will slay the wicked, is by the speech of his lips, since speech leaves the mouth with breath and vapour. His father explained וַהֲרִיחוֹ בְּיִרְאַת (Yeshayahu 11:3) from this sense: his speech will be in the fear of Hashem; and likewise לְרַוְחָתִי לְשַׁוְעָתִי (Eichah 3:56): do not hide Your ear from my words and from my cry. Radak himself explains that pasuk from relief.

לקק.sense: To lick: the dogs that licked, and whoever licks water with his tongue. Its sense, he says, is that of licking, and it is well known.

more.t: Beside the dogs stands הַמֲלַקְקִים בְּיָדָם אֶל־פִּיהֶם (Shoftim 7:6), those who licked with their hand to their mouth.

רעל.sense: רַעַל and תַּרְעֵלָה: bewilderment and tumult to Rabbi Yonah, trembling to Radak's father, and deadly poison as it is usually explained. Some read הָרְעָלוֹת as veils.

more.t: סַף־רַעַל (Zechariah 12:2), a cup of ra'al; with a tav and a hei added, הִשְׁקִיתָנוּ יַיִן תַּרְעֵלָה (Tehillim 60:5), You gave us wine of tar'elah to drink, and כּוֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָה (Yeshayahu 51:17), the cup of tar'elah; and in the passive, וְהַבְּרושִׁים הָרְעָלוּ (Nachum 2:4), and the cypresses were hor'alu. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the sense of all of it is bewilderment and tumult. Radak's father wrote that תַּרְעֵלָה and הָרְעָלוּ are a word for trembling. The line after it, ואנו רגילים לפרש סם המות, we are accustomed to explain it as deadly poison, is not marked as the father's or as Radak's own.

In another sense, וְהַשֵּׁירוֹת וְהָרְעָלוֹת (Yeshayahu 3:19), and the sheiros and the re'alos. Some explain it by a word in la'az. Some explain it from the Mishnah (Shabbos 6:6, 65a), ערביות יוצאות רעולות, Arab women go out veiled, which the Geonim explained as the re'alos of the pasuk, giving the word's name in Arabic. On this reading, its meaning is that they set a scarf over the head and cover the whole face, so that nothing shows but the eyes, and it is tied below.

Yonasan renders וְהַבְּרושִׁים הָרְעָלוּ as וְרַבָּנֵי מַשִׁרְיָתְהוֹן מְסַרְבְּלִין בְּצִבְעוֹנִין, and the chiefs of their camps are clothed in dyed colours. For וְהָרְעָלוֹת he gives חֲנִיסְנְסַיָא, as he renders וְהָחַמָּנִים (Yeshayahu 17:8); the entry does not say what either word means.

עכס.sense: The anklet, a rattling ornament that women wear on their feet; and the fetter, called by the same word because it rattles too.

more.t: אֵת תִּפְאֶרֶת הָֽעֲכָסִים (Yeshayahu 3:18), the splendour of the anklets; and the verb, וּבְרַגְלֵיהֶם תְּעַכַּֽסְנָה (Yeshayahu 3:16), and with their feet they rattle, that is, they rattle the anklets on their feet. The עכס is a rattling ornament that women wear on their feet.
Because it rattles in the same way, the shackle is called עכס: וּכְעֶכֶס אֶל־מוּסַר אֱוִיל (Mishlei 7:22), like a fetter to the chastening of a fool.

כהן.sense: Service in greatness, as the kohanim served Hashem and headed the people. Any servant is called so, even of avodah zarah, and so are a king's counsellor and chief men.

more.h: Not Aharon's sons but the firstborn
more.t: הַכֹּהֲנִים הַנִּגָּשִׁים (Shemos 19:22), the kohanim who draw near, he reads of the firstborn, since the service then was with the firstborn of Israel; anyone who serves is called a kohen.

One who serves avodah zarah carries the same word: כֹהֵן מִדְיָן (Shemos 18:1), the priest of Midyan, and רַק אַדְמַת הַכֹּהֲנִים לֹא קָנָה (Bereishis 47:22), only the land of the priests he did not buy.

הָיָה כֹהֵן לְדָוִד (Shmuel II 20:25 in his edition), was a kohen to David, is his servant and counsellor, heeded before all the rest, for a faithful beloved serves the one who loves him with sound counsel. So too אַתָּה כֹהֵן לְעוֹלָם (Tehillim 110:4), you are a kohen forever, meaning a servant of Hashem and head of Israel, because you are a king of righteousness, as the kohen is head of the people.

It is also the chief men: וּמְיֻדָּעָיו וְכֹהֲנָיו (Melachim II 10:11), his intimates and his chiefs, מוֹלִיךְ כֹּהֲנִים שׁוֹלָל (Iyov 12:19), leading chiefs away stripped, and חֶבֶר כֹּהֲנִים (Hoshea 6:9), a band of chiefs. יְכַהֵן פְּאֵר (Yeshayahu 61:10) means that he makes his splendour great with fine garments.

וּבְנֵי דָוִד כֹּהֲנִים הָיוּ (Shmuel II 8:18), and David's sons were כהנים, is of the same kind, and so Divrei HaYamim says in its place, וּבְנֵי דָוִיד הָרִאשֹׁנִים לְיַד הַמֶּלֶךְ (Divrei HaYamim 18:17, as his edition prints it), and David's sons were first at the king's hand. Or it means that they were servants of Hashem and fearers of Him. Yonasan renders רַבְרְבִין הֲווֹ, they were great men. Radak holds the first reading the true one because of what Divrei HaYamim has in its place.

כמר.sense: Of mercy, to be stirred and rolled about, or to grow hot; close to it, blackened, and from this the כְּמָרִים, servants of avodah zarah in black; and a net.

more.t: כִּי נִכְמְרוּ רַחֲמָיו אֶל־אָחִיו (Bereishis 43:30), for his mercy was stirred toward his brother, and יַחַד נִכְמְרוּ נִחוּמָי (Hoshea 11:8), my compassion is stirred all together. The word means rolled about and stirred, as its Targum has it, or else grown hot; and close to its sense is עוֹרֵנוּ כְּתַנּוּר נִכְמָרוּ (Eichah 5:10), which means our skin was blackened like an oven.

From this the הכומרים, the kmarim, are named: וְהִשְׁבִּית אֶת־הַכְּמָרִים (Melachim II 23:5), and he did away with the kmarim, and וּכְמָרָיו עָלָיו יָגִילוּ (Hoshea 10:5), and its kmarim rejoice over it. The Targum renders רַק אַדְמַת הַכֹּהֲנִים (Bereishis 47:26), only the land of the priests, as לְחוֹד אַרְעָא דְכֻמָּרַיָּא, only the land of the kumraya; and they are servants of avodah zarah who dress in black. In אֶת־שֵׁם הַכְּמָרִים עִם־הַכֹּהֲנִים (Tzefaniah 1:4), the name of the kmarim with the kohanim, the kohanim are the rest of the servants of avodah zarah, those not dressed in black.

In another sense, כְּתוֹא מִכְמָר (Yeshayahu 51:20), which he reads כתוא במכמר, like the creature called "to" in a net. Its other forms are יִפְּלוּ בְמַכְמֹרָיו רְשָׁעִים (Tehillim 141:10), let the wicked fall into his nets, וּפֹרְשֵׂי מִכְמֹרֶת (Yeshayahu 19:8), those who spread a net, and וְיַאַסְפֵהוּ בְּמִכְמַרְתּוֹ (Chavakuk 1:15), he gathers him in his net. They are the nets men hunt with.

צבר.sense: To heap up, as silver like dust, or grain; and the noun, a heap. All of it, he says, is the sense of gathering.

more.t: אִם־יִצְבֹּר כֶּעָפָר כָּסֶף (Iyov 27:16), if he heaps up silver like dust; וַיִּצְבְּרוּ אֹתָם חֳמָרִם חֳמָרִם (Shemos 8:10), and they heaped them up in heaps upon heaps; and וְיִצְבְּרוּ־בָר (Bereishis 41:35), and let them heap up grain.

וַיִּצְבֹּר עָפָר וַיִּלְכְּדָהּ (Chavakuk 1:10), and he heaps up dust and takes it: that is, the pouring out of a siege ramp, as he explains at the root סָלַל; or it means that he heaped up a people like dust and took it.
שִׂימוּ אֹתָם שְׁנֵי צִבֻּרִים (Melachim II 10:8), set them in two heaps. All of these, he says, are the sense of gathering.

פרס.sense: To break into pieces with the hands, as bread for the hungry; to spread the hands in mourning; the hoof, פַּרְסָה; and the פֶּרֶס, a large bird of the wilderness.

more.t: הֲלוֹא פָרֹס לָֽרָעֵב לַחְמֶךָ (Yeshayahu 58:7), is it not to break your bread for the hungry; and so פֹּרֵשׂ אֵין לָהֶֽם (Eichah 4:4), none breaks bread for them, and וּפָֽרְשׂוּ כַּֽאֲשֶׁר בַּסִּיר (Michah 3:3), and they break them up as in the pot: though written with a sin, their sense is breaking into pieces with the hands. Like it in the words of Chazal (Demai 5:5) is הנותן פרוסה לעני, one who gives a broken piece to a poor man. The Mesorah counts every such word with a sin but for two written with a samech, הֲלוֹא פָרֹס לָֽרָעֵב לַחְמֶךָ and וְלֹא יִפְרְסוּ לָהֶם, and they shall not break for them.

The word is used too of spreading out the hands and the body in mourning out of great grief: תִּתְיַפֵּחַ תְּפָרֵשׂ כַּפֶּיהָ (Yirmiyahu 4:31), she gasps, she spreads out her hands, and פֵּרְשָׂה צִיּוֹן בְּיָדֶיהָ (Eichah 1:17), Tzion spread out her hands; these too are written with a sin.

וְלֹא יִפְרְסוּ לָהֶם עַל־אֵבֶל (Yirmiyahu 16:7), they shall not break for them over mourning, he reads as that none will come to comfort him over the dead: none will lament the dead and none comfort the living. The commentators read it of the mourner's meal, where bread is broken and cut for him, and that is לנחמו על מת, to comfort him over the dead. His father reads פֵּרְשָׂה צִיּוֹן, Tzion broke bread, the same way: comforters break bread for a mourner, and she broke it with her own hands, having no comforter.

כֹּל מַפְרֶסֶת פַּרְסָה (Vayikra 11:3) means one that has two hooves, and וְשֹׁסַעַת שֶׁסַע, and cleaves a cleft, is further explained as hooves split below as they are above; for there is an animal whose hooves are split above and joined below, like the camel, the bear, the dog and the cat. The noun comes also in the masculine, וּפַרְסֵיהֶן יְפָרֵק (Zecharyah 11:16), he will tear off their hooves.

וְאֶת־הַפֶּרֶס (Vayikra 11:13), and the peres, is a large bird that dwells in the wilderness, as Chazal say (Chullin 62a), the peres and the ozniah are not commonly found in settled places. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the Arabic name for it is עקא"ב.

רגם.sense: To stone. מַרְגֵּמָה is a gathering of stones, or, as his father reads it, purple; רִגְמָתָם is their assembly, or, some say, their princes.

more.t: וְרָֽגְמוּ אֹתוֹ כָּל־הָֽעֵדָֽה (Vayikra 24:14), the whole congregation shall stone him, and יִרְגְּמֻהוּ בָאָֽבֶן (Vayikra 20:2), they shall stone him with the stone.

In כִּצְרוֹר אֶבֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָה (Mishlei 26:8), like binding a stone in a מַרְגֵּמָה, the מַרְגֵּמָה is a gathering of stones together, and the אבן is a precious stone. His father writes that בְּמַרְגֵּמָה is like אַרְגָּמָן, purple; and on that reading, as one binds a stone from the stones of the street in a purple garment, so is one who gives honour to a fool.

more.h: An assembly, or two men's names
more.t: שָׂרֵי יְהוּדָה רִגְמָתָם (Tehillim 68:28), the princes of Yehudah, their assembly: רִגְמָתָם is their assembly, and some explain it as princes. Targum Yonasan does not render ורגם מלך in וְרֶגֶם מֶלֶךְ וַֽאֲנָשָׁיו (Zecharyah 7:2), and Regem Melech and his men; perhaps, Radak says, these were two men so named, Sar'etzer and Regem Melech, and that is the correct reading.

סקל.sense: To stone; and turned about, to clear of stones. His father held them all one sense, reading the clearing as building with stones.

more.t: עוֹד מְעַט וּסְקָלֻֽנִי (Shemos 17:4), a little more and they will stone me; וּסְקַלְתּוֹ בָֽאֲבָנִים (Devarim 13:11), and you shall stone him with stones; סָקוֹל יִסָּקֵל הַשּׁוֹר (Shemos 21:28), the ox shall surely be stoned; וַיְסַקֵּל בָּֽאֲבָנִים אֶת־דָּוִד (Shmuel II 16:6), and he pelted David with stones; and כִּֽי־ סֻקַּל נָבוֹת וַיָּמֹת (Melachim I 21:15), that Navos had been stoned and was dead.

סַקְּלוּ מֵאֶבֶן (Yeshayahu 62:10), clear it of stone: the sense is turned about because it is joined to the mem of מֵאֶבֶן, from stone. And so וַיְסַקְּלֵהוּ (Yeshayahu 5:2), where the joining is left out: it means ויסקלהו מאבנים, he cleared it of stones, that is, took the stones away and cleared the vineyard of them.

more.h: His father makes it one sense
more.t: His father held them all one sense: ויסקלהו is building it a wall of stones after digging round it, which is וַיְעַזְּקֵהוּ, he dug about it, as in the words of Chazal ומצאו שהיה עוזק (Menachos 85b), and they found that he was digging; and סַקְּלוּ מֵאֶבֶן is to make a high road of great stones.

יסר.sense: To chasten, whether by words or by blows. In another sense, to bind, with the nouns for bonds and bands.

more.t: מוּסַר שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ עָלָיו (Yeshayahu 53:5), the chastening of our peace was upon him, and מוּסַר הֲבָלִים עֵץ הוּא (Yirmiyahu 10:8), the chastening of vanities is wood.
מוסר, he says, is sometimes in words and sometimes in blows. So וְיִסְּרוֹ לַמִּשְׁפָּט (Yeshayahu 28:26) is the striking of the plough's fists as the manner of sowing requires.

הֲרֹב עִם־שַׁדַּי יִסּוֹר (Iyov 40:2) he takes as an infinitive, chastening. His father takes יִסּוֹר for a noun like מוּסַר, and reads the pasuk as asking whether it is the way of מוסר that a man should quarrel with Shaddai.

In another sense, אַיְסִרֵם כְּשֵׁמַע לַעֲדָתָם (Hoshea 7:12), I will bind them as their congregation has heard, and וַאֲנִי יִסַּרְתִּי חִזַּקְתִּי זְרוֹעֹתָם (Hoshea 7:15), I bound, I strengthened their arms. The nouns are מוּסַר מְלָכִים פִּתֵּחַ (Iyov 12:18), He loosens the bond of kings, מוֹסְרֵי צַוָּארֵךְ (Yeshayahu 52:2), the bands of your neck, and נִתְּקוּ מוֹסֵרוֹת (Yirmiyahu 5:5), the bonds are snapped. All of them mean binding.

יכח.sense: To reprove: setting out words to one another in claims, making judgments known, and the chastening that comes of reproof; close to it, in two pesukim, to appoint.

more.t: הֲמִיִּרְאָתְךָ יֹכִיחֶךָ (Iyov 22:4), is it for your fear that He reproves you, means He will reason with you, that is, contend with you in claims. The sense of all these forms is setting out words to one another in claims, making judgments known, and the chastening that comes out of reproof.

וְאֶת־כֹּל וְנֹכָחַת (Bereishis 20:16), and with all, she was reproved, he reads as Moshe's own words: through all that befell her with Paroh and with Avimelech for saying he is my brother, Sarah was reproved and chastened out of saying he is my brother.

טוֹבָה תּוֹכַחַת מְגֻלָּה (Mishlei 27:5), better is reproof revealed, he reads as love revealed in reproof, as in הוֹכַח לְחָכָם וְיֶאֱהָבֶךָּ (Mishlei 9:8), reprove a wise man and he will love you: when a man reproves his fellow the love is revealed in the reproof, and that love is better than a love kept hidden, where a man loves his fellow in his heart, never reveals it to him, and does not reprove him when reproof is called for. His father takes it otherwise: reproof is good in any case, even in the open, but reproof that comes of love is hidden; that is, the lover reproves the one he loves privately, between the two of them, so that he is not shamed.

Close to this sense, he says, are אֲשֶׁר־ הֹכִיחַ י"י לְבֶן־אֲדֹנִֽי (Bereishis 24:44), whom Hashem has appointed for my master's son, and אֹתָהּ הֹכַחְתָּ לְעַבְדְּךָ לְיִצְחָק (Bereishis 24:14), her You have appointed for Your servant, for Yitzchak; he glosses them זִמֵּן, appointed, and זִמַּנְתָּ, You have appointed.

שׁכם.sense: To rise early; and שְׁכֶם, the part of the shoulder against the neck. A side, a quarter or a portion is the same sense, since the shoulder is a side.

more.t: וְהִשְׁכַּמְתֶּם וַֽהֲלַכְתֶּם לְדַרְכְּכֶם (Bereishis 19:2), and you will rise early and go your way, and מַשְׁכִּימֵי קוּם (Tehillim 127:2), you who rise early. וְכַטַּל מַשְׁכִּים הֹלֵֽךְ (Hoshea 6:4), and like the dew that goes early, is dew that goes off at the early hour; and מַשְׁכִּים הָיוּ (Yirmiyahu 5:8), they were early, is said of horses: every morning they were like well-fed horses, as it says of those who devise wrong on their beds, בְּאוֹר הַבֹּקֶר יַֽעֲשׂוּהָ (Michah 2:1), in the morning light they do it. He has given another explanation of it at the root מָשַׁך.

עַל־ שְׁכֶם שְׁנֵיהֶם (Bereishis 9:23), upon the shoulder of both of them, and וַיֵּט שִׁכְמוֹ (Bereishis 49:15), and he bent his shoulder: the part of the shoulder that is against the neck is called שכם, as it says כְּתֵפִי מִשִּׁכְמָה תִפּוֹל (Iyov 31:22), let my shoulder fall from the place at the neck.

כִּי תְּשִׁיתֵמוֹ שֶׁכֶם (Tehillim 21:13), for You will set them שֶׁכֶם, is to one side and to one quarter; דֶּרֶךְ יְרַצְּחוּ שֶׁכְמָה (Hoshea 6:9), they murder along the way שֶׁכְמָה, is on one way and one side; לְעָבְדוֹ שְׁכֶם אֶחָֽד (Tzefaniah 3:9), to serve Him with one שְׁכֶם, is with one heart and one mind; and וַֽאֲנִי נָתַתִּי לְךָ שְׁכֶם אַחַד (Bereishis 48:22), and I have given you one שְׁכֶם, is one portion. All of it is one sense, for the shoulder is a side and a quarter; and so a side is called כתף, a shoulder, as in וְלַכָּתֵף הַשֵּׁנִית (Shemos 27:15), and for the second side.

כתף.sense: The shoulder, a known word; כְתֵפֹת, shoulder pieces, called so for sitting on the shoulders; and in other places a side or a flank.

more.t: בַּכָּתֵף יִשָּֽׂאוּ (Bamidbar 7:9), they shall carry on the shoulder; וַיִּתְּנוּ כָתֵף סֹרָרֶת (Zecharyah 7:11), and they gave a stubborn shoulder; כְּתֵפִי מִשִּׁכְמָה תִפּוֹל (Iyov 31:22), let my shoulder fall from its blade; בִּכְתֵפָם בַּמֹּטוֹת (Divrei HaYamim I 15:15), on their shoulders with the poles. The word is known.
כְתֵפֹת חֹֽבְרֹת (Shemos 28:7), joined shoulder pieces, are called כתפות because they were on the shoulders.

וְלַכָּתֵף הַשֵּׁנִית (Shemos 27:15), and for the second side, and וְכִתְפוֹת הַפֶּתַח (Yechezkel 41:2), and the sides of the doorway: the sense of them is a side and a flank. In the construct, אֶל־ כֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת (Melachim I 6:8), to the side of the house, is pointed with six dots.

וְעָפוּ בְכָתֵף פְּלִשְׁתִּים (Yeshayahu 11:14) is of this sense as well: the Pelishtim will be weary and weak in their shoulder, that is, in their land. Or it may be of the first sense, meaning that Israel will be weary of shoulder from striking the Pelishtim so much. Yonasan renders וְיִתְחַבְּרוּן כְּתָף חָד לְמִמְחֵי פְּלִשְׁתָּאֵי, they will join as one shoulder to strike the Pelishtim.

שׁיר.sense: שֵּׁירוֹת, one of the ornaments. He adds no gloss of his own, only the Targum, which gives the same word for ornaments of the legs and for what is put in the jaws.

more.t: הַנְּטִיפוֹת וְהַשֵּׁירוֹת (Yeshayahu 3:19), the pendants and the rings, the Targum renders עַנְקַיָא וְשֵׁירֵי, necklaces and rings; הַפְּאֵרִים וְהַצְּעָדוֹת (Yeshayahu 3:20), the headdresses and the anklets, it renders כְּלִילַיָא וְשֵׁירֵי רְגִלַיָא, garlands and rings of the legs; and חַחִים בִּלְחָיֶיךָ (Yechezkel 29:4), hooks in your jaws, it renders וְאֶתֵּן שִׁירִין בְּלִיסָתָךְ, and I will put rings in your jaws. He adds no gloss of his own.

זמר.sense: To sing and make music, with songs and their instruments; the vine branch, its pruning and the pruning knife; also a foul smell, the land's best fruit, and an animal.

more.t: In עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ (Shemos 15:2), my strength and my song is Hashem, וְזִמְרָת lacks the yud of the speaker, its proper form being וְזִמְרָתי, my song. One proof is the kamatz under the resh, since a word in construct would be shorter, as וְזִמְרַת נְבָלֶיךָ (Amos 5:23), the music of your harps; so too בְּיָד (Shmuel I 26:23), into a hand, has a kamatz and is properly בידי, into my hand. A greater proof than the kamatz is the sense: the word carries the pronoun as עָזִי does, the yud of עזי standing for the two words; the kamatz proves less, since words in construct are also found with a kamatz, as וּמְנָת הַמֶּלֶךְ (Divrei HaYamim II 31:3), the king's portion.

With a mem added, the noun מִזְמוֹר (Tehillim 3:1), a song; זְמִרוֹת הָיוּ־לִי חֻקֶּיךָ (Tehillim 119:54), Your statutes were songs to me; and מְזַמְּרוֹת מִזְרָקוֹת חֲצֹצְרוֹת (Melachim II 12:14), mezamros, basins, trumpets, the mezamros being, he says, the instruments they make music on.

וְהִנָּם שֹׁלְחִים אֶת־הַזְּמוֹרָה אֶל־אַפָּם (Yechezkel 8:17), and behold they put the zemorah to their nose, means the foul smell. קְחוּ מִזִּמְרַת הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 43:11), take of the zimrah of the land, means the choicest of the fruits of the land, which he holds close to the first sense, since the best and most praised part of a song is called zamir, זָמִיר.

more.h: The vine branch and its cutting
more.t: הַזְּמוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר הָיָה בַּעֲצֵי הַיָּעַר (Yechezkel 15:2), the zemorah that was among the trees of the forest, and וּזְמֹרַת זָר תִּזְרָעֶנּוּ (Yeshayahu 17:10), you sow it with a foreign zemorah: their sense is a vine or a single plant, but mostly the word falls on the vine. The verb is the cutting of the branch, וְכַרְמְךָ לֹא תִזְמֹר (Vayikra 25:4), you shall not prune your vineyard, and the tool the branches are cut with is in וְכָרַת הַזַּלְזַלִּים בַּמַּזְמֵרוֹת (Yeshayahu 18:5), he cuts the shoots with pruning knives.

Rabbi Yonah explained זְמִיר עָרִיצִים יַעֲנֶה (Yeshayahu 25:5) from the cutting sense, since the word falls on the cutting of the branch, as the verb comes from it. On that reading יַעֲנֶה is like יקרא, will call, that is, Hashem will call for the cutting down of the tyrants. Radak holds the right reading takes יענה as יכניע, will subdue: the cutting that comes from Hashem will subdue the tyrants, with זמיר not in construct. It may also be of the first sense, meaning: the song and the delight the tyrants took pleasure in, He will subdue them.
וּתְאוֹ וָזָמֶר (Devarim 14:5), and the teo and the zemer, is the name of an animal; Rabbi Yonah wrote that the Arabic name for it is זוֹרָאפַ"ה.

תעה.sense: To stray, a sense he calls known: of a heart, of a lost sheep, of a man in a field or in strong drink; and to lead another astray.

more.t: תָּעָה לְבָבִי (Yeshayahu 21:4), my heart wanders, תָּעִיתִי כְּשֶׂה אֹבֵד (Tehillim 119:176), I have strayed like a lost sheep, וּבַשֵּׁכָר תָּעוּ (Yeshayahu 28:7), through strong drink they went astray, and וְהִנֵּה תֹעֶה בַּשָּׂדֶה (Bereishis 37:15), wandering in the field.

more.h: A form taken apart two ways
more.t: וְשִׁנֵּי כְפִירִים נִתָּעוּ (Iyov 4:10), and the teeth of the young lions נִתָּעוּ, is a form the authorities take apart differently. In Rabbi Yonah's view it is a word compounded within this one pattern out of past and future. Radak's brother Rabbi Moshe wrote that it is compounded of the passive and the reflexive patterns, its regular form being נִתְתָּעוּ, like וְנִכַּפֵּר לָהֶם הַדָּם (Devarim 21:8), and the blood shall be atoned for them. Radak himself has set the word down under the root לתע.

כִּי רוּחַ זְנוּנִים הִתְעָה (Hoshea 4:12), for a spirit of harlotry has led astray, and עַמִּי מְאַשְּׁרֶיךָ מַתְעִים (Yeshayahu 3:12), my people, those who guide you lead you astray. וְעוֹזֵב תּוֹכַחַת מַתְעֶה (Mishlei 10:17), and one who forsakes rebuke goes astray, is a verb that takes no object, like תּוֹעֶה, one straying, or else it means that he leads his own soul astray.

חוג.sense: To go round; the noun חוּג, the sphere that goes round the earth; and מְחוּגָה, the tool a circle is drawn with.

more.t: חֹק חָג עַל־פְּנֵי־מָיִם (Iyov 26:10), a bound He set round the face of the waters: חָג, he says, means went round.

הַיּשֵׁב עַל־ חוּג הָאָרֶץ (Yeshayahu 40:22), He who sits upon the circuit of the earth: that is, the sphere that goes round the earth. So too וְחוּג שָׁמַיִם יִתְהַלָּֽךְ (Iyov 22:14), He walks the circuit of the heavens, and בְּחוּקוֹ חוּג (Mishlei 8:27), when He inscribed a circuit.
מְחוּגָה is the tool with which a circle is drawn and set true: וּבַמְּחוּגָה יְתָֽאֳרֵהוּ (Yeshayahu 44:13), he marks it out with the compass. In the vernacular it is קונפ"ש, a compass.

נבא.sense: A prophet, and to prophesy: to receive prophecy from Hashem and speak it to those one is sent to. A נְבִיאָה is a prophetess, and also a prophet's wife.

more.t: יִהְיֶה נְבִיאֶֽךָ (Shemos 7:1), he shall be your prophet, answers to יִֽהְיֶה־לְּךָ לְפֶה (Shemos 4:16), he shall be a mouth for you: as the prophet speaks to the people on the mission of Hashem, so Aharon speaks on Moshe's mission whatever Moshe tells him.
וָֽאֶקְרַב אֶל־ הַנְּבִיאָה (Yeshayahu 8:3), and I drew near to the prophetess: she is called a prophetess because she was the prophet's wife.

וְגַם לְנֽוֹעַדְיָה הַנְּבִיאָה (Nechemiah 6:14), and also to Noadiah the prophetess. Rabbi Yonah wrote that the word is like הַנָבִיא, the prophet, Noadiah being no woman, and wrote further that it has been said he is Shemayah ben Delayah, called Noadiah for saying to Nechemiah נִוָּעֵד אֶל־בֵּית הָֽאֱלֹהִים (Nechemiah 6:10), let us meet at the house of Hashem. Radak rejects this: the language does not make a feminine into a masculine or a masculine into a feminine, and he has written of some of the like cases, and his view of them, in the grammar section. Noadiah was a woman, a false prophetess whom Sanvalat and Toviah hired to frighten Nechemiah, as other false prophets were hired to frighten him, as it says וליתר הנביאים אשר מיראים אותי (Nechemiah 6:14), and to the rest of the prophets who were making me afraid.

more.h: Why the verb takes a passive form
