more.t: The verb comes in the form of the passive because its sense is the receiving of prophecy from Hashem and the speaking of it to the one he is sent to, a single man or many. So אֲשֶׁר נִבֵּאתָ (Yirmiyahu 28:6), which you prophesied; וְנִבֵּאתִי כַּֽאֲשֶׁר צֻוֵּיתִי (Yechezkel 37:7), and I prophesied as I was commanded; and הִנָּבֵא בֶן־אָדָם (Yechezkel 38:14), prophesy, son of man. מַדּוּעַ נִבֵּיתָ (Yirmiyahu 26:9), why have you prophesied, is written with a yud.

הֵמָּה מִֽתְנַבְּאִים (Yirmiyahu 14:14), they prophesy; וַיִּֽתְנַבְּאוּ עַד לַֽעֲלוֹת הַמִּנְחָה (Melachim I 18:29), and they prophesied until the offering of the minchah; הִנַּבְּאוּ בַבַּעַל (Yirmiyahu 23:13), they prophesied by the Baal, whose regular form would be הִתְנַּבְּאוּ. At וַיִּתְנַבֵּא בְתוֹךְ־הַבַּיִת (Shmuel I 18:10), and he prophesied inside the house, the Targum has וְאִישְׁתַּטִי בְּגוֹ בֵיתָא, and he acted as a madman inside the house.

חזה.sense: To see, some of it plain seeing and some the sight of prophecy, with the nouns for vision and the seer; a separate sense, to be entangled; and the breast of an offering.

more.t: יִשְׂמַח צַדִּיק כִּי־ חָזָה נָקָם (Tehillim 58:11), the righteous man rejoices when he sees vengeance; וְזֶֽה־ חָזִיתִי וַֽאֲסַפֵּֽרָה (Iyov 15:17), this I have seen and will tell; וְתַחַז בְּצִיּוֹן עֵינֵֽינוּ (Michah 4:11), let our eyes look upon Tzion. All of them are the sense of seeing, and the Targum of רָאָה (Bereishis 29:10) is חֲזָא; of them some are plain seeing and some the sight of prophecy.

מַשָּׂא גֵּיא חִזָּיוֹן (Yeshayahu 22:1), the burden of the valley of vision; כְּחֶזְיוֹן לָֽיְלָה (Iyov 20:8), like a night vision, and in the plural מֵֽחֶזְיוֹנוֹת לָיְלָה (Iyov 4:13), out of night visions; חָזוֹן נִרְאָה אֵלַי (Daniel 8:1), a vision appeared to me, without the yud; בַּֽמַּֽחֲזֶה לֵאמֹר (Bereishis 15:1), in a vision, saying; and חָזוּת קשׁה (Yeshayahu 21:2), a hard vision.
וּמֶחֱזָה אֶל־ מֶחֱזָה (Melachim I 7:4), window opposite window, is the feminine form, and Targum Yonasan renders it וּזְוִי לָקֳבֵיל זְוִי, an opening facing an opening.

more.h: What was made with the grave
more.t: וְעִם־שְׁאוֹל עָשִׂינוּ חֹזֶה (Yeshayahu 28:15), and with the grave we have made a chozeh. Rabbi Yonah explained it so: we have already set a watchman with the grave who will let us know when it is coming, and when its time draws near we will push it off. It may also be that the word is of the pattern of כָל־ חֹזֶה לֵאמֹר (Melachim II 17:13), every seer, saying: that is, a vision we have made with the grave, and a covenant we have cut with it that it not take us. Apart from this, עַל דִּבְרֵי חוֹזָֽי (Divrei HaYamim II 33:19), upon the words of the seers, stands for חוזים, like וְאֹֽרְגִים חוֹרָֽי (Yeshayahu 19:9), and the weavers of white cloth, and others of their kind.

בֵּית אֲבָנִים יֶחֱזֶֽה (Iyov 8:17) is a different sense, which he explains as יסתבך, it becomes entangled: among a house of stones it is entangled. He ties it to קֶרֶן חָזוּת (Daniel 8:5), a horn of chazus. The chacham Rabbi Yehudah put וְעִם־שְׁאוֹל עָשִׂינוּ חֹזֶה into the sense of בֵּית אֲבָנִים יֶחֱזֶֽה, and Radak writes that we do not know what his view of the two of them was.

וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת־ הֶחָזֶה (Vayikra 8:29), and Moshe took the breast; חֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה (Vayikra 7:34), the breast of the waving; in the plural עַל־ הֶֽחָזוֹת (Vayikra 9:20), upon the breasts. Of the word he says only that it is known.

שׁקר.sense: Falsehood and treachery: to deal falsely, to break faith; the noun שֶׁקֶר, a lie, which in some pesukim means for nothing, without cause.

more.t: אִם־ תִּשְׁקֹר לִי וּלְנִינִי (Bereishis 21:23), that you will not deal falsely with me or with my offspring; וְלֹֽא־ שִׁקַּרְנוּ בִּבְרִיתֶֽךָ (Tehillim 44:18), and we did not break faith with Your covenant; וְלֹֽא־תְכַֽחֲשׁוּ וְלֹֽא־ תְשַׁקְּרוּ (Vayikra 19:11), you shall not deny and you shall not deal falsely. The sense is lying and betrayal, and the Targum of מַדּוּעַ נִבְגַּד אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו (Malachi 2:10), why do we betray one another, uses this very verb.

מִדְּבַר־ שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק (Shemos 23:7), keep far from a false word; דֹּבֵר שְׁקָרִים (Tehillim 101:7), a speaker of lies; בְּשִׁקְרֵיהֶם וּבְפַֽחֲזוּתָם (Yirmiyahu 23:32), by their lies and their recklessness.

Some of them carry the sense of חִנָּם, for nothing: אֹיְבַי שֶׁקֶר (Tehillim 35:19), my enemies without cause; שֶׁקֶר רְדָפוּנִי (Tehillim 119:86), they pursued me without cause; לַשֶּׁקֶר שָׁמַרְתִּי (Shmuel I 25:21), for nothing I kept guard; הִנֵּה לַשֶּׁקֶר עָשָׂה עֵט שֶׁקֶר סֹֽפְרִֽים (Yirmiyahu 8:8), see, it has worked for nothing, the pen of the scribes for nothing. The word שָׁוְא likewise can mean for nothing, as he has written.

שֹקר.sense: Of the eyes: to sharpen them and hint with them; the Targum renders a glimpsing eye with this root, and Chazal call a woman who gazes about סקרנית.

more.t: וּֽמְשַׂקְּרוֹת עֵינָיִם (Yeshayahu 3:16), and making signs with the eyes: that is, they sharpen their eyes and hint with them. He gives the vernacular word for it as well.

The Targum of עַיִן שְׁזָפַתּוּ (Iyov 20:9), an eye glimpsed him, is עֵינָא סְקַרְתֵּיהּ, an eye looked on him. And in the words of Chazal (Bereishis Rabbah 18): if I create her from the eye, she will be a gazer; and Chava stood and was a gazer, as it says ותרא האשה, and the woman saw.

כזב.sense: To lie, and to be proved a liar, all one sense; the noun כָּזָב is a lie, and with an added alef אַכְזָב, a lying spring.

more.t: כָּל־הָאָדָם כֹּזֵֽב (Tehillim 116:11), every man is a liar. The pasuk, as he explains it: I had great faith, for even when I was fleeing in my poverty and in my haste I would say that every man who says the kingship will not be mine is a liar, and that is the great faith.

יוֹכִיחַ בְּךָ וְנִכְזָֽבְתָּ (Mishlei 30:6), He will rebuke you and you will be shown a liar; הֵן־תֹּחַלְתּוֹ נִכְזָבָה (Iyov 41:1), his hope is proved false. עֵד אֱמוּנִים לֹא יְכַזֵּב (Mishlei 14:5), a faithful witness does not lie, even in matters that are not testimony, that is, even in idle talk. וְאִם־לֹא אֵפוֹ מִי יַכְזִיבֵנִי (Iyov 24:25), and if not, who will prove me a liar, means who will make my words out to be a lie. All of them are one sense.

אֲשֶׁר לֹֽא־ יְכַזְּבוּ מֵימָֽיו (Yeshayahu 58:11), whose waters do not fail, he takes the way of וְתִירוֹשׁ יְכַחֶשׁ בָּֽהּ (Hoshea 9:2), the wine fails her, and כִּחֵשׁ מַֽעֲשֵׂה־זַיִת (Chavakuk 3:17), the olive crop fails.

The noun with an added alef: תִֽהְיֶה לִי כְּמוֹ אַכְזָב (Yirmiyahu 15:18), will You be to me like an אַכְזָב, which he explains as like a lying spring. The prophet was complaining before Hashem, who had promised him נְתַתִּיךָ הַיּוֹם לְעִיר מִבְצָר (Yirmiyahu 1:18), I have made you today a fortified city, while they were cursing him and striking him. So too בתי אַכְזִיב לְאַכְזָב (Michah 1:14), the houses of Achziv shall be an אַכְזָב, which is said for elegance, since Achziv is the name of a town, as it says וּקְעִילָה וְאַכְזִיב וּמָֽרֵאשָׁה (Yehoshua 15:44), and Keilah and Achziv and Mareishah. אַכְזָב is כזב, a lie.

חכם.sense: To be wise, to grow wise, and to make another wise; the noun is חָכְמָה, wisdom, and the wise man is חָכָם.

more.t: בְּנִי אִם־ חָכַם לִבֶּךָ (Mishlei 23:16 in his edition), my son, if your heart is wise; אִם־ חָכַמְתָּ חָכַמְתָּ לָּךְ (Mishlei 9:12), if you have grown wise, you have grown wise for yourself; שִׁמְעוּ מוּסָר וַֽחֲכָמוּ (Mishlei 8:33), hear discipline and grow wise; וַיֶּחְכַּם מִכָּל־הָֽאָדָם (Melachim I 5:11), and he was wiser than any man.

חָכְמוֹת בַּחוּץ תָּרֹנָּה (Mishlei 1:20), wisdom cries aloud in the street, and חָכְמוֹת בָּֽנְתָה בֵיתָהּ (Mishlei 9:1), wisdom has built her house: the plural means every wisdom there is. חַכְמוֹת נָשִׁים בָּֽנְתָה (Mishlei 14:1), the wise among women has built her house, is pointed with a patach and means each one of the women who are wise.

וּזְקֵנָיו יְחַכֵּֽם (Tehillim 105:22), and he makes his elders wise; וּמֵעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם יְחַכְּמֵֽנוּ (Iyov 35:11), and from the birds of the heavens He makes us wise; מֵאֹֽיְבַי תְּחַכְּמֵנִי מִצְוֹתֶךָ (Tehillim 119:98), Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies.
הָבָה נִּֽתְחַכְּמָה לוֹ (Shemos 1:10), come, let us deal wisely with him; וְאַל־ תִּתְחַכַּם יוֹתֵר (Koheles 7:16), and do not make yourself overly wise.

בין.sense: To understand, to look into, to sense a thing, all one sense; תְּבוּנָֽה and בִּינָה, understanding. The same letters carry בֵּין, between.

more.t: בַּנְתָּה לְרֵעִי מֵרָחֽוֹק (Tehillim 139:2), You understand my thought from afar; עַם־חָכָם וְנָבוֹן (Devarim 4:6), a wise and understanding people; בִּינֹתִי בַּסְּפָרִים מִסְפַּר הַשָּׁנִים (Daniel 9:2), I understood from the books the number of the years. אָבְדָה עֵצָה מִבָּנִים (Yirmiyahu 49:7) can be read from this root too: counsel is lost from those who understand.

וְהַלְוִיִּם מְבִינִים אֶת־הָעָם לַתּוֹרָה (Nechemiah 8:7), and the Levi'im giving the people understanding in the Torah; מֵבִין פְּתָיִֽים (Tehillim 119:130), giving understanding to the simple; הָבֵן לְהַלָּז אֶת־הַמַּרְאֶֽה (Daniel 8:16), make this man understand the vision. Ibn Ezra reads אִם־ יָבִין מִפְרְשֵׂי־עָב (Iyov 36:29) the same way, if He gives understanding to the spreadings of cloud: as though He set understanding into the spreadings of cloud.

more.h: Understanding, said by way of figure
more.t: בְּטֶרֶם יָבִינוּ סִּֽירֹתֵיכֶם אָטָד (Tehillim 58:10), before your pots feel the thorn, is said by way of borrowing: before they feel the heat of the burning thorn beneath them. וּבִתְבוּנוֹת כַּפָּיו יַנְחֵֽם (Tehillim 78:72), and with the understanding of his palms he led them: understanding sits in the heart, but it is ascribed to the palms, since a shepherd who leads his flock with the staff in his palm along a straight way where they will not stumble, and leads them gently, is as though the understanding were in his palms. In the same way שִׂכֵּל אֶת־יָדָיו (Bereishis 48:14), he made his hands act wisely, and likewise הַוּוֹת תַּחְשֹׁב לְשׁוֹנֶךָ (Tehillim 52:4), your tongue devises mischief, though under הוה he gives that pasuk another explanation.

לִתְבוּנָתוֹ אֵין מִסְפָּֽר (Tehillim 147:5), to His understanding there is no number, means that the things He has understanding of are without number, for number is not said of understanding, only searching, as אֵין חֵקֶר לִתְבוּנָתֽוֹ (Yeshayahu 40:28), there is no searching of His understanding.
וַיַּרְא־אָוֶן וְלֹא יִתְבּוֹנָֽן (Iyov 11:11), He sees iniquity, and one does not consider: that is, He sees a man of iniquity, and the man does not consider that the Holy One sees him.

The same letters carry בֵּין: בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ (Bereishis 1:4), between the light and the darkness; בֵּין קֹדֶשׁ לְחֹל (Yechezkel 44:23), between holy and profane; their sense, he says, is known. From this comes אִישׁ־ הַבֵּנַיִם (Shmuel I 17:4), the man of the space between, the one standing between the two battle lines.

אתן.sense: אָתוֹן, the she-donkey, in two pesukim and with no gloss; the entry breaks off as it turns to the words of four letters.

more.t: וַתִּרְאַנִי הָֽאָתוֹן (Bamidbar 22:33), the she-donkey saw me, and אֲתֹנוֹת צְחֹרוֹת (Shoftim 5:10), white she-donkeys. He gives nothing beyond the two pesukim, and the entry breaks off as it turns to the words of four letters.

פרא.sense: פֶּרֶא, the wild donkey, and פֶּרֶא אָדָם, a man of the wilderness like one; and יַפְרִיא, he will increase and be fruitful, which Rabbi Yonah takes from פֶּרֶא.

more.h: The wild donkey, and a man like it
more.t: פֶּרֶא אָדָם (Bereishis 16:12), a wild donkey of a man, means a man of the wilderness like the wild donkey. It is written with a heh at פֶּרֶה לִמֻּד מִדְבָּר (Yirmiyahu 2:24), a wild donkey used to the wilderness, and the plural is הֵן פְּרָאִים בַּֽמִּדְבָּר (Iyov 24:5), behold, wild donkeys in the desert. The animal is the wild donkey.

כִּי הוּא בֵּן אַחִים יַפְרִיא (Hoshea 13:15), though he be fruitful among brothers: יַפְרִיא, he says, is he will increase and be fruitful. Rabbi Yonah explained it instead as the word פֶּרֶא, the wild donkey.

פרד.sense: פֶּרֶד, the mule, so named, Rav Hai Gaon wrote, because it does not beget and is apart; and to part, to be parted, and to separate others.

more.h: Why the mule is so named
more.t: וַיָּבֹא הַפֶּרֶד (Shmuel II 18:9), and the mule came; עַל־ הַפִּרְדָּה אֲשֶֽׁר־לִי (Melachim I 1:33), upon my own she-mule; וּבַצַּבִּים וּבַפְּרָדִים (Yeshayahu 66:20), in wagons and on mules. Rav Hai Gaon wrote that it is called פֶּרֶד because it does not breed and stands apart.

הִפָּרֶד נָא מֵֽעָלָי (Bereishis 13:9), part from me, please; מִמֵּעַיִךְ יִפָּרֵדוּ (Bereishis 25:23), from your womb they shall be parted; יַפְרִיד בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵֽךְ (Rus 1:17), it shall part between me and you; וְהִתְפָּֽרְדוּ כָּל־עַצְמוֹתָי (Tehillim 22:15), and all my bones came apart. וְכַנְפֵיהֶם פְּרֻדוֹת (Yechezkel 1:11), and their wings were parted, means spread out; and in עָֽבְשׁוּ פְרֻדוֹת תַּחַת מֶגְרְפֹתֵיהֶם (Yoel 1:17), the פְרֻדוֹת have rotted under their clods, the פְרֻדוֹת are the grains of seed lying separated and scattered under the earth.

לְֽתַֽאֲוָה יְבַקֵּשׁ נִפְרָד (Mishlei 18:1), the one who keeps apart seeks desire: he explains it of a man apart in his opinion and his counsel, who will not trust the counsel of his fellows and seeks his desires; and בְּכָל־תּֽוּשִׁיָּה יִתְגַּלָּֽע, into all wisdom he thrusts himself, meaning he shows himself mixing into every wisdom when he only follows the desires of his heart. Rav Saadiah Gaon explained the נִפְרָד as the traitor who separates from the mass of the people and abandons their faith: he follows desire and so separates from the mind of his community and from their faith, and with every argument you bring him he will quarrel with you and give you the lie; and so the pasuk after it says that the fool takes no delight in understanding.

כִּי־הֵם עִם־הַזֹּנוֹת יְפָרֵדוּ (Hoshea 4:14), for they part off with the harlots: he explains it as their parting the women from their husbands to commit harlotry with them. His father wrote it in the sense of the mule, meaning that they are as steeped in lewdness as the mule, no beast being so steeped in it as the mule. Some read that they do with the harlots the deed of the mule, which bears no fruit: so they lie with the harlots in a way that begets nothing.

שׁמט.sense: To leave a thing and abandon it, which he gives as the sense of all its forms: to release, to let drop; and of the oxen at the aron, to slip out from under it.

more.t: כִּי שָֽׁמְטוּ הַבָּקָֽר (Shmuel II 6:6), for the oxen slipped: that is, the oxen slipped out from under the aron. He counts the verb intransitive here. The Targum's view is that it is transitive, from the way it renders the pasuk, and it renders וְנִדְּחָה יָדוֹ (Devarim 19:5), and his hand slips, with the same Aramaic word. Rabbi Yonah explained that the oxen's joints and limbs came apart before the greatness of the aron and its purity, and Radak's father wrote the same.

תִּשְׁמְטֶנָּה וּנְטַשְׁתָּהּ (Shemos 23:11), you shall release the land and leave it; שָׁמוֹט כָּל־בַּעַל מַשֵּׁה יָדוֹ (Devarim 15:2), every creditor shall release what his hand holds. The heavy form: תַּשְׁמֵט יָדֶֽךָ (Devarim 15:3), your hand shall release, which Rabbi Yonah let drop and did not record. The noun is שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה (Devarim 15:9), the year of release. Radak gives the sense of them all as leaving a thing and abandoning it.

וְשָׁמַטְתָּה וּבְךָ מִנַּֽחֲלָֽתְךָ (Yirmiyahu 17:4), and you shall let go, and in you, from your inheritance: the release will be in you, that you are released from your inheritance, since you did not release it while you were in it.
וַיִּשְׁמְטוּהָ (Melachim II 9:33), and they let her drop; נִשְׁמְטוּ בִֽידֵי־סֶלַע שֹׁפְטֵיהֶם (Tehillim 141:6), their judges were let drop by the sides of the rock.

שׁלף.sense: To draw out, a sword from its sheath or a shoe from the foot; and, as a verb that takes no object, to come out.

more.t: וְלֹֽא־ שָׁלַף הַנַּעַר חַרְבּוֹ (Shoftim 8:20), and the lad did not draw his sword; כִּי לֹא שָׁלַף הַחֶרֶב מִבִּטְנוֹ (Shoftim 3:22), for he did not draw the sword out of his belly; שֹׁלֵֽף חָרֶב (Shoftim 20:15), a drawer of the sword. They mean bringing the sword out of its sheath.

Likewise שָׁלַף אִישׁ נַֽעֲלוֹ (Rus 4:7), a man drew off his shoe, is like חלץ, to take off; and for וְחָֽלְצָה נַֽעֲלוֹ (Devarim 25:9), and she shall take off his shoe, the Targum Yerushalmi has שְׁלוּפֵי סַנְדְּלָא, the drawing off of the sandal, with this same word.

As verbs that take no object: שָׁלַף וַיֵּצֵא מִגֵּוָה (Iyov 20:25), it came out and went forth from the body; שֶׁקַּדְמַת שָׁלַף יָבֵֽשׁ (Tehillim 129:6), which is dry before it comes out, that is, before it comes out and shows itself it is already dry.

נשׁל.sense: To slip off and drop, of itself; and with an object, to take off or drive out, which he gives as removal and overthrow: the shoe from the foot, nations from before you.

more.t: וְנָשַׁל הַבַּרְזֶל מִן־הָעֵץ (Devarim 19:5), and the iron slips off the wood; כִּי יִשַּׁל זֵיתֶֽךָ (Devarim 28:40), for your olives will drop off. These, he says, take no object.

With an object: וְנָשַׁל גּֽוֹיִם־רַבִּים מִפָּנֶיךָ (Devarim 7:1), and He will cast out many nations before you; שַֽׁל ־נְעָלֶיךָ (Shemos 3:5), take your shoes off; וַיְנַשֵּׁל אֶת־הַיְהוּדִים מֵֽאֵילוֹת (Melachim II 16:6), and he drove the Yehudim out of Eilos. Their sense is ההסרה והסתירה, removal and overthrow.

כִּי יֵשֶׁל אֱלוֹהַּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ (Iyov 27:8), when Hashem takes away his soul: the form should be יָשֵּׁל with a dagesh, and the quiescent letter came in its place, as at וַיָּזֶד יַֽעֲקֹב נָזִיד (Bereishis 25:29), and Yaakov cooked a stew. He says he will write more of it under the root שָׁלָה.

חשׁה.sense: To be silent, and to make others silent. Said of waves too, falling silent; every use is one sense, silence.

more.t: לְמַעַן צִיּוֹן לֹא אֶחֱשֶׁה (Yeshayahu 62:1), for the sake of Tzion I will not be silent; פֶּן־ תֶּֽחֱשֶׁה מִמֶּנִּי (Tehillim 28:1), lest You be silent toward me; וַיֶּחֱשׁוּ גַּלֵּיהֶֽם (Tehillim 107:29), and their waves fell silent; עֵת לַֽחֲשׁוֹת (Koheles 3:7), a time to be silent. In the heavy form: הֶחֱשֵׁיתִי מֵֽעוֹלָם אַֽחֲרִישׁ (Yeshayahu 42:14), I have long kept silent, I will hold my peace; וְאַתֶּם מַחְשִׁים אַל־תֵּעָצְלוּ, and you are silent, do not be idle; הֲלֹא אֲנִי מַחְשֶׁה (Yeshayahu 57:11), am I not silent?

more.h: הֶֽחֱשֽׁוּ, a command or a past?
more.t: גַּם־אֲנִי יָדַעְתִּי הֶֽחֱשֽׁוּ (Melachim II 2:3), I too know; they fell silent. Some say the last word is a command, be silent, and on that reading it should have been pointed with a patach. The right view is that it is past, as its form requires: when he said to them that he too knew, they fell silent and spoke to him no more.
Transitive, of making others silent: וְהַֽלְוִיִּם מַחְשִׁים לְכָל־הָעָם (Nechemiah 8:11), and the Levi'im silencing all the people. All of them, he says, are the sense of silence.

שׁתק.sense: To fall silent, to be quiet: of strife, of the sea. The sense of silence, he says, is known.

more.t: יִשְׁתֹּק מָדֽוֹן (Mishlei 26:20), strife falls quiet; וְיִשְׁתֹּק הַיָּם מֵֽעָלֵינוּ (Yonah 1:11), that the sea may be still from upon us; וַיִּשְׂמְחוּ כִֽי־ יִשְׁתֹּקוּ (Tehillim 107:30), and they rejoiced when they grew quiet. He says the sense of silence is well known, and adds nothing further.

דום.sense: Silence: being silenced or cut off, and stilling oneself; and דּוּמָה is also the name of a nation, one of the sons of Yishmael.

more.t: שָֽׁכְנָה דוּמָה נַפְשִֽׁי (Tehillim 94:17), my soul dwelt in silence, and כְּדֻמָה בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּֽם (Yechezkel 27:32), like one silenced in the midst of the sea: both mean silenced or cut off. The noun stands in שְׁבִי דוּמָם (Yeshayahu 47:5), sit silent, on the pattern of יוֹמָם, by day, save that the one has a shuruk and the other a cholam; and it may come from the root דָּמַם, as may לְאֶבֶן דּוּמָם (Chavakuk 2:19), to a silent stone.

גַּם־מַדְמֵן תִּדֹּמִּי (Yirmiyahu 48:2), you too, Madmen, shall be silent, is the reflexive compounded with the four letter root; according to Rabbi Yehudah its proper form is תִּתְדּוֹֽמְמִי, you shall still yourself, and Radak explains it as תשתקי, you shall be silent. The four letter root on its own gives אִם־לֹא שִׁוִּיתִי וְדֽוֹמַמְתִּ י (Tehillim 131:2), if I have not stilled and quieted myself.

Rabbi Yonah reads these words as loss and darkness, and so reads מַשָּׂא דּוּמָה אֵלַי קֹרֵא מִשֵּׂעִיר (Yeshayahu 21:11), the burden of Dumah, one calls to me from Seir, of the perishing nation, which is מלכות הרשעה, the wicked kingdom, taking מִשֵּׂעִיר as לשעיר, that is, on account of Seir. Radak answers that there is no need for all this forcing: Dumah is the nation of that name among Yishmael's sons, וּמִשְׁמָע וְדוּמָה וּמַשָּֽׂא (Bereishis 25:14), Mishma and Dumah and Massa; and מִשֵּׂעִיר means that from Seir the destroyer will come upon them, and out of fear of Seir they set watchmen on their towers, and in their great fear they rise at night and ask the watchmen מה מלילה, what of the night. Yonasan holds the same, that Dumah is a nation's name, since he left the word untranslated.

כלב.sense: כֶּלֶב, the dog, which he calls known; כְּלוּב, a basket, a vessel made of rods in lattice work, in which birds are raised; and כָלִבִּי, of Kalev's family.

more.t: הֲרֹאשׁ כֶּלֶב אָֽנֹכִי (Shmuel II 3:8), am I a dog's head, and לֹא יֶֽחֱרַץ־ כֶּלֶב לְשֹׁנוֹ (Shemos 11:7), no dog shall sharpen its tongue, both pointed with six dots; וְהַכְּלָבִים עַזֵּי־נֶפֶשׁ (Yeshayahu 56:11), the dogs are greedy of soul. The word he calls well known and glosses no further.

כְּלוּב קָֽיִץ (Amos 8:1), a basket of summer fruit, is סל, a basket, and like it is כִּכְלוּב מָלֵא עוֹף (Yirmiyahu 5:27), like a basket full of birds: it is a vessel made of rods, lattice work, in which birds are raised.

וְהוּא כָלִבִּֽו [ כָלִבִּֽי ] (Shmuel I 25:3), and he was a Kalevite, is traced to כָּלֵב: that is, he was of Kalev's family. Targum Yonasan renders it so, וְהוּא מִדְבֵית כָּלֵב, and he was of the house of Kalev.

כלכל.sense: וַיְכַלְכֵּל יוֹסֵף אֶת־אָבִיו (Bereishis 47:12), Yosef sustained his father: he glosses nothing here, having set both pesukim down under the root כּוּל.

more.t: He brings וַיְכַלְכֵּל יוֹסֵף אֶת־אָבִיו (Bereishis 47:12), Yosef sustained his father, and יְכַלְכֵּל דְּבָרָיו בְּמִשְׁפָּֽט (Tehillim 112:5), he sustains his affairs with judgment, and explains neither: he says he has already set them down with the words like them under the root כּוּל.

כפף.sense: To bend or bow down. From it כִּפָּה, a branch, and כַּף, the palm, both for being bent; כַּף is also the sole of the foot, the hollow of the thigh, and a spoon.

more.t: כָּפַף נַפְשִׁי (Tehillim 57:7), my soul was bowed down: the verb stands on its own, נפש being spoken of as a masculine word as in כָּל־נֶפֶשׁ שִׁבְעָֽה (Bereishis 46:25), all the souls were seven; or it may carry an object, and the sense is that each of them bowed down my soul. So too זֹקֵף כְּפוּפִים (Tehillim 146:8), He straightens the bent, and הֲלָכֹף כְּאַגְמֹן רֹאשׁוֹ (Yeshayahu 58:5), to bow his head like a bulrush. אִכַּף לֵֽאלֹהֵי מָרוֹם (Michah 6:6), shall I bow myself before God on high, has as its proper form אִכָּפֵף.

The noun for a branch is drawn from this: כִּפָּה וְאַגְמוֹן (Yeshayahu 9:13), branch and bulrush, וְכִפָּתוֹ לֹא רַֽעֲנָֽנָה (Iyov 15:32), his branch shall not be green, and כַּפֹּת תְּמָרִים (Vayikra 23:40), branches of palm trees, since the branch is bent. His father takes בְּעוֹדָהּ בְּכַפּוֹ יִבְלָעֶֽנָּה (Yeshayahu 28:4), while it is still in his כַּף he swallows it, from this same word for a branch, and Radak spells it out: when the one who sees it sees it on the branch, he swallows it while it is still on the branch.

more.h: כַּף, the hollow of the hand
more.t: From this the inside of the hand is called כַּף, because it is bent: וַיְמַלֵּא כַפּוֹ מִמֶּנָּה (Vayikra 9:17), he filled his palm from it, עַל לֹא־חָמָס בְּכַפָּי (Iyov 16:17), though no violence is in my palms, וְכַפָּיו פְּרֻשׂוֹת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם (Melachim I 8:54), his palms spread out to heaven, and וְכַף יָשִׂימוּ לְפִיהֶֽם (Iyov 29:9), they laid a hand upon their mouth. וְאַכְפִּי עָלֶיךָ לֹֽא־יִכְבָּֽד (Iyov 33:7), my hand upon you shall not be heavy, is וכפי with an added alef, which he treats under the root אָכַף. The sole of the foot is כַּף as well: מִכַּף רַגְלוֹ (Iyov 2:7), from the sole of his foot, and מִכַּף רַגְלְךָ (Devarim 28:35), from the sole of your foot.

עַל־ כַּפַּיִם כִּסָּה־אוֹר (Iyov 36:32), upon the כַּפַּיִם He covered the light, he reads of clouds, since at first a cloud is like a palm, as it says עָב קְטַנָּה כְּכַף ־אִישׁ (Melachim I 18:44), a little cloud like a man's hand, and because the clouds are like a dome over men. So וְשַׂכֹּתִי כַפִּי (Shemos 33:22), and I will screen you with My כַּף, meaning I will screen you with My clouds until I pass by; or it is a palm in its plain sense, said as a figure. נִשָּׂא לְבָבֵנוּ אֶל־כַּפָּיִם (Eichah 3:41), let us lift our heart to the כַּפָּיִם, is the clouds too; or it can be read from כף, the palm: we lift our heart together with our palms, on the way of בְּנָשְׂאִי יָדַי אֶל־דְּבִיר קָדְשֶֽׁךָ (Tehillim 28:2), when I lift my hands toward Your holy sanctuary; or we set our heart in our palms and lift it as an offering to God in heaven, which is how Rav Saadiah Gaon read it. הֵן עַל־ כַּפַּיִם חַקֹּתִיךְ (Yeshayahu 49:16), behold, upon כַּפַּיִם I have engraved you, Radak takes as clouds, and so his father writes; it may also be read plainly, as though you were engraved on palms, so that I see you always, and so Ibn Ezra read it.

more.h: The hip socket and the spoon
more.t: עַל־כַּף הַיָּרֵךְ (Bereishis 32:33), the hollow of the thigh, is so called because the bone the thigh bone enters is bent; and some explain that it is so called because the flesh around the upper thigh bone is shaped like a spoon. The vessel is כַּף as well, כַּף אַחַת עֲשָׂרָה זָהָב (Bamidbar 7:14), one spoon of ten, of gold, and כַּפּוֹת זָהָב (Bamidbar 7:84), golden spoons, since it too is bent; in la'az, קוֹקְיַיארַא.

טלל.sense: To roof over, to set a covering above; and in another sense טַל, dew.

more.t: הוּא יִבְנֶנּוּ וִֽיטַלְלֶנּוּ (Nechemiah 3:15), he shall build it and roof it over: that is, יסכהו, he shall cover it, meaning he shall set a roof above it. So too Chazal say לסוכא מטללתא (Sukkah 28b), of a sukkah that has been roofed; the Targum renders בַּסֻּכֹּת (Vayikra 23:42), in booths, as בִּמְטַלַּיָּא, in coverings, and בְּצֵל קֹֽרָתִֽי (Bereishis 19:8), in the shadow of my roof beam, as בִּטְלַל שֵׁרוּתִי, in the covering of my roof beam.

In another sense the word is dew: כִּי טַל אוֹרֹת טַלֶּךָ (Yeshayahu 26:19), for your dew is a dew of lights, נִמְלָא־ טָל (Shir HaShirim 5:2), filled with dew, and וְהַשָּׁמַיִם יִתְּנוּ טַלָּם (Zecharyah 8:12), and the heavens shall give their dew. The dagesh stands in place of the doubled letter that is missing, and the plural is טַלִים or טְלָלִים, dews, on the pattern of צְלָלִים, shadows.

גלם.sense: To fold over and wrap up, and a garment a man wraps himself in. In another sense גולם, a thing not yet finished into its form, and a man empty of wisdom.

more.t: אֶת־אַדַּרְתּוֹ וַיִּגְלֹם (Melachim II 2:8), his mantle, and he wrapped it: he folded it over and rolled it up, and struck the water with it. So בִּגְלוֹמֵי תְּכֵלֶת וְרִקְמָה (Yechezkel 27:24), in wraps of blue and embroidery, is a garment a man covers and wraps himself in, called in la'az קפ"א; and so in the words of Chazal, גלימא דמיכסא (Bava Metzia 65a), a cloak for covering. Some explain the word as rolls of garments, טרושל"ש in la'az.

In another sense, גָּלְמִי רָאוּ עֵינֶיךָ (Tehillim 139:16), Your eyes saw my body: גָּלְמִי is גופי, my body, since the body of a thing that does not yet have all its forms and is not finished into a vessel is called גולם. So גלמי כלי עץ, גלמי כלי מתכות (Chullin 25a), unfinished wooden vessels, unfinished metal vessels, are called so before their work into a vessel is done. A man empty of wisdom is called גולם too, as Chazal say, שבעה דברים בגולם ושבעה בחכם (Avos 5:10 in his edition), seven things are in a golem and seven in a wise man.

כרך.sense: To wind or wrap around; תַּכְרִיךְ is the cloak a man winds about himself, and in Chazal the shrouds of the dead.

more.t: וְתַכְרִיךְ בּוּץ וְאַרְגָּמָן (Esther 8:15), a wrap of fine linen and purple: a linen cloak, called תכריך because a man winds himself in it and covers himself with it. Chachamim speak of תכריכי המת (Kilayim 9:4), the shrouds of the dead.

They use the root in the plain verb, as אפילו נחש כרוך על עקבו לא יפסיק (Berachos 30b), even if a snake is wound around his heel he does not break off, and כרוכה ומנחת בקרן זויות (Kiddushin 66a), it lies wound up and set in a corner.

גלח.sense: To shave, of the head and the beard; the sense, he says, is known.

more.t: וְגִלְּחָה אֶת־רֹאשָׁהּ (Devarim 21:12), she shall shave her head, וְאֶת־הַנֶּתֶק לֹא יְגַלֵּחַ (Vayikra 13:33), he shall not shave the netek, and יְגַלַּח י"י בְּתַעַר הַשְּׂכִירָה (Yeshayahu 7:20), Hashem will shave with a hired razor. Where no doer is named: כַּאֲשֶׁר גֻּלָּֽח (Shoftim 16:22), after he had been shaved, and אִם־ גֻּלַּחְתִּי וְסָר מִמֶּנִּי כֹחִי (Shoftim 16:17), if I be shaved my strength will leave me. וְהִתְגַּלָּח (Vayikra 13:33) is to shave oneself.

מְגֻלְּחֵי זָקָן וּקְרֻעֵי בְגָדִים (Yirmiyahu 41:5), men shaven of beard and torn of garment, is in the manner of כְּאֵלָה נֹבֶלֶת עָלֶהָ (Yeshayahu 1:30), like a terebinth withering of leaf, as he will explain at the root נבל.

גזז.sense: To shear or cut off: the wool of the flock, the hair of the head, the grass that is mown, and hewn stone.

more.t: לִגְזֹז אֶת־צֹאנוֹ (Bereishis 31:19), to shear his flock, וְעַתָּה שָׁמַעְתִּי כִּי גֹֽזְזִים לָךְ (Shmuel I 25:7), now I have heard that they are shearing for you, גָּזִּי נִזְרֵךְ (Yirmiyahu 7:29), cut off your hair, and וַיָּגָז אֶת־רֹאשׁוֹ (Iyov 1:20), he shaved his head. In the passive, וְכֵן נָגוֹזּוּ וְעָבָר (Nachum 1:12), so are they cut down and he passes away, he glosses נכרתו, they were cut off.

יֵרֵֽד כְּמָטָר עַל־ גֵּז (Tehillim 72:6), he shall come down like rain upon the mown grass: the grass that has been cut, whose roots are left and which will grow again with the rain. So אַחַר גִּזֵּי הַמֶּֽלֶךְ (Amos 7:1), after the king's mowings.

So too the wool that is shorn from the flock: גֵּז צֹֽאנְךָ (Devarim 18:4), the shearing of your flock, וַיִּמֶץ טַל מִן־ הַגִּזָּה (Shoftim 6:38), he wrung dew out of the fleece, and אֶת־ גִּזַּת הַצֶּמֶר (Shoftim 6:37), the fleece of wool.

אַבְנֵי גָזִֽית (Melachim I 5:31), stones of hewn work, and לֹֽא־תִבְנֶה אֶתְהֶן גָּזִית (Shemos 20:22), you shall not build them of hewn stone, he glosses אבני כריתה, stones of cutting, that is, stones that are hewn. The form should have been גַּזִית with a dagesh, and the resting letter came in place of the dagesh, as the rule is.

גלב.sense: תַּעַר הַגַּלָּבִים (Yechezkel 5:1), the razor of the גלבים, who are הסופרים, the men who cut hair; the Targum uses the word for a shorn beard and for knives.

more.t: תַּעַר הַגַּלָּבִים (Yechezkel 5:1), the razor of the גלבים: הם הסופרים, they are the men who cut hair. In Bereishis Rabbah, parsha 44, היה המלאך עומד ומגלב בידו, the angel stood with a מגלב, a blade, in his hand. The Targum renders וְכָל־זָקָן גְּרֻעָה (Yirmiyahu 48:37), and every beard shorn, with גליבא, and חַֽרְבוֹת צֻרִים (Yehoshua 5:2), knives of flint, with גלבים דטור, where the same word stands for the blades.

נגף.sense: Thrusting and striking, some of it deadly and some not: striking a thing, a foot knocking against a stone, being beaten; and נֶגֶף and מַגֵּפָה, the stroke.

more.t: וְנָגְפוּ אִשָּׁה הָרָה (Shemos 21:22), and they strike a pregnant woman, וְכִֽי־ יִגֹּף שׁוֹר־אִישׁ (Shemos 21:35), and if a man's ox strikes, נָגֹף וְרָפוֹא (Yeshayahu 19:22), smiting and healing, and לִנְגֹּף אֶת־מִצְרַיִם (Shemos 12:23), to smite Egypt: all of these, he says, take an object. וַיִּגֹּף, and He struck, said of אֶת־הַיֶּלֶד אֲשֶׁר יָֽלְדָה אֵֽשֶׁת־אֽוּרִיָּה לְדָוִד וַיֵּֽאָנַֽשׁ (Shmuel II 12:15), the child whom Uriyah's wife bore to David, and he fell sick, is נגפו בחולי קשה, He struck him with a hard illness.

Taking no object, it is knocking against: פֶּן־ תִּגֹּף בָּאֶבן רַגְלֶֽךָ (Tehillim 91:12), lest your foot strike against a stone, and וְרַגְלְךָ לֹא תִגּֽוֹף (Mishlei 3:23), and your foot shall not strike. In the form for what one does to himself, וּבְטֶרֶם יִתְנַגְּפוּ רַגְלֵיכֶם עַל־הָרֵי נָשֶׁף (Yirmiyahu 13:16), and before your feet strike against the mountains of dusk.

כִּי נִגַּף לִפְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shmuel II 10:15), that he had been beaten before Yisrael, is pointed with a patach and is past. אַךְ נִגּוֹף נִגָּף הוּא (Shoftim 20:39), surely he is smitten, and נִגָּף (Devarim 28:25), smitten, are pointed with a kamatz and are present. And בְּֽהִנָּגֵף עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim I 8:33), when Your people Yisrael are beaten.

The noun stands in וְלֹא־יִֽהְיֶה בָכֶם נֶגֶף (Shemos 12:13), and there shall be no stroke among you, pointed with six dots; and on another pattern אַֽחֲרֵי הַמַּגֵּפָה (Bamidbar 26:1), after the stroke, and אֶת־כָּל־ מַגֵּֽפֹתַי (Shemos 9:14), all My strokes. All of them are the sense of thrusting and striking, some with death and some without.

צפרדע.sense: The frog, a word whose sense he calls known; the singular הַצְּפַרְדֵּעַ may name the whole kind rather than a single frog.

more.h: Perhaps the name of the whole kind
more.t: וַתַּעַל הַצְּפַרְדֵּעַ (Shemos 8:2), and the frog came up; וַיַּֽעֲלוּ אֶת־ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִים (Shemos 8:3), and they brought up the frogs; and וְשָׁרַץ הַיְאֹר צְפַרְדְּעִים (Shemos 7:28), and the river shall swarm with frogs: its sense is known. It may be that הַצְּפַרְדֵּעַ in וַתַּעַל הַצְּפַרְדֵּעַ is the name of the whole kind and is not said of a single one, as also וַתְּהִי הַכִּנָּם (Shemos 8:14), and there were lice; and so it says, וּצְפַרְדֵּעַ וַתַּשְׁחִיתֵֽם (Tehillim 78:45), and the frog, and it destroyed them.

שׁחן.sense: שְׁחִין, an affliction that comes of heat other than fire; the Targum and the Kohen Gadol's tefillah use the word for warmth.

more.t: שְׁחִין אֲבַעְבֻּעֹת (Shemos 9:10), a boil of blisters, and לִשְׁחִין פֹּרֵחַ (Shemos 9:9), a boil breaking out: he says it is an affliction that comes of heat other than fire, as Chazal teach (Negaim 9:1), איזהו שחין, what is a shechin? לקה בעץ או באבן או בזפת או במי טבריא, one struck by wood or by stone or by pitch or by the waters of Teveriah. And they say further (Negaim 9:1), כל שאינו מחמת האש זהו שחין, whatever is not from fire is a shechin, הבא מחמת האש זה מכוה, and what comes of fire is a burn.

The Targum renders וַיִּקַּח מֵהֶם וַיָּחָם (Yeshayahu 44:15), he takes of them and warms himself, with וּנְסֵיב מִנְהוֹן וּשְׁחֵין, and he took of them and warmed himself; and so the Kohen Gadol's tefillah (Yoma 53b) runs יהי רצון שתהא שנה זו שחונה וגשומה, may it be His will that this year be warm and rainy.

גרב.sense: The גָּרָב, one of the diseases of itching: וּבַגָּרָב וּבֶחָרֶס (Devarim 28:27), with the garav and with the cheres.

ילף.sense: יַלֶּפֶת, the affliction named at Vayikra 22:22; the Chachamim take it for the Egyptian lichen, which winds itself about a man until the day he dies.

more.t: One line, and no gloss of his own: אוֹ גָרָב אוֹ יַלֶּפֶת (Vayikra 22:22), or garav or yalefes. What he gives in place of a gloss is the Chachamim's (Bechoros 41a): this is the Egyptian lichen, שמלפפתו עד יום המיתה, which winds itself about a man until the day of death. The edition prints a gap in the middle of their words.

חפשֹ.sense: To search out, a searching akin to inquiry; and, reflexively, changing one's veil or garment for another.

more.t: חֹפֵשׂ כָּל־חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן (Mishlei 20:27), searching all the chambers of the belly, and וְֽכַמַּטְמוֹנִים תַּחְפְּשֶֽׂנָּה (Mishlei 2:4), and you search her out as men search for hidden treasure. וַיְחַפֵּשׂ בַּגָּדוֹל הֵחֵל (Bereishis 44:12), he searched, beginning with the eldest, and וְחִפַּשְׂתִּי אֹתוֹ בְּכֹל אַלְפֵי יְהוּדָֽה (Shmuel I 23:23), and I will search him out among all the thousands of Yehudah. Of עִם־לְבָבִי אָשִׂיחָה וַיְחַפֵּשׂ רוּחִֽי (Tehillim 77:7) the sense is: if I speak with my heart, he searches my spirit and knows my thought.

The passive is אֵיךְ נֶחְפְּשׂוּ עֵשָׂו, in Ovadiah, how Esav has been searched out, and וּבְקוּם רְשָׁעִים יְחֻפַּשׂ אָדָֽם (Mishlei 28:12), when the wicked rise, a man is searched out. The noun is חֵפֶשׂ, in תַּמְנוּ חֵפֶשׂ מְחֻפָּשׂ (Tehillim 64:7), we have finished a search well searched; its sense is the known one of searching, like inquiry.

The reflexive is of exchanging and changing the veil or the garment for another: וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ בָּֽאֲפֵר (Melachim I 20:38), he changed his garb with a covering; וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל (Melachim I 22:30), the king of Yisrael changed his garb; וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ שָׁאוּל וַיִּלְבַּשׁ בְּגָדִים אֲחֵרִים, Shaul changed his garb and put on other clothes; and בְּרָב־כֹּחַ יִתְחַפֵּשׂ לְבוּשִׁי (Iyov 30:18), by great force my garment is changed.

more.h: The two kings going to battle
more.t: הִתְחַפֵּשׂ וָבֹא בַמִּלְחָמָה (Melachim I 22:30), to change garb and go into the battle, he reads as an infinitive: the king of Yisrael said he would change his garb and go into the battle, as though he said, I will change my garb and go into the war, and you wear your own garments, since you have no need to change. His father reads it as a command: the king of Yisrael told Yehoshafat to take off his royal clothes and go into the battle, his view being that both of them would change their garb. On that reading Yehoshafat answered, and you wear your garments, if I am to change mine, since one of us should go in with the majesty of kingship; the king of Yisrael did not accept it from him and changed his garb, and when Yehoshafat saw that, he did not take off his royal clothes, and it was for this that the officers of the chariots thought Yehoshafat was the king of Yisrael, until he cried out and they knew his voice.

חפשׁ.sense: Free: חָפְשִׁי is one free of his master, or of the toil of the world; the nouns are חֹפֶשׁ, freedom, and חֻפְשָׁה, release.

more.t: וְעֶבֶד חָפְשִׁי מֵֽאֲדֹנָֽיו (Iyov 3:19), and the slave is free of his master, and הָֽעִבְרִי וְהָֽעִבְרִיָּה חָפְשִׁים (Yirmiyahu 34:9), the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman going free. בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי (Tehillim 88:6), free among the dead, he explains as free of the toil of the world, as it says, ושם ינוחו יגיעי כח, and there the weary of strength are at rest; and so, he says, is וְעֶבֶד חָפְשִׁי מֵֽאֲדֹנָֽיו.

יֵצֵא לַֽחָפְשִׁי (Shemos 21:2), he shall go out to be free, he explains as going out to a place where he will be free, that is, out of his master's house to his own house. Some explain that the yud is added and the word is like לחופש, to freedom; others say the lamed is added.

כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּֽשָׁה (Vayikra 19:20), because she was not set free, and the noun אוֹ חֻפְשָׁה לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ (Vayikra 19:20), or freedom was not given her, on the pattern of טֻמְאָה, uncleanness. The heh may be the feminine suffix, her freedom, though it is soft, for he has written of many like it in the grammar; חֻפְשָׁה would then be joined from חֹפֶשׁ, as מְלֹא קֻמְצוֹ (Vayikra 5:12), the full of his fist, is from קֹמֶץ, and כְּרֹב גֻּדְּלֽוֹ (Tehillim 150:2), according to His abundant greatness, is from גֹּדֶל.

more.h: Clothes of freedom, house of freedom
more.t: בְבִגְדֵי־ חֹפֶשׁ לְרִכְבָּֽה (Yechezkel 27:20), garments of freedom for riding, are costly clothes, the kind fit for a free man and a nobleman. בְּבֵית הַֽחָפְשִׁית (Melachim II 15:5), in the house of freedom, is so called because he kept apart there from people, as though free of their company. Rabbi Yonah reads it otherwise, a small house, from the Arabic, where a small house is called חפשי. The Yerushalmi in Kesubos says he made him a house in the graveyard, as you say בַּמֵּתִים חָפְשִׁי, free among the dead.

דרר.sense: Freedom: freedom proclaimed, the good myrrh free of counterfeit and mixture, and the bird דְּרוֹר, named for nesting in houses without fear, as though free of men.

more.t: וּקְרָאתֶם דְּרוֹר (Vayikra 25:10), and you shall proclaim דרור: חופש, freedom.
מָר־דְּרוֹר (Shemos 30:23) is the good myrrh, the myrrh that is free of counterfeit and of anything mixed into it.

וּדְרוֹר קֵן לָהּ (Tehillim 84:4), the deror has a nest of her own, and כַּדְּרוֹר לָעוּף (Mishlei 26:2), like the deror in its flying. It is the name of an unclean bird, the one called irondela in la'az, and it is called דרור because it nests in houses without fear, as though it were free of men and safe from being caught.

חור.sense: White, and to turn white, with shame spoken of as whiteness; in another sense, a hole. חֹרִים, the nobles, Rabbi Yonah also draws from whiteness.

more.t: חוּר כַּרְפַּס וּתְכֵלֶת (Esther 1:6), white, karpas and blue: חוּר is white, and so Chazal (Megillah 12a) say that he spread for them a couch of white wool; and תְּכֵלֶת וָחוּר (Esther 8:15), blue and white. The verb shows its middle letter in וְלֹא עַתָּה פָּנָיו יֶחֱוָרוּ (Yeshayahu 29:22), and his face shall not now turn white, and the Targum renders לָבָן (Bereishis 30:35), white, as חִוָּר.
Shame is spoken of in the way of whiteness, since a man who feels shame goes white in the face; and so Chazal (Bava Metzia 58b) speak of one who whitens his fellow's face in public.

Rabbi Yonah explains וְאֹרְגִים חוֹרָי (Yeshayahu 19:9), and the weavers of chorai, from whiteness, as white cloth, and סַלֵּי חֹרִי (Bereishis 40:16), baskets of chori, the same way. They could well be white baskets, that is, baskets made of peeled rods, which are white once the bark is off; but Radak holds this a far reading.

From this sense too Rabbi Yonah explains בֶּן־חוֹרִים (Koheles 10:17), a son of nobles, כָּל־חֹרֵי יְהוּדָה וִירוּשָׁלָם (Yirmiyahu 27:20), all the nobles of Yehudah and Yerushalayim, וָאָרִיבָה אֶת־הַחֹרִים (Nechemiah 5:7), and I contended with the nobles, and חֹרֶיהָ וְאֵין־שָׁם מְלוּכָה (Yeshayahu 34:12), her nobles, and no kingship there. Rabbi Yonah says that in the language of Yishmael the princes and the great men are called by a word for whiteness.

The other sense is a hole: וַיִּקֹּב חֹר בְּדַלְתּוֹ (Melachim II 12:10), he bored a hole in its door, וַיְמַלֵּא־טֶרֶף חֹרָיו (Nachum 2:13), he filled his holes with prey, חֹרֵי עָפָר וְכֵפִים (Iyov 30:6), holes of the dust and of the rocks, and מִן־הַחֹרִים אֲשֶׁר הִתְחַבְּאוּ־שָׁם (Shmuel I 14:11), out of the holes where they had hidden. With a shuruk it is עַל־חֻר פָּתֶן (Yeshayahu 11:8), over the hole of an asp, and הָפֵחַ בַּֽחוּרִים כֻּלָּם (Yeshayahu 42:22), all of them snared in holes; the sense is known.

more.h: The woven work read as holes
more.t: The same two words may be read from the hole instead: וְאֹרְגִים חוֹרָי (Yeshayahu 19:9) would be cloth pierced with holes at the weaving, for ornament, or else the nets, which are holes upon holes, and that suits the passage, as the pasuk before it says וּפֹרְשֵׂי מִכְמֹרֶת עַל־פְּנֵי־מַיִם (Yeshayahu 19:8), and those who spread nets upon the water; and סַלֵּי חֹרִי (Bereishis 40:16) would be pierced baskets, for that is how they are made. It is explained further under the root חרר.

more.h: Words he keeps out of the root
more.t: Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Yonah put into this root וְחָרָה נְחֻשְׁתָּהּ (Yechezkel 24:11), and its bottom grows hot, וְעַצְמִי־חָרָה מִנִּי־חֹרֶב (Iyov 30:30), and my bone burns with heat, and חָרוּ יֹשְׁבֵי אֶרֶץ (Yeshayahu 24:6), the dwellers of the earth are scorched. Radak holds the right and straight course is to set them among the doubled verbs.

בצר.sense: Plucking, of the grape harvest; another sense is strength, of the fortified city; another is being withheld, as rain is in a drought. בָּצֶר is gold.

more.t: לֹא תִבְצֹר (Vayikra 25:5), you shall not pluck, כִּי תִבְצֹר כַּרְמְךָ (Devarim 24:21), when you pluck your vineyard, and כְּבוֹצֵר עַל־סַלְסִלּוֹת (Yirmiyahu 6:9), like one plucking over the baskets. The noun is בָּצִיר, the vintage: וְהִשִּׂיג לָכֶם דַּיִשׁ אֶת־בָּצִיר (Vayikra 26:5), your threshing shall reach the vintage, and מִבְצִיר אֲבִיעֶזֶר (Shoftim 8:2), than the vintage of Aviezer, where the beis is soft though it ought to carry a dagesh. All of them are plucking.

כִּי יָרַד יַעַר הַבָּצוּר (Zecharyah 11:2), read הַבָּצִיר, for the forest has come down. It may be read from the plucking, the forest of the vintage, as a figure for the great men of Yisrael: the pasuk likens them to a forest because forest trees are tall and many, and joins them to the vintage, meaning that they give fruit, which forest trees do not. It may also be read from the sense of strength.

וְהֶעָרִים בְּצֻרוֹת (Bamidbar 13:28), and the cities are fortified, לְחוֹמַת נְחֹשֶׁת בְּצוּרָה (Yirmiyahu 15:20), a fortified wall of copper, and וְאַגִּידָה לְּךָ גְּדֹלוֹת וּבְצֻרוֹת לֹא יְדַעְתָּם (Yirmiyahu 33:3), and I will tell you great things and fortified things you have not known. The verb makes strong: וַתִּתְצוּ הַבָּתִּים לְבַצֵּר הַחוֹמָה (Yeshayahu 22:10), you pulled the houses down to fortify the wall, and וְכִי תְבַצֵּר מְרוֹם עֻזָּהּ (Yirmiyahu 51:53), though she fortify the height of her strength. The nouns are שׁוּבוּ לְבִצָּרוֹן (Zecharyah 9:12), return to the stronghold, which he reads as the cities of strength, עָרֵי הַמִּבְצָר (Yehoshua 10:20), the fortified cities, הַבְּמַחֲנִים אִם בְּמִבְצָרִים (Bamidbar 13:19), whether in camps or in strongholds, and עִיר מִבְצָרוֹת (Daniel 11:15), a city of strongholds. All of them are strength.

יִבְצֹר רוּחַ נְגִידִים (Tehillim 76:13) he reads from the strength: He will raise it up and make it strong. It can also be read from the plucking: He will pluck and bring the spirit of princes low from its pride, which fits what comes after it, נוֹרָא לְמַלְכֵי־אָרֶץ, feared by the kings of the earth.

וְעַתָּה לֹא־יִבָּצֵר מֵהֶם (Bereishis 11:6), now nothing will be withheld from them, and וְלֹא־יִבָּצֵר מִמְּךָ מְזִמָּה (Iyov 42:2), no purpose is withheld from You: their sense is not being kept back. In this sense are וּבִשְׁנַת בַּצֹּרֶת לֹא יִדְאָג (Yirmiyahu 17:8), in a year of drought he will not worry, and עַל־דִּבְרֵי הַבַּצָּרוֹת (Yirmiyahu 14:1), concerning the droughts, which is the withholding of the rains and their being held back. Some read לְעִתּוֹת בַּצָּרָה (Tehillim 9:10) from this too, for times of withholding, taking the beis as a root letter. It may be said, Radak adds, that the fortified city and this sense lie close together, since a thing great and strong is withheld from a man's reaching it.

וְשִׁית־עַל־עָפָר בָּצֶר (Iyov 22:24), and lay gold upon the dust, and the plural בצרים in וְהָיָה שַׁדַּי בְּצָרֶיךָ (Iyov 22:25), and the Almighty will be your gold. There are careful books with no yud, and then it is singular, the resh taking a segol for the esnachta; and it may still be plural even with the yud missing, since many like it are found.

זהב.sense: Gold, a known word; since gold is clear and clean, what is clear and clean is called זָהָב too: wind, wine, oil, though in Iyov Ibn Ezra reads the sky's brightness.

more.t: זָהָב וָכֶסֶף (Shemos 25:3), gold and silver: the word is known.

Since gold is clear and clean, a thing that is clear and clean is called gold as well. מִצָּפוֹן זָהָב יֶֽאֱתֶה (Iyov 37:22), out of the north comes gold, means the clear and clean wind. The Chacham Rabbi Avraham Ibn Ezra explains it as the brightness of the sky, which looks like gold, since it is from the northern side that it begins to clear. Further, כּֽוֹס־ זָהָב בָּבֶל (Yirmiyahu 51:7), Bavel is a cup of gold, means the clear and clean wine; and הַֽמְרִיקִים מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶם הַזָּהָֽב (Zecharyah 4:12), that empty the gold out from themselves, means the clear and clean oil.

כתם.sense: כֶּתֶם, the good gold: Rabbi Yonah wrote that it is pearls, but its tie to Ophir and to פָּז makes it look like gold. Also נִכְתָּם, marked; Chazal call a mark כתם.

more.t: בְּכֶתֶם אוֹפִֽיר (Tehillim 45:10), in the gold of Ophir, pointed with six dots; וְלַכֶּתֶם אָמַרְתִּי מִבְטַחִֽי (Iyov 31:24), and to the gold I said, my trust; יִשְׁנֶא הַכֶּתֶם הַטּוֹב (Eichah 4:1), the good gold is changed; and וַֽחֲלִי־ כָתֶם (Mishlei 25:12), and an ornament of gold: it is the good gold. Rabbi Yonah wrote that they are pearls. But from its being tied to Ophir and to פָּז it looks like gold and not pearls.

כֶּתֶם פָּז (Shir HaShirim 5:11) means כתם and פז, gold and refined gold, with the vav missing, as in שֶׁמֶשׁ יָרֵחַ (Chavakuk 3:11), sun and moon, and others like it; or else כתם stands in the construct with פז, joined to it for its worth, as in זָהָב מוּפָז (Melachim I 10:18), refined gold.

From this sense is מִכְתָּם לְדָוִד (Tehillim 16:1), a michtam of David, that is, the mizmor was upon him like gold. נִכְתָּם עֲוֹנֵךְ (Yirmiyahu 2:22), your sin is marked, is like נרשם, marked in; and Chazal call the mark of a thing כתם, טק"א in the vernacular.

חמץ.sense: To become leavened, of dough. Vinegar, חֹמֶץ, is one with it in sense, as overleavened dough tastes of it. It also means to oppress. חֲמוּץ בְּגָדִים is red of garment.

more.t: כִּי לֹא חָמֵץ (Shemos 12:39), because it was not leavened, טֶרֶם יֶחְמָץ (Shemos 12:34), before it was leavened, and מִלּוּשׁ בָּצֵק עַד־חֻמְצָתוֹ (Hoshea 7:4), from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened, which he marks as an infinitive on the pattern of לְחֻמְלָה עָלָיִךְ (Yechezkel 16:5), to have pity on you. חָמֵץ תֵּאָפֶינָה (Vayikra 23:17), they shall be baked leavened, is the adjective, and כָּל־מַחְמֶצֶת (Shemos 12:20), anything leavened, the noun; though he allows that מחמצת may be an adjective describing the עריסה, the dough, and says their sense is known. חֹמֶץ יַיִן וְחֹמֶץ שֵׁכָר (Bamidbar 6:3), vinegar of wine and vinegar of strong drink, is one sense with the leavening of dough, he says, since dough leavened more than enough tastes of vinegar.

more.h: The judge who leavens his ruling
more.t: Chazal read אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ (Yeshayahu 1:17) in this sense, call fortunate the one who leavens. Radak explains: the one who leavens the judgment, not judging at once but only after much looking into it. So they said (Sanhedrin 35a), fortunate is the judge who leavens his judgment; that is, they called him fortunate.
כִּי יִתְחַמֵּץ לְבָבִי (Tehillim 73:21), when my heart was soured, he calls a borrowed use of the word, and it is anger.

בְּלִיל חָמִיץ יֹאכֵלוּ (Yeshayahu 30:24), they shall eat fodder that is חָמִיץ: Rabbi Yonah explains חמיץ as clean and good, and likens it to the Arabic, where clean good fodder for a beast is called חמצ"ה with a dot on the tzadi. Targum Yonasan has בְּלִיל מְפַטֵם, fattening provender.

Radak himself takes אַשְּׁרוּ חָמוֹץ (Yeshayahu 1:17) as a word describing the oppressed man, set the oppressed right; and in מִכַּף מְעַוֵּל וְחוֹמֵץ (Tehillim 71:4), from the hand of the wrongdoer and the oppressor, the word is one who oppresses, and is like חוֹמֵס with a samech, as הַשְּׁבִיסִים (Yeshayahu 3:18), the ornaments, with a samech, is of the sense of ושבצת, checkered work, with a tzadi. וְקַטֵּר מֵחָמֵץ תּוֹדָה (Amos 4:5), and burn a thanks offering of what was got by oppression, can be read from this, and Targum Yonasan has וּמַגְבַן מִן אוֹנֶס תּוֹדָתָא, an offering of thanks out of what was seized; on וְרֹעֶה זוֹלְלִים יַכְלִים אָבִיו (Mishlei 28:7), he who keeps company with gluttons shames his father, the Targum has וּדְמִתְחַבֵּר לִזְלִילֵי מַחֲמֵץ אֲבוּי, whoever joins himself to gluttons oppresses his father.
חֲמוּץ בְּגָדִים (Yeshayahu 63:1), red of garments: the word is red, as the sense of the pasuk shows.

גנב.sense: To steal, with the theft and the thief; and to steal a heart, which is to steal a man's knowledge: Lavan thought Yaakov was with his flock, and he had fled.

more.t: לָמָּה גָנַבְתָּ אֶת־אֱלֹהָֽי (Bereishis 31:30), why did you steal my gods? וַיִּגְנֹב יַֽעֲקֹב אֶת־לֵב לָבָן הָֽאֲרַמִּי (Bereishis 31:20), and Yaakov stole the heart of Lavan the Arami, means he stole his knowledge: Lavan thought Yaakov was with his flock, and he had fled. Likewise וַתִּגְנֹב אֹתִי (Bereishis 31:27), and you stole me, is as though it said my knowledge; or אותי, me, stands in place of מן, from, that is, you stole your knowledge from me, and so the Targum has וְכַסֵּיתָא מִנִּי, you hid it from me.

more.h: Stolen by day and by night
more.t: גְּנֻֽבְתִי יוֹם וּגְנֻֽבְתִי לָֽיְלָה (Bereishis 31:39), what was stolen by day and what was stolen by night. The yud in both is added, and the proper form is גְּנוּבַת יום וּגְנוּבַת לילה.

וְאִם־ גָּנֹב יִגָּנֵב (Shemos 22:11), and if it be stolen, מְגַנְּבֵי דְבָרַי (Yirmiyahu 23:30), who steal My words, וַיְגַנֵּב אַבְשָׁלוֹם אֶת־לֵב אַנְשֵׁי יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (Shmuel II 15:6), and Avshalom stole the heart of the men of Yisrael, כִּֽי־ גֻנֹּב גֻּנַּבְתִּי (Bereishis 40:15), for I was surely stolen away, וְאֵלַי דָּבָר יְגֻנָּב (Iyov 4:12), and a word was stolen to me, וְגֻנַּב מִבֵּית הָאִישׁ (Shemos 22:6), and it is stolen out of the man's house, and וַיִּתְגַּנֵּב הָעָם בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא (Shmuel II 19:4), and the people stole away that day.

The noun is גְּנֵבָה: אִם־הִמָּצֵא תִמָּצֵא בְיָדוֹ הַגְּנֵבָה (Shemos 22:3), if the theft is found in his hand, and וְנִמְכַּר בִּגְנֵֽבָתֽוֹ (Shemos 22:2), he is sold for his theft. The man is הַגַּנָּב: אִם־בַּמַּחְתֶּרֶת יִמָּצֵא הַגַּנָּב (Shemos 22:1), if the thief is found breaking in; אִם־ גַּנָּבִים בָּאוּ לְךָ, if thieves came to you, in Ovadiah; and כְּבֹשֶׁת גַּנָּב כִּי יִמָּצֵא (Yirmiyahu 2:26), like the shame of a thief when he is found, which Targum Yonasan renders כְּבַהֲתַת גְבַר דְמִתְחַשֵׁיב מְהֵימָן וּמִשְׁתְּכַח גְנִיב, like the shame of a man held trustworthy who is found to be a thief.

חמס.sense: Removing a thing from its place (so Rabbi Yonah gives it in Arabic): robbing it, pulling it down, taking its covering off; the תַּחְמָס is a bird that robs.

more.h: Taking a thing from its place
more.t: חָֽמְסוּ תוֹרָתִי (Yechezkel 22:26), they have robbed My Torah: since they do not keep it, it is as though they robbed it and removed it from its place. So too Rabbi Yonah wrote that the sense of חמס in Arabic is the removing of a thing from its place.

וּמְזִמּוֹת עָלַי תַּחְמֹֽסוּ (Iyov 21:27), the schemes of violence you think against me, means that you think of me that the violence is with me; or else it means that your schemes, which you think up against me, are violence and sin. וְֽחֹֽטְאִי חֹמֵס נַפְשׁוֹ (Mishlei 8:36), and he who sins against me does violence to his own soul.

וַיַּחְמֹס כגן שֹכו (Eichah 2:6), and He took away His booth as a garden, is rightly understood as כסכת גן, like a garden's booth: as a garden's booth is easily pulled down and taken away, so He did with His booth, which is Tzion.

יַחְמֹס כַּגֶּפֶן בִּסְרוֹ (Iyov 15:33), he will strip his unripe grapes like the vine, means he will remove and lay bare. So too, in the passive, נֶחְמְסוּ עֲקֵבָֽיִךְ (Yirmiyahu 13:22), your heels were laid bare: they were uncovered and the covering on them taken off.

וְאֶת־ הַתַּחְמָס (Devarim 14:16 in his edition), and the tachmas, is one of the unclean birds, called so because it does violence to the other birds and robs them; and so the Targum Yerushalmi has חטופיתא, the snatcher.

נהג.sense: To drive or to lead: a flock, cattle, a wagon, an east wind. Of the heart, to conduct oneself, as with wisdom. The noun is the manner of driving.

more.t: אוֹתִי נָהַג וַיֹּלַךְ (Eichah 3:2), He drove me and made me walk, נֹהֵג כַּצֹּאן יוֹסֵף (Tehillim 80:2), who leads Yosef like a flock, וַיִּנְהַג אֶת־כָּל־מִקְנֵהוּ (Bereishis 31:18), and he drove all his cattle, and נְהַג וָלֵךְ (Melachim II 4:24), drive and go. Also וְעֻזָּא וְאַחְיוֹ נֹֽהֲגִים בַּֽעֲגָלָֽה (Divrei HaYamim I 13:7), Uzza and Achyo driving the wagon, and וּמַלְכֵיהֶם נְהוּגִים (Yeshayahu 60:11), their kings led along.
וְלִבִּי נֹהֵג בַּחָכְמָה (Koheles 2:3), and my heart leading with wisdom, he reads as conducting himself with wisdom.

more.h: Driving with madness, and the noun
more.t: כִּי בְשִׁגָּעוֹן יִנְהָג (Melachim II 9:20), for he drives with madness, means that he drives his camp so; and the noun is כְּמִנְהַג יֵהוּא בֶן־נִמְשִׁי (Melachim II 9:20), like the driving of Yehu son of Nimshi.

נָהֲגוּ לִפְנֵי הַמִּקְנֶה הַהוּא (Shmuel I 30:20), they drove on before that cattle. נהגו is said of the flock and the cattle just named: as David took everything, so they drove everything off and left nothing, having no fear; and some of them went ahead of the cattle saying, this is David's spoil.

נִהַג רוּחַ־קָדִים (Shemos 10:13), He drove an east wind, וַתְּנַהֵג אֶת־בְּנֹתַי (Bereishis 31:26), and you drove my daughters off, and מְנַהֲגוֹת כְּקוֹל יוֹנִים (Nachum 2:8), leading her with a sound like doves: he reads מנהגות as leading her, their voice being like the voice of doves. All of these take an object.

נחה.sense: To lead and conduct: the sense of them all, he says, is conducting and leading. The word מִנְחָה, a gift, he explains elsewhere, under the root מָנַח.

more.t: נָחִיתָ כַצֹּאן עַמֶּךָ (Tehillim 77:21), You led Your people like a flock; מִי נָחַנִי עַד־אֱדֽוֹם (Tehillim 60:11), who has led me to Edom; וְנָֽחֲךָ י"י תָּמִיד (Yeshayahu 58:11), and Hashem will lead you always; לֵךְ נְחֵה אֶת־הָעָם (Shemos 32:34), go, lead the people; וּנְחֵנִי בְּאֹרַח מִישׁוֹר (Tehillim 27:11), and lead me in a level path.

תַּנְחֶה אֹתָךְ (Mishlei 6:22), it will lead you; לַנְחֹתָם הַדֶּרֶךְ (Shemos 13:21), to lead them the way; יַנְחֵנִי בְמַעְגְּלֵי־צֶדֶק (Tehillim 23:3), He leads me in paths of righteousness; וְלִפְנֵי גְדֹלִים יַנְחֶֽנּוּ (Mishlei 18:16), and it leads him before great men; וּבִתְבוּנוֹת כַּפָּיו יַנְחֵֽם (Tehillim 78:72), and with the skill of his hands he led them; וַיַּנְחֵם בַּחְלַח וּבְחָבוֹר (Melachim II 18:11), and he led them to Chalach and Chavor; שֹׁטֵחַ לַגּוֹיִם וַיַּנְחֵֽם (Iyov 12:23), He spreads the nations out and leads them; וְעַיִשׁ עַל־בָּנֶיהָ תַנְחֵֽם (Iyov 38:32), and Ayish with her sons, will you lead them; וַיַּנְחֵם אֶת־פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב (Shmuel I 22:4), and he led them before the king of Moav. All of them, he says, are conducting and leading.
וַיָּכִינוּ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָה (Bereishis 43:25), and they made the gift ready, he does not treat here: he says he has explained that word under the root מָנַח.

נהל.sense: To lead: of its verbs he says ענין נוהג, their sense is leading; and הַנַּהֲלֹלִים, a kind of low, lesser tree, which his father takes from הלל.

more.t: נֵהַלְתָּ בְעָזְּךָ (Shemos 15:13), You led in Your strength; וְעַל־מַבּוּעֵי מַיִם יְנַהֲלֵם (Yeshayahu 49:10), and by springs of water He will lead them; and אֵין־מְנַהֵל לָהּ (Yeshayahu 51:18), she has none to lead her.

more.h: With bread, and in His kindness
more.t: וַיְנַהֲלֵם בַּלֶּחֶם (Bereishis 47:17), and he led them on with bread, and וַיְנַהֲלֵם מִסָּבִיב (Divrei HaYamim II 32:22), and He led them on every side, which Radak explains as leading them in His kindness, so that they feared none of those around them. The reflexive is אֶתְנַהֲלָה לְאִטִּי (Bereishis 33:14), let me lead on at my slow pace. Of them all he says ענינם ענין נוהג, their sense is leading.

וּבְכֹל הַנַּהֲלֹלִים (Yeshayahu 7:19), and upon all the nahalolim, Radak takes as one of the kinds of low and lesser trees. His father wrote it under the root הָלַל, the nun being added; and Yonasan renders it the same way, וּבְכֹל בָּתֵּי תוּשׁבְּחָתָא, and in all the houses of praise.

מזג.sense: Mixture: הַמָּזֶג, a word known from Chazal, who speak of יין מזוג, mixed wine, explained as wine that water is mixed into.

more.t: אַל־יֶחְסַר הַמָּזֶג (Shir HaShirim 7:3), let the mixture not be wanting. The word is known from the Chachamim, who speak of יין מזוג (Negaim 1:2), mixed wine, explained as wine they mix water into.

דמע.sense: Tears, and to shed them, a sense he calls known; and וְדִמְעֲךָ, a byname for the oil or the wine running from the press like a tear, drop by drop.

more.t: וְדָמֹעַ תִּדְמַע וְתֵרַד עֵינִי דִּמְעָה (Yirmiyahu 13:17), my eye shall surely weep and run down with tears, וְדִמְעָתָהּ עַל לֶחֱיָהּ (Eichah 1:2), her tear upon her cheek, וְלוֹא תָבוֹא דִּמְעָתֶךָ (Yechezkel 24:16), and your tears shall not come, and in the plural כָּלוּ בַדְּמָעוֹת עֵינַי (Eichah 2:11), my eyes are spent with tears. The sense, he says, is known.
מְלֵאָתְךָ וְדִמְעֲךָ (Shemos 22:28), your fullness and your tear, the tear being a byname for the oil or the wine that comes down from the press like a tear, drop by drop.

ערם.sense: To be shrewd, the sense of stratagems and cunning; in a second sense, naked; in a third, a heap, as of grain. And עַרְמוֹן, a tree.

more.t: עָרֹם יַעְרִם הוּא (Shmuel I 23:22), he is very crafty; וּפֶתִי יַעְרִם (Mishlei 19:25), the simple one will grow shrewd; עַל־עַמְּךָ יַעֲרִימוּ סוֹד (Tehillim 83:4), against Your people they lay crafty counsel. The adjective is עָרוּם, as וְהַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה עָרוּם (Bereishis 3:1), and the snake was cunning. The noun is עָרְמָה, as וַיַּעֲשׂוּ גַם־הֵמָּה בְּעָרְמָה (Yehoshua 9:4), they too acted with cunning. In לֹכֵד חֲכָמִים בְּעָרְמָם (Iyov 5:13), He catches the wise in their cunning, the form is rightly בערמתם, as in כִּתְבוּנָם עֲצַבִּים (Hoshea 13:2), idols by their understanding, it is rightly בתבונתם. It is the sense of stratagems and cunning.

A second sense is the bare body: וְאַתְּ עֵרֹם וְעֶרְיָה (Yechezkel 16:7), and you were naked and bare, where עֵרֹם too is an adjective, masculine and feminine standing together because when Scripture speaks of Knesses Yisrael it speaks in both. It is written with a yud after the ayin in כִּי־עֵירֹם אָנֹכִי (Bereishis 3:10), for I am naked, and כִּי עֵירֻמִּם הֵם (Bereishis 3:7), that they were naked. Another pattern is עָרוֹם וְיָחֵף (Yeshayahu 20:2), naked and barefoot, and the plural takes a dagesh, וַיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם עֲרוּמִּים (Bereishis 2:25), the two of them were naked. The Mesorah marks the shrewd ones soft and the naked ones with a dagesh. The noun stands in וּבְעֵירֹם וּבְחֹסֶר כֹּל (Devarim 28:48), in nakedness and in want of everything, and עֵרֹם וְעֶרְיָה may be the noun as well, in nakedness and in bareness.

A third sense is a heap: בִּקְצֵה הָעֲרֵמָה (Rus 3:7), at the end of the heap, and עֲרֵמַת חִטִּים (Shir HaShirim 7:3), a heap of wheat. The plural is both feminine, עֲרֵמוֹת עֲרֵמוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 31:6), heaps upon heaps, and masculine, סָלּוּהָ כְמוֹ־עֲרֵמִים (Yirmiyahu 50:26), pile her up like heaps. The passive of it is נֶעֶרְמוּ מַיִם (Shemos 15:8), the waters were heaped up, which he glosses as their standing in heaps, as it says there, נִצְּבוּ כְמוֹ־נֵד, they stood up like a heap. By way of borrowing, מֵעֲרֵמוֹת הֶעָפָר (Nechemiah 3:34), out of the heaps of dust.

עַרְמוֹן is a tree: לַח וְלוּז וְעַרְמוֹן (Bereishis 30:37), fresh, and almond, and ערמון, and וְעַרְמֹנִים לֹא־הָיוּ כְּפֹארֹתָיו (Yechezkel 31:8), the trees of that name were not like its boughs. These are what Chazal call דופלי, and so the Targum renders it, וְדִדְלוּף. Some say it is the tree named in the vernacular קשטני"ר.

גדשׁ.sense: גָּדִישׁ, a stack: the grain once reaped, while it lies heaped on the threshing floor; from it Chazal speak of a measure heaped above its rim.

more.t: מִגָּדִישׁ וְעַד־קָמָה (Shoftim 15:5), from the stack to the standing grain, and וְנֶאֱכַל גָּדִישׁ (Shemos 22:5), and a stack was consumed. Grain that has been reaped and piled in the threshing floor is called גדיש.

From it Chazal use the word for filling a measure above its rim: כל חמדות שהיו במקדש היו נגדשות, all the measures in the Mikdash were heaped (Menachos 90a), and אין מוחקין במקום שגודשין, one does not level off a measure in a place where the custom is to heap it (Bava Basra 89a).

וְעַל־גָּדִישׁ יִשְׁקוֹד (Iyov 21:32), and on the stack he hastens, which he explains: he will hurry to be gathered to the graves; as the stack is gathered in its season once the crop has ripened, so he will be gathered in his time. Rabbeinu Hai explained גָּדִישׁ as the dome built over a grave, after the custom of the land of Yishmael, and Radak holds that he explained it well, since the text says just before it, והוא לקברות יובל (Iyov 21:32), and he is carried to the graves, and the dome is made like a stack.

עמר.sense: Making use of a person along with trading in him; and the עֹמֶר, a measure, with עָמִיר, which he explains as gathered bundles of ears.

more.h: Using a man and trading him
more.t: וְהִתְעַמֶּר־בּוֹ וּמְכָרוֹ (Devarim 24:7), and he makes use of him and sells him, and לֹֽא־תִתְעַמֵּר בָּהּ (Devarim 21:14), you shall not make use of her. The sense is use together with trading, as Chazal taught (Sanhedrin 85b): one who kidnaps a person of Israel is not liable until he brings him into his house and uses him and sells him, as it says וְהִתְעַמֶּר־בּוֹ וּמְכָרוֹ, that he uses him. And לֹֽא־תִתְעַמֵּר בָּהּ is glossed לא תשתמש ותשתעבד בה, you shall not use her and make her serve you, after you have lived with her as a husband.
עֹמֶר לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת (Shemos 16:16), an omer a head, is a measure, as the pasuk says, וְהָעֹמֶר עֲשִׂרִית הָאֵיפָה הוּא (Shemos 16:36), the omer is a tenth of an eifah.

And so too: וְהֵנִיף אֶת־הָעֹמֶר (Vayikra 23:11), he shall wave the omer; וְשָֽׁכַחְתָּ עֹמֶר בַּשָּׂדֶה (Devarim 24:19), and you forget an omer in the field; וְאָסַפְתִּי בָֽעֳמָרִים (Rus 2:7), and I will gather among the omers. Another pattern is עָמִיר: וּכְעָמִיר מֵאַֽחֲרֵי הַקֹּצֵר (Yirmiyahu 9:21), and like amir behind the reaper, and וּכְלַפִּיד אֵשׁ בְּעָמִיר (Zecharyah 12:6), and like a torch of fire among amir, which he explains as אגורות השבלים, gathered bundles of ears. The verb from it, with a dagesh, is וְחִצְנוֹ מְעַמֵּֽר (Tehillim 129:7), and his bosom, the one who gathers bundles of ears.

משׁה.sense: Drawing and bringing out, as from water; and מֶשִׁי, silk.

more.t: כִּי מִן־הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִהוּ (Shemos 2:10), because I drew him out of the water. Some read וַיִּזְכֹּר יְמֵי־עוֹלָם מֹשֶׁה עַמּוֹ (Yeshayahu 63:11), and he remembered the days of old, מֹשֶׁה his people, from this sense; or it is as it sounds, and means Moshe and his people. So too יַמְשֵׁנִי מִמַּיִם רַבִּים (Tehillim 18:17), He drew me out of many waters. The sense of all of them is drawing and bringing out.
וָאֲכַסֵּךְ מֶשִׁי (Yechezkel 16:10), and I covered you with silk, which he glosses as garments of silk, a thing well known.

משׁך.sense: To draw or pull: a bow, a yoke, kindness toward someone, a thing drawn out; מֶשֶׁךְ is also preciousness, a precious thing's name being drawn far; and Meshech, a nation.

more.t: וְאִישׁ מָשַׁךְ בַּקֶּשֶׁת לְתֻמּוֹ (Melachim I 22:34), and a man drew the bow in his innocence; אֲשֶׁר לֹא־ מָֽשְׁכָה בְּעֹֽל (Devarim 21:3), which has not pulled in a yoke; תִּמְשֹׁךְ לִוְיָתָן בְּחַכָּה (Iyov 40:25), can you draw out the livyasan with a hook. Of a scribe, מֹֽשְׁכִים בְּשֵׁבֶט סֹפֵֽר (Shoftim 5:14), those who draw with the scribe's pen, because the scribe draws the pen across the page as he writes. And לִמְשׁוֹךְ בַּיַּיִן אֶת־בְּשָׂרִי (Koheles 2:3), to draw my flesh with wine, is to lead it and draw it along with wine.

עַל־כֵּן מְשַׁכְתִּיךְ חָֽסֶד (Yirmiyahu 31:3) he reads as therefore I have drawn kindness toward you, and so מְשֹׁךְ חַסְדְּךָ לְיֹדְעֶיךָ (Tehillim 36:11), draw Your kindness to those who know You, after the manner of וַיֵּט אֵילָו חָסֶד (Bereishis 39:21), and He inclined kindness to him.

לֵךְ וּמָֽשַׁכְתָּ בְּהַר תָּבוֹר (Shoftim 4:6), go and draw at Har Tavor, he explains as draw the people to you at Har Tavor. The word of drawing is used because the sense is: bring them out against their will and win them over with words until you bring them to the war, for they were afraid of Sisra's army. And so he explains וּמָֽשַׁכְתִּי אֵלֶיךָ אֶל־נַחַל קִישׁוֹן אֶת־סִֽיסְרָא (Shoftim 4:6 in his edition), and I will draw Sisra to you at Nachal Kishon: for it is said that his astrologers saw his downfall and held him back from going out to war, and the Holy One strengthened his heart and drew him to Nachal Kishon. וַיִּמְשֹׁךְ הָאֹרֵב (Shoftim 20:37), and the ambush drew, means either that the ambush drew out a blast on the shofar or that it drew the people who were with it toward the city.

לֹא תִמָּשֵׁךְ עוֹד (Yechezkel 12:25), it shall no longer be drawn out; וְיָמֶיהָ לֹא יִמָּשֵֽׁכוּ (Yeshayahu 13:22), and her days shall not be drawn out; and תּוֹחֶלֶת מְמֻשָּׁכָה (Mishlei 13:12), hope drawn out.

But כִּי־גַרְתִּי מֶשֶׁךְ (Tehillim 120:5), that I have sojourned in Meshech, is the name of a nation named in the Torah, וּמֶשֶׁךְ וְתִירָֽס (Bereishis 10:2), and Meshech and Tiras. Yosef ben Gorion says they are the men of Tuscany. Ibn Ezra explained מַשְׁכִּים הָיוּ (Yirmiyahu 5:8), they were of Meshech, from this: horses belonging to Meshech, since from there come the mighty horses, neighing and lusting after the female.

וּמֶשֶׁךְ חָכְמָה מִפְּנִינִֽים (Iyov 28:18) he reads as the preciousness of wisdom is above pearls, since the name of a precious thing is drawn out far. So too נֹשֵׂא מֶֽשֶׁךְ ־הַזָּרַע (Tehillim 126:6), carrying the precious seed, since the seed is precious to the one who sows it, all the more so in the Negev; and for this reason the one who carries seed to sow is spoken of as בְּמֹשֵׁךְ הַזָּרַע (Amos 9:13), with the carrier of the seed.

שׁאף.sense: Drawing air into the nose or the mouth; by overstatement, swallowing; and looking and watching for a thing, which all its senses stand close to.

more.t: שָֽׁאֲפָה רוּחַ (Yirmiyahu 2:24), she draws in the wind, and שָֽׁאֲפוּ רוּחַ כַּתַּנִּים (Yirmiyahu 14:6), they drew in the wind like jackals: this is smelling and drawing the air into the nose. And so of drawing air into the mouth, פִּֽי־פָעַרְתִּי וָאֶשְׁאָפָה (Tehillim 119:131), I opened my mouth and drew in breath.

In this sense too, by way of overstatement: וְשָׁאַף צַמִּים חֵילָֽם (Iyov 5:5), and the thirsty swallow their wealth; כִּֽי־ שְׁאָפַנִי אֱנוֹשׁ (Tehillim 56:2), for man would swallow me; הַשֹּֽׁאֲפִים עַל־עֲפַר־אֶרֶץ (Amos 2:7), who swallow upon the dust of the earth; הַשֹּֽׁאֲפִים אֶבְיוֹן (Amos 8:4), who swallow the needy; אֶשֹּׁם וְאֶשְׁאַף יָֽחַד (Yeshayahu 42:14), I will lay waste and swallow together. All of them, he says, are swallowing.

In the sense of looking and watching for a thing: כְּעֶבֶד יִשְׁאַף ־צֵל (Iyov 7:2), like a servant who looks toward the shade; אַל־ תִּשְׁאַף הַלָּיְלָה (Iyov 36:20), do not look toward the night; שׁוֹאֵף זוֹרֵחַֽ הוּא שָֽׁם (Koheles 1:5), it looks toward the place where it rises. שָֽׁאֲפָה רוּחַ (Yirmiyahu 2:24) may be like these, רוּחַ then being a side and quarter. All the senses in this root, he says, stand close to looking at a thing and setting one's aim on it.

בית.sense: A house; a bird's nest, the grave and the prison are called so too; the people of a house; the inside of a thing; and a place, as a place of stones.

more.t: כִּי תִבְנֶה בַּיִת חָדָשׁ (Devarim 22:8), when you build a new house, and אֵין לְשִׁפְחָֽתְךָ כֹל בַּבַּיִת (Melachim II 4:2), your maidservant has nothing in the house, a sense he calls known.

A bird's nest is called a house: גַּם־צִפּוֹר מָצְאָה בַיִת (Tehillim 84:4), even the bird has found a house, and חֲסִידָה בְּרוֹשִׁים בֵּיתָֽהּ (Tehillim 104:17), the stork has her house in the cypresses. So too the grave, שָֽׁכְבוּ בְכָבוֹד אִישׁ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ (Yeshayahu 14:18), they lie in honour, each in his house; and the prison, אֲסִירָיו לֹֽא־פָתַח בָּֽיְתָה (Yeshayahu 14:17), he did not open the house for his prisoners.

וְשָֽׂמַחְתָּ אַתָּה וּבֵיתֶֽךָ (Devarim 14:26), and you shall rejoice, you and your house, is you and the people of your house. וַיַּעַשׂ לָהֶם בָּתִּֽים (Shemos 1:21), and He made them houses, is explained as people of a house, that is, that they were fruitful and multiplied, and likewise מוֹשִׁיב יְחִידִים בַּיְתָה (Tehillim 68:7), He settles the solitary in a household. What seems right to Radak is that it means He hid them from Pharaoh so that he did them no harm, in the way said of Yirmiyahu and Baruch, וַיַּסְתִּרֵם (Yirmiyahu 36:26), and Hashem hid them.

מִבַּיִת וּמִחוּץ (Shemos 25:11), within and without; כְּמַרְאֵה־אֵשׁ בֵּֽית ־לָהּ סָבִיב (Yechezkel 1:27), the look of fire inside it round about; אֲחֹֽרֵיהֶם בָּֽיְתָה (Melachim I 7:25), their backs turned inward.

בִּיתָן is the palace, so called because a palace is a large and honoured house: שָׁב מִגִּנַּת הַבִּיתָן (Esther 7:8), he came back from the palace garden. בָּֽתִּים לַבַּדִּים (Shemos 37:14), houses for the staves, are places; the בָּתִּים of אֲשֶׁר הַנָּשִׁים אֹֽרְגוֹת שָׁם בָּתִּים לָֽאֲשֵׁרָֽה (Melachim II 23:7), where the women wove houses for the Asherah, are hangings; כְּבֵית סָאתַיִם (Melachim I 18:32), as a house of two se'ah, is ground in which two se'ah are sown; בֵּית אֲבָנִים יֶחֱזֶֽה (Iyov 8:17), he beholds a house of stones, is a place of stones; and וּבָתֵּי הַנֶּפֶשׁ (Yeshayahu 3:20), the houses of the soul, is an ornament the women hang over their hearts.

Some say בית is found as a delicate way of speaking, because they found כִּי שָׁחָה אֶל־מָוֶת בֵּיתָהּ (Mishlei 2:18), for her house sinks down to death. It can be read that שָׁחָה is said of the harlot herself, who sinks toward death, which is her house. His father writes that שָׁחָה is masculine, on the weight of עָשָֹה, made, and בָּנָה, built, even though the accent falls on the earlier syllable.

חנה.sense: To encamp, and to encamp against a city. The camp, מַחֲנֶה, comes from it, and the spear, חֲנִית, may as well.

more.t: קִרְיַת חָנָה דָוִד (Yeshayahu 29:1), the city where David encamped; וַיִּֽחַן ־שָׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל (Shemos 19:2), and Yisrael encamped there; וַֽחֲנֵה עַל־הָעִיר וְלָכְדָהּ (Shmuel II 12:28), encamp against the city and capture it. At פִּזַּר עַצְמוֹת חֹנָךְ (Tehillim 53:6), He scattered the bones of חֹנָךְ, which Radak explains as one encamping against you, just as בָּנַי יְצָאֻנִי (Yirmiyahu 10:20) means my sons have gone out from me, and לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָֽע (Tehillim 5:5) means evil shall not dwell with You. All of these he counts as verbs that take no object.

וְחָנִיתִי כַדּוּר עָלָיִךְ (Yeshayahu 29:3) he explains as וחניתי בכדור, I will encamp against you in a ring; and וְחָנִיתִי לְבֵיתִי מִצָּבָה (Zecharyah 9:8) as I will encamp in my house, and they will not fear a garrison that would encamp against them. He allows that both may instead be verbs that take an object.

מַֽחֲנֶה is found masculine and feminine. Masculine: וְהָיָה הַמַּֽחֲנֶה הַנִּשְׁאָר (Bereishis 32:9), the camp that is left. Feminine: אִם־ תַּֽחֲנֶה עָלַי מַֽחֲנֶה (Tehillim 27:3), if a camp encamps against me, and הַמַּֽחֲנֶה הָאַחַת (Bereishis 32:9), the one camp. The plural runs both ways too: masculine in וַיָּשֹׁסּוּ אֶת־ מַֽחֲנֵיהֶֽם (Shmuel I 17:53), they plundered their camps, and feminine in לִשְׁנֵי מַֽחֲנֽוֹת (Bereishis 32:11), into two camps. וַיִּקְרָא שֵׁם־הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא מַֽחֲנָֽיִם (Bereishis 32:3), he called the name of that place Machanayim, means two camps: he called the place so for his camp that had been with Lavan and for the camp of Hashem that he saw afterward.

Of this root and this sense is אֶל־בֵּית הַבּוֹר וְאֶל־ הַֽחֲנֻיוֹת (Yirmiyahu 37:16), to the dungeon house and to the chanuyos. The word is well known in the words of Chazal (Pesachim 31b), חנות של ישראל ומלאי של ישראל, a Jew's shop and a Jew's wares; and it is called so because travellers encamp there.

חֲנִית, the spear, may be of this root: וְלַהֶבֶת חֲנִיתוֹ (Shmuel I 17:7), the blade of his spear; וַתֵּצֵא הַֽחֲנִית מֵאַֽחֲרָיו (Shmuel II 2:23), and the spear came out behind him; נִשְׁעָן עַל־ חֲנִיתוֹ (Shmuel II 1:6), leaning on his spear. The plural is found masculine, הַֽחֲנִיתִים וְאֶת־הַמָּגִנּוֹת (Divrei HaYamim II 23:9), the spears and the shields, and feminine, וַֽחֲנִיתֽוֹתֵיהֶם לְמַזְמֵרוֹת (Yeshayahu 2:4), their spears into pruning hooks.

שֹאר.sense: שְׂאֹר, the leaven with which the dough is leavened.

more.t: כִּי כָל־שְׂאֹר (Vayikra 2:11), for any leaven, and שְׂאֹר לֹא יִמָּצֵא בְּבָתֵּיכֶם (Shemos 12:19), no leaven shall be found in your houses: it is the leavening with which the dough is leavened.

שׁאר.sense: To remain, be left, and leave over, with שְׁאֵרִית, the remnant; a second sense, שְׁאֵר, flesh, and from it a near relative; also food, and the kneading trough.

more.t: עוֹד שָׁאַר הַקָּטָן (Shmuel I 16:11), the youngest still remains; וְאִם־מְעַט נִשְׁאַר (Vayikra 25:52), and if little remains; וְהָעָם הַנִּשְׁאָר (Melachim II 25:22), the people who were left. Where the verb takes an object, לֹא הִשְׁאִיר שָׂרִיד (Yehoshua 10:28), he left no survivor, and תַּשְׁאִיר מֵאָה (Amos 5:3), it shall leave a hundred. The noun is שְׁאֵרִית יִשְׂרָאֵל (Tzefaniah 3:13), the remnant of Yisrael, written also without the alef, שֵׁרִית יִשְׂרָאֵל (Divrei HaYamim I 12:38 in his edition).

In וְכָל־ הַנִּשְׁאָר מִֽכָּל־הַמְּקֹמוֹת אֲשֶׁר הוּא גָֽר־שָׁם (Ezra 1:4), and everyone who is left, from all the places where he sojourns, the mem of מִכָּל goes not with הַנִּשְׁאָר but with יְנַשְּׂאוּהוּ אַנְשֵׁי מְקֹמוֹ in the same pasuk, the men of his place shall support him, since נשאר is linked only by a beis.

אִם־לֹא שֵֽׁרִותִךָ, read שֵֽׁרִיתִיךָ, לְטוֹב (Yirmiyahu 15:11) may be from this root, and the Targum says as much: אם לָא סוֹפֵךְ יְהֵא לְטַב, if your end will not be for good. Dunash wrote it from וּמְשָׁרֵא קִטְרִין (Daniel 5:12), and loosing knots, and then its sense is like I have released you. On that reading the pasuk is Hashem telling the navi that He will release him from his confinement, and in the time of Yisrael's trouble will make the enemy entreat him to stay in the land or to go with him and be there in honour. That is what the chief of the guard said to Yirmiyahu, הִנֵּה פִתַּחְתִּיךָ הַיּוֹם מִן־הָֽאזִקִּים אֲשֶׁר עַל־יָדֶךָ (Yirmiyahu 40:4), see, I have freed you today from the chains on your hand.

שְׁאָר יָשׁוּב (Yeshayahu 10:21), a remnant shall return. וּשְׁאָר רוּחַ לוֹ (Malachi 2:15), and he had a remnant of spirit, can be read as excellence and eminence, since יתר and שאר are one in sense, and as the root יתר holds eminence and advantage, so does the root שאר. ולא אחד עשה, and the one did not do so, is then Avraham, who was one and a father in his faith to those who came after him: he did not do as you do, for he did not chase after desire, but sought to leave seed of Hashem. His father reads ולא אחד עשה as the people's own words to the navi, put in wonder: Avraham avinu, who was one, did he not do as we do, leaving his wife and living with Hagar her maidservant, though he had a remnant of spirit and was a navi? And the navi answered them that he was seeking seed of Hashem: that is, when he lived with Hagar he did so only to seek seed of Hashem, since he had no seed from Sarah, and even so he did not betray his wife, for he acted by her will and at her bidding; but you are to guard your spirit, and let none of you betray his wife by leaving her and living with the daughter of a foreign god.

A second sense is flesh: אִם־יָכִין שְׁאֵר לְעַמּֽוֹ (Tehillim 78:20), can He prepare flesh for His people; וַיַּמְטֵר עֲלֵיהֶם כֶּעָפָר שְׁאֵר (Tehillim 78:27), He rained flesh upon them like dust; כָּלָה שְׁאֵרִי וּלְבָבִי (Tehillim 73:26), my flesh and my heart fail.
